Also use for: permissions (\"allow X\", \"add permission\", \"move permission to\"), env vars (\"set X=Y\"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: \"allow npm commands\", \"add bq permission to global settings\", \"move permission to user settings\", \"set DEBUG=true\", \"when claude stops show X\". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.\n- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. \"check the deploy every 5 minutes\", \"keep running /babysit-prs\"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.\n- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run (\"run this once at 3pm\", \"remind me to check X tomorrow\").\n- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps.       "content":"-- SoraMech runner — entry point for FSM execution.\n-- Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then executes it synchronously.\n-- Run: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\n-- Output goes to map-dir/tmp/last-run.json; logs to map-dir/tmp/logs/.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal loader   = require(\"003-loader\")\nlocal executor = require(\"004-executor\")\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if not map_dir then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n\n    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n    if not graph then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local ok, val_errs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\n    if not ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: validation failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(val_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local run_ok, run_err = executor.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    if not run_ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: execution failed: \" .. tostring(run_err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    print(\"runner: OK — \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json written\")\n    os.exit(0)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n"
    }
  },
  "uuid":"9ee85a78-43d1-42ae-b03a-bfcdae69d652",

      "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Creates a new SoraMech map directory with all required files and a tmp/ symlink.\n# The map directory is created under ${DIR}/maps/<name>.\n# Run: scripts/create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nMAP_NAME=\"${1}\"\nMAPS_ROOT=\"${2:-${DIR}/maps}\"\n\nif [ -z \"${MAP_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"usage: create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nMAP_DIR=\"${MAPS_ROOT}/${MAP_NAME}\"\n\nif [ -d \"${MAP_DIR}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: map directory already exists: ${MAP_DIR}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# create directory structure\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/boxes\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/data\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/src\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers\"\n\n# create /tmp target before symlinking — logs/ and cache/ live there at runtime\nTMP_TARGET=\"/tmp/soramech-${MAP_NAME}\"\nmkdir -p \"${TMP_TARGET}\"\n\n# tmp/ is a symlink to /tmp/soramech-<name>/ so ephemeral files stay in RAM\nln -s \"${TMP_TARGET}\" \"${MAP_DIR}/tmp\"\n\n# write meta.json with placeholders\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\"\n}\nMETAJSON\n\n# write drivers.json pointing at the built-in driver scripts in the soramech root\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers.json\" << DRIVERSJSON\n{\n  \".lua\": \"${DIR}/drivers/lua.sh\",\n  \".c\":   \"${DIR}/drivers/c.sh\",\n  \".sh\":  \"${DIR}/drivers/bash.sh\"\n}\nDRIVERSJSON\n\necho \"created: ${MAP_DIR}\"\necho \"next: edit meta.json to set entry_box_id, then add boxes in ${MAP_DIR}/boxes/\"\n"

          "content":"# 214 — tmp symlink recreation on reboot\n\n## Status\nin-progress\n\n## Current Behavior\nEach map directory has a `tmp/` symlink pointing to `/tmp/soramech-<name>/`.\nOn system reboot, `/tmp/` is cleared, so the symlink target no longer exists.\nSubsequent runs fail when trying to read or write files through the broken symlink:\n\n```\ncat: /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/maps/classify-demo/tmp/last-run.json: No such file or directory\n```\n\nThe runner's existing `mkdir -p .../tmp/logs` call does not reliably recreate\nthe symlink target because the broken symlink is traversed, not the target itself.\n\n## Intended Behavior\nBefore any tmp/ access, the runner should resolve the symlink target and ensure\nthe directory exists, creating it if /tmp/ was wiped since last run.\n\n## Suggested Implementation Steps\n1. In `soramech-runner.lua`, before the existing `mkdir -p .../tmp/logs`:\n   - Use `readlink` (read-only) to resolve `map_dir .. \"/tmp\"` to its target path\n   - Run a separate `mkdir -p` on the resolved target path\n2. The existing `mkdir -p .../tmp/logs` then succeeds as before.\n\n## Relevant Files\n- `soramech-runner.lua` — entry point; line 24 is where the fix is applied\n- `scripts/create-map.sh` — originally creates the symlink and its target\n",

    "originalFile":"-- SoraMech runner — entry point for FSM execution.\n-- Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then executes it synchronously.\n-- Run: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\n-- Output goes to map-dir/tmp/last-run.json; logs to map-dir/tmp/logs/.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal loader   = require(\"003-loader\")\nlocal executor = require(\"004-executor\")\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if not map_dir then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n\n    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n    if not graph then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local ok, val_errs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\n    if not ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: validation failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(val_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local run_ok, run_err = executor.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    if not run_ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: execution failed: \" .. tostring(run_err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    print(\"runner: OK — \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json written\")\n    os.exit(0)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n",
    "oldString":"    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")",
    "newString":"    -- if /tmp/ was cleared on reboot, the symlink target is gone; recreate it\n    local rp = io.popen(\"readlink \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp\")\n    local tmp_target = rp and rp:read(\"*l\")\n    if rp then rp:close() end\n    if tmp_target then\n        os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmp_target)\n    end\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")",

      "content":"\n    -- if /tmp/ was cleared on reboot, the symlink target is gone; recreate it\n    local rp = io.popen(\"readlink \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp\")\n    local tmp_target = rp and rp:read(\"*l\")\n    if rp then rp:close() end\n    if tmp_target then\n        os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmp_target)\n    end\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n\n    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n    if not graph then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do"
    }
  },
  "uuid":"f9f7baed-43f9-469f-a037-7e265835ff37",

    "originalFile":"# 211 — File browser library directories\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe file browser only shows files in the map's own `src/` directory. Shared\nlibraries in `libs/` or other directories cannot be browsed or selected as a\nbox ref without manually typing the path.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA button at the top of the file browser (\"+ library dir\") prompts the user\nfor an absolute directory path and stores it in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`.\nThese directories appear as collapsible groups in the browser alongside `src/`.\nA `▶/▼` toggle collapses or expands each group. Files in extra dirs are fetched\nand parsed identically to src/ files.\n\nServer adds two routes:\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc` — returns extra dirs and their file listings\n- `GET /maps/:name/extrasrc/:index/:file` — returns a file from extra dir at\n  that index as text/plain\n\nExtra dirs are stored as absolute paths in `meta.json.extra_src_dirs`. The\nserver reads them at request time; no restart needed when dirs are added.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — add `handle_list_extrasrc` and\n   `handle_get_extrasrc`; add both to the dispatch table.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js` — add `list_extra_src()` and `get_extra_src_file(i, f)`.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — refactor `render()` to load both src/ and\n   extra dirs; render as collapsible groups with toggle state in a local Set;\n   add \"+ library dir\" button that calls `API.put_meta`.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/005-http-server.lua — handle_list_src, dispatch table\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- assets/js/007-filebrowser.js — render, render_fn_list\n- maps/*/meta.json — extra_src_dirs field\n",
    "oldString":"## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — add `handle_list_extrasrc` and\n   `handle_get_extrasrc`; add both to the dispatch table.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js` — add `list_extra_src()` and `get_extra_src_file(i, f)`.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — refactor `render()` to load both src/ and\n   extra dirs; render as collapsible groups with toggle state in a local Set;\n   add \"+ library dir\" button that calls `API.put_meta`.",
    "newString":"## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — add `handle_list_extrasrc` and\n   `handle_get_extrasrc`; add both to the dispatch table.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js` — add `list_extra_src()` and `get_extra_src_file(i, f)`.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — refactor `render()` to load both src/ and\n   extra dirs; render as collapsible groups with toggle state in a local Set;\n   add \"+ library dir\" button that calls `API.put_meta`.\n4. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — right-click on an extra-dir group header\n   shows a \"hide directory\" context menu item that removes the path from\n   `meta.extra_src_dirs` and re-renders. 'ctx-item danger' : 'ctx-item';\n      el.textContent = item.label;\n      // stopPropagation so the document click listener above doesn't immediately close it\n      el.addEventListener('click', e => { e.stopPropagation(); menu.style.display = 'none'; item.action(); });\n      menu.appendChild(el);\n    });\n    menu.style.left    = screen_x + 'px';\n    menu.style.top     = screen_y + 'px';\n    menu.style.display = 'block';\n    const r = menu.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (r.right  > window.innerWidth)  menu.style.left = (screen_x - r.width)  + 'px';\n    if (r.bottom > window.innerHeight) menu.style.top  = (screen_y - r.height) + 'px';\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, path?, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {",

      "content":"  // {{{ show_fb_ctx_menu\n  // Displays a small floating context menu; reuses .ctx-item CSS from the global stylesheet.\n  // items: [{label, action, danger?}]\n  function show_fb_ctx_menu(screen_x, screen_y, items) {\n    let menu = document.getElementById('fb-ctx-menu');\n    if (!menu) {\n      menu = document.createElement('div');\n      menu.id = 'fb-ctx-menu';\n      menu.style.cssText =\n        'position:fixed;background:#181c28;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:4px;padding:4px 0;z-index:1001;min-width:150px;' +\n        'box-shadow:0 4px 16px #00000066;display:none;';\n      document.body.appendChild(menu);\n      // close on any click or Escape — attached once at creation\n      document.addEventListener('click', () => { menu.style.display = 'none'; });\n      document.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n        if (e.key === 'Escape') menu.style.display = 'none';\n      });\n    }\n    menu.innerHTML = '';\n    items.forEach(item => {\n      const el = document.createElement('div');\n      el.className  = item.danger ? 'ctx-item danger' : 'ctx-item';\n      el.textContent = item.label;\n      // stopPropagation so the document click listener above doesn't immediately close it\n      el.addEventListener('click', e => { e.stopPropagation(); menu.style.display = 'none'; item.action(); });\n      menu.appendChild(el);\n    });\n    menu.style.left    = screen_x + 'px';\n    menu.style.top     = screen_y + 'px';\n    menu.style.display = 'block';\n    const r = menu.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (r.right  > window.innerWidth)  menu.style.left = (screen_x - r.width)  + 'px';\n    if (r.bottom > window.innerHeight) menu.style.top  = (screen_y - r.height) + 'px';\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, path?, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n    // collapsed state: set of group labels\n    const collapsed = new Set();\n\n    // load src/ and extra dirs in parallel\n    let src_files = [], extra_dirs = [];\n    try {\n      [src_files, extra_dirs] = await Promise.all([\n        API.list_src_files().catch(() => []),\n        API.list_extra_src().catch(() => []),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">load error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // build unified group list\n    const groups = [];\n    if (src_files.length > 0) {\n      groups.push({\n        label: 'src/',\n        files: src_files,\n        fetch_file: f => API.get_src_file(f),\n      });\n    }\n    (extra_dirs || []).forEach(d => {\n      if (d.files && d.files.length > 0) {\n        groups.push({\n          label:      d.label + '/',\n          path:       d.path,   // absolute path; used by \"hide directory\" right-click action\n          files:      d.files,\n          fetch_file: f => API.get_extra_src_file(d.index, f),\n        });\n      }\n    });\n\n    const show_file_list = () => {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // add-library-dir button\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ library dir';\n      add_btn.className   = 'fb-add-dir-btn';\n      add_btn.onclick = () => {\n        show_dir_picker(container,\n          async (path) => {\n            try {\n              const meta = await API.get_meta();\n              const dirs = meta.extra_src_dirs || [];\n              if (!dirs.includes(path)) {\n                dirs.push(path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, extra_src_dirs: dirs });\n              }\n              render(container, on_select);\n            } catch(e) {\n              show_file_list();\n              const note = document.createElement('div');\n              note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n              note.textContent = 'could not save dir: ' + e.message;\n              container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n            }\n          },\n          () => show_file_list()\n        );\n      };\n      container.appendChild(add_btn);\n\n      if (groups.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = 'src/ is empty — add source files or a library dir';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      groups.forEach(group => {\n        const is_collapsed = collapsed.has(group.label);"

      "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
    }

The Firefox errors** — these have nothing to do with SoraMech:\n- `moz-extension://...Could not establish connection` — a Firefox browser extension on your machine is failing to message a tab/background page. Harmless noise from whatever extension that UUID belongs to.\n- The `gtk_widget_get_window` warning — a harmless GTK assertion in Firefox itself on Linux, fires commonly during window lifecycle events.\n\n**2. Call vs Data boxes** — currently only a visual distinction. Both execute identically in the runner — the executor doesn't branch on `kind` at all. The color difference (`call` = blue, `data` = green) is the only runtime effect. The intent is semantic: `call` for side-effecting computation, `data` for pure data transformation — but that branching logic hasn't been implemented yet.\n\n**3. The collapse bug** — the collapsed Set uses `group.label` (just the last folder name, e.g. `libs/`) as its key. If two added library dirs share the same folder name, they toggle together. Fix: use the full path as the key for extra dirs."

      "content":"// Thin fetch wrapper for the soramech-server REST API.\n// All functions are async and throw on non-2xx responses.\n\nconst API = (() => {\n  let base_url = '';\n  let map_name = '';\n\n  // {{{ init\n  function init(url, name) { base_url = url.replace(/\\/$/, ''); map_name = name; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ request\n  async function request(method, path, body) {\n    const opts = { method, headers: {} };\n    if (body !== undefined) {\n      opts.headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';\n      opts.body = JSON.stringify(body);\n    }\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + path, opts);\n    const text = await res.text();\n    let data;\n    try { data = JSON.parse(text); } catch { data = { error: text }; }\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(data.error || `HTTP ${res.status}`);\n    return data;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_maps\n  async function list_maps() { return request('GET', '/maps'); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ list_boxes\n  async function list_boxes() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_box\n  async function get_box(id) {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ put_box\n  async function put_box(id, data) {\n    return request('PUT', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`, data);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_box\n  async function delete_box(id) {\n    return request('DELETE', `/maps/${map_name}/boxes/${id}`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_meta\n  async function get_meta() {\n    return request('GET', list_src_files\n  async function list_src_files() {\n    return request('GET', `/maps/${map_name}/src`);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_src_file\n  // Returns raw text, not JSON — the request() helper would mis-parse source code.\n  async function get_src_file(filename) {\n    const res = await fetch(base_url + `/maps/${map_name}/src/${encodeURIComponent(filename)}`);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new get_box, put_box, delete_box,\n           get_meta, put_meta, get_data, put_data,\n           list_src_files, get_src_file,\n           list_extra_src, get_extra_src_file,\n           list_dirs };\n})();\n"

          "content":"# 211a — Unify src/ into the same directory pipeline as extra dirs\n\n## Status\nin-progress\n\n## Current behavior\nThe file browser treats `src/` as a special case:\n- `src/` is always shown (implicit, not stored in meta.json)\n- Extra dirs are stored in `meta.json` → `extra_src_dirs`\n- The server has two separate endpoints: `/maps/:name/src` and `/maps/:name/extrasrc`\n- The client calls both and merges them\n- The context menu \"hide directory\" only works for extra dirs (`if (group.path)`)\n\nThe implicit exception violates the principle that all dirs go through the same pipeline.\n\n## Intended behavior\nAll browseable directories, including `src/`, flow through the same data path:\n- `meta.json` gains a `src_dirs` field: an array of absolute paths\n- `src/` is just the first entry; extra dirs are appended as before\n- One server endpoint returns all of them\n- One client call fetches all of them\n- \"Hide\" removes from `src_dirs` for any entry, including `src/`\n- No `if (group.path)` exception in the UI — all groups are treated identically\n\nMigration: if `src_dirs` is absent in meta.json, the server synthesizes it at read-time\nfrom the map's `src/` path + any existing `extra_src_dirs` entries.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — update `handle_list_extrasrc` and `handle_get_extrasrc`\n   to read from `src_dirs` (with migration from `extra_src_dirs` + implicit `src/`).\n2. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — remove `list_src_files()` call; only use\n   `list_extra_src()`; remove separate `src/` group construction; remove `if (group.path)`\n   exception; update hide/add actions to use `src_dirs` field.\n3. `scripts/create-map.sh` — initialize `src_dirs` in meta.json with the map's absolute\n   `src/` path at creation time.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — handle_list_extrasrc, handle_get_extrasrc\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — render, show_file_list, show_dir_picker\n- `scripts/create-map.sh` — meta.json template\n- `maps/*/meta.json` — needs `src_dirs` field (server migrates on first read)\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/211a-unify-src-dirs-pipeline.md"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01ES4u8brmnKNyM4kARidbGF"
      }]
  },

1, label = label, path = dir_path, files = files }\n    end\n    json_ok(client, result)\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ handle_get_extrasrc\n-- Returns the raw text of a file from src_dirs[index].\nlocal function handle_get_extrasrc(client, req, maps_root)\n    local map_name  = req.parts[2]\n    local dir_index = tonumber(req.parts[4])\n    local file_name = req.parts[5]\n    if not dir_index or not file_name then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"missing dir index or filename\")\n    end\n    if file_name:find(\"%.%.\", 1, true) or file_name:find(\"/\", 1, true) then\n        return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid filename\")\n    end\n\n    local meta_path = safe_path(maps_root, map_name, \"meta.json\")\n    if not meta_path then return json_err(client, \"400 Bad Request\", \"invalid path\") end\n\n    local raw, _ = read_file(meta_path)\n    if not raw then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"meta.json not found\") end\n    local meta, _, _ = json.decode(raw)\n    if not meta then return json_err(client, \"500 Internal Server Error\", \"bad meta.json\") end\n\n    local src_dirs = resolve_src_dirs(meta, maps_root, map_name)\n    local dir_path = src_dirs[dir_index + 1]  -- lua 1-indexed\n    if not dir_path then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", \"no src dir at index \" .. dir_index) end\n\n    local file_path = dir_path .. \"/\" .. file_name\n    local content, ferr = read_file(file_path)\n    if not content then return json_err(client, \"404 Not Found\", tostring(ferr)) end\n    respond(client, \"200 OK\", content, \"text/plain\")\nend\n-- }}}",

    "originalFile":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Creates a new SoraMech map directory with all required files and a tmp/ symlink.\n# The map directory is created under ${DIR}/maps/<name>.\n# Run: scripts/create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nMAP_NAME=\"${1}\"\nMAPS_ROOT=\"${2:-${DIR}/maps}\"\n\nif [ -z \"${MAP_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"usage: create-map.sh <map-name> [maps-root]\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nMAP_DIR=\"${MAPS_ROOT}/${MAP_NAME}\"\n\nif [ -d \"${MAP_DIR}\" ]; then\n    echo \"error: map directory already exists: ${MAP_DIR}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# create directory structure\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/boxes\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/data\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/src\"\nmkdir -p \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers\"\n\n# create /tmp target before symlinking — logs/ and cache/ live there at runtime\nTMP_TARGET=\"/tmp/soramech-${MAP_NAME}\"\nmkdir -p \"${TMP_TARGET}\"\n\n# tmp/ is a symlink to /tmp/soramech-<name>/ so ephemeral files stay in RAM\nln -s \"${TMP_TARGET}\" \"${MAP_DIR}/tmp\"\n\n# write meta.json with placeholders\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\"\n}\nMETAJSON\n\n# write drivers.json pointing at the built-in driver scripts in the soramech root\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/drivers.json\" << DRIVERSJSON\n{\n  \".lua\": \"${DIR}/drivers/lua.sh\",\n  \".c\":   \"${DIR}/drivers/c.sh\",\n  \".sh\":  \"${DIR}/drivers/bash.sh\"\n}\nDRIVERSJSON\n\necho \"created: ${MAP_DIR}\"\necho \"next: edit meta.json to set entry_box_id, then add boxes in ${MAP_DIR}/boxes/\"\n",
    "oldString":"# write meta.json with placeholders\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\"\n}\nMETAJSON",
    "newString":"# write meta.json — src_dirs seeds the file browser with this map's own src/ dir\ncat > \"${MAP_DIR}/meta.json\" << METAJSON\n{\n  \"name\": \"${MAP_NAME}\",\n  \"description\": \"\",\n  \"entry_box_id\": \"\",\n  \"src_dirs\": [\"${MAP_DIR}/src\"]\n}\nMETAJSON",

The `.sh` driver (`drivers/bash.sh`) sources your script file and calls the named function with positional args. Any `.sh` file with named functions works as a box ref. The `driver-test` map exercises it — you can look at `maps/driver-test/boxes/bash-box.json` as a working example.\n\nThe `src/` unification is done: existing maps migrate transparently on first server request (the `resolve_src_dirs` function synthesizes `src_dirs` from the implicit `src/` path + any old `extra_src_dirs`). New maps get `src_dirs` initialized by `create-map.sh`. All groups go through the same pipeline with no exceptions."

        "content":"-- Ollama API client — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"ollama\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ directory\n-- to use it directly as a call box via the file browser.\n-- Uses curl; no extra Lua packages needed beyond dkjson.\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\nlocal DEFAULT_HOST  = \"http://localhost:11434\"\nlocal DEFAULT_MODEL = \"llama3.2\"\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ curl_post\nlocal function curl_post(url, payload)\n    local cmd = \"curl -s --max-time 120 -X POST \" .. shell_quote(url) ..\n                \" -H \" .. shell_quote(\"Content-Type: application/json\") ..\n                \" -d \" .. shell_quote(payload)\n    local ph  = io.popen(cmd)\n    local out = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    ph:close()\n    return out\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.query\n-- Plain text generation. model and host are optional; nil or empty uses defaults.\nfunction M.query(prompt, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/generate\", json.encode({\n        model  = model,\n        prompt = tostring(prompt),\n        stream = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.query: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.response\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.chat\n-- Chat-style query. system prompt is optional; nil or empty omits it.\n-- model and host default when nil or empty.\nfunction M.chat(prompt, system, model, host)\n    model = (model ~= nil and model ~= \"\") and model or DEFAULT_MODEL\n    host  = (host  ~= nil and host  ~= \"\") and host  or DEFAULT_HOST\n    local messages = {}\n    if system ~= nil and system ~= \"\" then\n        messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"system\", content = tostring(system) }\n    end\n    messages[#messages + 1] = { role = \"user\", content = tostring(prompt) }\n    local out  = curl_post(host .. \"/api/chat\", json.encode({\n        model    = model,\n        messages = messages,\n        stream   = false,\n    }))\n    local resp, _, err = json.decode(out)\n    if not resp then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: bad response: \" .. tostring(err) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    if resp.error then\n        io.stderr:write(\"ollama.chat: \" .. tostring(resp.error) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    return resp.message and resp.message.content or nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M",

        "content":"# claude-conversation-exporter.sh\n\nFull-featured conversation export with per-project output paths, multiple verbosity levels, and TUI-based project selection. interface.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh\n```\n\n### Export Specific Project\nBrowse conversations for a named project.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh handheld-office\n```\n\n### Export Specific Conversation\nExport a single conversation by ID or partial match.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh handheld-office c0567703\n```\n\n### Export All Conversations\nDump all conversations for a project.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh handheld-office all > backup.md\n```\n\n### Minimal Output for Code Extraction\nStrip everything except code blocks and essential content.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh -v0 project-name conversation-id\n```\n\n### Complete Debug Output\nInclude all LLM execution details and intermediate steps.\n\n```bash\n./claude-conversation-exporter.sh -v4 project-name all > debug.md\n```\n\n### Raw Unfiltered Export\nInclude absolutely everything from the         "content":"backup_project() {\n    local project_dir=\"$1\"\n    local conv_count=\"$2\"\n\n    # Create llm-transcripts directory if it doesn't exist\n    local transcripts_dir=\"${project_dir}/llm-transcripts\"\n    mkdir -p \"$transcripts_dir\"\n\n    # Check if we have required scripts\n    local backup_script=\"${DIR}/backup-conversations\"\n    local exporter=\"${DIR}/claude-conversation-exporter.sh\"\n\n    if [[ ! -x \"$backup_script\" ]]; then\n        error \"  backup-conversations not found at $backup_script\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    # Step 1: Run backup-conversations to create baseline summaries\n    echo \"  Step 1/2: Running backup-conversations...\"\n    local backup_output\n    backup_output=$(\"$backup_script\" \"$project_dir\" 2>&1)\n\n    # Count baseline summary files created\n    local baseline_files\n    baseline_files=$(find \"$transcripts_dir\" -name \"*_summary.md\" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)\n\n    if [[ $baseline_files -eq 0 ]]; then\n        warn \"  No summary files created by backup-conversations\"\n        return 0\n    fi\n\n    success \"  Created $baseline_files baseline summary files\"\n\n    # Step 2: If multi-verbosity mode, export at different verbosity levels\n    local total_files=$baseline_files\n\n    if $ALL_VERBOSITY_LEVELS && [[ -x \"$exporter\" ]]; then\n        echo \"  Step 2/2: Generating multi-verbosity exports...\"\n\n        # Determine verbosity range\n        local -a verbosity_levels=()\n        if [[ -n \"$VERBOSITY_RANGE\" ]]; then\n            IFS='-' read -r start_v end_v <<< \"$VERBOSITY_RANGE\"\n            for ((v=start_v; v<=end_v; v++)); do\n                verbosity_levels+=(\"$v\")\n            done\n        else\n            verbosity_levels=(0 1 2 3 4 5)\n        fi\n\n        # Export each conversation at each verbosity level\n        local conv_num=0\n        for summary_file in \"$transcripts_dir\"/*_summary.md; do\n            [[ ! -f \"$summary_file\" ]] && continue\n            ((conv_num++))\n\n            local conv_id\n            conv_id=$(basename \"$summary_file\" _summary.md)\n\n            echo \"    Processing $conv_num/$baseline_files: $conv_id\"\n\n            for level in \"${verbosity_levels[@]}\"; do\n                local level_name\n                case \"$level\" in\n                    0) level_name=\"minimal\" ;;\n                    1) level_name=\"compact\" ;;\n                    2) level_name=\"standard\" ;;\n                    3) level_name=\"verbose\" ;;\n                    4) level_name=\"complete\" ;;\n                    5) level_name=\"raw\" ;;\n                esac\n\n                local output_file=\"${transcripts_dir}/${conv_id}-v${level}-${level_name}.md\"\n\n                # Run exporter at this verbosity level\n                if \"$exporter\" -v\"$level\" \"$project_dir\" \"$conv_id\" > \"$output_file\" 2>/dev/null && [[ -s \"$output_file\" ]]; then\n                    ((total_files++))\n                else\n                    # If export failed, remove empty file\n                    rm -f \"$output_file\"\n                fi\n            done\n\n            echo \"      Generated ${#verbosity_levels[@]} verbosity variants\"\n        done\n\n        success \"  Total files generated: $total_files (baseline + variants)\"",

Appends analysis to each issue file and supports creating sub-issue skeleton files.\n\n**Features:**\n- Interactive TUI mode with lua-menu integration\n- Parallel streaming mode for batch processing\n- Session mode for context reuse across issues\n- Feedback loop for iterative refinement\n- Archive mode for preserving analyses\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./issue-splitter.sh -I                    # Interactive mode\n./issue-splitter.sh --dir /path/to/project\n./issue-splitter.sh -x                    # Execute recommendations (create sub-issues)\n./issue-splitter.sh -G                    # Generate complete issue files via Claude\n```\n\n### progress-dashboard.lua\nScans issue directories and generates progress statistics with ASCII visualizations. Works on any project following the phase-based issue naming convention (e.g., `301-feature-name.md`).\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\nlua progress-dashboard.lua -d /path/to/project    # Terminal output\nlua progress-dashboard.lua -m                      # Markdown output\nlua progress-dashboard.lua -p 3                    # Show only phase 3\n```\n\n### git-history.sh\nGenerates prettified commit logs segmented by project phase. Outputs human-readable markdown files preserving statistics and metadata.\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./git-history.sh -p 2           # Generate for phase 2\n./git-history.sh -a             # All phases\n./git-history.sh -I             # Interactive TUI mode\n```\n\n### sync-visions.sh\nDiscovers and symlinks vision documents from all projects into a centralized `visions/` directory. Provides statistics on documentation coverage.\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./sync-visions.sh                     # Scan default directory\n./sync-visions.sh -v                  # Verbose output\n./sync-visions.sh --stats             # Show statistics only\n```\n\n### state-daemon.sh\nA background service that holds key-value state in RAM using FIFO pipes for IPC. Enables inter-script communication without file-based locking.\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./state-daemon.sh start               # Start daemon\n./state-daemon.sh set KEY VALUE       # Set value\n./state-daemon.sh get KEY             # Get value\n./state-daemon.sh list                # List all keys\n./state-daemon.sh stop                # Stop daemon\n```\n\n### backup-conversations\nExtracts Claude conversation transcripts from `~/.claude/projects/` and writes summaries to project-specific `llm-transcripts/` directories. Uses native `<details>`/`<summary>` elements for collapsible folders.\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./project-file-server /path/to/projects         # Scan directory\n./project-file-server -I                        # Interactive mode\n./project-file-server -o ~/server.html          # Custom output file\n```\n\n### filesystem_scanner.sh\nScans filesystem hierarchy and generates a text-based tree. Supports cron scheduling for periodic scans.\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./filesystem_scanner.sh /path/to/scan\n```",

        "content":"# backup-conversations\n\nExtracts Claude conversation transcripts from `~/.claude/projects/` and writes summaries to project-specific `llm-transcripts/` directories. Filters intermediate problem-solving dialogue for clarity, keeping only user requests and final assistant responses.\n\n## Use Cases\n\n### Backup All Conversations for a Project\nExtract and save transcripts from Claude Code sessions for a specific project.\n\n```bash\n./backup-conversations /path/to/project\n```\n\n### Backup Current Project\nRun from within a project directory to backup its conversations.\n\n```bash\ncd /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/my-project\n/path/to/scripts/backup-conversations\n```\n\n### Create Archive of AI Collaboration History\nUseful for documenting how AI assistance was used during development.\n\n```bash\n./backup-conversations /home/ritz/programming/ai-stuff/world-edit-to-execute\n# Output: world-edit-to-execute/llm-transcripts/*.md\n```\n\n## Configuration Options\n\n| Option | Description |\n|--------|-------------|\n| `[project-dir]` | Project directory to backup (default: current directory) |\n\n## Capabilities\n\n- **Automatic Claude Directory Discovery**: Maps project paths to Claude's internal project directories\n- **User/Assistant Extraction**: Parses JSONL conversation files to extract the dialogue flow\n- **Intermediate Filtering**: Removes tool results and intermediate problem-solving steps\n- **Markdown Formatting**: Outputs clean, readable markdown summaries\n- **Text Wrapping**: Wraps long lines at 80 characters while preserving markdown structure\n- **Timestamp Preservation**: Sets file modification times to match the conversation's final timestamp\n- **Descriptive Naming**: Uses local LLM (if available via fuzzy-computing) to generate descriptive filenames\n\n## Output Format\n\nEach conversation is saved as a markdown file with:\n\n```markdown\n# Conversation Summary: {conversation_id}\n\nGenerated on: {date}\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n### User Request 1\n\n{first user message}\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n### Assistant Response 1\n\n{final assistant response to that request}\n\n--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n```\n\n## Output Location\n\n- Standard projects: `{project-dir}/llm-transcripts/`\n- Home directory: `/home/ritz/ai/llm-transcripts/`\n- Nested transcripts: `{dir}/llm-transcripts/transcripts/`\n\n## Related Functions\n\nThe script defines several functions that can be sourced:\n\n- `backup-conversations` / `backup-conversation` - Main backup function\n- `write-transcripts-to-project-directory` - Core extraction logic\n- `start-claude` - Launch Claude CLI\n- `claude-next` - Create numbered todo files for Claude\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Python 3 (for JSONL parsing)\n- Optional: `fuzzy-computing` for descriptive filename generation\n\n## Related Scripts\n\n- `claude-conversation-exporter.sh` - More feature-rich exporter with TUI and verbosity controls",

-d \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" ]; then\n      echo \"Could not find Claude project directory: $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"\n      return 1\n   fi\n   \n   echo \"Extracting transcripts from $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to $TRANSCRIPT_DIR\"\n   \n   # Process each JSONL file\n   for jsonl_file in \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/*.jsonl; do\n      if [ -f \"$jsonl_file\" ]; then\n         conversation_id=$(basename \"$jsonl_file\" .jsonl)\n         output_file=\"$TRANSCRIPT_DIR/${conversation_id}_summary.md\"\n         \n         echo \"Processing conversation: $conversation_id\"\n\n         # Use Lua conversation parser instead of Python\n         SCRIPT_DIR=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n         PARSER=\"${SCRIPT_DIR}/libs/conversation-parser.lua\"\n\n         # Run the Lua parser and capture timestamp from stderr\n         TIMESTAMP_OUTPUT=$(lua \"$PARSER\" \"$jsonl_file\" \"$output_file\" 2>&1 >/dev/null)\n         FINAL_TIMESTAMP=$(echo \"$TIMESTAMP_OUTPUT\" | grep \"FINAL_TIMESTAMP:\" | cut -d: -f2)\n         \n         # Set file modification time if we have a timestamp\n         if [ !         "content":"    fi\n\n    log \"Found ${#discovered_projects[@]} projects with conversations\"\n    echo \"\"\n\n    # Determine which projects to process\n    local -a projects_to_process=()\n\n    if $PROCESS_ALL; then\n        projects_to_process=(\"${discovered_projects[@]}\")\n    elif [[ ${#SELECTED_PROJECTS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then\n        # Filter to selected projects\n        for selected in \"${SELECTED_PROJECTS[@]}\"; do\n            for project in \"${discovered_projects[@]}\"; do\n                IFS='|' read -r name path count <<< \"$project\"\n                if [[ \"$name\" == \"$selected\" ]]; then\n                    projects_to_process+=(\"$project\")\n                    break\n                fi\n            done\n        done\n    elif $INTERACTIVE_MODE; then\n        warn \"Interactive mode not yet implemented - using --all for now\"\n        projects_to_process=(\"${discovered_projects[@]}\")\n    else\n        error \"Must specify --all, -I, or project names\"\n        show_help\n        exit 1\n    fi\n\n    if [[ ${#projects_to_process[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then\n        warn \"No projects selected for processing.\"\n        exit 0\n    fi\n\n    # Show summary\n    echo -e \"${BLUE}═══════════════════════════════════════════════${NC}\"\n    echo -e \"${BLUE}  Projects to process: ${#projects_to_process[@]}${NC}\"\n    if $ALL_VERBOSITY_LEVELS; then\n        if [[ -n \"$VERBOSITY_RANGE\" ]]; then\n            echo -e \"${BLUE}  Verbosity range: ${VERBOSITY_RANGE}${NC}\"\n        else\n            echo -e \"${BLUE}  Verbosity levels: 0-5 (all)${NC}\"\n        fi\n    else\n        echo -e \"${BLUE}  Verbosity level: ${VERBOSITY_LEVEL}${NC}\"\n    fi\n    if $DRY_RUN; then\n        echo -e \"${YELLOW}  DRY RUN MODE${NC}\"\n    fi\n    echo -e \"${BLUE}═══════════════════════════════════════════════${NC}\"\n    echo \"\"\n\n    # Process each project\n    local total_conversations=0\n    local total_files_generated=0",

        "content":"140\t- when speaking with a user, prefer describing a variable, function, or datastructure with english words over using the code name.\n141\t- documentation and scripting work doesn't need an issue file. The scripts should be self-documenting, explaining different \"options\" rather than changes or mistakes. Ideally, it remains focused, but add as much capability as you please. Just make sure that you don't get lost in similar meanings, keep all entries similar but different in processese.\n142\t\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\t### 🔮 Vision: notes/vision\n146\t\n147\t```\n148\tSoraMech — Vision\n149\t=================\n150\t\n151\tA visual editor and execution engine for finite state machines built from\n152\tcomposable boxes. Best of both: explicit wires for the values that\nmatter at this step, named data store for\n\nstate that persists across many steps.\n\n\n\nso, we probably aren't going to have an LLM chat history per-se - each prompt\nwill be dynamically generated, with history pulled in only when necessary. The\nhistory would be written to /tmp/ datafiles probably, and in the box we'd have\nto explicitely mark that we want some or all of it included. Probably what we're\ngoing to do is treat text as atomic elements that can be passed around like\nvariables or arguments, and split or otherwise modified carefully and\nintentionally.\n\n\nTool results should be treated as return values. They will be returned slightly\nasync, since the LLM can craft the tool call and then continue processing (I\nthink? We should make it so) - in the thread pool implementation, read more\nabout that if you haven't, but in that system there's a \"blocking\" mechanic\nwhere certain tasks can be blocked by other thread tasks running. The idea is,\nand the reason it'd be useful here, is that if you're running, say, a database\nquery, something that takes a while, it'll return and fill a slot in shared\nmemory and anything that depends on that return value is blocked until that\nreturn value arrives. We explicitely want to design the system around that. In\nfact, we might want to transition the thread pool library to this project\neventually so we can make our own tweaks to it, but that's for another time.\nLet's get the UI and the project setup and stuff first.",

        "content":"--------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n### Assistant Response 34\n\nThe `ollama.lua` call box and the `llm-route` box solve different problems, and\nthe executor treats them very differently.\n\n\n**`call` box using `ollama.lua`:**\n\n\nThe executor doesn't know or care that it's talking to Ollama. It just sees a\nbox with `kind: \"call\"`, looks up the driver (`drivers/lua.sh`), spawns a\nsubprocess, passes the inputs as JSON arguments, and collects the return values\nas named output ports. The Lua function does the HTTP call internally. The\nexecutor's job is done after the function returns — it pushes the output\nvalues into the store and enqueues whatever downstream boxes are now satisfied.\n\n\n**`llm-route` box:**\n\n\nThe executor handles it directly in `fire_connections` without spawning any\nsubprocess. There's no driver involved. Instead, when the box runs,\n`llm_route_call()` in the executor itself calls `require(\"ollama\")` and makes\nthe Ollama request inline in Lua. The result isn't an output value pushed to\ndownstream ports — it's a **routing decision**. The executor looks at which\noutput port name matches the LLM's reply, then fires only that port's wire,\npassing the original `text` input through as the value.           "new_string":"## Implementation notes (bugs found during testing)\n\n**Bug: add/hide handlers read `meta.src_dirs` instead of `groups`.**\nThe server migrates old maps on read (synthesizes `src_dirs` from `extra_src_dirs` + implicit\n`src/`), but the client's add and hide handlers read raw `meta.src_dirs || []`, which is\n`[]` on old maps. So adding a library dir saves `src_dirs: [new_path]` with no prior entries,\ndiscarding whatever the server just migrated. Fix: both handlers must derive the current list\nfrom the already-resolved `groups` array (the live server view), not from `meta.src_dirs`.\n\n**Bug: dir picker opens at `/home` every time.**\nShould open at the parent of the last directory in `groups`, so the user lands near where they\nlast browsed. Fixed by passing a computed `initial_path` to `show_dir_picker`.\n\n## Relevant files",

          "content":"# 216 — Read-file box: output contents of a text or data file\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box exists for loading text from disk into the wire graph. A user who\nwants to supply file contents as input to a downstream box must write a custom\nLua function from scratch.\n\n## Intended behavior\nA reusable source file (in `libs/` or a map's `src/`) that exposes two functions:\n- `M.read_text(path)` — reads a plain text file; returns its full contents as a string.\n- `M.read_data(path, key)` — reads a dkjson data file; returns the value at `key` as\n  a string (strips metadata fields like `constant`). If `key` is nil/empty, returns\n  the full JSON-decoded table encoded back to a plain string.\n\nBoth functions output a single port (`text`) carrying the file contents. Error cases\n(file not found, bad JSON) write to stderr and return nil — the executor surfaces nil\nas an empty string on downstream inputs.\n\nThe design follows the established pattern: a regular Lua file that the user picks\nvia the file browser and wires into their map. No executor changes needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/files.lua` with `M.read_text` and `M.read_data`.\n2.           "content":"# 217 — Concat box with configurable separator and dynamic input ports\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box for joining multiple text strings. Combining two chat histories,\na system prompt with a user message, or any multi-source text assembly requires\na custom function.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — concat library box\nA reusable `libs/text.lua` exposing `M.concat(sep, ...)`, where:\n- `sep` is the separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`, `\" \"`, `\"\"`)\n- `...` are the text values to join (variadic — any number)\n- returns a single `result` port with the joined string\n\nThe variadic signature means the executor passes positional args: the box's\n`inputs` array in the JSON determines how many wires feed in. The function\nhandles any count without modification.\n\nTypical usage: set `sep` as a literal port value (issue 208), wire two or more\n`text` inputs, wire `result` downstream.\n\n### Part B — dynamic input ports (research / open question)\n\nThe user needs to concatenate N inputs where N is only known at map-design time.\nAdding a \"+\" button to the inspector that appends a new named input port to the\nbox JSON (`inputs: [\"text1\", \"text2\"] → [\"text1\", \"text2\", \"text3\"]`) is the\ncandidate approach. Requirements:\n\n1. The source function must accept variadic args (language-dependent).\n   - Lua: `function M.concat(sep, ...)` — works\n   - Bash: `$@` after shifting fixed args — works\n   - C: requires explicit argc/argv handling — works with the existing driver contract\n2. The editor must allow adding and removing named ports without editing the source\n   file. The box JSON's `inputs` array is already the right place to store this.\n3. The \"+\" button appears in the inspector when the selected box's source function\n   is variadic — OR always, treating it as a user declaration.\n4. The \"-\" button removes the last input port (only if no wire is connected to it).\n\nOpen questions before implementing Part B:\n- Should the \"+\" button be general (any box) or only on boxes whose source has `...`?\n  General is simpler and language-agnostic; parser-gated is more correct but requires\n  per-language variadic detection.\n- How does the executor know how many args to pass? It already reads `box.inputs` and\n  passes them positionally — no change needed. The dynamic count is purely a box JSON\n  concern.\n\nRecommended sequence: implement Part A first (concat box), then address Part B once\nthe use pattern is confirmed in practice.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Add `libs/text.lua.info.md`.\n3. (Part B) Add \"+\" / \"−\" port buttons to the inspector's input port list for call boxes.\n   These modify `box.inputs` in place and call `API.put_box` to persist.\n4. (Part B) Add wire-connected guard: block \"−\" if the port has an incoming connection.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference for variadic-friendly library pattern\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list rendering\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how positional args are built from box.inputs (no changes needed)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — literal port values (sep will use this)\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md"
        },

    "content":"# 217 — Concat box with configurable separator and dynamic input ports\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box for joining multiple text strings. Combining two chat histories,\na system prompt with a user message, or any multi-source text assembly requires\na custom function.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — concat library box\nA reusable `libs/text.lua` exposing `M.concat(sep, ...)`, where:\n- `sep` is the separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`, `\" \"`, `\"\"`)\n- `...` are the text values to join (variadic — any number)\n- returns a single `result` port with the joined string\n\nThe variadic signature means the executor passes positional args: the box's\n`inputs` array in the JSON determines how many wires feed in. The function\nhandles any count without modification.\n\nTypical usage: set `sep` as a literal port value (issue 208), wire two or more\n`text` inputs, wire `result` downstream.\n\n### Part B — dynamic input ports (research / open question)\n\nThe user needs to concatenate N inputs where N is only known at map-design time.\nAdding a \"+\" button to the inspector that appends a new named input port to the\nbox JSON (`inputs: [\"text1\", \"text2\"] → [\"text1\", \"text2\", \"text3\"]`) is the\ncandidate approach. Requirements:\n\n1. The source function must accept variadic args (language-dependent).\n   - Lua: `function M.concat(sep, ...)` — works\n   - Bash: `$@` after shifting fixed args — works\n   - C: requires explicit argc/argv handling — works with the existing driver contract\n2. The editor must allow adding and removing named ports without editing the source\n   file. The box JSON's `inputs` array is already the right place to store this.\n3. The \"+\" button appears in the inspector when the selected box's source function\n   is variadic — OR always, treating it as a user declaration.\n4. The \"-\" button removes the last input port (only if no wire is connected to it).\n\nOpen questions before implementing Part B:\n- Should the \"+\" button be general (any box) or only on boxes whose source has `...`?\n  General is simpler and language-agnostic; parser-gated is more correct but requires\n  per-language variadic detection.\n- How does the executor know how many args to pass? It already reads `box.inputs` and\n  passes them positionally — no change needed. The dynamic count is purely a box JSON\n  concern.\n\nRecommended sequence: implement Part A first (concat box), then address Part B once\nthe use pattern is confirmed in practice.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Add `libs/text.lua.info.md`.\n3. (Part B) Add \"+\" / \"−\" port buttons to the inspector's input port list for call boxes.\n   These modify `box.inputs` in place and call `API.put_box` to persist.\n4. (Part B) Add wire-connected guard: block \"−\" if the port has an incoming connection.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference for variadic-friendly library pattern\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list rendering\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how positional args are built from box.inputs (no changes needed)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — literal port values (sep will use this)\n"
  },

(last.replace(/\\/[^/]+$/, '') || '/') : '/home';\n        show_dir_picker(container,\n          async (path) => {\n            try {\n              const meta = await API.get_meta();\n              // derive current list from groups, not meta.src_dirs:\n              // groups already reflects the server-migrated state (extra_src_dirs + src/),\n              // whereas meta.src_dirs is absent on old maps and would discard prior entries\n              const current = groups.map(g => g.path);\n              if (!current.includes(path)) {\n                current.push(path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: current });\n              }\n              render(container, on_select);\n            } catch(e) {\n              show_file_list();\n              const note = document.createElement('div');\n              note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n              note.textContent = 'could not save dir: ' + e.message;\n              container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n            }\n          },\n          () => show_file_list(),\n          initial\n        );\n      };",

        "text":"Three issue files created (215, 216, 217), and both bugs fixed. Summary of what changed in `007-filebrowser.js`:\n\n- **libs bug**: add and hide handlers now build the directory list from `groups.map(g => g.path)` instead of `meta.src_dirs || []`. `groups` is the server-resolved view (already includes migration from `extra_src_dirs` + implicit `src/`), so saving from it never drops previously configured dirs.\n- **picker default**: `show_dir_picker` now takes a 4th `initial_path` arg; the add button computes it as the parent of the last group's path (one level up from the most recently added dir).\n\nOn the dynamic inputs question — issue 217 documents the design. The short version: the executor already builds positional args from `box.inputs`, so it's purely a JSON and inspector concern. A variadic-designed function (`M.concat(sep, ...)`) plus a \"+\" button in the inspector that appends to `box.inputs` is the clean path. The only open question is whether \"+\" should be gated on detecting varargs in the source or just always available."
      }]
  },

    "id":"msg_01Wmbqi3Yd1cTQRWWmwC2zVV",
    "model":"claude-sonnet-4-6",
    "stop_reason":"end_turn",
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"The auto-grow approach is cleaner, and I think it can work language-agnostically — but not through language detection. Here's my thinking:\n\n**Don't detect, declare.** Add a `variadic: true` flag to the box JSON. When `variadic` is true and a wire is connected to the last input port, the editor automatically appends a new port. The executor already ignores this flag — it just passes `box.inputs` positionally, however many there are.\n\nThe parser sets this flag when it can — Lua's `...` in the signature is detectable, bash's `$@` usage after a `shift` is detectable. For anything else, the user flips a toggle in the inspector.\n\n**On C specifically:** the driver contract already passes `arg_count` before the args (you can see it in `004-executor.lua`: `fn arg_count arg1 arg2...`). So a C function reading from `argv[]` in a loop already handles N inputs without needing `va_list`. `variadic: true` works the same way in C — the author just designs their function to loop over argv. No special casing needed.\n\n**What the auto-grow actually looks like:**\n- Connect a wire to the last port → new empty port appears below it\n- Disconnect from a port that's no longer the last → it collapses away (unless it still has a wire)\n- The port names are just `text1`, `text2`, `text3`... — sequential and predictable\n\nThe only open question: do you want auto-grow to also auto-shrink when a wire is removed from a middle port? I'd say no — leave empty ports until explicitly removed. Mid-port gaps are fine; the function just gets an empty string there.\n\nThe \"+\" button becomes a fallback for when `variadic` isn't set and the user knows they want more ports — or we skip it entirely and just say \"design your concat function with `...` and the ports manage themselves.\"\n\nShould I update issue 217 with this design and drop the unresolved questions?"
      }]
  },

    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with configurable separator and dynamic input ports\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box for joining multiple text strings. Combining two chat histories,\na system prompt with a user message, or any multi-source text assembly requires\na custom function.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — concat library box\nA reusable `libs/text.lua` exposing `M.concat(sep, ...)`, where:\n- `sep` is the separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`, `\" \"`, `\"\"`)\n- `...` are the text values to join (variadic — any number)\n- returns a single `result` port with the joined string\n\nThe variadic signature means the executor passes positional args: the box's\n`inputs` array in the JSON determines how many wires feed in. The function\nhandles any count without modification.\n\nTypical usage: set `sep` as a literal port value (issue 208), wire two or more\n`text` inputs, wire `result` downstream.\n\n### Part B — dynamic input ports (research / open question)\n\nThe user needs to concatenate N inputs where N is only known at map-design time.\nAdding a \"+\" button to the inspector that appends a new named input port to the\nbox JSON (`inputs: [\"text1\", \"text2\"] → [\"text1\", \"text2\", \"text3\"]`) is the\ncandidate approach. Requirements:\n\n1. The source function must accept variadic args (language-dependent).\n   - Lua: `function M.concat(sep, ...)` — works\n   - Bash: `$@` after shifting fixed args — works\n   - C: requires explicit argc/argv handling — works with the existing driver contract\n2. The editor must allow adding and removing named ports without editing the source\n   file. The box JSON's `inputs` array is already the right place to store this.\n3. The \"+\" button appears in the inspector when the selected box's source function\n   is variadic — OR always, treating it as a user declaration.\n4. The \"-\" button removes the last input port (only if no wire is connected to it).\n\nOpen questions before implementing Part B:\n- Should the \"+\" button be general (any box) or only on boxes whose source has `...`?\n  General is simpler and language-agnostic; parser-gated is more correct but requires\n  per-language variadic detection.\n- How does the executor know how many args to pass? It already reads `box.inputs` and\n  passes them positionally — no change needed. The dynamic count is purely a box JSON\n  concern.\n\nRecommended sequence: implement Part A first (concat box), then address Part B once\nthe use pattern is confirmed in practice.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Add `libs/text.lua.info.md`.\n3. (Part B) Add \"+\" / \"−\" port buttons to the inspector's input port list for call boxes.\n   These modify `box.inputs` in place and call `API.put_box` to persist.\n4. (Part B) Add wire-connected guard: block \"−\" if the port has an incoming connection.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference for variadic-friendly library pattern\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list rendering\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how positional args are built from box.inputs (no changes needed)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — literal port values (sep will use this)\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md",
    "content":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — concat library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes `M.concat(sep, ...)` where:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n"
  },

        "text":"Good clarification — the variadic flag is per-port, not per-box. That changes the data model. Let me think through the implications before updating the issue:\n\nIf `variadic` is per-input, the box might have `[\"sep\", \"text\"]` where `sep` is fixed and `text` is the variadic one. When the variadic input expands, the `inputs` array grows: `[\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"]` — indexed instances of the base name. Connections reference these by the indexed name. Auto-shrink on wire cut means: remove that slot, compact the remaining ones, and update the `to_input` field on all connections that reference later indices. That last part — remapping connection names — is where middle-port cutting gets complex. The connection is stored in both endpoint box files, so a rename has to touch both.\n\nLet me update 217 with the full finalized design:"

          "new_string":"### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns each part as a separate output port: `part_1`, `part_2`, ... up to\n  however many parts the split produces\n\nThe output count is not known at wire-design time, so in practice this is most\nuseful when the number of parts is known and stable (e.g. splitting a\n\"key: value\" line always produces two parts). For unknown-count splits, the\ncaller should use `M.split_array` (see below) and pass the result through a\ndata file or handle it in a single downstream box.\n\n`M.split_array(text, sep)` — same split, returns a JSON-encoded array string\non a single `result` port. The downstream box decodes it. Useful when the part\ncount is variable and the caller wants to keep a single wire.",

    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — concat library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes `M.concat(sep, ...)` where:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"### Part A — concat library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes `M.concat(sep, ...)` where:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.",
    "newString":"### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns each part as a separate output port: `part_1`, `part_2`, ... up to\n  however many parts the split produces\n\nThe output count is not known at wire-design time, so in practice this is most\nuseful when the number of parts is known and stable (e.g. splitting a\n\"key: value\" line always produces two parts). For unknown-count splits, the\ncaller should use `M.split_array` (see below) and pass the result through a\ndata file or handle it in a single downstream box.\n\n`M.split_array(text, sep)` — same split, returns a JSON-encoded array string\non a single `result` port. The downstream box decodes it. Useful when the part\ncount is variable and the caller wants to keep a single wire.",

A box"],
