    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns each part as a separate output port: `part_1`, `part_2`, ... up to\n  however many parts the split produces\n\nThe output count is not known at wire-design time, so in practice this is most\nuseful when the number of parts is known and stable (e.g. splitting a\n\"key: value\" line always produces two parts). For unknown-count splits, the\ncaller should use `M.split_array` (see below) and pass the result through a\ndata file or handle it in a single downstream box.\n\n`M.split_array(text, sep)` — same split, returns a JSON-encoded array string\non a single `result` port. The downstream box decodes it. Useful when the part\ncount is variable and the caller wants to keep a single wire.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns each part as a separate output port: `part_1`, `part_2`, ... up to\n  however many parts the split produces\n\nThe output count is not known at wire-design time, so in practice this is most\nuseful when the number of parts is known and stable (e.g. splitting a\n\"key: value\" line always produces two parts). For unknown-count splits, the\ncaller should use `M.split_array` (see below) and pass the result through a\ndata file or handle it in a single downstream box.\n\n`M.split_array(text, sep)` — same split, returns a JSON-encoded array string\non a single `result` port. The downstream box decodes it. Useful when the part\ncount is variable and the caller wants to keep a single wire.",
    "newString":"`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.",

    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"Output ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.",
    "newString":"Output ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\nNote: the executor currently only supports one output port per box regardless.\n`fire_connections` takes a single value from `run_task` and routes it to all\nconnected wires. The driver contract (stdout as a JSON array) leaves room to\nextend this later, but until `fire_connections` is updated to map array elements\nto named output ports, all boxes are effectively single-output.",

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"You're right — it's inconsistent. The array is almost certainly there from the original intent to support multiple outputs (the driver contract says \"return a JSON array, one element per output port\"), but `fire_connections` was only ever wired up for the first element. The full contract was designed but only half implemented.\n\nTwo directions to resolve it:\n\n**Simplify**: change the driver contract to a single JSON value. Drivers echo one thing, executor reads it directly. Honest about what's actually supported. Downside: if multiple outputs are ever implemented later, all drivers need updating again.\n\n**Complete it**: implement multiple outputs properly now — `fire_connections` iterates the array, matches each element to the corresponding named port in `box.outputs` by index, routes each one independently. The array contract stays, it just stops being wasteful. This is the direction the design was clearly heading.\n\nGiven that the driver contract and box schema already have everything in place for multiple outputs, completing the implementation seems like the lower-effort and more correct path — it's filling in a gap rather than changing course. The simplify route would mean doing work now and then undoing it.\n\nShould I create an issue for implementing multiple outputs properly? It would unlock `M.split` having named output ports too, which was the original question that led here."
      }]
  },

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Here's the concrete path. The infrastructure is almost entirely already there — look at what the connection record in `stamp.json` already carries:\n\n```json\n{\"from_box\":\"stamp\", \"from_output\":\"stamped\", \"to_box\":\"router\", \"to_input\":\"text\"}\n```\n\n`from_output` is already a named port. And `box.outputs` already names the ports in order. The driver already returns a JSON array. The only thing missing is that `fire_connections` ignores `from_output` entirely — it just blasts `output_val` (always `result_arr[1]`) to every connection.\n\nThe change is two small things:\n\n**1. `run_task` returns the whole array instead of element 1:**\n```lua\n-- currently:\nreturn output_val, nil   -- just result_arr[1]\n\n-- becomes:\nreturn result_arr, nil   -- the full array\n```\n\n**2. `fire_connections` builds a name→value map from `box.outputs` + the array, then routes by `from_output`:**\n```lua\n-- build map: output port name → value\nlocal output_map = {}\nfor i, port in ipairs(box.outputs or {}) do\n    output_map[port.name] = result_arr[i]\nend\n\n-- then instead of:\nstore[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n\n-- use:\nstore[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_map[c.from_output]\n```\n\nThat's it. Fully backward compatible — existing single-output boxes have one entry in `outputs`, `result_arr[1]` maps to it, all their connections reference that one port name, nothing changes for them.\n\nThe reason it feels impossible is that `from_output` looks like it's already doing something — but in the current code it's completely unused in the non-comparator path. Once you route by it, multiple outputs work automatically.\n\nWant me to create an issue for this and implement it?"
      }]
  },

{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T19:45:14.734Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"No I don't mean that it's physically impossible, I'm sure we could write the code for it. But it's logically impossible. Consider - if we have two separate return statements, and they each have the same number of outputs (like, a tuple with 3 values, but it's a different value each time) how would we know which one to put on which wire? We could do it positionally, but that's too fragile. Also, what if we only return 2 values, what happens then? We need to be deterministic about it, so we decided that we could only ever return one thing, and if the function returns multiple values (like an array or whatever) then we'd bundle them all and pass them along the wire. Do you remember what I'm talking about? You can check the LLM transcripts if you don't.",
    "role":"user"
  },

    "snippet":"1\t# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\tNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\n8\tnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n9\t\n10\t## Intended behavior\n11\t\n12\t### Part A — text library box\n13\t`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n14\t\n15\t`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n16\t- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n17\t- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n18\t- returns a single `result` port\n19\t\n20\tThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\n21\tmodifying the source file.\n22\t\n23\t`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n24\t- `text` — the input string\n25\t- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n26\t- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n27\t\n28\tOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\n29\tparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\n30\tconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n31\t\n32\tNote: the executor currently only supports one output port per box regardless.\n33\t`fire_connections` takes a single value from `run_task` and routes it to all\n34\tconnected wires. The driver contract (stdout as a JSON array) leaves room to\n35\textend this later, but until `fire_connections` is updated to map array elements\n36\tto named output ports, all boxes are effectively single-output.\n37\t\n38\t### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n39\t\n40\tVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\n41\tcould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\n42\teach input to mark it variadic.\n43\t\n44\t#### Data model\n45\t\n46\tThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n47\t```json\n48\t{\n49\t  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n50\t  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n51\t}\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\n55\tThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\n56\tConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n57\t\n58\tThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n59\t`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n60\t(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\n61\talready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\n62\tin a loop work without any changes.\n63\t\n64\t#### Auto-grow\n65\tWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\n66\ta new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\n67\tappears immediately as an open port.\n68\t\n69\t#### Auto-shrink\n70\tWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n71\t1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n72\t2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n73\t3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n74\t   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n75\t   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n76\t     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n77\t4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n78\t\n79\tMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\n80\tslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\n81\ta dense, gap-free list of ports.\n82\t\n83\t## Open questions before implementing Part B\n84\t- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n85\t  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n86\t  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n87\t  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n88\t  is worth adding first.\n89\t- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n90\t  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n91\t\n92\t  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n93\t     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n94\t\n95\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n96\t1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n97\t2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n98\t3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n99\t4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n100\t5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n101\t\n102\t## Relevant files\n103\t- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n104\t- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n105\t- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n106\t- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n107\t- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n108\t- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md"

        "oldStart":29,
        "oldLines":11
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\nNote: the executor currently only supports one output port per box regardless.\n`fire_connections` takes a single value from `run_task` and routes it to all\nconnected wires. The driver contract (stdout as a JSON array) leaves room to\nextend this later, but until `fire_connections` is updated to map array elements\nto named output ports, all boxes are effectively single-output.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"Note: the executor currently only supports one output port per box regardless.\n`fire_connections` takes a single value from `run_task` and routes it to all\nconnected wires. The driver contract (stdout as a JSON array) leaves room to\nextend this later, but until `fire_connections` is updated to map array elements\nto named output ports, all boxes are effectively single-output.",
    "newString":"Note: one output wire per box is a deliberate design constraint, not a missing\nfeature. Positional multi-output was explicitly rejected as fragile (multiple\nreturn statements with the same tuple width are indistinguishable). The\ncomparator (lt/eq/gt branching) is the only multi-path mechanism. Whatever the\nfunction returns goes down the single output wire as one value — arrays or JSON\nobjects if multiple values need to travel together.",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

        "content":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\nthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n    logs/            — run logs\n    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n```\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"outputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"ports\": [\n    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [...]\n}\n```\n\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\nat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n\n## Language driver interface\n\nDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n\nOutputs are returned as JSON on stdout. Exit code non-zero = box failure.\nSee docs/003-driver-system.md for the full driver contract.\n\n## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n\n  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n  3. Collect outputs: parse JSON from driver stdout\n  4. Store outputs: held in runner memory, keyed by box id + output name\n  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\nby effil-jit or the custom thread pool from the 3d-rts project.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only. Individual\nfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\nwhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. It survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.",

        "content":"# 108 — Branch box and predicate routing\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nSchema fix (2026-05-07): `src/001-schema.lua` `validate_box` previously applied\nkind-specific connection validation to ALL connections in a box file. Since both\nendpoint boxes store the identical 4-field connection record, a call box file\ncan contain a reciprocal record with `from_port` (from a branch box), and a\nbranch box file can contain a reciprocal record with `from_output` (from a call\nbox). Fixed by routing connection validation on `c.from_box == box.id`:\noutgoing records get the strict kind-specific validator; incoming reciprocal\nrecords get a looser validator (`validate_incoming_connection`) that accepts\neither `from_output` or `from_port`.\n\nExecutor retry: branch inputs are cleared from the store on retry so the\nupstream box re-fires cleanly. `retry_vary` fields are pseudo-randomized in\nthe range before the upstream box is re-queued.\n\nVerified with `maps/branch-test/`: n=30 routes to write-low (result=\"30\"),\nn=70 routes to write-high (result=\"70\"). hello and driver-test maps pass\nregression.\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 104 (executor must exist; predicate evaluation is added to it here)\n- 107 (wire UI must exist; branch port wires need visual distinction)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo branch box type exists. All routing is linear (one output, one wire).\nThere is no mechanism to conditionally fire one box vs. another based on\na value.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box with \"kind\": \"branch\" has named output ports instead of positional\noutputs. Each port (except \"else\") carries a predicate. The executor\nevaluates each predicate against the input value and fires the first port\nwhose predicate is true. If no predicate matches, the \"else\" port fires.\n\nPort predicates:\n  { \"op\": \"eq\"|\"lt\"|\"gt\"|\"lte\"|\"gte\"|\"contains\"|\"matches\", \"value\": <literal> }\n\n\"matches\" uses lua pattern matching against a string input.\n\"contains\" checks whether a string input contains the literal as a substring.\n\nBranch box behavior in two scenarios:\n\n  Numeric/string predicate branch:\n    - \"else\" port must be wired to something, or the runner refuses to start\n    - If no predicate matches and \"else\" fires, the program continues from\n      the \"else\" port's connection\n    - The runner logs which port fired for each branch box in last-run.json\n\n  LLM output classification:\n    - \"else\" port may be left unwired in the box file (omit the connection)\n    - If \"else\" fires on an unwired port, the runner re-queues the box\n      whose output fed this branch box (the immediately upstream box in the\n      path that led here)\n    - The upstream box is re-invoked with any fields marked \"retry_vary\"\n      in its box file pseudo-randomized (e.g., temperature, top_p)\n    - Retry limit: configurable per branch box, default 3. Exceeded retry\n      limit is a hard error, not a silent loop.\n\nThe \"retry_vary\" field on a box:\n  \"retry_vary\": { \"temperature\": { \"min\": 0.5, \"max\": 1.2 } }\n  On retry, any field listed here is replaced with a random value in range.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Add branch box handling to src/004-executor.lua:\n   - When a branch box fires, evaluate each port's predicate in order.\n   - Fire the first matching port's connection.\n   - If no match, fire \"else\". If \"else\" has no connection, trigger retry.\n2. Add retry state to the executor: a per-box retry counter in run state.\n   On retry trigger, decrement counter; if zero, halt with error.\n3. Implement retry_vary: before re-invoking the upstream box, for each\n   field in its retry_vary table, generate a random value in the given\n   range and override the corresponding input before invocation.\n4. Update src/003-loader.lua validation: branch boxes without an \"else\"\n   connection are valid only if at least one upstream box has a retry_vary\n   field. If neither condition is met, the validator rejects the map.\n5. Update assets/js/006-wires.js: branch box ports each get a distinct\n   color from a cycling palette. Port labels (\"rogue\", \"wizard\", \"else\")\n   are drawn alongside the port dot on the canvas.\n6. Update assets/js/004-inspector.js: branch box inspector shows port list\n   with add/remove, predicate editor per port (op dropdown + value input),\n   and retry limit input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — branch box file format\n- issues/104 — executor (predicate evaluation added here)\n- issues/107 — wire UI (port color and label rendering)\n\n## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n\n## Architecture update (2026-05-07)\n\nThe `branch` box kind is removed as part of the single-wire output redesign.\nConditional routing is now handled by an optional **comparator** on any box\n(see issue 210): when active, the output wire splits into lt / eq / gt paths\ncompared against a literal number. Non-number values are a hard error.\n\nThe named-port model (`box.ports`, `from_port` in connections, predicate\nobjects, retry_vary) is fully removed. The retry mechanism goes away with it —\nthe loop-through-a-branch-box pattern is the recommended alternative if\nretry logic is needed.\n\nAll executor code specific to the branch kind (`fire_connections` branch\nsection, `retry_counts`, `retry_vary` application) should be reverted when\nissue 210 is implemented.",

        "type":"tool_result"
      }],

If no predicate matches, the \"else\" port fires.\n\nPort predicates:\n  { \"op\": \"eq\"|\"lt\"|\"gt\"|\"lte\"|\"gte\"|\"contains\"|\"matches\", \"value\": <literal> }\n\n\"matches\" uses lua pattern matching against a string input.\n\"contains\" checks whether a string input contains the literal as a substring.\n\nBranch box behavior in two scenarios:\n\n  Numeric/string predicate branch:\n    - \"else\" port must be wired to something, or the runner refuses to start\n    - If no predicate matches and \"else\" fires, the program continues from\n      the \"else\" port's connection\n    - The runner logs which port fired for each branch box in last-run.json\n\n  LLM output classification:\n    - \"else\" port may be left unwired in the box file (omit the connection)\n    - If \"else\" fires on an unwired port, the runner re-queues the box\n      whose output fed this branch box (the immediately upstream box in the\n      path that led here)\n    - The upstream box is re-invoked with any fields marked \"retry_vary\"\n      in its box file pseudo-randomized (e.g., temperature, top_p)\n    - Retry limit: configurable per branch box, default 3. Add branch box handling to src/004-executor.lua:\n   - When a branch box fires, evaluate each port's predicate in order.\n   - Fire the first matching port's connection.\n   - If no match, fire \"else\". If \"else\" has no connection, trigger retry.\n2. Add retry state to the executor: a per-box retry counter in run state.\n   On retry trigger, decrement counter; if zero, halt with error.\n3. Implement retry_vary: before re-invoking the upstream box, for each\n   field in its retry_vary table, generate a random value in the given\n   range and override the corresponding input before invocation.\n4. Update src/003-loader.lua validation: branch boxes without an \"else\"\n   connection are valid only if at least one upstream box has a retry_vary\n   field. If neither condition is met, the validator rejects the map.\n5. Update assets/js/006-wires.js: branch box ports each get a distinct\n   color from a cycling palette. Port labels (\"rogue\", \"wizard\", \"else\")\n   are drawn alongside the port dot on the canvas.\n6. Update assets/js/004-inspector.js: branch box inspector shows port list\n   with add/remove, predicate editor per port (op dropdown + value input),\n   and retry limit input.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/001-architecture.md — branch box file format\n- issues/104 — executor (predicate evaluation added here)\n- issues/107 — wire UI (port color and label rendering)\n\n## Notes\n\nPort predicate evaluation order matters: ports are evaluated in the order\nthey appear in the \"ports\" array. The first matching predicate fires. This\nis intentional — the user controls priority by ordering ports. Document\nthis in the inspector UI (e.g., \"ports are evaluated top to bottom\").\n\nThe retry mechanism is deliberately minimal: it re-runs one upstream box\nwith varied parameters. It is not a general loop construct. If the user\nneeds complex retry logic (backoff, multiple retries with different\nstrategies), they should model it with explicit boxes wired in a cycle\nthrough a branch box. The built-in retry is for the common case of\n\"ask the LLM again with a different temperature.\"\n\n## Architecture update (2026-05-07)\n\nThe `branch` box kind is removed as part of the single-wire output redesign.\nConditional routing is now handled by an optional **comparator** on any box\n(see issue 210): when active, the output wire splits into lt / eq / gt paths\ncompared against a literal number. Non-number values are a hard error.\n\nThe named-port model (`box.ports`, `from_port` in connections, predicate\nobjects, retry_vary) is fully removed. The retry mechanism goes away with it —\nthe loop-through-a-branch-box pattern is the recommended alternative if\nretry logic is needed.\n\nAll executor code specific to the branch kind (`fire_connections` branch\nsection, `retry_counts`, `retry_vary` application) should be reverted when\nissue 210 is implemented.",

        "content":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\nNote: one output wire per box is a deliberate design constraint, not a missing\nfeature. Positional multi-output was explicitly rejected as fragile (multiple\nreturn statements with the same tuple width are indistinguishable). The\ncomparator (lt/eq/gt branching) is the only multi-path mechanism. Whatever the\nfunction returns goes down the single output wire as one value — arrays or JSON\nobjects if multiple values need to travel together.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n"
      }
    },

        "numLines":34,

        "totalLines":34,
        "content":"# 216 — Read-file box: output contents of a text or data file\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box exists for loading text from disk into the wire graph. A user who\nwants to supply file contents as input to a downstream box must write a custom\nLua function from scratch.\n\n## Intended behavior\nA reusable source file (in `libs/` or a map's `src/`) that exposes two functions:\n- `M.read_text(path)` — reads a plain text file; returns its full contents as a string.\n- `M.read_data(path, key)` — reads a dkjson data file; returns the value at `key` as\n  a string (strips metadata fields like `constant`). If `key` is nil/empty, returns\n  the full JSON-decoded table encoded back to a plain string.\n\nBoth functions output a single port (`text`) carrying the file contents. Error cases\n(file not found, bad JSON) write to stderr and return nil — the executor surfaces nil\nas an empty string on downstream inputs.\n\nThe design follows the established pattern: a regular Lua file that the user picks\nvia the file browser and wires into their map. No executor changes needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/files.lua` with `M.read_text` and `M.read_data`.\n2. Add `libs/files.lua.info.md` listing the two public functions, their inputs, and\n   their single `text` output.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box source file\n- `libs/dkjson.lua` — used by `read_data` for JSON parsing\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how call box outputs are threaded (no changes needed)\n"
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"issues/216-read-file-box.md",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/216-read-file-box.md"
  },
  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

        "content":"# 215 — View source code of a box from the inspector and canvas context menu\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nWhen a box isn't working as expected, the user has no way to inspect its source file\nfrom within the editor. They must find the file path in the inspector's `ref` field\nand open it manually in a separate editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\nTwo entry points to view a box's source:\n- Inspector: a \"view source\" button next to the `ref` field. Clicking replaces the\n  inspector content with a read-only code view of the file.\n- Canvas right-click context menu: a \"view source\" item that does the same.\n\nThe code view shows the raw file text in a `<pre>` block with a \"← back\" button to\nreturn to the normal inspector state. No editing — read-only only for now.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add \"view source\" button next to the ref field;\n   clicking fetches the file via `API.get_extra_src_file` or `API.get_src_file` (based\n   on which group the ref belongs to) and calls a `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)`\n   helper.\n2. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas right-click context\n   menu when a box is selected; calls the same inspector view.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)` helper:\n   renders a `<pre class=\"fb-source-view\">` block, wraps in the inspector panel, adds\n   \"← back\" button.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add `.fb-source-view` CSS: monospace, small font, overflow scroll,\n   dark background.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_extra_src_file, get_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS\n"
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"issues/215-view-box-source.md",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/215-view-box-source.md"
  },
  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T19:49:36.507Z",
  "uuid":"4cdf7802-7c2c-412a-aba9-db5ddc99d9f4",
  "userType":"external",
  "slug":"snug-booping-dove",
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "parentUuid":"88912805-465d-44bb-8001-8ad106b41215",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "type":"attachment",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "attachment":{
    "type":"file",
    "content":{
      "type":"text",
      "file":{
        "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/211a-unify-src-dirs-pipeline.md",
        "numLines":56,
        "startLine":1,
        "totalLines":56,
        "content":"# 211a — Unify src/ into the same directory pipeline as extra dirs\n\n## Status\nin-progress\n\n## Current behavior\nThe file browser treats `src/` as a special case:\n- `src/` is always shown (implicit, not stored in meta.json)\n- Extra dirs are stored in `meta.json` → `extra_src_dirs`\n- The server has two separate endpoints: `/maps/:name/src` and `/maps/:name/extrasrc`\n- The client calls both and merges them\n- The context menu \"hide directory\" only works for extra dirs (`if (group.path)`)\n\nThe implicit exception violates the principle that all dirs go through the same pipeline.\n\n## Intended behavior\nAll browseable directories, including `src/`, flow through the same data path:\n- `meta.json` gains a `src_dirs` field: an array of absolute paths\n- `src/` is just the first entry; extra dirs are appended as before\n- One server endpoint returns all of them\n- One client call fetches all of them\n- \"Hide\" removes from `src_dirs` for any entry, including `src/`\n- No `if (group.path)` exception in the UI — all groups are treated identically\n\nMigration: if `src_dirs` is absent in meta.json, the server synthesizes it at read-time\nfrom the map's `src/` path + any existing `extra_src_dirs` entries.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `src/005-http-server.lua` — update `handle_list_extrasrc` and `handle_get_extrasrc`\n   to read from `src_dirs` (with migration from `extra_src_dirs` + implicit `src/`).\n2. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — remove `list_src_files()` call; only use\n   `list_extra_src()`; remove separate `src/` group construction; remove `if (group.path)`\n   exception; update hide/add actions to use `src_dirs` field.\n3. `scripts/create-map.sh` — initialize `src_dirs` in meta.json with the map's absolute\n   `src/` path at creation time.\n\n## Implementation notes (bugs found during testing)\n\n**Bug: add/hide handlers read `meta.src_dirs` instead of `groups`.**\nThe server migrates old maps on read (synthesizes `src_dirs` from `extra_src_dirs` + implicit\n`src/`), but the client's add and hide handlers read raw `meta.src_dirs || []`, which is\n`[]` on old maps. So adding a library dir saves `src_dirs: [new_path]` with no prior entries,\ndiscarding whatever the server just migrated. Fix: both handlers must derive the current list\nfrom the already-resolved `groups` array (the live server view), not from `meta.src_dirs`.\n\n**Bug: dir picker opens at `/home` every time.**\nShould open at the parent of the last directory in `groups`, so the user lands near where they\nlast browsed. Fixed by passing a computed `initial_path` to `show_dir_picker`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — handle_list_extrasrc, handle_get_extrasrc\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — render, show_file_list, show_dir_picker\n- `scripts/create-map.sh` — meta.json template\n- `maps/*/meta.json` — needs `src_dirs` field (server migrates on first read)\n"
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"issues/211a-unify-src-dirs-pipeline.md",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/211a-unify-src-dirs-pipeline.md"
  },
  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

      "content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Lua/LuaJIT language driver for SoraMech.\n# Loads a .lua module, calls the named function with JSON-decoded arguments,\n# and writes the return value(s) as a JSON array to stdout.\n# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nFILE_PATH=\"${1}\"\nFN_NAME=\"${2}\"\nARG_COUNT=\"${3}\"\nshift 3\n\nif [ -z \"${FILE_PATH}\" ] || [ -z \"${FN_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# set LUA_PATH so dkjson is findable before the shim runs its first require\nexport LUA_PATH=\"${DIR}/libs/?.lua;${LUA_PATH:-;}\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- add libs and the module's own directory to the path for any further requires\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- expose map root as a global so box functions can access data files without\n-- needing it wired as an explicit input; convention: src/ is one level below root\nSORAMECH_MAP_DIR = script_dir:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or script_dir\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n"

branch = \"gt\"\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_cmp_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == branch then\n The SoraMech runner invokes any driver\n5\tidentically, regardless of language. Adding support for a new language means\n6\tadding one script to this directory and one entry in drivers.json.\n7\t\n8\tContract\n9\t--------\n10\t\n11\tThe runner calls a driver as:\n12\t\n13\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n14\t\n15\t  file-path   absolute or relative path to the source file\n16\t  fn-name     name of the function to call within that file\n17\t  arg-count   number of arguments that follow\n18\t  args        zero or more argument strings; structured values are JSON strings\n19\t\n20\tOn success:\n21\t  - exit code 0\n22\t  - stdout: a JSON array where each element is one return value\n23\t    single-value functions: [\"result\"]\n24\t    multi-value (tuple) functions: [\"val1\", \"val2\", ...]\n25\t\n26\tOn failure:\n27\t  - exit code non-zero\n28\t  - stderr: human-readable error message\n29\t  - stdout: empty or ignored\n30\t\n31\tBuilt-in drivers\n32\t----------------\n33\t\n34\t  lua.sh    — calls a function in a .lua module via luajit\n35\t  bash.sh   — sources a .sh file and calls a bash function\n36\t  c.sh      — compiles a .c file (caches binary in tmp/cache/) and runs it\n37\t\n38\tRegistering a driver\n39\t--------------------\n40\t\n41\tIn the map's drivers.json:\n42\t\n43\t  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n44\t\n45\tWrite drivers/rust.sh following the contract above. The runner has no\n46\tknowledge of any language — it reads the extension, finds the script, calls it.\n47\t\n48\tWriting a driver\n49\t----------------\n50\t\n51\tMinimum viable driver (bash pseudocode):\n52\t\n53\t  FILE=\"${1}\"   FN=\"${2}\"   N=\"${3}\"   shift 3\n54\t  # compile / interpret FILE if needed\n55\t  # invoke FN with \"$@\" as arguments\n56\t  # print result as JSON array to stdout\n57\t  # exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n58\t\n59\tThe arg-count field is informational. Drivers may use \"$@\" directly.\n60\t",

      "totalLines":60,
      "content":"SoraMech Language Drivers\n=========================\n\nEach file here is a driver script. The SoraMech runner invokes any driver\nidentically, regardless of language. Adding support for a new language means\nadding one script to this directory and one entry in drivers.json.\n\nContract\n--------\n\nThe runner calls a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\n  file-path   absolute or relative path to the source file\n  fn-name     name of the function to call within that file\n  arg-count   number of arguments that follow\n  args        zero or more argument strings; structured values are JSON strings\n\nOn success:\n  - exit code 0\n  - stdout: a JSON array where each element is one return value\n    single-value functions: [\"result\"]\n    multi-value (tuple) functions: [\"val1\", \"val2\", ...]\n\nOn failure:\n  - exit code non-zero\n  - stderr: human-readable error message\n  - stdout: empty or ignored\n\nBuilt-in drivers\n----------------\n\n  lua.sh    — calls a function in a .lua module via luajit\n  bash.sh   — sources a .sh file and calls a bash function\n  c.sh      — compiles a .c file (caches binary in tmp/cache/) and runs it\n\nRegistering a driver\n--------------------\n\nIn the map's drivers.json:\n\n  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n\nWrite drivers/rust.sh following the contract above. The runner has no\nknowledge of any language — it reads the extension, finds the script, calls it.\n\nWriting a driver\n----------------\n\nMinimum viable driver (bash pseudocode):\n\n  FILE=\"${1}\"   FN=\"${2}\"   N=\"${3}\"   shift 3\n  # compile / interpret FILE if needed\n  # invoke FN with \"$@\" as arguments\n  # print result as JSON array to stdout\n  # exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n\nThe arg-count field is informational. Drivers may use \"$@\" directly.\n"
    }
  },

        "content":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## What a driver is\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\nfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n\nLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\ncases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\ndriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\nwrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n\n## Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n\nThe driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n    single-output functions)\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\nand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\ndeclaration order.\n\n## Shell script vs. binary caller\n\nTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n        JSON as with a normal driver.\n\nBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\nbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n\n## Built-in driver scripts\n\nShipped in a global drivers/ directory alongside soramech-runner.lua.\nMaps can override any driver by defining the same extension in their\nlocal drivers.json pointing at a map-local script.\n\n### drivers/lua.sh\n\nInvokes a single function from a Lua file using luajit. The function\nmust be a module-level export (returned from the file or set in a\npackage). Args are decoded from JSON; return values are encoded to JSON.\n\n### drivers/c.sh\n\nCompiles the .c file if its mtime is newer than the cached binary in\ntmp/cache/. The cache key is the source file's absolute path hashed.\nInvokes the compiled binary with the args. The binary must follow the\ndriver output contract (JSON to stdout).\n\nThe binary is expected to expose a `main`-style entry that reads args\nfrom argv and writes JSON to stdout. A small C header (shipped with\nsoramech) provides helpers for this.\n\n### drivers/bash.sh\n\nInvokes a bash function defined in the .sh file by sourcing the file\nand calling the function with the args as positional parameters.\nThe function must echo a JSON value (or array) to stdout.\n\n## User-defined drivers",

        "type":"tool_result"

        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01WhDaJTH78r7qAZRtVqoJjv",
        "content":"/*\n * String operations for driver-test map.\n * Each function is exposed via a dispatch on argv[1] (fn-name).\n * Reads a JSON string from argv[2], writes a JSON string to stdout.\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <ctype.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ strip_json_string\n * Remove surrounding double-quotes from a JSON string value.\n * Returns a malloc'd buffer the caller must free. */\nstatic char *strip_json_string(const char *s) {\n    int len = strlen(s);\n    if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '\"' && s[len - 1] == '\"') {\n        char *out = malloc(len - 1);\n        memcpy(out, s + 1, len - 2);\n        out[len - 2] = '\\0';\n        return out;\n    }\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    strcpy(out, s);\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ uppercase */\nstatic void uppercase(const char *json_in) {\n    char *s = strip_json_string(json_in);\n    int len = strlen(s);\n    /* convert in-place */\n    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {\n        s[i] = toupper((unsigned char)s[i]);\n    }\n    /* output as a JSON string wrapped in an array (driver contract) */\n    printf(\"[\\\"%s\\\"]\\n\", s);\n    free(s);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main */\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    if (argc < 3) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"strops: usage: strops <fn-name> <json-arg>\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    const char *fn   = argv[1];\n    const char *arg1 = argv[2];\n\n    if (strcmp(fn, \"uppercase\") == 0) {\n        uppercase(arg1);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr, \"strops: unknown function '%s'\\n\", fn);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */",

        "type":"tool_result"

        "content":"# 102 — Language driver interface\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo driver scripts exist. The runner has no mechanism to invoke functions\nin any language. There is no defined contract for how a driver receives\narguments or returns values.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA drivers/ directory exists alongside soramech-runner.lua containing\nthree built-in driver scripts: lua.sh, c.sh, and bash.sh. Each follows\nthe same interface. The runner invokes any driver identically regardless\nof language. A user can write a fourth driver for any language by copying\nthe pattern.\n\nDriver invocation contract:\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nAll args are strings. Structured values are JSON strings. Driver writes\none JSON value (or JSON array for tuples) to stdout on success. Exits\nnon-zero on failure, error message to stderr.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. Write drivers/lua.sh — sources the target .lua file via luajit,\n   calls the named function with decoded JSON args, encodes return value\n   to JSON on stdout. Single-value and multi-value (tuple) returns both\n   produce a JSON array.\n2. Write drivers/c.sh — checks mtime of .c file against cached binary\n   in tmp/cache/. Compiles if stale (using gcc or cc, flags configurable\n   via env). Invokes the binary with args as argv. Binary must write JSON\n   to stdout per the contract.\n3. Write drivers/bash.sh — sources the .sh file, calls the named\n   function with args as positional params. Function must echo JSON to\n   stdout.\n4. Write a small test map maps/driver-test/ with one box per driver type\n   to verify each driver works end-to-end before the runner is built.\n5. Document the driver contract in drivers/README (plain text, short).\n\n## Related documents\n\n- docs/003-driver-system.md — full driver system spec\n- issues/101 — map scaffold (tmp/cache/ directory created there)\n- issues/103 — runner uses these drivers once they exist\n\n## Notes\n\nFor lua.sh: luajit must be on PATH. The script should fail with a clear\nerror if luajit is not found, not silently produce wrong output.\n\nFor c.sh: the cache key for compiled binaries is the absolute path of the\nsource file. A sha1 or md5 of the path is sufficient; the binary is\nstored as tmp/cache/<hash>. Stale check: stat both files, compare mtimes.\n\nFor bash.sh: functions in a sourced file may have side effects and access\nthe filesystem. This is expected and correct — bash boxes are intentionally\nless constrained than lua or C boxes.\n\nThe \"no special cases in the runner\" constraint means the runner must not\nhave any if-elseif chain on file extension. All dispatch goes through\nthe driver table loaded from drivers.json.",

    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/218-single-output-driver-contract.md",
    "content":"# 218 — Enforce single-output driver contract throughout\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe driver contract was originally written to support multi-return tuples: drivers\noutput a JSON array where each element is one return value. The executor unwraps\n`result_arr[1]` and discards everything else. Three concrete artifacts of this:\n\n- `drivers/lua.sh` shim: collects all return values into `results`, encodes each\n  as a JSON string, then wraps in another JSON array (`json.encode(encoded)`).\n  A single-return function produces `[\"\\\"hello\\\"\"]` — doubly-encoded.\n- `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` and `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh`: bash\n  functions that explicitly output `['value']` — following the now-dead contract.\n- `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c`: C binary that outputs `[\"VALUE\"]`.\n- `src/004-executor.lua`: parses a JSON array, checks it's a table, takes `[1]`.\n- Docs (`drivers/README`, `docs/003-driver-system.md`): describe the array contract.\n\n## Intended behavior\nOne output wire per box. Whatever the function returns is the single output value.\nThe driver contract is:\n  - stdout: a single JSON value (string, number, boolean, object, or null)\n  - exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n\nNo wrapping in an array. No `result_arr[1]`. The executor decodes stdout directly\nas the output value.\n\n## Why multi-output was ruled out\nMultiple return statements with the same-width tuples are indistinguishable\npositionally. The mapping from return position to output port name is ambiguous.\nA single return value is always unambiguous. This was decided in the design phase\n(see `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md`).\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `drivers/lua.sh` shim — replace multi-return collection with `print(json.encode(results[1]))`.\n2. `src/004-executor.lua` — decode stdout as a single JSON value; remove array unwrapping.\n3. `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` — change printf to output `\"value\"` not `[\"value\"]`.\n4. `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` — same fix.\n5. `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c` — change printf to output `\"VALUE\"` not `[\"VALUE\"]`.\n6. `drivers/README` — update contract description.\n7. `docs/003-driver-system.md` — update contract description.\n8. `docs/001-architecture.md` — note `outputs` field in box JSON is display metadata only.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `drivers/lua.sh` — LUASHIM section: results collection and encoding\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — `run_task` function, lines 94-112\n- `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` — outputs `['value']`\n- `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` — outputs `['value']`\n- `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c` — outputs `[\"VALUE\"]`\n- `drivers/README` — driver contract docs\n- `docs/003-driver-system.md` — driver system spec\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — execution model description\n"
  },
  "uuid":"951e535d-da97-4593-8f12-fcfde0cf7be7",
  "parentUuid":"d098ea61-6490-4f26-93f2-493552e7b836",
