    "originalFile":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns a single output value and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: each input port's value as a JSON-encoded shell arg\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n\n    local cmd\n    if fn then\n        -- source caller: driver file fn arg_count [args...]\n        cmd = driver .. \" \" .. shell_quote(abs_ref) .. \" \" ..\n              shell_quote(fn) .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    else\n        -- binary caller: run ref directly with args\n        cmd = abs_ref .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    end\n\n    -- invoke driver; capture stdout; errors go to stderr (visible in terminal)\n    local tmpfile = map_dir .. \"/tmp/driver-stderr-\" .. box.id .. \".txt\"\n    local full_cmd = \"sh -c \" .. shell_quote(cmd .. \" 2>\" .. tmpfile)\n    local ph = io.popen(full_cmd, \"r\")\n    local stdout = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    local ok_close = ph:close()\n\n    -- read stderr if any\n    local sf = io.open(tmpfile, \"r\")\n    local stderr_text = sf and sf:read(\"*a\") or \"\"\n    if sf then sf:close() end\n    os.remove(tmpfile)\n\n    if not ok_close then\n        local err_msg = \"driver failed for box '\" .. box.id .. \"'\"\n        if stderr_text and #stderr_text > 0 then\n            err_msg = err_msg .. \": \" .. stderr_text:gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\")\n        end\n        return nil, err_msg\n    end\n\n    -- parse output JSON array from stdout\n    local result_arr, _, jerr = json.decode(stdout)\n    if not result_arr then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver stdout is not valid JSON: \" ..\n            tostring(jerr) .. \" (got: \" .. tostring(stdout):sub(1, 80) .. \")\"\n    end\n    if type(result_arr) ~= \"table\" then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver output must be a JSON array\"\n    end\n\n    -- take the first element of the array as the single output value\n    local raw = result_arr[1]\n    local output_val\n    if raw ~= nil then\n        local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw)\n        output_val = aerr and raw or val\n    end\n\n    return output_val, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ inputs_satisfied\nlocal function inputs_satisfied(box, store)\n    -- a box is ready when all its declared input ports have a value in the store\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        if store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name] == nil then\n            return false\n        end\n    end\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ collect_inputs\nlocal function collect_inputs(box, store)\n    local inputs = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name]\n    end\n    return inputs\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ fire_connections\n-- Routes the single output value through wired connections.\n-- If box.comparand is set: compare output against it (must be a number or error).\n-- Otherwise: fire all connections whose from_branch is nil.\n-- Returns nil on success, or an error string.\nlocal function fire_connections(box, output_val, store, queue, boxes)\n    if box.comparand and box.comparand ~= \"\" then\n        -- comparator mode: output must be a number\n        local comparand = tonumber(box.comparand)\n        if not comparand then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': comparand '\" ..\n                tostring(box.comparand) .. \"' is not a valid number\"\n        end\n        local num_val = tonumber(output_val)\n        if not num_val then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': output value '\" ..\n                tostring(output_val) .. \"' is not a number, but comparator is configured\"\n        end\n\n        -- determine which branch to fire\n        local branch\n        if num_val < comparand then\n            branch = \"lt\"\n        elseif num_val == comparand then\n            branch = \"eq\"\n        else\n            branch = \"gt\"\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_cmp_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == branch then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n            end\n            ::next_cmp_conn::\n        end\n    else\n        -- single-wire mode: fire connections where from_branch is nil\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == nil then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_last_run\nlocal function write_last_run(map_dir, run_state)\n    local tmp_dir = map_dir .. \"/tmp\"\n    local path    = tmp_dir .. \"/last-run.json\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"executor: cannot write last-run.json: \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return\n    end\n    f:write(json.encode(run_state, { indent = true }))\n    f:close()\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ execute\nfunction M.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    local boxes    = graph.boxes\n    local drivers  = graph.drivers\n    local entry_id = whose inputs are not yet satisfied\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n        visited[id] = true\n\n        local inputs = collect_inputs(box, store)\n\n        local output_val, task_err = run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n\n        run_log[id] = {\n false\n            map_err = task_err\n            io.stderr:write(\"executor: \" .. task_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- route output through wired connections\n then\n    echo \"lua.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif ! command -v luajit > /dev/null 2>&1; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: luajit not found on PATH\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# set LUA_PATH so dkjson is findable before the shim runs its first require\nexport LUA_PATH=\"${DIR}/libs/?.lua;${LUA_PATH:-;}\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- add libs and the module's own directory to the path for any further requires\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- expose map root as a global so box functions can access data files without\n-- needing it wired as an explicit input; convention: src/ is one level below root\nSORAMECH_MAP_DIR = script_dir:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or script_dir\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n",

then\n    echo \"lua.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# build a JSON array of the raw argument strings for passing into lua\nARGS_JSON=\"[\"\nSEP=\"\"\nfor ARG in \"$@\"; do\n    ARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}${SEP}${ARG}\"\n    SEP=\",\"\ndone\nARGS_JSON=\"${ARGS_JSON}]\"\n\n# set LUA_PATH so dkjson is findable before the shim runs its first require\nexport LUA_PATH=\"${DIR}/libs/?.lua;${LUA_PATH:-;}\"\n\n# run luajit with the driver shim inline; the shim loads the module,\n# decodes arguments, calls the function, and encodes the result\nluajit - \"${FILE_PATH}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"${ARGS_JSON}\" << 'LUASHIM'\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\n\n-- read driver arguments\nlocal file_path = arg[1]\nlocal fn_name   = arg[2]\nlocal args_raw  = arg[3]\n\n-- add libs and the module's own directory to the path for any further requires\nlocal script_dir = file_path:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or \".\"\npackage.path = script_dir .. \"/?.lua;\" ..\n               \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\n-- expose map root as a global so box functions can access data files without\n-- needing it wired as an explicit input; convention: src/ is one level below root\nSORAMECH_MAP_DIR = script_dir:match(\"^(.+)/[^/]+$\") or script_dir\n\n-- decode args array\nlocal args_table, _, jerr = json.decode(args_raw)\nif not args_table then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: failed to decode args JSON: \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- load the module\nlocal ok, mod = pcall(dofile, file_path)\nif not ok then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: error loading \" .. file_path .. \": \" .. tostring(mod) .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- resolve the function\nlocal fn = mod[fn_name]\nif type(fn) ~= \"function\" then\n    io.stderr:write(\"lua.sh: no public function '\" .. fn_name .. \"' in \" .. file_path .. \"\\n\")\n    os.exit(1)\nend\n\n-- decode each arg from JSON to lua value; strings are passed as-is\nlocal call_args = {}\nfor i, raw_arg in ipairs(args_table) do\n    local val, _, aerr = json.decode(raw_arg)\n    if aerr then\n        -- not valid JSON — treat as a plain string\n        call_args[i] = raw_arg\n    else\n        call_args[i] = val\n    end\nend\n\n-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))\nLUASHIM\n",
    "oldString":"-- call the function; collect all return values into a table\nlocal results = table.pack(fn(table.unpack(call_args)))\n\n-- encode results as a JSON array (each return value is one element)\nlocal encoded = {}\nfor i = 1, results.n do\n    encoded[i] = json.encode(results[i])\nend\nprint(json.encode(encoded))",
    "newString":"-- call the function; one output wire, so only the first return value matters\nlocal result = fn(table.unpack(call_args))\n\n-- encode the single return value as a JSON value\nprint(json.encode(result))",

        "oldStart":33,

    "originalFile":"/*\n * String operations for driver-test map.\n * Each function is exposed via a dispatch on argv[1] (fn-name).\n * Reads a JSON string from argv[2], writes a JSON string to stdout.\n */\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <ctype.h>\n#include <stdlib.h>\n\n/* {{{ strip_json_string\n * Remove surrounding double-quotes from a JSON string value.\n * Returns a malloc'd buffer the caller must free. */\nstatic char *strip_json_string(const char *s) {\n    int len = strlen(s);\n    if (len >= 2 && s[0] == '\"' && s[len - 1] == '\"') {\n        char *out = malloc(len - 1);\n        memcpy(out, s + 1, len - 2);\n        out[len - 2] = '\\0';\n        return out;\n    }\n    char *out = malloc(len + 1);\n    strcpy(out, s);\n    return out;\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ uppercase */\nstatic void uppercase(const char *json_in) {\n    char *s = strip_json_string(json_in);\n    int len = strlen(s);\n    /* convert in-place */\n    for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) {\n        s[i] = toupper((unsigned char)s[i]);\n    }\n    /* output as a JSON string wrapped in an array (driver contract) */\n    printf(\"[\\\"%s\\\"]\\n\", s);\n    free(s);\n}\n/* }}} */\n\n/* {{{ main */\nint main(int argc, char **argv) {\n    if (argc < 3) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"strops: usage: strops <fn-name> <json-arg>\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    const char *fn   = argv[1];\n    const char *arg1 = argv[2];\n\n    if (strcmp(fn, \"uppercase\") == 0) {\n        uppercase(arg1);\n        return 0;\n    }\n\n    fprintf(stderr, \"strops: unknown function '%s'\\n\", fn);\n    return 1;\n}\n/* }}} */\n",
    "oldString":"    /* output as a JSON string wrapped in an array (driver contract) */\n    printf(\"[\\\"%s\\\"]\\n\", s);",
    "newString":"    /* output as a single JSON string (driver contract: one value per box) */\n    printf(\"\\\"%s\\\"\\n\", s);",
    "replaceAll":false,

  },

        "content":"1\t# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n2\t\n3\t## What a driver is\n4\t\n5\tA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\n6\tlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\n7\tfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n8\t\n9\tLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\n10\tcases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\n11\tdriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\n12\twrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n13\t\n14\t## Driver contract\n15\t\n16\tThe runner invokes a driver as:\n17\t\n18\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n19\t\n20\tArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\n21\tpassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n22\t\n23\tThe driver must:\n24\t  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n25\t  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n26\t    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n27\t    single-output functions)\n28\t  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n29\t    it)\n30\t\n31\tNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\n32\tand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\n33\tdeclaration order.\n34\t\n35\t## Shell script vs. binary caller\n36\t\n37\tTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n38\t\n39\t  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n40\t      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n41\t        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n42\t\n43\t  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n44\t      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n45\t        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n46\t        JSON as with a normal driver.\n47\t\n48\tBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\n49\tbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n50\t",

      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":106,
      "content":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## What a driver is\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\nfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n\nLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\ncases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\ndriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\nwrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n\n## Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n\nThe driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n    single-output functions)\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\nand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\ndeclaration order.\n\n## Shell script vs. binary caller\n\nTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n        JSON as with a normal driver.\n\nBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\nbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n"
    }
  },

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## What a driver is\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\nfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n\nLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\ncases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\ndriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\nwrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n\n## Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n\nThe driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n    single-output functions)\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\nand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\ndeclaration order.\n\n## Shell script vs. binary caller\n\nTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n        JSON as with a normal driver.\n\nBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\nbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n\n## Built-in driver scripts\n\nShipped in a global drivers/ directory alongside soramech-runner.lua.\nMaps can override any driver by defining the same extension in their\nlocal drivers.json pointing at a map-local script.\n\n### drivers/lua.sh\n\nInvokes a single function from a Lua file using luajit. The function\nmust be a module-level export (returned from the file or set in a\npackage). Args are decoded from JSON; return values are encoded to JSON.\n\n### drivers/c.sh\n\nCompiles the .c file if its mtime is newer than the cached binary in\ntmp/cache/. The cache key is the source file's absolute path hashed.\nInvokes the compiled binary with the args. The binary must follow the\ndriver output contract (JSON to stdout).\n\nThe binary is expected to expose a `main`-style entry that reads args\nfrom argv and writes JSON to stdout. A small C header (shipped with\nsoramech) provides helpers for this.\n\n### drivers/bash.sh\n\nInvokes a bash function defined in the .sh file by sourcing the file\nand calling the function with the args as positional parameters.\nThe function must echo a JSON value (or array) to stdout.\n\n## User-defined drivers\n\nAdd the file extension and path to the map's drivers.json:\n\n  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n\nWrite drivers/rust.sh. It receives the same arguments as any built-in\ndriver. Compile, interpret, or delegate however the language requires.\nThe runner doesn't care.\n\n## Driver lookup order\n\n  1. Map-local drivers.json (maps/<name>/drivers.json)\n  2. Global drivers.json (alongside soramech-runner.lua)\n  3. Hard error if extension not found — no fallback, no silent skip\n\n## Passing structured values between boxes\n\nAll inter-box values are JSON at the transport layer. Inside a Lua box,\ndkjson decodes input strings to Lua tables. The driver re-encodes return\nvalues to JSON. Inside a C box, the shipped helper header decodes argv\nJSON strings to C structs and encodes results back.\n\nThis means structured values cross language boundaries cleanly: a Lua\ntable produced by one box can be consumed by a C function in the next\nbox, because both sides see JSON at the wire level.\n",
    "oldString":"The driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success: either a JSON array\n    (for multi-output / tuple returns) or a single JSON value (for\n    single-output functions)\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, parses JSON,\nand maps the array positions to the box's declared output port names in\ndeclaration order.",

The binary must write a JSON\n# array to stdout per the driver contract.\n# Contract: <script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n# The fn-name is passed as argv[1] so the binary can dispatch to the right function.\n# Cache location: TMP_DIR/cache/<md5-of-absolute-path>\n\nDIR=\"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nFILE_PATH=\"${1}\"\nFN_NAME=\"${2}\"\nARG_COUNT=\"${3}\"\nshift 3\n\nif [ -z \"${FILE_PATH}\" ] || [ -z \"${FN_NAME}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: missing file-path or fn-name\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nif [ ! -f \"${FILE_PATH}\" ]; then\n    echo \"c.sh: file not found: ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# resolve to absolute path for stable cache key\nABS_PATH=$(realpath \"${FILE_PATH}\")\n\n# the map's tmp/cache dir lives relative to the file; walk up to find it\n# convention: src/ is one level below the map root, cache is in tmp/cache/\nMAP_ROOT=$(dirname \"$(dirname \"${ABS_PATH}\")\")\nCACHE_DIR=\"${MAP_ROOT}/tmp/cache\"\nmkdir -p \"${CACHE_DIR}\"\n\n# cache key: md5 of the absolute source path (not contents — path is stable per binary)\nCACHE_KEY=$(echo -n \"${ABS_PATH}\" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)\nBINARY=\"${CACHE_DIR}/${CACHE_KEY}\"\n\n# compile if binary is missing or source is newer than the binary\nNEEDS_COMPILE=0\nif [ ! -f \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nelif [ \"${ABS_PATH}\" -nt \"${BINARY}\" ]; then\n    NEEDS_COMPILE=1\nfi\n\nif [ \"${NEEDS_COMPILE}\" -eq 1 ]; then\n    CC=\"${CC:-gcc}\"\n    CFLAGS=\"${CFLAGS:--O2 -Wall}\"\n    \"${CC}\" ${CFLAGS} -o \"${BINARY}\" \"${ABS_PATH}\" 2>&1\n    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then\n        echo \"c.sh: compilation failed for ${FILE_PATH}\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\nfi\n\n# invoke binary: fn-name as first arg, then the caller's args\n\"${BINARY}\" \"${FN_NAME}\" \"$@\"\n",

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\nthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n    logs/            — run logs\n    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n```\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"outputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"ports\": [\n    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [...]\n}\n```\n\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\nat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n\n## Language driver interface\n\nDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n\nOutputs are returned as JSON on stdout. Exit code non-zero = box failure.\nSee docs/003-driver-system.md for the full driver contract.\n\n## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n\n  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n  3. Collect outputs: parse JSON from driver stdout\n  4. Store outputs: held in runner memory, keyed by box id + output name\n  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\nby effil-jit or the custom thread pool from the 3d-rts project.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only. Individual\nfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\nwhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. It survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n",
    "oldString":"Outputs are returned as JSON on stdout. Exit code non-zero = box failure.\nSee docs/003-driver-system.md for the full driver contract.",
    "newString":"The single return value is encoded as a JSON value on stdout. Exit code\nnon-zero = box failure. Each box has exactly one output wire — multi-return\ntuples are not supported (see docs/003-driver-system.md).",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false

    "structuredPatch":[{
        "newStart":1,
        "newLines":7,
        "lines":[" # 218 — Enforce single-output driver contract throughout"," "," ## Status","-open","+completed"," "," ## Current behavior"," The driver contract was originally written to support multi-return tuples: drivers"],
        "oldStart":1,
        "oldLines":7
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 218 — Enforce single-output driver contract throughout\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe driver contract was originally written to support multi-return tuples: drivers\noutput a JSON array where each element is one return value. The executor unwraps\n`result_arr[1]` and discards everything else. Three concrete artifacts of this:\n\n- `drivers/lua.sh` shim: collects all return values into `results`, encodes each\n  as a JSON string, then wraps in another JSON array (`json.encode(encoded)`).\n  A single-return function produces `[\"\\\"hello\\\"\"]` — doubly-encoded.\n- `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` and `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh`: bash\n  functions that explicitly output `['value']` — following the now-dead contract.\n- `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c`: C binary that outputs `[\"VALUE\"]`.\n- `src/004-executor.lua`: parses a JSON array, checks it's a table, takes `[1]`.\n- Docs (`drivers/README`, `docs/003-driver-system.md`): describe the array contract.\n\n## Intended behavior\nOne output wire per box. Whatever the function returns is the single output value.\nThe driver contract is:\n  - stdout: a single JSON value (string, number, boolean, object, or null)\n  - exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n\nNo wrapping in an array. No `result_arr[1]`. The executor decodes stdout directly\nas the output value.\n\n## Why multi-output was ruled out\nMultiple return statements with the same-width tuples are indistinguishable\npositionally. The mapping from return position to output port name is ambiguous.\nA single return value is always unambiguous. This was decided in the design phase\n(see `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md`).\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `drivers/lua.sh` shim — replace multi-return collection with `print(json.encode(results[1]))`.\n2. `src/004-executor.lua` — decode stdout as a single JSON value; remove array unwrapping.\n3. `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` — change printf to output `\"value\"` not `[\"value\"]`.\n4. `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` — same fix.\n5. `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c` — change printf to output `\"VALUE\"` not `[\"VALUE\"]`.\n6. `drivers/README` — update contract description.\n7. `docs/003-driver-system.md` — update contract description.\n8. `docs/001-architecture.md` — note `outputs` field in box JSON is display metadata only.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `drivers/lua.sh` — LUASHIM section: results collection and encoding\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — `run_task` function, lines 94-112\n- `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` — outputs `['value']`\n- `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh` — outputs `['value']`\n- `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c` — outputs `[\"VALUE\"]`\n- `drivers/README` — driver contract docs\n- `docs/003-driver-system.md` — driver system spec\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — execution model description\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncompleted",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },
  "uuid":"fb2aff39-78dc-47a6-9602-bf0114bdbb13",

        "text":"The refactor is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what changed:\n\n**Driver contract (before → after):**\n- `drivers/lua.sh` shim: was collecting all returns into an array and double-encoding (`[\"\\\"hello\\\"\"]`). Now just `print(json.encode(result))` — single value.\n- `maps/classify-demo/src/stamp.sh` and `maps/driver-test/src/utils.sh`: were doing `printf '[\"%s\"]\\n'`. Now `printf '\"%s\"\\n'`.\n- `maps/driver-test/src/strops.c`: was `printf(\"[\\\"%s\\\"]\\n\", s)`. Now `printf(\"\\\"%s\\\"\\n\", s)`.\n\n**Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`):** Was decoding a JSON array, checking it was a table, taking `[1]`, then decoding the inner JSON string. Now just one `json.decode(stdout)` call.\n\n**Docs:** `drivers/README`, `docs/003-driver-system.md`, `docs/001-architecture.md` all updated to describe single-value output. The `from_output` field in existing connection records is left as harmless metadata — the executor already ignores it in non-comparator mode."

## [748]

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T19:56:58.074Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"Can you tell me what the soramech-runner/server.lua files in the root of the project directory are? I think they're in the wrong spot.\n\nAlso. We need to think about redesigning the soramech-runner. I think instead of having a program that runs maps, we should instead build a system that auto-generates lua or other code. Like, a compiler. Or a transpiler. Something that generates a source file / binary or whatever that can be run by the user. The idea is, the editor should be something that creates programs that are fully functional. But if we require our own software to RUN the programs, then it's less useful. Can you create an issue file for that? Some sort of, source-code generator. It should properly network the various box functions, treating them like the source-code they are. The box json that we're building when using the editor is just for viewing them IN the editor - to keep track of connections and such. Well, we should be able to re-create the connectiosn by just looking at which functions are calling which other functions, but we won't know where the user placed them on the canvas unless we store that in json or whatever.\n\nAlso... I don't think piping the output of each box through stdout is the right way to go. We need something more stable than that. If we need to coalesce to just supporting lua, bash, and C, then we can, but let's try to avoid that. If we can build the integration systems into the runners, that would help a lot, because it just means we'd need to write a new runner (with standardized requirements) when we wanted to add a new language.",
    "role":"user"
  },
  "slug":"snug-booping-dove",
  "gitBranch":"master",

{

  "message":{

  },
  "slug":"snug-booping-dove",

  "version":"2.1.121",
  "userType":"external",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/219-map-compiler.md",
    "content":"# 219 — Map compiler: generate standalone source code from a box graph\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe soramech-runner interprets the box graph at runtime. To execute a map, the\nuser must have SoraMech installed. The runner shells out to a language driver for\neach box, captures stdout, and routes values to the next box. The runtime\ndependency on SoraMech and the stdout-as-IPC design are both fragile.\n\n## Intended behavior\nThe editor compiles a map into a standalone source file (or script) that runs\nwithout SoraMech. The box graph is an authoring artifact — the output of the\neditor is a real program.\n\n### What the compiler produces\n\n**Pure Lua map** → a single `.lua` file that requires each box's source file\nand chains calls directly:\n```lua\nlocal greet = require(\"src/greet\")\nlocal write = require(\"src/write_result\")\nwrite.write_result(greet.hello())\n```\nRunnable with `luajit generated.lua`. No SoraMech, no drivers, no IPC.\n\n**Mixed-language map** → a shell script that invokes each box's binary or\ninterpreter in sequence, passing values through named temp files rather than\nstdout. Each step reads its input from a file and writes its output to a file.\nThe script is self-contained and inspectable.\n\n**Comparator (branch) nodes** → if/elseif chains in the generated code.\n\n### What stays in the box JSON\nCanvas positions, labels, wire layout — everything the editor needs to display\nand edit the graph. The JSON is the editor's internal representation. The\ncompiled output is the deliverable.\n\n### Why stdout-as-IPC is the wrong model\nThe current runtime pipes each box's return value through stdout. Problems:\n- A box that prints debug output corrupts the wire value\n- Shell process overhead per box\n- Can't pass binary or large values reliably\n- Values are transient — can't inspect mid-run\n\nThe compiler eliminates IPC for same-language maps (direct function calls).\nFor mixed-language maps, file-based IPC is used instead of stdout:\neach wire becomes a named temp file. The generated script writes/reads\nexplicitly. Files persist after the run and can be inspected.\n\n### Language runner libraries (alternative to the current driver model)\nFor multi-language support without a runtime, each language needs a small\nshim that:\n- reads its input value from a file path passed as argv\n- calls the box function\n- writes the output value to a file path passed as argv\n\nThe compiler generates calls to these shims. The shims are minimal (~30 lines)\nand are the only per-language artifact needed. No driver contract, no stdout,\nno JSON array wrapping. A new language requires only a new shim, not a new\ndriver script with a parsing contract.\n\n### The canvas/connection relationship\nThe box JSON currently stores connections in both endpoint files. The compiler\nreads these to determine call order (topological sort). Once compiled, the\nconnections are embedded in the generated code — the JSON is not needed at\nruntime. If someone reads the generated code, they can see exactly which\nfunctions call which, without needing the JSON.\n\n## Open questions\n- What is the primary target language for the compiler output? Lua first,\n  with shell script fallback for mixed maps, seems right.\n- Does the compiler live in `src/` (run by the server on demand) or is it\n  a separate CLI tool?\n- Should the editor have a \"compile\" button that writes `output/generated.lua`\n  into the map directory?\n- For mixed-language maps, are the runner shims checked into the map's `src/`\n  or shipped globally with SoraMech?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Write the topological sort: given a box graph, produce a linear execution\n   order respecting dependency edges. (This already partially exists in the\n   executor's queue logic.)\n2. Write a Lua code emitter: for a pure-Lua map, emit `require` calls and\n   chained function calls in topo order, handling comparator branches as\n   if/elseif.\n3. Wire a \"compile\" endpoint into the HTTP server: `POST /maps/:name/compile`\n   writes `maps/:name/output/run.lua`.\n4. Add a \"compile\" button to the editor that hits the endpoint and shows the\n   generated file path.\n5. For mixed maps: emit a shell orchestration script using file-based IPC\n   instead of the Lua emitter.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — topological sort and execution model to adapt\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — box graph loading, connection traversal\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — where the compile endpoint goes\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — where the compile button goes\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — needs update once compiler exists\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — the driver model\n  this partially supersedes (drivers remain for the interpreter path)\n"
  },
  "uuid":"70127cee-dec8-4dc5-b387-b1c15266e892",
  "parentUuid":"bdfe9625-4a2a-402d-bad9-7e6a5ff6d1da",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",

}

        "type":"text",
        "text":"On the root files: they're intentionally there. `soramech-runner.lua` and `soramech-server.lua` are entry points (like `main.c`) — they just `require` the real implementation from `src/`. The `scripts/` bash files call them. That separation is correct; no move needed.\n\nOn the design: the issue captures three things you raised that connect:\n\n1. **Compiler output over runtime interpretation** — the compiled `.lua` (or shell script for mixed-language maps) is the real deliverable. The box JSON is purely the editor's view.\n\n2. **Stdout-as-IPC is the wrong model** — the compiler eliminates it entirely for same-language maps (direct function calls). For mixed maps, it uses named temp files instead of stdout — values persist between steps, can be inspected, can't be corrupted by debug prints.\n\n3. **Language runner shims** — instead of the current driver model (driver.sh shells out, captures stdout, parses JSON), each language just needs a tiny shim (~30 lines) that reads an input file path, calls the function, and writes an output file path. That's the new \"driver contract.\" A new language needs only a shim, not a parsing contract.\n\nThe open question worth thinking about: should the current runner/driver system be kept in parallel (for the interactive \"run this map\" button in the editor), or does the compiler replace it entirely? I lean toward keeping the interpreter path for interactive use and the compiler for export/deployment."
      }]

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-08T20:03:41.844Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"  On the design question: The compiler idea is compelling — instead of SoraMech interpreting the box graph at runtime, it generates a standalone program.\n  For the IPC concern, the right framing is: a compiler eliminates the IPC problem entirely for same-language maps (direct function calls). For\n  cross-language maps, the compiler can generate a shell orchestration script that passes values through temp files (inspectable, debuggable) rather than\n  ephemeral stdout.\n\n\nI know lua can do things like, FFI or whatever. Is that type of thing something we could build into the runners / drivers? How would that work? Something that doesn't involve using temp files, because my understanding is that working with the filesystem (even if it's in /tmp/) is very slow. Can you confirm? If /tmp/ is on RAM, does that imply that it'll be faster than the regular filesystem access?\n\n  On the root files: soramech-runner.lua and soramech-server.lua are entry points — they require the real implementation from src/. They're in the right\n  spot: the root is conventional for \"main\" files you invoke directly. scripts/ is for bash wrappers. No action needed there.\n\nokay but for my projects I like to only have things that the user can run in the root. So, usually I have a \"run\" script that'll run the things we need. In this case that'd probably mean starting the editor, then starting the server. That's something the user can just run and it'll get them into working mode ASAP. If they wanted to run a map file, they should run the \"run\" script that we're working on generating for it haha let's work on that for now...!\n\n  The open question worth thinking about: should the current runner/driver system be kept in parallel (for the interactive \"run this map\" button in the\n  editor), or does the compiler replace it entirely? I lean toward keeping the interpreter path for interactive use and the compiler for export/deployment.\n\nthe editor doesn't have a \"run this map\" button, can you check to see where you remember reading that and update it? We want the editor to simply be for creating map files, it should have no conception of running them.\n\n  3. Language runner shims — instead of the current driver model (driver.sh shells out, captures stdout, parses JSON), each language just needs a tiny shim\n   (~30 lines) that reads an input file path, calls the function, and writes an output file path. That's the new \"driver contract.\" A new language needs\n  only a shim, not a parsing contract.\n\n\nI like this idea, but I'm still concerned about the filesystem. Can you give me ideas for how to integrate them more... strongly?",
    "role":"user"
  },

    "stop_reason":"tool_use",
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Good questions. Let me answer them precisely, then fix the issue file and build the root `run` script.\n\n---\n\n**On `/tmp/` speed:** Confirmed — `/tmp` is `tmpfs` on this machine (RAM-backed). No disk access. But even tmpfs has syscall cost. The hierarchy per value transfer:\n\n- Same-process call: ~nanoseconds\n- LuaJIT FFI call: ~nanoseconds + tiny overhead\n- Anonymous pipe: ~microseconds (2 syscalls: write + read)\n- tmpfs file: ~microseconds × 3 (open, write, close — twice, once per side = 6 syscalls)\n- Real disk: milliseconds\n\nSo tmpfs beats disk massively but is still 3× more syscalls than a pipe, and both are orders of magnitude slower than in-process.\n\n---\n\n**On FFI:** LuaJIT FFI is exactly the right answer for Lua↔C tight integration. Instead of shelling out to `c.sh`, the compiler output would:\n1. Compile the C source to a shared library (`.so`) at compile time\n2. Generate `ffi.load(\"./strops.so\")` and `ffi.cdef[[...]]` in the output Lua file\n3. Call it as a direct in-process function — zero subprocess, zero IPC, zero files\n\nFor Lua↔Bash: FFI doesn't help (bash can't become a `.so`). The best you can do is a **persistent subprocess** — spawn the bash runtime once, keep it alive, and send inputs/outputs over an anonymous pipe per call. One spawn per language runtime, not one per box call.\n\n---\n\n**On stronger shim integration:** Three realistic options ordered by integration strength:\n\n1. **In-process FFI (Lua↔C):** No IPC at all. C becomes a `.so`, LuaJIT calls it like a Lua function. This is tight enough that it's essentially the same as direct Lua calls.\n\n2. **Shared memory (`shm_open`):** A named kernel memory segment. Lua accesses it via FFI (`ffi.C.shm_open` + `mmap`), C accesses it natively, bash can access it at `/dev/shm/<name>`. No filesystem I/O — just a pointer after setup. This is the right IPC primitive for cross-language wire values: write once, read from any language.\n\n3. **Persistent subprocess + anonymous pipe:** Spawn a bash (or Python, etc.) runtime once at program start, keep stdin/stdout open, send a request per box call. Amortizes the spawn cost, keeps data in kernel pipe buffers — never touches the filesystem.\n\nFor the compiler target: same language → direct calls, Lua↔C → FFI, anything else → persistent subprocess over pipe. That tiering eliminates temp files entirely.\n\n---\n\nNow fixing the issue file and the root, then creating the `run` script:"
      }]
  },

    "originalFile":"# 219 — Map compiler: generate standalone source code from a box graph\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe soramech-runner interprets the box graph at runtime. To execute a map, the\nuser must have SoraMech installed. The runner shells out to a language driver for\neach box, captures stdout, and routes values to the next box. The runtime\ndependency on SoraMech and the stdout-as-IPC design are both fragile.\n\n## Intended behavior\nThe editor compiles a map into a standalone source file (or script) that runs\nwithout SoraMech. The box graph is an authoring artifact — the output of the\neditor is a real program.\n\n### What the compiler produces\n\n**Pure Lua map** → a single `.lua` file that requires each box's source file\nand chains calls directly:\n```lua\nlocal greet = require(\"src/greet\")\nlocal write = require(\"src/write_result\")\nwrite.write_result(greet.hello())\n```\nRunnable with `luajit generated.lua`. No SoraMech, no drivers, no IPC.\n\n**Mixed-language map** → a shell script that invokes each box's binary or\ninterpreter in sequence, passing values through named temp files rather than\nstdout. Each step reads its input from a file and writes its output to a file.\nThe script is self-contained and inspectable.\n\n**Comparator (branch) nodes** → if/elseif chains in the generated code.\n\n### What stays in the box JSON\nCanvas positions, labels, wire layout — everything the editor needs to display\nand edit the graph. The JSON is the editor's internal representation. The\ncompiled output is the deliverable.\n\n### Why stdout-as-IPC is the wrong model\nThe current runtime pipes each box's return value through stdout. Problems:\n- A box that prints debug output corrupts the wire value\n- Shell process overhead per box\n- Can't pass binary or large values reliably\n- Values are transient — can't inspect mid-run\n\nThe compiler eliminates IPC for same-language maps (direct function calls).\nFor mixed-language maps, file-based IPC is used instead of stdout:\neach wire becomes a named temp file. The generated script writes/reads\nexplicitly. Files persist after the run and can be inspected.\n\n### Language runner libraries (alternative to the current driver model)\nFor multi-language support without a runtime, each language needs a small\nshim that:\n- reads its input value from a file path passed as argv\n- calls the box function\n- writes the output value to a file path passed as argv\n\nThe compiler generates calls to these shims. The shims are minimal (~30 lines)\nand are the only per-language artifact needed. No driver contract, no stdout,\nno JSON array wrapping. A new language requires only a new shim, not a new\ndriver script with a parsing contract.\n\n### The canvas/connection relationship\nThe box JSON currently stores connections in both endpoint files. The compiler\nreads these to determine call order (topological sort). Once compiled, the\nconnections are embedded in the generated code — the JSON is not needed at\nruntime. If someone reads the generated code, they can see exactly which\nfunctions call which, without needing the JSON.\n\n## Open questions\n- What is the primary target language for the compiler output? Lua first,\n  with shell script fallback for mixed maps, seems right.\n- Does the compiler live in `src/` (run by the server on demand) or is it\n  a separate CLI tool?\n- Should the editor have a \"compile\" button that writes `output/generated.lua`\n  into the map directory?\n- For mixed-language maps, are the runner shims checked into the map's `src/`\n  or shipped globally with SoraMech?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Write the topological sort: given a box graph, produce a linear execution\n   order respecting dependency edges. (This already partially exists in the\n   executor's queue logic.)\n2. Write a Lua code emitter: for a pure-Lua map, emit `require` calls and\n   chained function calls in topo order, handling comparator branches as\n   if/elseif.\n3. Wire a \"compile\" endpoint into the HTTP server: `POST /maps/:name/compile`\n   writes `maps/:name/output/run.lua`.\n4. Add a \"compile\" button to the editor that hits the endpoint and shows the\n   generated file path.\n5. For mixed maps: emit a shell orchestration script using file-based IPC\n   instead of the Lua emitter.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — topological sort and execution model to adapt\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — box graph loading, connection traversal\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — where the compile endpoint goes\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — where the compile button goes\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — needs update once compiler exists\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — the driver model\n  this partially supersedes (drivers remain for the interpreter path)\n",
    "oldString":"## Open questions\n- What is the primary target language for the compiler output? Lua first,\n  with shell script fallback for mixed maps, seems right.\n- Does the compiler live in `src/` (run by the server on demand) or is it\n  a separate CLI tool?\n- Should the editor have a \"compile\" button that writes `output/generated.lua`\n  into the map directory?\n- For mixed-language maps, are the runner shims checked into the map's `src/`\n  or shipped globally with SoraMech?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Write the topological sort: given a box graph, produce a linear execution\n   order respecting dependency edges. (This already partially exists in the\n   executor's queue logic.)\n2. Write a Lua code emitter: for a pure-Lua map, emit `require` calls and\n   chained function calls in topo order, handling comparator branches as\n   if/elseif.\n3. Wire a \"compile\" endpoint into the HTTP server: `POST /maps/:name/compile`\n   writes `maps/:name/output/run.lua`.\n4. Add a \"compile\" button to the editor that hits the endpoint and shows the\n   generated file path.\n5. For mixed maps: emit a shell orchestration script using file-based IPC\n   instead of the Lua emitter.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — topological sort and execution model to adapt\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — box graph loading, connection traversal\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — where the compile endpoint goes\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — where the compile button goes\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — needs update once compiler exists\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — the driver model\n  this partially supersedes (drivers remain for the interpreter path)",
    "newString":"## Design constraints\n- The editor has no conception of running maps. It creates and edits box graphs.\n  The compiler is a separate CLI tool invoked outside the editor.\n- The compiler writes its output into `maps/:name/output/run.lua` (pure Lua) or\n  `maps/:name/output/run.sh` (mixed). The user invokes this directly.\n- No \"compile\" button in the editor. No \"run\" button in the editor.\n\n## Open questions\n- Primary target language: Lua first, shell script fallback for mixed maps?\n- For Lua↔C wires: emit LuaJIT FFI calls (C compiled to `.so`) or persistent\n  subprocess? FFI is faster; subprocess is simpler to generate.\n- For Lua↔Bash wires: persistent subprocess + anonymous pipe (one spawn per\n  bash runtime at program start, reused across all calls).\n- Are runner shims checked into the map's `src/` or shipped globally?\n- Should the compiler use `shm_open` shared memory for cross-language wire\n  values, or persistent subprocess + pipe? Shared memory is language-agnostic\n  and faster; pipe is simpler and works without FFI.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Write the topological sort: given a box graph, produce a linear execution\n   order respecting dependency edges. (Executor queue logic is the reference.)\n2. Write a Lua code emitter: for a pure-Lua map, emit `require` calls and\n   chained function calls in topo order, handling comparator branches as\n   if/elseif in the generated file.\n3. Write a CLI entry point: `soramech-compile.lua <map-dir>` that loads the\n   graph, runs the emitter, and writes `output/run.lua`.\n4. For mixed maps: choose IPC mechanism (FFI, shm, or persistent subprocess)\n   and emit the appropriate glue in the generated script.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — topological sort and execution model to adapt\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — box graph loading, connection traversal\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — needs update once compiler exists\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — driver model reference",

No runner management.\n-- Run: luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path  = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\"\n             .. DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\"\n             .. package.path\npackage.cpath = DIR .. \"/libs/luasocket/lib/lua/5.1/?.so;\"\n             .. package.cpath\n\nlocal server_mod = require(\"005-http-server\")\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local maps_root = args[1]\n    local port      = tonumber(args[2]) or 7700\n\n    if not maps_root then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- resolve to absolute path\n    local handle = io.popen(\"realpath \" .. maps_root)\n    maps_root = handle:read(\"*l\")\n    handle:close()\n\n    server_mod.serve(maps_root, port)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n"

        "content":"1\t-- SoraMech runner — entry point for FSM execution.\n2\t-- Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then executes it synchronously.\n3\t-- Run: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\n4\t-- Output goes to map-dir/tmp/last-run.json; logs to map-dir/tmp/logs/.\n5\t\n6\tlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n7\t\n8\tpackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n9\t               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n10\t               package.path\n11\t\n12\tlocal loader   = require(\"003-loader\")\n13\tlocal executor = require(\"004-executor\")\n14\t\n15\t-- {{{ main\n16\tlocal function main(args)\n17\t    local map_dir = args[1]\n18\t    if not map_dir then\n19\t        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n20\t        os.exit(1)\n21\t    end\n22\t\n23\t    -- if /tmp/ was cleared on reboot, the symlink target is gone; recreate it\n24\t    local rp = io.popen(\"readlink \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp\")\n25\t    local tmp_target = rp and rp:read(\"*l\")\n26\t    if rp then rp:close() end\n27\t    if tmp_target then\n28\t        os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmp_target)\n29\t    end\n30\t    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n31\t    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n32\t\n33\t    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n34\t    if not graph then\n35\t        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n36\t        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do\n37\t            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n38\t        end\n39\t        os.exit(1)\n40\t    end\n41\t\n42\t    local ok, val_errs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\n43\t    if not ok then\n44\t        io.stderr:write(\"runner: validation failed:\\n\")\n45\t        for _, e in ipairs(val_errs) do\n46\t            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n47\t        end\n48\t        os.exit(1)\n49\t    end\n50\t\n51\t    local run_ok, run_err = executor.execute(graph, map_dir)\n52\t    if not run_ok then\n53\t        io.stderr:write(\"runner: execution failed: \" .. tostring(run_err) .. \"\\n\")\n54\t        os.exit(1)\n55\t    end\n56\t\n57\t    print(\"runner: OK — \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json written\")\n58\t    os.exit(0)\n59\tend\n60\t-- }}}\n61\t\n62\tmain(arg)\n63\t",

      "content":"-- SoraMech runner — entry point for FSM execution.\n-- Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then executes it synchronously.\n-- Run: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\n-- Output goes to map-dir/tmp/last-run.json; logs to map-dir/tmp/logs/.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal loader   = require(\"003-loader\")\nlocal executor = require(\"004-executor\")\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if not map_dir then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- if /tmp/ was cleared on reboot, the symlink target is gone; recreate it\n    local rp = io.popen(\"readlink \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp\")\n    local tmp_target = rp and rp:read(\"*l\")\n    if rp then rp:close() end\n    if tmp_target then\n        os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmp_target)\n    end\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n\n    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n    if not graph then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local ok, val_errs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\n    if not ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: validation failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(val_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local run_ok, run_err = executor.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    if not run_ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: execution failed: \" .. tostring(run_err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    print(\"runner: OK — \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json written\")\n    os.exit(0)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n"
    }

    "content":"-- SoraMech interpreter runner — loads a map and executes it synchronously.\n-- This is the interpreter path. The compiler (issue 219) generates standalone\n-- output that replaces this for deployment.\n-- Run: luajit src/007-runner-main.lua <map-dir>\n-- Output goes to map-dir/tmp/last-run.json; logs to map-dir/tmp/logs/.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal loader   = require(\"003-loader\")\nlocal executor = require(\"004-executor\")\n\n-- {{{ main\nlocal function main(args)\n    local map_dir = args[1]\n    if not map_dir then\n        io.stderr:write(\"usage: luajit src/007-runner-main.lua <map-dir>\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    -- if /tmp/ was cleared on reboot, the symlink target is gone; recreate it\n    local rp = io.popen(\"readlink \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp\")\n    local tmp_target = rp and rp:read(\"*l\")\n    if rp then rp:close() end\n    if tmp_target then\n        os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. tmp_target)\n    end\n    -- ensure tmp/logs/ exists (tmp/ is the /tmp/<name>/ symlink from create-map.sh)\n    os.execute(\"mkdir -p \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/logs\")\n\n    local graph, load_errs = loader.load_map(map_dir)\n    if not graph then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: load failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(load_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local ok, val_errs = loader.validate_graph(graph)\n    if not ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: validation failed:\\n\")\n        for _, e in ipairs(val_errs) do\n            io.stderr:write(\"  \" .. e .. \"\\n\")\n        end\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    local run_ok, run_err = executor.execute(graph, map_dir)\n    if not run_ok then\n        io.stderr:write(\"runner: execution failed: \" .. tostring(run_err) .. \"\\n\")\n        os.exit(1)\n    end\n\n    print(\"runner: OK — \" .. map_dir .. \"/tmp/last-run.json written\")\n    os.exit(0)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nmain(arg)\n"
  },

    "originalFile":"# 220 — Root run script and entry point cleanup\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe project root contains `soramech-runner.lua` and `soramech-server.lua` —\nLua entry points that users are not expected to invoke directly. The intended\ninvocation path is through bash scripts in `scripts/`. There is no single\n\"start working\" command at the root.\n\n## Intended behavior\nThe project root contains exactly one user-facing script: `run`. Running it\nstarts the HTTP server and opens the editor in a browser — the complete\ndevelopment environment in one command.\n\nThe Lua entry points (`soramech-runner.lua`, `soramech-server.lua`) move to\n`src/` since they are part of the source, not user-facing commands. The\n`scripts/start-server.sh` and `scripts/open-editor.sh` update their paths\naccordingly. The root `run` script calls `scripts/start-server.sh` (background)\nthen `scripts/open-editor.sh`.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Move `soramech-server.lua` → `src/006-server-main.lua`; update\n   `scripts/start-server.sh` to reference the new path.\n2. Move `soramech-runner.lua` → `src/007-runner-main.lua`; note that the\n   compiled run script (issue 219) replaces this for user invocation.\n3. Write root `run` script: starts the server in the background, waits a\n   moment for it to bind, then opens the editor.\n4. Delete `soramech-runner.lua` and `soramech-server.lua` from root.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `soramech-server.lua` → `src/006-server-main.lua`\n- `soramech-runner.lua` → `src/007-runner-main.lua`\n- `scripts/start-server.sh` — references server entry point\n- `scripts/open-editor.sh` — editor open command\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncompleted",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

Cross-language and very fast.\n3. **Persistent subprocess + anonymous pipe:** Spawn a language runtime once per language at program start, keep it alive across all calls.     "stop_reason":"end_turn",
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"---\n\n## Option 1 — LuaJIT FFI (Lua calling C in-process)\n\nThe Foreign Function Interface in LuaJIT is a mechanism that lets Lua call C functions that live in a shared library (`.so` file) as if they were Lua functions — no subprocess, no shell, no serialization. You give LuaJIT a C declaration (`ffi.cdef[[ const char* uppercase(const char* s); ]]`), point it at a compiled shared library (`ffi.load(\"./strops.so\")`), and then `lib.uppercase(s)` is a direct in-process call. The CPU jumps from Lua bytecode execution into compiled native code, the function runs, and returns. The overhead is a few nanoseconds — comparable to calling any native function — because there's no context switch, no kernel involvement, and no copying of data between processes.\n\nThe reason this is only available for C (and languages that compile to C-compatible ABIs, like Rust with `#[no_mangle] extern \"C\"`) is that the FFI boundary requires a stable, typed calling convention. C has one. Bash does not — bash is a script interpreter, not a compiled language, so there is no `.so` to load. This is why FFI solves Lua↔C cleanly but doesn't help with Lua↔Bash at all. The tradeoff you make is that C box authors need to compile their source to a `.so` instead of an executable binary. That's a different compiler flag (`-shared -fPIC` instead of a plain link), and the box function signature changes slightly — instead of a `main()` that reads from `argv`, it's a plain function the Lua caller can name directly.\n\nFor SoraMech's compiler output, this means the generated `run.lua` would contain `ffi.load` calls and `ffi.cdef` declarations at the top, and then the body of the program would call C box functions as if they were Lua functions. The entire map runs inside a single LuaJIT process. Values are passed as LuaJIT-managed C pointers or numbers — no encoding, no decoding, no temp files. The downside is that a crash in a C box can take down the whole process (no process isolation), and writing the FFI declarations by hand is fiddly. The compiler would need to generate those declarations, which requires knowing the exact C function signature — something the box's source file already contains, but the compiler would need to parse.\n\n---\n\n## Option 2 — Shared Memory (`shm_open` + `mmap`)\n\nShared memory is a region of RAM that the OS kernel makes accessible to multiple processes simultaneously under a name. You call `shm_open(\"/soramech-wire-0\", ...)` and get back a file descriptor that refers to a block of memory — not a file on disk, but a named object managed entirely in the kernel. Then `mmap()` maps that block into your process's address space, meaning you read and write it with ordinary pointer dereferences. Any other process that calls `shm_open` with the same name gets access to the exact same physical memory. There is no copying between processes — when process A writes a value at offset 0, process B, which has the same region mapped, sees that value immediately because they're both looking at the same RAM.\n\nWhat makes this interesting for SoraMech is that every language can use it. Lua accesses it via LuaJIT FFI (calling the POSIX `shm_open` and `mmap` functions from libc). C accesses it natively with those same calls. Bash accesses the underlying file at `/dev/shm/<name>` — on Linux, the `tmpfs` filesystem that backs shared memory is exposed at that path, so a bash box can read and write values with plain file I/O (and `/dev/shm` IS RAM, so it's fast). In the compiled map, each wire between two boxes would correspond to a named shared memory slot. The compiler generates code that writes the output value into the slot and the downstream box reads from it. The process model doesn't matter — boxes could even run in parallel processes and still share the wire values correctly, with some coordination.\n\nThe drawback is complexity at the edges. Shared memory is untyped — you're writing raw bytes, so you need a serialization convention (how do you encode a Lua table? a C struct? a bash string?) and a size convention (how does the reader know how many bytes to read?). You also need to handle lifetime: who creates the segment, who destroys it, what happens if the program crashes mid-run and the segment is left behind? On Linux the segment persists until explicitly deleted or the system reboots. None of these are unsolvable — a small header in the segment can store the size and type tag — but it adds a layer that the compiler has to generate correctly for every wire.\n\n---\n\n## Option 3 — Persistent Subprocess + Anonymous Pipe\n\nAn anonymous pipe is the primitive behind every shell pipeline you've ever written. When you do `a | b` in bash, the kernel creates two file descriptors — one write end, one read end — connected through a buffer that lives entirely in kernel memory. No filesystem path, no temp file, no disk. `a` writes bytes to the write end; `b` reads bytes from the read end. The kernel manages the buffer. If `b` hasn't read yet, the buffer fills and `a` blocks. When `b` reads, the buffer drains and `a` unblocks. The data never touches the filesystem at any point — it moves from one process's virtual memory into the kernel buffer and then into the other process's virtual memory.\n\nThe \"persistent subprocess\" part is the key improvement over what the current driver system does. Right now, every box call spawns a new shell process, which loads the interpreter, sources or compiles the file, runs the function, and exits. The spawn cost dominates — on Linux, forking a process costs on the order of a millisecond, and starting a Lua interpreter costs another few milliseconds. If you have ten bash boxes and call each one once, you've spent 10+ ms just on process management. The persistent approach instead spawns ONE bash process at the start of the program, with its stdin and stdout connected to the parent via pipes that stay open. When a bash box needs to run, the parent sends a message down the pipe (\"call function `stamp` with argument `hello`\"), the persistent bash process runs it and writes the result back up the pipe, and the parent reads it. The pipe is always open; there is no spawn per call.\n\nThe protocol design is the interesting part. You need a framing convention so the parent knows where one response ends and the next begins. Length-prefix framing is the standard approach: the sender writes a 4-byte integer (the message length in bytes), then that many bytes of content. The receiver reads the 4-byte length, then reads exactly that many bytes, and knows it has the complete message. Newline-delimited framing (which is what the current stdout approach effectively uses) is simpler but breaks if the value itself contains a newline. For SoraMech, where values are JSON-encoded, a simple newline delimiter is probably safe for most cases — JSON strings can contain `\\n` escape sequences, but the encoded form is a literal backslash-n, not a real newline. Either way, the compiler would generate the framing logic as part of the persistent runtime's startup code, and box functions themselves wouldn't need to know anything about it — they'd just `echo` their output as they do now, and the persistent runtime would intercept and forward it."
      }]
  },
