It iterates\n`tests/maps/`, runs each, diffs against expected (with a normalizer\nthat drops timestamps, durations, worker indices — anything non-\ndeterministic), and reports pass/fail.\n\n### Test maps\n\nCoverage targets:\n\n| Test map                  | What it exercises                                    |\n|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| `hello`                   | Single Lua box, one input, one output                |\n| `data-only`               | Data box → call box. No inputs, just stored values   |\n| `fan-out-3`               | One output → three consumer boxes (peek, refcount)   |\n| `fan-in-iterator`         | Three producers → iterator with queued input         |\n| `comparator-routing`      | Comparator with all three branches (lt/eq/gt)        |\n| `iterator-100`            | Iterator with 100 input values, round-robin to 3 paths |\n| `multilang`               | One Lua box, one C box, one Bash box, all wired      |\n| `large-output`            | Box producing a 1 MB string (variable-size heap)     |\n| `cycle-detector-fail`     | Non-iterator cycle — load must abort                 |\n| `missing-input-fail`      | Connection references a nonexistent box — load aborts|\n| `box-error-fail`          | Box function returns nonzero — runner aborts         |\n\nThe `*-fail` tests verify error behavior — the runner is expected\nto exit nonzero with a precise error message. The driver matches\nexit code and stderr against expected.\n\n### Test driver\n\n```bash\n# scripts/run-tests.sh\nfor test_dir in tests/maps/*/; do\n    name=$(basename \"${test_dir}\")\n    expected=\"tests/expected/${name}.jsonl\"\n\n    actual=$( \"${SOURCE_DIR}/soramech-pool\" \"${test_dir}\" )\n    rc=$?\n\n    if [ -f \"${expected}.exit\" ]; then\n        # *-fail tests: assert exit code and stderr substring\n        check_failure \"${name}\" \"${rc}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\"\n    else\n        # success tests: diff normalized last-run.jsonl\n        check_success \"${name}\" \"${test_dir}/last-run.jsonl\" \"${expected}\"\n    fi\ndone\n```\n\n`normalize_jsonl` strips timestamps, durations, worker indices,\nslot ids, and task ids (all non-deterministic) and sorts events by\nevent type. The result should be deterministic across runs.\n\n### Phase 3 demo map\n\nA single map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` that\ndemonstrates everything working together:\n\n- Multiple entry-point data boxes\n- Lua, C, and Bash boxes all wired together\n- An iterator with a queued input\n- A comparator routing into different downstream paths\n- A large-output box (variable-size heap)\n- Non-trivial graph topology (≥ 10 boxes)\n\nRun with `./run.sh` from the demo directory. Prints a short summary\nof what happened (parsing the `last-run.jsonl`) so the demo is\nvisible without a viewer utility.\n\nThis satisfies the standing project rule (CLAUDE.md) that each\nphase produces a runnable demo in `issues/completed/demos/`.\n\n### Test infrastructure constraints\n\n- Tests must not depend on the editor or any HTTP server\n- Tests must not depend on internet access\n- Tests must run in under 60 seconds total on a developer machine\n- Tests must be deterministic when normalized (any\n  non-determinism is normalized out, not papered over with retries)\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Whether to log inputs/outputs by default. Useful for development,\n  noisy for production. Current decision: opt-in via env var,\n  default off.\n- Slot-event logging: also opt-in. Useful for diagnosing memory\n  issues. Off by default.\n- File format: JSON Lines is the choice. An alternative was a\n  protobuf or msgpack binary log, which is faster to write but\n  harder to inspect by hand. JSONL wins on inspectability.\n- Whether to keep timestamps as Unix epoch floats or ISO 8601\n  strings. Epoch floats are smaller and easier to diff. Stick with\n  floats.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n### Run output (Part A)\n1. Define the event struct and JSONL line format. Start with\n   `run_start`, `task_start`, `task_end`, `run_end`.\n2. Implement the MPSC ring buffer for events.\n3. Implement the writer thread: pulls from ring, serializes,\n   appends a line to the output file.\n4. Wire event emission into the pool runner: `run_start` at\n   startup, `task_start` and `task_end` in the dispatch action,\n   `run_end` after quiescence.\n5. Add the verbosity env vars and the optional event types.\n\n### Tests (Part B)\n6. Create `tests/maps/` and `tests/expected/` directory structure.\n7. Write the `hello` test as the first end-to-end smoke check.\n8. Write the test driver `scripts/run-tests.sh` and the JSONL\n   normalizer.\n9. Add tests one at a time as each runtime feature lands. The\n   `*-fail` tests can land before their corresponding successful\n   tests if the failure path is implemented first.\n10. Build the phase 3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/`\n    once the rest of phase 3 is implemented.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `scripts/run-tests.sh` — test driver (to be written)\n- `tests/maps/`, `tests/expected/` — test fixtures (to be created)\n- `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` — phase 3 demo (to be built)\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — emits run_start / run_end\n- `src/dispatch.c` — emits task_start / task_end\n- `src/slot-store.c` — emits slot_alloc / slot_free (verbose mode)\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool lifecycle\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slot events\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — task lifecycle events\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — load-time errors\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — `make test` invokes this\n- `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` — blocking semantics relevant to\n  test design\n"
  },

    "oldString":"Input values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued\ninputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the\ncounter and firing a different output path each time.\n\n---\n\n## The three IPC options",
    "newString":"Input values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued\ninputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the\ncounter and firing a different output path each time.\n\n### Blocking semantics for long-running operations\n\nThe pool's parallelism comes from running N worker threads concurrently\non N cores. Each worker is sitting inside a single dispatch task at any\ngiven moment. If a box function does something that takes a long time —\n`sleep`, blocking I/O, a synchronous network request, waiting on a long-\nrunning subprocess — **the worker thread is occupied for the full\nduration**. It cannot pick up other tasks while it waits.\n\nConcretely:\n- 16-worker pool, 1 box sleeping 10 seconds → the other 15 workers\n  continue normally.\n- 16-worker pool, 16 boxes all sleeping → all workers parked, no other\n  task runs until a sleep finishes.\n- The pool size is also the budget for \"blocking activities\". Heavy\n  use of `sleep`-style boxes means raising `SORAMECH_WORKERS`.\n\nWhy the runtime does not have a scheduler: SoraMech is deliberately not\nin the business of \"park this task and wake it at time T.\" There is no\ndelayed-spawn primitive, no timer thread, no polling loop. Adding one\nwould mean a second concurrency model alongside the pool, with its own\nsynchronization story. Instead, we lean on the pool's existing\nmechanism: a task either runs (occupying a worker) or is blocked on a\nslot waiting for a value (parked, no worker held). Long sleeps are an\n\"occupying a worker\" case.\n\nFor users who need many concurrent waits without burning workers, the\ngraph-level pattern is cooperative: split the operation into \"kick off\nthe thing\" (returns immediately) and \"check whether the thing is done\"\n(returns immediately, returns a status), and wire them through an\niterator with a queued input. The iterator polls. No individual box\nblocks for long. Each box completes quickly, freeing its worker.\n\nThis is a documented constraint, not a bug. Box authors should know\nthat an unbounded `sleep` inside a function is the equivalent of\nholding a worker hostage. The cooperative pattern is the way around\nit.\n\n---\n\n## The three IPC options",
    "userModified":false
  },

          "new_string":"Input values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued\ninputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the\ncounter and firing a different output path each time.\n\n### Blocking semantics for long-running operations\n\nThe pool's parallelism comes from running N worker threads concurrently\non N cores. Each worker is sitting inside a single dispatch task at any\ngiven moment. If a box function does something that takes a long time —\n`sleep`, blocking I/O, a synchronous network request, waiting on a long-\nrunning subprocess — **the worker thread is occupied for the full\nduration**. It cannot pick up other tasks while it waits.\n\nConcretely:\n- 16-worker pool, 1 box sleeping 10 seconds → the other 15 workers\n  continue normally.\n- 16-worker pool, 16 boxes all sleeping → all workers parked, no other\n  task runs until a sleep finishes.\n- The pool size is also the budget for \"blocking activities\". Heavy\n  use of `sleep`-style boxes means raising `SORAMECH_WORKERS`.\n\nWhy the runtime does not have a scheduler: SoraMech is deliberately not\nin the business of \"park this task and wake it at time T.\" There is no\ndelayed-spawn primitive, no timer thread, no polling loop. Adding one\nwould mean a second concurrency model alongside the pool, with its own\nsynchronization story. Instead, we lean on the pool's existing\nmechanism: a task either runs (occupying a worker) or is blocked on a\nslot waiting for a value (parked, no worker held). Long sleeps are an\n\"occupying a worker\" case.\n\nFor users who need many concurrent waits without burning workers, the\ngraph-level pattern is cooperative: split the operation into \"kick off\nthe thing\" (returns immediately) and \"check whether the thing is done\"\n(returns immediately, returns a status), and wire them through an\niterator with a queued input. The iterator polls. No individual box\nblocks for long. Each box completes quickly, freeing its worker.\n\nThis is a documented constraint, not a bug. Box authors should know\nthat an unbounded `sleep` inside a function is the equivalent of\nholding a worker hostage. The cooperative pattern is the way around\nit.\n\n---\n\n## The three IPC options",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"Input values are processed one-at-a-time in arrival order. Ten queued\ninputs means the iterator task visits the queue ten times, advancing the\ncounter and firing a different output path each time.\n\n---\n\n## The three IPC options"

        "text":"All four artifacts done.\n\n**309 — Build system & Makefile orchestration**:\n- Top-level Makefile orchestrating the runner build and per-spec builds via `$(MAKE) -C langs/<name>/`\n- Directory layout: `src/` for runner sources (split into pool-runner / slot-store / graph-loader / dispatch / spec-registry), `libs/task-pool/` and `libs/json/` vendored, `langs/<name>/` per spec, `build/` for intermediates\n- Three build modes: release (default), `DEBUG=1`, `STRICT=1`\n- Vendoring policy: copied source, no submodules, with `VENDOR.md` per directory\n- Spec discovery at runtime: runner reads `/proc/self/exe`, finds `langs/` next to itself; `SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR` overrides\n- macOS `.dylib`/`_NSGetExecutablePath` flagged in open questions\n\n**310 — Priority queue: wired in, no-op behaviorally**:\n- Every `pool_spawn` passes `SM_PRIORITY_DEFAULT = 1`; `SM_MAX_PRIORITY = 1`\n- Reasoning: future hooks become config changes, not refactors\n- Speculative future priority schema noted (cleanup at 0, urgent at 3, etc.) but explicitly out of scope\n- Implementation is essentially \"define two constants, use them everywhere\"\n\n**311 — Integration tests & run output (combined)**:\n- **Part A** — Run output: switched format to **JSON Lines** (`last-run.jsonl`), one event per line. Append-only, thread-safe with a single dedicated writer thread consuming an MPSC ring buffer. Decoupled from editor (LLM, viewer utility, test harness consumers). Default verbosity logs task lifecycle (submit/start/end); `SORAMECH_LOG_VALUES` and `SORAMECH_LOG_SLOTS` opt-in to inputs/outputs and allocator events.\n- **Part B** — Tests: 11 test maps covering hello / data-only / fan-out / fan-in / comparator / iterator-100 / multilang / large-output, plus three `*-fail` tests for cycle detection / missing input / box error. Test driver normalizes timestamps, durations, worker indices, slot/task IDs out and diffs against expected JSONL.\n- Phase 3 demo map under `issues/completed/demos/phase-3/` with multiple entry boxes, all three languages wired together, iterator + comparator + large-output box.\n\n**docs/004 update**: Added a \"Blocking semantics for long-running operations\" subsection explaining that `sleep` and blocking I/O occupy a worker thread for the duration; the cooperative graph-level pattern (split kick-off + check-done, wire through an iterator); pool size as the budget for blocking activities; explicit \"no scheduler\" stance.\n\nThat's all of phase 3 specified: 301–311."

## [1578]

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T06:08:15.564Z",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "tool_use_id":"toolu_0121Rwq7y1xdHSapveF6L8CJ",
        "content":"1\t# SoraMech — Architecture\n2\t\n3\t## Three programs, one data format\n4\t\n5\tSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\n6\tthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n7\t\n8\t```\n9\t  Browser (index.html)\n10\t       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n11\t       v\n12\t  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n13\t                               maps/<name>/\n14\t                                 boxes/\n15\t                                 data/\n16\t                                 drivers.json\n17\t                                 meta.json\n18\t                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n19\t       ^\n20\t       | reads & writes\n21\t  soramech-runner.lua\n22\t```\n23\t\n24\t### soramech-server.lua\n25\t\n26\tThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\n27\tthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\n28\tpath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\n29\tthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n30\t\n31\tStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\n32\tDefault port: 7700\n33\t\n34\tEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n35\t  GET  /maps                        list maps\n36\t  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n37\t  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n38\t  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n39\t  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n40\t  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n41\t  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n42\t  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n43\t  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n44\t  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n45\t\n46\t### soramech-runner.lua\n47\t\n48\tFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\n49\texecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n50\t`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\n51\taction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n52\t\n53\tStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n54\t\n55\tExecution steps:\n56\t  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n57\t  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n58\t  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n59\t  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n60\t  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n61\t\n62\t### index.html\n63\t\n64\tStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\n65\tTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\n66\tthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n67\t\n68\t## Map directory format\n69\t\n70\t```\n71\tmaps/<name>/\n72\t  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n73\t  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n74\t  boxes/\n75\t    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n76\t  data/\n77\t    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n78\t  drivers/\n79\t    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n80\t    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n81\t    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n82\t  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n83\t    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n84\t    logs/            — run logs\n85\t    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n86\t```\n87\t\n88\t## Box file format\n89\t\n90\t```json\n91\t{\n92\t  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n93\t  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n94\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n95\t  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n96\t  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n97\t  \"inputs\": [\n98\t    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n99\t  ],\n100\t  \"outputs\": [\n101\t    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n102\t  ],\n103\t  \"connections\": [\n104\t    {\n105\t      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n106\t      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n107\t      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n108\t      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n109\t    }\n110\t  ],\n111\t  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n112\t}\n113\t```\n114\t\n115\tFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n116\t```json\n117\t{\n118\t  \"id\": \"classify\",\n119\t  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n120\t  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n121\t  \"ports\": [\n122\t    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n123\t    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n124\t    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n125\t  ],\n126\t  \"connections\": [...]\n127\t}\n128\t```\n129\t\n130\tConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\n131\tat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n132\t\n133\t## Language driver interface\n134\t\n135\tDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n136\t\n137\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n138\t\n139\tThe single return value is encoded as a JSON value on stdout. Exit code\n140\tnon-zero = box failure. Each box has exactly one output wire — multi-return\n141\ttuples are not supported (see docs/003-driver-system.md).\n142\t\n143\t## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n144\t\n145\tThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n146\t\n147\t  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n148\t  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n149\t  3. Collect output: decode single JSON value from driver stdout\n150\t  4. Store output: held in runner memory, keyed by box id (one value per box)\n151\t  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n152\t\n153\tEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\n154\tthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\n155\tby the 3d-rts custom thread pool. The intermediate path is coroutine-based\n156\tnon-blocking I/O before the full thread pool is integrated.\n157\t\n158\t## Data files\n159\t\n160\tPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n161\t\n162\t```json\n163\t{\n164\t  \"constant\": false,\n165\t  \"fields\": {\n166\t    \"history\": [],\n167\t    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n168\t  }\n169\t}\n170\t```\n171\t\n172\tTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only.       "content":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\nthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n    logs/            — run logs\n    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n```\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"outputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"ports\": [\n    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [...]\n}\n```\n\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\nat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n\n## Language driver interface\n\nDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n\nThe single return value is encoded as a JSON value on stdout. Exit code\nnon-zero = box failure. Each box has exactly one output wire — multi-return\ntuples are not supported (see docs/003-driver-system.md).\n\n## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n\n  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n  3. Collect output: decode single JSON value from driver stdout\n  4. Store output: held in runner memory, keyed by box id (one value per box)\n  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\nby the 3d-rts custom thread pool. The intermediate path is coroutine-based\nnon-blocking I/O before the full thread pool is integrated.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only. Individual\nfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\nwhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. It survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n"
    }
  },

The browser shows the same map\n29\tvisually with correct wiring drawn.\n30\t\n31\t## Phase 2 — Concurrent execution\n32\t\n33\tGoal: boxes whose inputs are all satisfied fire concurrently.\n34\t\n35\t- Coroutine-based non-blocking executor: the ready-queue becomes a\n36\t  coroutine scheduler; boxes yield while waiting on upstream results\n37\t- Cross-language calls use Unix domain socket servers (one per language\n38\t  runtime per worker), non-blocking on the Lua side via LuaSocket\n39\t- Multiple maps running concurrently share nothing (separate processes)\n40\t- Integration path toward the 3d-rts custom thread pool: the coroutine\n41\t  scheduler and task boundary are designed to swap in the thread pool\n42\t  without changing the box execution model\n43\t\n44\t## Phase 3 — SoraMind integration\n45\t\n46\tGoal: boxes that call SoraMind inference endpoints on the Alpine cluster.\n47\t\n48\t- LLM call box type: sends a prompt, receives a completion string\n49\t- Prompt assembly: text values wired from upstream boxes, data file\n50\t  sections explicitly loaded into prompt context\n51\t- Branch box connected to an LLM classifier: \"rogue, wizard, or else\"\n52\t- Else port retry with pseudo-randomized temperature parameter\n53\t- Streaming output from SoraMind inference back to the runner\n54\t\n55\t## Phase 4 — Map-to-map calls\n56\t\n57\tGoal: a box that invokes another map as a subroutine.\n58\t\n59\t- Map call box type: specifies another map directory, passes inputs,\n60\t  receives outputs\n61\t- Maps can run concurrently with each other\n62\t- Entry/exit contracts defined in meta.json\n63\t\n64\t## Phase 5 — Remote runner\n65\t\n66\tGoal: run a map on the Alpine cluster, edit it from a laptop.\n67\t\n68\t- Runner process on a remote machine (Alpine node)\n69\t- Server on the same machine exposes map files over HTTP\n70\t- Browser editor on the laptop connects to the remote server\n71\t- Results written to remote data files, accessible via server\n72\t",

      "content":"# SoraMech — Roadmap\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation\n\nGoal: a map you can edit in the browser and execute from the terminal.\n\nAt the end of phase 1, the user can:\n- Open index.html, connect it to a running server, and see a canvas\n- Create boxes, set their ref/fn/inputs/outputs, wire them together\n- Edit branch boxes with named ports and predicates\n- Save all edits as box files on disk\n- Run `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>` and have it execute the map\n- Write a custom language driver and have the runner use it\n\nIssues:\n  101 — project scaffold and map directory format\n  102 — language driver interface\n  103 — runner: graph loader and validator\n  104 — runner: synchronous executor (task boundary)\n  105 — HTTP server: file CRUD API\n  106 — web editor: canvas and box rendering\n  107 — web editor: wiring and connection UI\n  108 — branch box and predicate routing\n  109 — data files: persistent and ephemeral storage\n  110 — phase 1 demo\n\nDemo: a small lua FSM (3-4 boxes) runs via the CLI, exercises a branch\nbox, reads a data file, writes an output.         "content":"1\t# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n2\t\n3\t## What a driver is\n4\t\n5\tA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\n6\tlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\n7\tfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n8\t\n9\tLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\n10\tcases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\n11\tdriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\n12\twrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n13\t\n14\t## Driver contract\n15\t\n16\tThe runner invokes a driver as:\n17\t\n18\t  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n19\t\n20\tArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\n21\tpassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n22\t\n23\tThe driver must:\n24\t  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n25\t  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success (string, number,\n26\t    boolean, object, or null) — one output wire per box\n27\t  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n28\t    it)\n29\t\n30\tNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, decodes the JSON\n31\tvalue, and passes it to all wired downstream inputs.\n32\t\n33\tNote: multi-output tuple returns are not supported. Each box has exactly\n34\tone output wire. If multiple values need to travel together, encode them\n35\tas a JSON object or array and decode downstream.\n36\t\n37\t## Shell script vs. binary caller\n38\t\n39\tTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n40\t\n41\t  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n42\t      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n43\t        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n44\t\n45\t  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n46\t      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n47\t        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n48\t        JSON as with a normal driver.\n49\t\n50\tBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\n51\tbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n52\t\n53\t## Built-in driver scripts\n54\t\n55\tShipped in a global drivers/ directory alongside soramech-runner.lua.\n56\tMaps can override any driver by defining the same extension in their\n57\tlocal drivers.json pointing at a map-local script.\n58\t\n59\t### drivers/lua.sh\n60\t\n61\tInvokes a single function from a Lua file using luajit. The function\n62\tmust be a module-level export (returned from the file or set in a\n63\tpackage). Args are decoded from JSON; return values are encoded to JSON.\n64\t\n65\t### drivers/c.sh\n66\t\n67\tCompiles the .c file if its mtime is newer than the cached binary in\n68\ttmp/cache/. The cache key is the source file's absolute path hashed.\n69\tInvokes the compiled binary with the args. The binary must follow the\n70\tdriver output contract (JSON to stdout).\n71\t\n72\tThe binary is expected to expose a `main`-style entry that reads args\n73\tfrom argv and writes JSON to stdout.       "totalLines":108,
      "content":"# SoraMech — Language Driver System\n\n## What a driver is\n\nA driver is a shell script. It knows how to invoke a function in one\nlanguage. The runner knows nothing about any language — it looks up the\nfile extension in drivers.json, finds the driver script, and calls it.\n\nLua and C ship with pre-written driver scripts. They are not special\ncases in the runner. They use exactly the same interface a user-written\ndriver uses. If you want to call a Haskell function or a Rust function,\nwrite a driver script and add the extension to drivers.json.\n\n## Driver contract\n\nThe runner invokes a driver as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg> ...]\n\nArguments are always strings. Structured values (tables, arrays) are\npassed as JSON strings and must be decoded by the driver before use.\n\nThe driver must:\n  - Exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure\n  - Print a single JSON value to stdout on success (string, number,\n    boolean, object, or null) — one output wire per box\n  - Print an error message to stderr on failure (runner captures and logs\n    it)\n\nNothing else. No side channels. The runner reads stdout, decodes the JSON\nvalue, and passes it to all wired downstream inputs.\n\nNote: multi-output tuple returns are not supported. Each box has exactly\none output wire. If multiple values need to travel together, encode them\nas a JSON object or array and decode downstream.\n\n## Shell script vs. binary caller\n\nTwo kinds of refs exist in a box file:\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",  \"fn\": \"trim\"\n      → source caller. runner looks up \".lua\" in drivers.json and\n        invokes the driver with file + fn + args.\n\n  \"ref\": \"src/trim.sh\"       (no \"fn\")\n      → binary caller. runner invokes the script directly with just\n        the args. The script is its own driver. Stdout is parsed as\n        JSON as with a normal driver.\n\nBinary callers include compiled binaries too: if the ref ends in a\nbinary extension or has no extension, the runner execs it directly.\n\n## Built-in driver scripts\n\nShipped in a global drivers/ directory alongside soramech-runner.lua.\nMaps can override any driver by defining the same extension in their\nlocal drivers.json pointing at a map-local script.\n\n### drivers/lua.sh\n\nInvokes a single function from a Lua file using luajit. The function\nmust be a module-level export (returned from the file or set in a\npackage). Args are decoded from JSON; return values are encoded to JSON.\n\n### drivers/c.sh\n\nCompiles the .c file if its mtime is newer than the cached binary in\ntmp/cache/. The cache key is the source file's absolute path hashed.\nInvokes the compiled binary with the args. The binary must follow the\ndriver output contract (JSON to stdout).\n\nThe binary is expected to expose a `main`-style entry that reads args\nfrom argv and writes JSON to stdout. A small C header (shipped with\nsoramech) provides helpers for this.\n\n### drivers/bash.sh\n\nInvokes a bash function defined in the .sh file by sourcing the file\nand calling the function with the args as positional parameters.\nThe function must echo a JSON value (or array) to stdout.\n\n## User-defined drivers\n\nAdd the file extension and path to the map's drivers.json:\n\n  { \".rs\": \"drivers/rust.sh\" }\n\nWrite drivers/rust.sh. It receives the same arguments as any built-in\ndriver. Compile, interpret, or delegate however the language requires.\nThe runner doesn't care.\n\n## Driver lookup order\n\n  1. Map-local drivers.json (maps/<name>/drivers.json)\n  2. Global drivers.json (alongside soramech-runner.lua)\n  3. Hard error if extension not found — no fallback, no silent skip\n\n## Passing structured values between boxes\n\nAll inter-box values are JSON at the transport layer. Inside a Lua box,\ndkjson decodes input strings to Lua tables. The driver re-encodes return\nvalues to JSON. Inside a C box, the shipped helper header decodes argv\nJSON strings to C structs and encodes results back.\n\nThis means structured values cross language boundaries cleanly: a Lua\ntable produced by one box can be consumed by a C function in the next\nbox, because both sides see JSON at the wire level.\n"
    }
  },

Strings flow between boxes like variables. History is explicit, loaded from disk only when a box needs it.\n10\t\n11\t**Three independent programs sharing a map directory:**\n12\t- `soramech-server.lua` — thin HTTP file CRUD proxy only. No runner management. Started for remote editing.\n13\t- `soramech-runner.lua` — FSM execution engine, invoked from CLI independently. Connections written to BOTH endpoint files; runner validates both ends agree — hard error if not.\n18\t- Language drivers are shell scripts. No special cases for any language in the runner. Lua/C/bash ship as pre-written driver scripts, same interface as user-defined ones.\n19\t- Driver invocation: `<driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [args...]`. Outputs JSON to stdout.\n20\t- Branch box: dedicated node kind with named output ports + always an \"else\" port. LLM-based \"else\" can be unwired (triggers retry of upstream box with pseudo-randomized retry_vary fields). Numeric/string \"else\" must be wired or map won't start.\n21\t- Data files: per-map JSON in `data/`. Section-level `constant` flag. Accessed via `libs/soramech-data.lua` library (not a built-in runner API).\n22\t- State/ephemeral: `tmp/` is a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\n8\tnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n9\t\n10\t## Intended behavior\n11\t\n12\t### Part A — text library box\n13\t`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n14\t\n15\t`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n16\t- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n17\t- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n18\t- returns a single `result` port\n19\t\n20\tThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\n21\tmodifying the source file.\n22\t\n23\t`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n24\t- `text` — the input string\n25\t- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n26\t- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n27\t\n28\tOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\n29\tparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\n30\tconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n31\t\n32\tNote: one output wire per box is a deliberate design constraint, not a missing\n33\tfeature. Positional multi-output was explicitly rejected as fragile (multiple\n34\treturn statements with the same tuple width are indistinguishable). The\n35\tcomparator (lt/eq/gt branching) is the only multi-path mechanism. Whatever the\n36\tfunction returns goes down the single output wire as one value — arrays or JSON\n37\tobjects if multiple values need to travel together.\n38\t\n39\t### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n40\t\n41\tVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\n42\tcould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\n43\teach input to mark it variadic.\n44\t\n45\t#### Data model\n46\t\n47\tThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n48\t```json\n49\t{\n50\t  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n51\t  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n52\t}\n53\t```\n54\t\n55\tSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\n56\tThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\n57\tConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n58\t\n59\tThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n60\t`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n61\t(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\n62\talready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\n63\tin a loop work without any changes.\n64\t\n65\t#### Auto-grow\n66\tWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\n67\ta new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\n68\tappears immediately as an open port.\n69\t\n70\t#### Auto-shrink\n71\tWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n72\t1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n73\t2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n74\t3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n75\t   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n76\t   - The corresponding `from_output` side on the source box (connections are stored\n77\t     in both endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n78\t4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n79\t\n80\tMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\n81\tslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\n82\ta dense, gap-free list of ports.\n83\t\n84\t## Open questions before implementing Part B\n85\t- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n86\t  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n87\t  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n88\t  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n89\t  is worth adding first.\n90\t- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n91\t  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n92\t\n93\t  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n94\t     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n95\t\n96\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n97\t1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n98\t2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n99\t3. To execute a map, the\n8\tuser must have SoraMech installed. The runner shells out to a language driver for\n9\teach box, captures stdout, and routes values to the next box. The runtime\n10\tdependency on SoraMech and the stdout-as-IPC design are both fragile.\n11\t\n12\t## Intended behavior\n13\tThe editor compiles a map into a standalone source file (or script) that runs\n14\twithout SoraMech. The box graph is an authoring artifact — the output of the\n15\teditor is a real program.\n16\t\n17\t### What the compiler produces\n18\t\n19\t**Pure Lua map** → a single `.lua` file that requires each box's source file\n20\tand chains calls directly:\n21\t```lua\n22\tlocal greet = require(\"src/greet\")\n23\tlocal write = require(\"src/write_result\")\n24\twrite.write_result(greet.hello())\n25\t```\n26\tRunnable with `luajit generated.lua`. No SoraMech, no drivers, no IPC.\n27\t\n28\t**Mixed-language map** → a shell script that invokes each box's binary or\n29\tinterpreter in sequence, passing values through named temp files rather than\n30\tstdout. Each step reads its input from a file and writes its output to a file.\n31\tThe script is self-contained and inspectable.\n32\t\n33\t**Comparator (branch) nodes** → if/elseif chains in the generated code.\n34\t\n35\t### What stays in the box JSON\n36\tCanvas positions, labels, wire layout — everything the editor needs to display\n37\tand edit the graph. The JSON is the editor's internal representation. The\n38\tcompiled output is the deliverable.\n39\t\n40\t### Why stdout-as-IPC is the wrong model\n41\tThe current runtime pipes each box's return value through stdout. Problems:\n42\t- A box that prints debug output corrupts the wire value\n43\t- Shell process overhead per box\n44\t- Can't pass binary or large values reliably\n45\t- Values are transient — can't inspect mid-run\n46\t\n47\tThe compiler eliminates IPC for same-language maps (direct function calls).\n48\tFor mixed-language maps, file-based IPC is used instead of stdout:\n49\teach wire becomes a named temp file. The generated script writes/reads\n50\texplicitly. Files persist after the run and can be inspected.\n51\t\n52\t### Language runner libraries (alternative to the current driver model)\n53\tFor multi-language support without a runtime, each language needs a small\n54\tshim that:\n55\t- reads its input value from a file path passed as argv\n56\t- calls the box function\n57\t- writes the output value to a file path passed as argv\n58\t\n59\tThe compiler generates calls to these shims. The shims are minimal (~30 lines)\n60\tand are the only per-language artifact needed. No driver contract, no stdout,\n61\tno JSON array wrapping. A new language requires only a new shim, not a new\n62\tdriver script with a parsing contract.\n63\t\n64\t### The canvas/connection relationship\n65\tThe box JSON currently stores connections in both endpoint files. The runtime\ndependency on SoraMech and the stdout-as-IPC design are both fragile.\n\n## Intended behavior\nThe editor compiles a map into a standalone source file (or script) that runs\nwithout SoraMech. Files persist after the run and can be inspected.\n\n### Language runner libraries (alternative to the current driver model)\nFor multi-language support without a runtime, each language needs a small\nshim that:\n- reads its input value from a file path passed as argv\n- calls the box function\n- writes the output value to a file path passed as argv\n\nThe compiler generates calls to these shims. A new language requires only a new shim, not a new\ndriver script with a parsing contract.\n\n### The canvas/connection relationship\nThe box JSON currently stores connections in both endpoint files. The compiler\nreads these to determine call order (topological sort). Once compiled, the\nconnections are embedded in the generated code — the JSON is not needed at\nruntime. FFI is faster; subprocess is simpler to generate.\n- For Lua↔Bash wires: persistent subprocess + anonymous pipe (one spawn per\n  bash runtime at program start, reused across all calls).\n- Are runner shims checked into the map's `src/` or shipped globally?\n- Should the compiler use `shm_open` shared memory for cross-language wire\n  values, or persistent subprocess + pipe? Shared memory is language-agnostic\n  and faster; pipe is simpler and works without FFI.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Write a CLI entry point: `soramech-compile.lua <map-dir>` that loads the\n   graph, runs the emitter, and writes `output/run.lua`.\n4.       "content":"# 222 — Compile button and assets directory\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe editor has no mechanism to trigger compilation of a map. Maps are only\nrunnable via the synchronous interpreter path (`src/007-runner-main.lua`).\nThere is no compiled artifact, no assets directory, and no binary output.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### UI: compile button\nA \"Compile\" button appears in the editor toolbar. Clicking it does nothing\nyet — it is a placeholder for the compilation pipeline (issue 219). The\nbutton is present so the UI layout is established before the backend is wired\nin.\n\nThe button label is \"Compile\". It has no loading state, no progress\nindicator, and no output for now. It simply exists in the toolbar next to\nthe existing controls.\n\n### Compiled artifacts: assets directory\nWhen compilation is eventually wired in, pressing the button triggers a\nbuild that produces a self-contained output directory alongside the map:\n\n```\nmaps/<map-name>/compiled/\n    pool-runner          ← the compiled C entry point (008-pool-runner.c)\n    src/                 ← copy of all source files used by the map\n    bin/                 ← compiled per-box binaries (C boxes → .so or binary)\n    manifest.json        ← list of every box, its language, and its binary path\n```\n\nThe compiled directory is the map's deployment artifact. Running\n`maps/<map-name>/compiled/pool-runner` executes the map using the thread\npool executor, with no dependency on the editor or the Lua interpreter path.\n\nThe `src/` copy inside `compiled/` is what the pool runner references at\nruntime — box files are not read from the map's live src/ during execution.\nThis isolates deployed maps from edits in progress.\n\n### Language-agnostic design note\nThe compile step does not treat any language as special. Each box's language\ndetermines which invocation wrapper is selected at compile time. The same\nbuild path handles a Lua box, a C box, and a Bash box without branching on\nthe language at the top level. The per-language wrapper spec (issue 303) is\nwhat parameterizes the build for each box.\n\n## Open questions\n- Should the compile button be disabled until the map has at least one entry\n  box designated? Or always enabled (and let the backend reject invalid maps)?\n- Where in the toolbar does it live — left side with map controls, or right\n  side with a \"run\" / \"export\" group?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Add a \"Compile\" button element to the editor toolbar in `assets/index.html`.\n2. Wire a click handler in `assets/js/005-app.js` that logs \"compile clicked\"\n   (placeholder). No server call yet.\n3. Leave the `compiled/` directory layout as a comment in the handler — the\n   structure is established here for when issue 219 fills it in.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `assets/index.html` — editor toolbar\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — click handler\n- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — compilation pipeline that this button triggers\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — per-language invocation wrapper spec\n  (to be written; parameterizes what goes into `compiled/bin/`)\n"

    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk format:\nthe map directory. None of the three knows about the others at runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  soramech-server.lua          [map directory]\n                               maps/<name>/\n                                 boxes/\n                                 data/\n                                 drivers.json\n                                 meta.json\n                                 tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  soramech-runner.lua\n```\n\n### soramech-server.lua\n\nThin HTTP proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and translates\nthem into file reads and writes on the map directory. No logic beyond\npath validation and basic consistency checks (e.g., reject a delete if\nthe box is still referenced by another box's connection list).\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-server.lua <maps-root> [port]`\nDefault port: 7700\n\nEndpoints (all operate on map files):\n  GET  /maps                        list maps\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes           list box IDs\n  GET  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      read box file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>      write box file\n  DELETE /maps/<name>/boxes/<id>    remove box (validates no dangling refs)\n  GET  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     read data file\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/data/<name>     write data file\n  GET  /maps/<name>/drivers         read drivers.json\n  PUT  /maps/<name>/drivers         write drivers.json\n  GET  /maps/<name>/meta            read meta.json\n\n### soramech-runner.lua\n\nFSM execution engine. Loads a map directory, validates the graph, then\nexecutes boxes in dependency order. Each box invocation is wrapped in a\n`task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` call — matching the 3d-rts thread pool's\naction chain signature for future threading compatibility.\n\nStarted with: `luajit soramech-runner.lua <map-dir>`\n\nExecution steps:\n  1. Read all box files from boxes/\n  2. Validate: all connection endpoints exist, branch \"else\" handled\n  3. Determine entry box from meta.json\n  4. Execute: resolve inputs, invoke driver, collect outputs, fire wires\n  5. On completion, write last-run snapshot to tmp/last-run.json\n\n### index.html\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to soramech-server.lua for all file operations. No run button —\nthe user starts the runner separately from the terminal.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id }\n  drivers.json       — { \".lua\": \"drivers/lua.sh\", \".c\": \"drivers/c.sh\", ... }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  drivers/\n    lua.sh           — built-in lua driver (shipped with soramech)\n    c.sh             — built-in C driver\n    bash.sh          — built-in bash driver\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — snapshot of last run (ephemeral)\n    logs/            — run logs\n    cache/           — compiled binaries (C driver cache)\n```\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"unique-string\",\n  \"label\": \"Human name\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"outputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"result\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"unique-string\",\n      \"from_output\": \"result\",\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nFor branch boxes (`\"kind\": \"branch\"`):\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"branch\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"string\" }],\n  \"ports\": [\n    { \"name\": \"rogue\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"rogue\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"wizard\", \"predicate\": { \"op\": \"eq\", \"value\": \"wizard\" } },\n    { \"name\": \"else\" }\n  ],\n  \"connections\": [...]\n}\n```\n\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner validates\nat load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard error.\n\n## Language driver interface\n\nDrivers are shell scripts. The engine invokes them as:\n\n  <driver-script> <file-path> <fn-name> <arg-count> [<arg1> <arg2> ...]\n\nThe single return value is encoded as a JSON value on stdout. Exit code\nnon-zero = box failure. Each box has exactly one output wire — multi-return\ntuples are not supported (see docs/003-driver-system.md).\n\n## Execution model (v1 — synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box call:\n\n  1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes\n  2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script\n  3. Collect output: decode single JSON value from driver stdout\n  4. Store output: held in runner memory, keyed by box id (one value per box)\n  5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now met\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nthreaded later by substituting the synchronous executor with one backed\nby the 3d-rts custom thread pool. The intermediate path is coroutine-based\nnon-blocking I/O before the full thread pool is integrated.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in data/<name>.json. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only. Individual\nfields can be flagged constant within an otherwise mutable file.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, logs, last-run snapshot) goes to tmp/,\nwhich is a symlink to /tmp/<map-name>/. It survives the run but not a\nreboot — intentionally.\n",

    "content":"# SoraMech — Architecture\n\n## Three programs, one data format\n\nSoraMech is three independent programs that share a common on-disk\nformat: the map directory. None of the three knows about the others\nat runtime.\n\n```\n  Browser (assets/index.html)\n       |  HTTP (file CRUD)\n       v\n  src/006-server-main.lua       [map directory]\n                                maps/<name>/\n                                  meta.json\n                                  boxes/\n                                  data/\n                                  src/\n                                  compiled/   (after compile button)\n                                  tmp/ -> /tmp/<name>/\n       ^\n       | reads & writes\n  Runner (one of):\n    src/007-runner-main.lua     ← phase 2, synchronous Lua interpreter\n    soramech-pool (binary)      ← phase 3, C thread pool runner\n```\n\n### src/006-server-main.lua (the editor's HTTP backend)\n\nThin file CRUD proxy. Receives JSON requests from the browser and\ntranslates them into reads and writes on the map directory. No logic\nbeyond path validation and basic consistency checks (e.g. reject a\ndelete if the box is still referenced by another box's connection\nlist).\n\nStarted with: `luajit src/006-server-main.lua [port]` (default 7700).\nThe `run` script at the project root starts the server and opens the\neditor.\n\nThe editor is editor-only — no run button, no run results display.\nThe runner is invoked separately, by command line. `last-run.jsonl`\n(issue 311) is the runner's output, consumed by external tooling, not\nby the editor.\n\n### Phase 2 runner — `src/007-runner-main.lua`\n\nSynchronous Lua interpreter. Loads a map directory, validates the\ngraph, walks boxes in dependency order, invokes language drivers per\nbox (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/c.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`). Each box\ninvocation is wrapped in a `task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` boundary that\nmatches the phase 3 thread pool's action signature.\n\nThis is the development target while the editor is being built out.\n\n### Phase 3 runner — `soramech-pool` (planned, issues 301–311)\n\nC binary that owns a 3d-rts thread pool. Each box invocation is a\npool task; worker threads run them concurrently. Language code is\ncalled through **language specs** (issue 303), shared libraries\n(`langs/<name>/spec.so`) loaded via `dlopen` at startup. Lua and C\nspecs are in-process; the Bash spec talks to a persistent subprocess\nover a Unix domain socket. Wire values live in **slots** in process\nheap memory (issue 302) — fixed-size with reference counting, plus a\nlarge-value heap for variable-size payloads.\n\nPhase 3 replaces the phase 2 runner wholesale. The synchronous path\ndoes not survive into phase 3; the editor and the map directory\nformat are unchanged across the cutover.\n\n### assets/index.html (the editor)\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to `src/006-server-main.lua` for all file operations. No run\nbutton, no compile button (yet — issue 222 adds a placeholder\n\"Compile\" button as part of phase 2). The runner is invoked\nseparately.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id, src_dirs?, lang? }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — Lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  src/\n    *.lua, *.c, *.sh — box function source files\n  compiled/          — produced by the compile button (issue 222)\n    pool-runner      — the compiled C entry point for this map\n    src/             — copy of every source file the map uses\n    bin/             — compiled .so files (C boxes via the C language spec)\n    manifest.json    — every box, its language, its compiled artifact path\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — phase 2 run snapshot (single document)\n    last-run.jsonl   — phase 3 run log (JSON Lines, issue 311)\n    logs/            — additional run logs\n```\n\nNote: the phase 2 `drivers.json` file is gone. Language selection in\nphase 2 is by file extension via the `drivers/` directory; in phase 3\nthe spec registry resolves languages by `box.lang` against\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` — no map-local config file needed.\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"trim\",\n  \"label\": \"Trim whitespace\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"lang\": \"lua\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"output_capacity\": 4096,\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"trim\",\n      \"from_branch\": null,\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nEvery box has exactly **one output wire**. There is no `outputs`\narray. Whatever the function returns travels down the single output\nwire as one value (issue 218). Multiple values that need to travel\ntogether are encoded as JSON or a struct and decoded downstream.\n\n`output_capacity` declares the maximum number of bytes the slot\nallocator (issue 302) reserves for the output. `0` (or omitted) means\nvariable-size — the slot stores a handle into the large-value heap.\n\n### Comparator boxes\nA box may carry a `comparand` field (a literal number as a string).\nWhen set, the dispatch layer compares the input value to the\ncomparand and fires only the connection whose `from_branch` matches\n`\"lt\"` / `\"eq\"` / `\"gt\"`. Comparators have no `ref` / `fn` — the\nrouting logic lives in the dispatch layer (issue 304). The output\nslot carries the input value through unchanged.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"comparand\": \"0\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"number\" }],\n  \"connections\": [\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"lt\", \"to_box\": \"negative\", \"to_input\": \"n\" },\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"eq\", \"to_box\": \"zero\",     \"to_input\": \"n\" },\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"gt\", \"to_box\": \"positive\", \"to_input\": \"n\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe earlier `branch` box kind with named ports is removed (see issue\n210). Comparator + `from_branch` is the only branching mechanism.\n\n### Iterator boxes\nA box may carry an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\noutput slot names. The dispatch layer routes the input value to the\nslot named `iterator_outputs[counter]`, advances the counter (mod\nlength), and re-spawns itself to consume the next queued input. No\nfunction is invoked — iterators are pure routing primitives. Issue\n221 covers the model; 213 covers the queued-input semantics.\n\n### Connections\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner\nvalidates at load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard\nerror.\n\n```json\n{ \"from_box\": \"...\", \"from_branch\": null|\"lt\"|\"eq\"|\"gt\"|\"<iter-slot>\",\n  \"to_box\": \"...\",   \"to_input\": \"...\" }\n```\n\n`from_branch` is `null` for plain call boxes (single output wire).\n\n## Language spec system (phase 3)\n\nEach language is a **spec** — a `.so` library at\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` that exports a `lang_spec_t` symbol with\n`init` / `teardown` / `compile` / `invoke` callbacks. The pool runner\nloads every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup via `dlopen`. The spec\ncontract (issue 303) is uniform across languages; no language is\nprivileged.\n\nReference specs ship with SoraMech:\n- `langs/lua/spec.so` — in-process via `lua_State`, no compile step (issue 306)\n- `langs/c/spec.so`   — in-process via `dlopen`, with a compile step that generates a wrapper (issue 307)\n- `langs/bash/spec.so`— out-of-process via Unix domain socket to a persistent subprocess (issue 308)\n\nA user adds a new language (Python, Rust, anything) by writing a new\nspec under `langs/<name>/`. SoraMech itself does not transpile or\nconvert source between languages.\n\nThe phase 2 `drivers/*.sh` scripts retire when phase 3 lands. They\nimplement the same idea (one process per call, stdout as channel)\nthat the spec system replaces with persistent runtimes and\nlength-prefix-framed sockets / direct function pointers.\n\n## Execution model — phase 2 (synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box\ncall:\n\n1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes.\n2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script.\n3. Collect output: decode single JSON value from driver stdout.\n4. Store output: held in runner memory, keyed by box id.\n5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now\n   met.\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nswapped for the phase 3 pool runner without changing the box\nexecution model. Phase 2 is single-threaded.\n\n## Execution model — phase 3 (thread pool)\n\nThe C pool runner owns a 3d-rts task pool with N worker threads.\nEach box invocation is a task. The dispatch layer (issue 304) is the\nworker-side action: read inputs from slots → invoke the language\nspec (or route, for comparators / iterators) → write output to a\nslot → unref consumed inputs → fire downstream connections.\n\nSlots are per-task ring buffers with reference-counted lifetime\n(issue 302). Wires hold references; producers push, consumers peek\nor pop. The wait list on each slot is the synchronization primitive\nthat parks blocked tasks until a producer fills the slot.\n\nThe pool runner has no embedded Lua. It is C from `main` down to the\nlanguage spec boundary; only inside a Lua spec's `invoke` does Lua\ncode run, and only inside that worker's `lua_State`. The graph\nloader is also pure C (issue 305) — phase 2's\n`src/003-loader.lua` retires.\n\nSee `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` for the full IPC and threading\ndiscussion, including the blocking-semantics constraint on long-\nrunning operations.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in `data/<name>.json`. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only.\nIndividual fields can be flagged constant within an otherwise\nmutable file. Accessed via `libs/soramech-data.lua`.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, run logs, the `last-run.jsonl`\noutput) goes to `tmp/`, a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Survives\nthe run but not a reboot — intentionally.\n"

No logic\nbeyond path validation and basic consistency checks (e.g. reject a\ndelete if the box is still referenced by another box's connection\nlist).\n\nStarted with: `luajit src/006-server-main.lua [port]` (default 7700).\nThe `run` script at the project root starts the server and opens the\neditor.\n\nThe editor is editor-only — no run button, no run results display.\nThe runner is invoked separately, by command line. `last-run.jsonl`\n(issue 311) is the runner's output, consumed by external tooling, not\nby the editor.\n\n### Phase 2 runner — `src/007-runner-main.lua`\n\nSynchronous Lua interpreter. Loads a map directory, validates the\ngraph, walks boxes in dependency order, invokes language drivers per\nbox (`drivers/lua.sh`, `drivers/c.sh`, `drivers/bash.sh`). Each box\ninvocation is wrapped in a `task_fn(inputs) -> outputs` boundary that\nmatches the phase 3 thread pool's action signature.\n\nThis is the development target while the editor is being built out.\n\n### Phase 3 runner — `soramech-pool` (planned, issues 301–311)\n\nC binary that owns a 3d-rts thread pool. Each box invocation is a\npool task; worker threads run them concurrently. Language code is\ncalled through **language specs** (issue 303), shared libraries\n(`langs/<name>/spec.so`) loaded via `dlopen` at startup. Lua and C\nspecs are in-process; the Bash spec talks to a persistent subprocess\nover a Unix domain socket. Wire values live in **slots** in process\nheap memory (issue 302) — fixed-size with reference counting, plus a\nlarge-value heap for variable-size payloads.\n\nPhase 3 replaces the phase 2 runner wholesale. The synchronous path\ndoes not survive into phase 3; the editor and the map directory\nformat are unchanged across the cutover.\n\n### assets/index.html (the editor)\n\nStatic HTML + vanilla JS. Infinite-scroll canvas. Box diagram editor.\nTalks to `src/006-server-main.lua` for all file operations. No run\nbutton, no compile button (yet — issue 222 adds a placeholder\n\"Compile\" button as part of phase 2). The runner is invoked\nseparately.\n\n## Map directory format\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/\n  meta.json          — { name, description, entry_box_id, src_dirs?, lang? }\n  boxes/\n    <id>.json        — one file per box (see Box file format below)\n  data/\n    <name>.json      — Lua table as JSON; sections have \"constant\": bool\n  src/\n    *.lua, *.c, *.sh — box function source files\n  compiled/          — produced by the compile button (issue 222)\n    pool-runner      — the compiled C entry point for this map\n    src/             — copy of every source file the map uses\n    bin/             — compiled .so files (C boxes via the C language spec)\n    manifest.json    — every box, its language, its compiled artifact path\n  tmp/               — symlink to /tmp/<name>/\n    last-run.json    — phase 2 run snapshot (single document)\n    last-run.jsonl   — phase 3 run log (JSON Lines, issue 311)\n    logs/            — additional run logs\n```\n\nNote: the phase 2 `drivers.json` file is gone. Language selection in\nphase 2 is by file extension via the `drivers/` directory; in phase 3\nthe spec registry resolves languages by `box.lang` against\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` — no map-local config file needed.\n\n## Box file format\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"trim\",\n  \"label\": \"Trim whitespace\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"lang\": \"lua\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/strings.lua\",\n  \"fn\": \"trim\",\n  \"inputs\": [\n    { \"name\": \"text\", \"type\": \"string\" }\n  ],\n  \"output_capacity\": 4096,\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"trim\",\n      \"from_branch\": null,\n      \"to_box\": \"next-box-id\",\n      \"to_input\": \"text\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"ui\": { \"x\": 120, \"y\": 340 }\n}\n```\n\nEvery box has exactly **one output wire**. There is no `outputs`\narray. Whatever the function returns travels down the single output\nwire as one value (issue 218). Multiple values that need to travel\ntogether are encoded as JSON or a struct and decoded downstream.\n\n`output_capacity` declares the maximum number of bytes the slot\nallocator (issue 302) reserves for the output. `0` (or omitted) means\nvariable-size — the slot stores a handle into the large-value heap.\n\n### Comparator boxes\nA box may carry a `comparand` field (a literal number as a string).\nWhen set, the dispatch layer compares the input value to the\ncomparand and fires only the connection whose `from_branch` matches\n`\"lt\"` / `\"eq\"` / `\"gt\"`. Comparators have no `ref` / `fn` — the\nrouting logic lives in the dispatch layer (issue 304). The output\nslot carries the input value through unchanged.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"classify\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"comparand\": \"0\",\n  \"inputs\": [{ \"name\": \"value\", \"type\": \"number\" }],\n  \"connections\": [\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"lt\", \"to_box\": \"negative\", \"to_input\": \"n\" },\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"eq\", \"to_box\": \"zero\",     \"to_input\": \"n\" },\n    { \"from_box\": \"classify\", \"from_branch\": \"gt\", \"to_box\": \"positive\", \"to_input\": \"n\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe earlier `branch` box kind with named ports is removed (see issue\n210). Comparator + `from_branch` is the only branching mechanism.\n\n### Iterator boxes\nA box may carry an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\noutput slot names. The dispatch layer routes the input value to the\nslot named `iterator_outputs[counter]`, advances the counter (mod\nlength), and re-spawns itself to consume the next queued input. No\nfunction is invoked — iterators are pure routing primitives. Issue\n221 covers the model; 213 covers the queued-input semantics.\n\n### Connections\nConnections are written to BOTH endpoint box files. The runner\nvalidates at load time that both ends agree. Disagreement is a hard\nerror.\n\n```json\n{ \"from_box\": \"...\", \"from_branch\": null|\"lt\"|\"eq\"|\"gt\"|\"<iter-slot>\",\n  \"to_box\": \"...\",   \"to_input\": \"...\" }\n```\n\n`from_branch` is `null` for plain call boxes (single output wire).\n\n## Language spec system (phase 3)\n\nEach language is a **spec** — a `.so` library at\n`langs/<name>/spec.so` that exports a `lang_spec_t` symbol with\n`init` / `teardown` / `compile` / `invoke` callbacks. The pool runner\nloads every `langs/*/spec.so` at startup via `dlopen`. The spec\ncontract (issue 303) is uniform across languages; no language is\nprivileged.\n\nReference specs ship with SoraMech:\n- `langs/lua/spec.so` — in-process via `lua_State`, no compile step (issue 306)\n- `langs/c/spec.so`   — in-process via `dlopen`, with a compile step that generates a wrapper (issue 307)\n- `langs/bash/spec.so`— out-of-process via Unix domain socket to a persistent subprocess (issue 308)\n\nA user adds a new language (Python, Rust, anything) by writing a new\nspec under `langs/<name>/`. SoraMech itself does not transpile or\nconvert source between languages.\n\nThe phase 2 `drivers/*.sh` scripts retire when phase 3 lands. They\nimplement the same idea (one process per call, stdout as channel)\nthat the spec system replaces with persistent runtimes and\nlength-prefix-framed sockets / direct function pointers.\n\n## Execution model — phase 2 (synchronous)\n\nThe runner walks the graph depth-first from the entry box. Each box\ncall:\n\n1. Collect inputs: read wired output values from predecessor boxes.\n2. Invoke driver: shell out to the appropriate driver script.\n3. Collect output: decode single JSON value from driver stdout.\n4. Store output: held in runner memory, keyed by box id.\n5. Fire connections: enqueue boxes whose input dependencies are now\n   met.\n\nEach step is wrapped in a `task_fn` boundary so the runner can be\nswapped for the phase 3 pool runner without changing the box\nexecution model. Phase 2 is single-threaded.\n\n## Execution model — phase 3 (thread pool)\n\nThe C pool runner owns a 3d-rts task pool with N worker threads.\nEach box invocation is a task. The dispatch layer (issue 304) is the\nworker-side action: read inputs from slots → invoke the language\nspec (or route, for comparators / iterators) → write output to a\nslot → unref consumed inputs → fire downstream connections.\n\nSlots are per-task ring buffers with reference-counted lifetime\n(issue 302). Wires hold references; producers push, consumers peek\nor pop. The wait list on each slot is the synchronization primitive\nthat parks blocked tasks until a producer fills the slot.\n\nThe pool runner has no embedded Lua. It is C from `main` down to the\nlanguage spec boundary; only inside a Lua spec's `invoke` does Lua\ncode run, and only inside that worker's `lua_State`. The graph\nloader is also pure C (issue 305) — phase 2's\n`src/003-loader.lua` retires.\n\nSee `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md` for the full IPC and threading\ndiscussion, including the blocking-semantics constraint on long-\nrunning operations.\n\n## Data files\n\nPersistent data lives in `data/<name>.json`. Format:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"constant\": false,\n  \"fields\": {\n    \"history\": [],\n    \"config\": { \"constant\": true, \"value\": { \"model\": \"soramind-default\" } }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nTop-level `constant: true` makes the whole file read-only.\nIndividual fields can be flagged constant within an otherwise\nmutable file. Accessed via `libs/soramech-data.lua`.\n\nEphemeral state (scratch tables, run logs, the `last-run.jsonl`\noutput) goes to `tmp/`, a symlink to `/tmp/<map-name>/`. Survives\nthe run but not a reboot — intentionally.\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/docs/001-architecture.md"
        },

The same `.so` will end up\n42\tloaded once per worker, since `dlopen` with the same path on the same\n43\tprocess returns a refcounted handle (the underlying code segment is\n44\tshared across all callers — the per-worker `dlopen` is just a\n45\trefcount bump after the first).\n46\t\n47\t## Compile callback\n48\t\n49\tThe C spec's `compile` callback receives the box's metadata in\n50\taddition to the source and output paths, so it knows the function's\n51\tsignature and can generate the wrapper:\n52\t\n53\t```c\n54\tint c_compile(const char *src_path, const char *out_path, const box_t *box);\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\t(This is a small extension to `lang_spec_t` in issue 303 — `compile`\n58\tgains a `box_t` pointer. Waits for the compiler, returns 0 on success, 1 on failure.\n73\t\n74\tIf the resulting `.so` is newer than the user's source and the\n75\twrapper, compile is skipped (mtime check, same as phase 2).\n76\t\n77\tThe compiler is `cc` — the system default. `gcc` on most Linux,\n78\t`clang` on macOS. No SoraMech-specific compiler dependency.\n79\t\n80\t### cflags in box JSON\n81\tThe `cflags` field on the box JSON is a string of additional compiler\n82\tflags (`-O0 -g`, `-mavx2`, etc.). The editor saves it as part of the box's JSON; reads\n85\tpreserve the field; saves write it back. Nothing overwrites it.\n86\t\n87\t## Box file convention: any C function, no boilerplate\n88\t\n89\tUsers do not write a SoraMech-specific C signature.
