        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01S56eX4vBf44MDuWNhQ4J9J",
        "content":"=== 202 ===\n# 202 — Fit-to-view on map load\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 201 (boxes must render before fit-to-view can be tested)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen a map loads, the camera stays at its default position (origin, zoom 1).\nIf boxes were placed at coordinates far from (0,0), they are off-screen and\nthe user has no way to know where to look.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nAfter `load_map()` completes, the camera is moved and zoomed so that all\nloaded boxes are visible with a small margin. If the map is empty, the camera\nresets to the origin.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js`, after populating `Boxes.boxes`, compute the bounding box\n   of all box positions (using `box.ui.x`, `box.ui.y`, and `Boxes.box_height`).\n2. Compute the center of the bounding box and set `cam.x` / `cam.y` to center\n   it in the canvas.\n3. Compute zoom so the bounding box fits within the canvas with ~60px margin\n   on each side. Clamp zoom to [0.25, 1.5].\n4. Call `Canvas.mark_dirty()`.\n5. Expose a `fit_to_view()` function from App and wire it to a toolbar button\n   so the user can re-center at any time.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — cam, mark_dirty\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — box_height, BOX_W\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map\n\n=== 203 ===\n# 203 — Map picker panel\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nOn first load, the editor shows a browser `prompt()` asking for a server URL\nand map name. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe \"switch map\" button opens this panel again without clearing all of\nlocalStorage (so the server URL is remembered).\n\nThe panel should be rendered in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content\nwhile open. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. On `DOMContentLoaded`, if `soramech_map` is not in localStorage, show the\n   picker panel instead of loading immediately.\n2. The picker panel: server URL text input + \"connect\" button. On connect,\n   call `API.list_maps()` and render a clickable list of map names.\n3. On map name click: store URL + name in localStorage, call `API.init()`,\n   close the picker, call `load_map()`.\n4. \"switch map\" button opens the picker panel without wiping the server URL.\n5. If the server is unreachable, show an error in the panel with a retry\n   option.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps()\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init(), load_map()\n- assets/index.html — sidebar and inspector panel\n\n=== 204 ===\n# 204 — Visible interaction hints\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe editor has no visible instructions. A new user sees a blank canvas with\ntwo toolbar buttons (\"reload\", \"switch map\") and no indication of what to do.\nAll interactions are undiscoverable:\n- Double-click to create a box\n- Drag an output port to draw a wire\n- Click a wire then Delete to remove it\n- Space+drag or middle-mouse to pan\n- Scroll to zoom\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe canvas shows a short hint overlay when the map is empty or when nothing\nis selected. The hint disappears once the user has at least one box on the\ncanvas. It should not reappear after that.\n\nSuggested hint text (monospace, centered, dim):\n```\ndouble-click  create box\ndrag port →   draw wire\nspace+drag    pan\nscroll        zoom\n```\n\nAdditionally, the status bar at the bottom-left should reflect the current\ninteraction state:\n- Idle with boxes: \"N boxes loaded  —  double-click to create\"\n- Wire drawing in progress: \"drawing wire — release on an input port\"\n- Box selected: \"selected: <box-id>\"\n- Wire selected: \"wire selected — Delete to remove\"\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In the render loop (`005-app.js`), if `Boxes.boxes` is empty, draw the\n   hint text centered on the canvas using the canvas 2D context (not a DOM\n   overlay, so it transforms with the camera only for pan/zoom-invariant\n   display use `ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)` before drawing).\n2. Update `status_msg` calls in mouse handlers to reflect interaction state.\n3. No persistent storage needed — the hint is purely runtime state based on\n   whether the boxes object is empty.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — render loop, mouse handlers, status_msg\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — start_frame / end_frame (canvas transform)\n\n=== 206 ===\n# 206 — Entry box designation\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe entry box is set in `meta.json` (`entry_box_id` field), but the editor\nhas no way to show which box is the entry point or to change it. The user\nmust edit meta.json directly (via the server API or a text editor) to set or\nchange the entry box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe entry box is visually distinct on the canvas — a small marker or badge\n(e.g. a filled triangle or \"▶\" label) drawn in the top-left corner of the\nbox header.\n\nAny box can be designated as the entry box from the inspector. When a box is\nselected, a \"set as entry\" button appears at the top of the inspector panel.\nClicking it updates `meta.json` via PUT /maps/:name/meta and redraws the\ncanvas.\n\nOnly one box can be the entry at a time. Changing the entry box immediately\nupdates the visual marker on the canvas.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js` `load_map()`, also fetch `meta.json` and store\n   `App.meta` (or a module-level variable) with the current entry_box_id.\n2. In `002-boxes.js` `draw_box()`, if `box.id === entry_box_id`, draw a\n   small \"▶\" badge in the header area (e.g., left of the label, in the\n   accent color for the box kind).\n3. In `004-inspector.js` `show()`, add a \"set as entry\" button at the top\n   of the inspector. On click: update the local entry_box_id, call\n   `API.put_meta({...meta, entry_box_id: box.id})`, mark canvas dirty.\n4. Pass `entry_box_id` into `draw_all` so the renderer knows which box to\n   mark.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — draw_box\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map, meta storage\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- docs/001-architecture.md — meta.json format\n\n=== 208 ===\n# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\nPort names on both input and output ports are editable text fields in the\ninspector. This is fragile — the names must match the actual function signature\nexactly or the box silently misfires at runtime.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n**Input port names are read-only.** They are derived from the function's\nparameter names when the user selects a function via the file browser (issue\n207). The inspector displays them as non-editable labels. Only the literal\nvalue field is editable per input port.\n\n**Literal values:** Each input port has an optional literal value editable\ndirectly in the inspector panel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is\nconnected to that port, the literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS\nconnected, the wire's value overwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\n**Output ports are gone.** Every call box has exactly one output wire carrying\nthe raw return value (see issue 210). The output section of the inspector is\nreplaced by the comparator toggle (see issue 210). `box.outputs` is removed\nfrom the call box schema.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant, and eliminates the class\nof runtime failures caused by mistyped port names.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — `box.inputs` port objects gain an optional `value` string\n   field. `box.outputs` is removed from call box schema (not needed; see\n   issue 210 for the single-wire model).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - `mk_port_display()` renders input port names as non-editable labels\n     (remove the name input). Each row shows the type label and a value input.\n   - On value change, update `ports[i].value` and call `save()`.\n   - Remove the output port section for call boxes entirely.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the\n   main execution loop: for every box, for every input port with a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n\n=== 212 ===\n# 212 — Editor interaction modes\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nCreating a box requires a double-click on the canvas. There is no dedicated\nwire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\ndeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\nwith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\nthe delete.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n\n**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\nnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\nto select mode automatically.\n\n**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\nWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\nany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\nexits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n\nDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\npath.\n\nBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\nstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\naffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\nlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\nclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n\nErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\ndouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n   Remove dblclick handler.\n2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n\n=== 215 ===\n# 215 — View source code of a box from the inspector and canvas context menu\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nWhen a box isn't working as expected, the user has no way to inspect its source file\nfrom within the editor. They must find the file path in the inspector's `ref` field\nand open it manually in a separate editor.\n\n## Intended behavior\nTwo entry points to view a box's source:\n- Inspector: a \"view source\" button next to the `ref` field. Clicking replaces the\n  inspector content with a read-only code view of the file.\n- Canvas right-click context menu: a \"view source\" item that does the same.\n\nThe code view shows the raw file text in a `<pre>` block with a \"← back\" button to\nreturn to the normal inspector state. No editing — read-only only for now.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add \"view source\" button next to the ref field;\n   clicking fetches the file via `API.get_extra_src_file` or `API.get_src_file` (based\n   on which group the ref belongs to) and calls a `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)`\n   helper.\n2. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas right-click context\n   menu when a box is selected; calls the same inspector view.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)` helper:\n   renders a `<pre class=\"fb-source-view\">` block, wraps in the inspector panel, adds\n   \"← back\" button.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add `.fb-source-view` CSS: monospace, small font, overflow scroll,\n   dark background.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_extra_src_file, get_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS\n\n=== 216 ===\n# 216 — Read-file box: output contents of a text or data file\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box exists for loading text from disk into the wire graph. A user who\nwants to supply file contents as input to a downstream box must write a custom\nLua function from scratch.\n\n## Intended behavior\nA reusable source file (in `libs/` or a map's `src/`) that exposes two functions:\n- `M.read_text(path)` — reads a plain text file; returns its full contents as a string.\n- `M.read_data(path, key)` — reads a dkjson data file; returns the value at `key` as\n  a string (strips metadata fields like `constant`). If `key` is nil/empty, returns\n  the full JSON-decoded table encoded back to a plain string.\n\nBoth functions output a single port (`text`) carrying the file contents. Error cases\n(file not found, bad JSON) write to stderr and return nil — the executor surfaces nil\nas an empty string on downstream inputs.\n\nThe design follows the established pattern: a regular Lua file that the user picks\nvia the file browser and wires into their map. No executor changes needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/files.lua` with `M.read_text` and `M.read_data`.\n2. Add `libs/files.lua.info.md` listing the two public functions, their inputs, and\n   their single `text` output.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box source file\n- `libs/dkjson.lua` — used by `read_data` for JSON parsing\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how call box outputs are threaded (no changes needed)",

No editing — read-only only for now.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add \"view source\" button next to the ref field;\n   clicking fetches the file via `API.get_extra_src_file` or `API.get_src_file` (based\n   on which group the ref belongs to) and calls a `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)`\n   helper.\n2. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas right-click context\n   menu when a box is selected; calls the same inspector view.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)` helper:\n   renders a `<pre class=\"fb-source-view\">` block, wraps in the inspector panel, adds\n   \"← back\" button.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add `.fb-source-view` CSS: monospace, small font, overflow scroll,\n   dark background.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_extra_src_file, get_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS\n\n=== 216 ===\n# 216 — Read-file box: output contents of a text or data file\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box exists for loading text from disk into the wire graph. A user who\nwants to supply file contents as input to a downstream box must write a custom\nLua function from scratch.\n\n## Intended behavior\nA reusable source file (in `libs/` or a map's `src/`) that exposes two functions:\n- `M.read_text(path)` — reads a plain text file; returns its full contents as a string.\n- `M.read_data(path, key)` — reads a dkjson data file; returns the value at `key` as\n  a string (strips metadata fields like `constant`). If `key` is nil/empty, returns\n  the full JSON-decoded table encoded back to a plain string.\n\nBoth functions output a single port (`text`) carrying the file contents. Error cases\n(file not found, bad JSON) write to stderr and return nil — the executor surfaces nil\nas an empty string on downstream inputs.\n\nThe design follows the established pattern: a regular Lua file that the user picks\nvia the file browser and wires into their map. No executor changes needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/files.lua` with `M.read_text` and `M.read_data`.\n2. Add `libs/files.lua.info.md` listing the two public functions, their inputs, and\n   their single `text` output.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box source file\n- `libs/dkjson.lua` — used by `read_data` for JSON parsing\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how call box outputs are threaded (no changes needed)",

        "content":"1\t# 206 — Entry box designation\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\t\n5\topen\n6\t\n7\t## Current behavior\n8\t\n9\tThe entry box is set in `meta.json` (`entry_box_id` field), but the editor\n10\thas no way to show which box is the entry point or to change it. The user\n11\tmust edit meta.json directly (via the server API or a text editor) to set or\n12\tchange the entry box.\n13\t\n14\t## Intended behavior\n15\t\n16\tThe entry box is visually distinct on the canvas — a small marker or badge\n17\t(e.g. a filled triangle or \"▶\" label) drawn in the top-left corner of the\n18\tbox header.\n19\t\n20\tAny box can be designated as the entry box from the inspector. When a box is\n21\tselected, a \"set as entry\" button appears at the top of the inspector panel.\n22\tClicking it updates `meta.json` via PUT /maps/:name/meta and redraws the\n23\tcanvas.\n24\t\n25\tOnly one box can be the entry at a time. In `005-app.js` `load_map()`, also fetch `meta.json` and store\n31\t   `App.meta` (or a module-level variable) with the current entry_box_id.\n32\t2. In `002-boxes.js` `draw_box()`, if `box.id === entry_box_id`, draw a\n33\t   small \"▶\" badge in the header area (e.g., left of the label, in the\n34\t   accent color for the box kind).\n35\t3. In `004-inspector.js` `show()`, add a \"set as entry\" button at the top\n36\t   of the inspector. On click: update the local entry_box_id, call\n37\t   `API.put_meta({...meta, entry_box_id: box.id})`, mark canvas dirty.\n38\t4. Pass `entry_box_id` into `draw_all` so the renderer knows which box to\n39\t   mark.\n40\t\n41\t## Related documents\n42\t\n43\t- assets/js/002-boxes.js — draw_box\n44\t- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show\n45\t- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map, meta storage\n46\t- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n47\t- docs/001-architecture.md — meta.json format\n48\t",

      "numLines":48,
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":48,
      "content":"# 206 — Entry box designation\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe entry box is set in `meta.json` (`entry_box_id` field), but the editor\nhas no way to show which box is the entry point or to change it. The user\nmust edit meta.json directly (via the server API or a text editor) to set or\nchange the entry box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe entry box is visually distinct on the canvas — a small marker or badge\n(e.g. a filled triangle or \"▶\" label) drawn in the top-left corner of the\nbox header.\n\nAny box can be designated as the entry box from the inspector. When a box is\nselected, a \"set as entry\" button appears at the top of the inspector panel.\nClicking it updates `meta.json` via PUT /maps/:name/meta and redraws the\ncanvas.\n\nOnly one box can be the entry at a time. Changing the entry box immediately\nupdates the visual marker on the canvas.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js` `load_map()`, also fetch `meta.json` and store\n   `App.meta` (or a module-level variable) with the current entry_box_id.\n2. In `002-boxes.js` `draw_box()`, if `box.id === entry_box_id`, draw a\n   small \"▶\" badge in the header area (e.g., left of the label, in the\n   accent color for the box kind).\n3. In `004-inspector.js` `show()`, add a \"set as entry\" button at the top\n   of the inspector. On click: update the local entry_box_id, call\n   `API.put_meta({...meta, entry_box_id: box.id})`, mark canvas dirty.\n4. Pass `entry_box_id` into `draw_all` so the renderer knows which box to\n   mark.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — draw_box\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map, meta storage\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- docs/001-architecture.md — meta.json format\n"
    }
  },

        "oldStart":2,
        "oldLines":8
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 206 — Entry box designation\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe entry box is set in `meta.json` (`entry_box_id` field), but the editor\nhas no way to show which box is the entry point or to change it. The user\nmust edit meta.json directly (via the server API or a text editor) to set or\nchange the entry box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe entry box is visually distinct on the canvas — a small marker or badge\n(e.g. a filled triangle or \"▶\" label) drawn in the top-left corner of the\nbox header.\n\nAny box can be designated as the entry box from the inspector. When a box is\nselected, a \"set as entry\" button appears at the top of the inspector panel.\nClicking it updates `meta.json` via PUT /maps/:name/meta and redraws the\ncanvas.\n\nOnly one box can be the entry at a time. Changing the entry box immediately\nupdates the visual marker on the canvas.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js` `load_map()`, also fetch `meta.json` and store\n   `App.meta` (or a module-level variable) with the current entry_box_id.\n2. In `002-boxes.js` `draw_box()`, if `box.id === entry_box_id`, draw a\n   small \"▶\" badge in the header area (e.g., left of the label, in the\n   accent color for the box kind).\n3. In `004-inspector.js` `show()`, add a \"set as entry\" button at the top\n   of the inspector. On click: update the local entry_box_id, call\n   `API.put_meta({...meta, entry_box_id: box.id})`, mark canvas dirty.\n4. Pass `entry_box_id` into `draw_all` so the renderer knows which box to\n   mark.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — draw_box\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — show\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map, meta storage\n- assets/js/003-api.js — get_meta, put_meta\n- docs/001-architecture.md — meta.json format\n",
    "oldString":"# 206 — Entry box designation\n\n## Status\n\nopen",
    "newString":"# 206 — Entry box designation\n\n## Status\n\nwon't implement\n\n## Resolution\n\nThe phase 3 runtime (issue 305) auto-detects entry boxes from graph\ntopology: any box with zero inputs, or whose inputs are all wired\nonly to `data` boxes, is an entry. A map can have any number of\nentries. There is no singular `main`. The `meta.json entry_box_id`\nfield becomes vestigial when phase 3 lands and replaces the phase 2\nsynchronous runner.\n\nImplementing the editor UI for `entry_box_id` would be throwaway\nwork — UI for a field the next runtime ignores. Closing without\nimplementation. The phase 2 runner continues to read\n`meta.json entry_box_id` as it does today; the editor simply does\nnot surface it.\n\nIf a future need surfaces for marking \"this box should fire first\"\nin the phase 3 model — for instance, a manual override of the\nauto-detected entry set — a new issue captures that requirement\nagainst the phase 3 design directly.\n\nSee:\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — entry-box detection in phase 3\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — current architecture overview",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

There is no dedicated\n10\twire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\n11\tdeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\n12\twith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\n13\tthe delete.\n14\t\n15\t## Intended behavior\n16\t\n17\tTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n18\t\n19\t**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\n20\tnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\n21\tto select mode automatically.\n22\t\n23\t**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\n24\tWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\n25\tany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\n26\texits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n27\t\n28\tDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\n29\tpath.\n30\t\n31\tBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\n32\tstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\n33\taffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\n34\tlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n35\t\n36\t## Implementation notes\n37\t\n38\t`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\n39\tclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n40\t\n41\tErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\n42\tdouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n43\t(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n44\t\n45\t## Suggested implementation steps\n46\t\n47\t1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n48\t   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n49\t   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n50\t   Remove dblclick handler.\n51\t2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n52\t   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n53\t\n54\t## Related documents\n55\t\n56\t- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n57\t- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n58\t",

      "content":"# 212 — Editor interaction modes\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nCreating a box requires a double-click on the canvas. There is no dedicated\nwire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\ndeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\nwith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\nthe delete.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n\n**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\nnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\nto select mode automatically.\n\n**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\nWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\nany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\nexits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n\nDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\npath.\n\nBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\nstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\naffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\nlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\nclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n\nErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\ndouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n   Remove dblclick handler.\n2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n"
    }

    "originalFile":"# 212 — Editor interaction modes\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nCreating a box requires a double-click on the canvas. There is no dedicated\nwire-erase tool; wires must be clicked individually to select them and then\ndeleted with the keyboard. Deleting a box that has incoming connections fails\nwith a server 409 error because the server checks for references before allowing\nthe delete.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nTwo tool-mode buttons appear in the top toolbar:\n\n**+ box**: clicking the button enters add-box mode (button highlights). The\nnext click on the canvas places a new box at the cursor position and returns\nto select mode automatically.\n\n**✕ wire**: clicking the button enters erase-wire mode (button highlights).\nWhile the mouse button is held down and the cursor is dragged across the canvas,\nany wire the cursor passes over is immediately erased. Releasing the mouse button\nexits erase-wire mode and returns to select mode.\n\nDouble-click to create a box is removed; the + box tool is the only creation\npath.\n\nBox deletion is unconditional: before calling the server DELETE, the client\nstrips all connection records referencing the box from every other box (PUT each\naffected box), then issues the DELETE. The server's 409 reference guard is no\nlonger triggered. No confirmation dialog is shown.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`set_tool_mode(mode)` exposed from the App closure manages the active button\nclass and canvas cursor ('copy' for add-box, 'cell' for erase-wire).\n\nErase-wire tracks a Set of already-queued wire signatures per drag to avoid\ndouble-deletes. Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `005-app.js` — add `tool_mode`, `set_tool_mode`, `wire_sig` helpers.\n   Update mousedown/mousemove/mouseup handlers for new modes.\n   Rewrite `delete_box` to strip references before deleting.\n   Remove dblclick handler.\n2. `index.html` — add `#tool-add-box` and `#tool-erase-wire` buttons to toolbar.\n   Add `.toolbar-btn.active` CSS.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/005-app.js — App closure, event handlers\n- assets/index.html — toolbar HTML and CSS\n",

Connections are removed from the local Boxes cache immediately\n(for instant visual feedback) and then deleted from the server asynchronously.",

No editing — read-only only for now.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add \"view source\" button next to the ref field;\n   clicking fetches the file via `API.get_extra_src_file` or `API.get_src_file` (based\n   on which group the ref belongs to) and calls a `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)`\n   helper.\n2. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas right-click context\n   menu when a box is selected; calls the same inspector view.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show_source_view(container, text, on_back)` helper:\n   renders a `<pre class=\"fb-source-view\">` block, wraps in the inspector panel, adds\n   \"← back\" button.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add `.fb-source-view` CSS: monospace, small font, overflow scroll,\n   dark background.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_extra_src_file, get_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS\n"

        "input":{
          "content":"# 215 — View source code of a box in a draggable canvas window\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nWhen a box isn't working as expected, the user has no way to inspect\nits source file from within the editor. They must find the file path\nin the inspector's `ref` field and open it manually in a separate\neditor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source-code\nwindow that appears over the canvas. Two entry points open it:\n\n1. **Inspector** — a \"view source\" button next to the `ref` field.\n2. **Canvas right-click context menu** — a \"view source\" item when\n   a box is selected.\n\nBoth call into the same window-creation helper. Multiple source\nwindows can be open at once (one per box the user opens), each\nindependently positioned.\n\n### Window behavior\n\n- **Floating**: rendered as an absolutely-positioned DOM element\n  layered above the canvas (not drawn into the canvas 2D context).\n  This makes scroll, text selection, and resize the browser's\n  native behavior — no per-frame redraw needed.\n- **Draggable**: a header bar at the top of the window is the drag\n  handle. Mousedown on the header initiates drag; mousemove updates\n  the window's `left` / `top`; mouseup releases.\n- **Confined to the canvas area**: the window cannot be dragged\n  outside the canvas's bounding box. The drag handler clamps\n  position so the window stays fully inside (drag stops at edges).\n  Resize is similarly clamped — the window cannot extend past the\n  canvas boundary.\n- **Resizable**: standard CSS `resize: both` on the inner pre or a\n  custom resize grip in the bottom-right corner. Either way, the\n  resize is constrained to keep the window inside the canvas.\n- **Scrollable**: the inner content area scrolls when the file\n  exceeds the window's dimensions. Standard browser scrolling, both\n  axes if needed.\n- **Closeable**: an `×` button in the header closes the window.\n\n### Default size\n\nComputed from the file content when the window opens:\n\n- **Width**: the average line length of the file (in characters)\n  plus three, multiplied by the monospace character width. Three\n  extra characters of breathing room past the average. Lines longer\n  than the window scroll horizontally.\n- **Height**: half the canvas's current height. The user resizes if\n  they want more or less.\n\nIf the file is empty, fall back to a sensible default (e.g. 40\ncharacters wide, half-canvas tall).\n\n### Default position\n\nCentered over the box that the user opened the source for, when\nopened from the canvas context menu. Centered on the canvas when\nopened from the inspector. If the default position would push the\nwindow outside the canvas, clamp to the nearest edge.\n\n### Window structure\n\n```\n┌─ classify.lua ──────────────────────────── × ┐  ← drag handle\n│ local M = {}                                  │\n│                                               │\n│ function M.classify(text)                     │  ← <pre> with file content\n│   if text:match(\"^%d+$\") then ...             │\n│   ...                                         │\n│ end                                           │\n│                                               │\n│ return M                                      │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                              ↘ ← resize grip\n```\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### File text fetch\nThe same API call as the existing file-browser preview (issue 207's\n`API.get_src_file`). The `ref` field on the box is the file path\nrelative to the map. Some refs may be in `libs/` (vendored or\nshipped), some in the map's `src/` — the fetch routes appropriately\n(via `API.get_src_file` for the map's source, `API.get_extra_src_file`\nfor libs/extra dirs). The existing browser does this distinction\nalready; the source viewer reuses it.\n\n### Average line length\n\n```js\nconst lines = text.split('\\n');\nconst avg = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0) / lines.length;\nconst width_chars = Math.ceil(avg) + 3;\n```\n\nMultiply by the monospace character width (computed once via a\nhidden `<span>` measurement at load, or hard-coded as ~7.2px for the\nfont we use).\n\n### Drag clamping\nOn mousemove during drag:\n\n```js\nconst canvas_rect = Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\nconst win_w = win.offsetWidth;\nconst win_h = win.offsetHeight;\nconst new_x = clamp(mouse_x - drag_offset_x, canvas_rect.left, canvas_rect.right - win_w);\nconst new_y = clamp(mouse_y - drag_offset_y, canvas_rect.top,  canvas_rect.bottom - win_h);\n```\n\nSame idea for resize: the new size cannot push the window past the\ncanvas edges given its current position.\n\n### Multiple windows\n\nEach window is a separately-tracked DOM node. A small registry\n(`open_source_windows[]`) tracks them so they can all be closed when\nthe map is switched, and so a click on a window brings it to the\nfront (z-index increment).\n\n### CSS\n\nFloating window styles are scoped under a class like\n`.source-view-window`. Header bar uses the project's existing accent\ncolor. The `<pre>` body uses the same monospace font as the\ninspector's existing port labels.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/008-source-view.js` (new) — module exposing\n   `open_source_view(box, ref, anchor_box?)`. Handles fetch, default\n   sizing, window creation, drag/resize bindings, close.\n2. `assets/index.html` — add `.source-view-window`,\n   `.source-view-header`, `.source-view-body` CSS.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add a \"view source\" button next\n   to the ref field; clicks call into the new module.\n4. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas\n   right-click context menu when a box is selected; clicks call the\n   same module with the selected box as `anchor_box`.\n5. Test: open the same source from two boxes (or twice from one\n   box) — verify two independent windows. Drag both around. Resize\n   both. Confirm clamping at canvas edges.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Bring-to-front on click: standard expectation, easy to implement\n  via a global z-counter. Worth doing.\n- Edit support: explicitly out of scope for now. Read-only. Editing\n  source files happens in the user's preferred editor on disk; the\n  viewer just shows what's there. (A future \"edit in editor\" issue\n  could add a \"save back\" capability with conflict warnings against\n  on-disk mtime.)\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_src_file, get_extra_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for the floating window\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — canvas bounding rect for clamping\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/215-view-box-source.md"
        },

Multiple source\nwindows can be open at once (one per box the user opens), each\nindependently positioned.\n\n### Window behavior\n\n- **Floating**: rendered as an absolutely-positioned DOM element\n  layered above the canvas (not drawn into the canvas 2D context).\n  This makes scroll, text selection, and resize the browser's\n  native behavior — no per-frame redraw needed.\n- **Draggable**: a header bar at the top of the window is the drag\n  handle. Mousedown on the header initiates drag; mousemove updates\n  the window's `left` / `top`; mouseup releases.\n- **Confined to the canvas area**: the window cannot be dragged\n  outside the canvas's bounding box. The drag handler clamps\n  position so the window stays fully inside (drag stops at edges).\n  Resize is similarly clamped — the window cannot extend past the\n  canvas boundary.\n- **Resizable**: standard CSS `resize: both` on the inner pre or a\n  custom resize grip in the bottom-right corner. Either way, the\n  resize is constrained to keep the window inside the canvas.\n- **Scrollable**: the inner content area scrolls when the file\n  exceeds the window's dimensions. Standard browser scrolling, both\n  axes if needed.\n- **Closeable**: an `×` button in the header closes the window.\n\n### Default size\n\nComputed from the file content when the window opens:\n\n- **Width**: the average line length of the file (in characters)\n  plus three, multiplied by the monospace character width. Three\n  extra characters of breathing room past the average. Lines longer\n  than the window scroll horizontally.\n- **Height**: half the canvas's current height. The user resizes if\n  they want more or less.\n\nIf the file is empty, fall back to a sensible default (e.g. 40\ncharacters wide, half-canvas tall).\n\n### Default position\n\nCentered over the box that the user opened the source for, when\nopened from the canvas context menu. Centered on the canvas when\nopened from the inspector. If the default position would push the\nwindow outside the canvas, clamp to the nearest edge.\n\n### Window structure\n\n```\n┌─ classify.lua ──────────────────────────── × ┐  ← drag handle\n│ local M = {}                                  │\n│                                               │\n│ function M.classify(text)                     │  ← <pre> with file content\n│   if text:match(\"^%d+$\") then ...             │\n│   ...                                         │\n│ end                                           │\n│                                               │\n│ return M                                      │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                              ↘ ← resize grip\n```\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### File text fetch\nThe same API call as the existing file-browser preview (issue 207's\n`API.get_src_file`). The `ref` field on the box is the file path\nrelative to the map. Some refs may be in `libs/` (vendored or\nshipped), some in the map's `src/` — the fetch routes appropriately\n(via `API.get_src_file` for the map's source, `API.get_extra_src_file`\nfor libs/extra dirs). The existing browser does this distinction\nalready; the source viewer reuses it.\n\n### Average line length\n\n```js\nconst lines = text.split('\\n');\nconst avg = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0) / lines.length;\nconst width_chars = Math.ceil(avg) + 3;\n```\n\nMultiply by the monospace character width (computed once via a\nhidden `<span>` measurement at load, or hard-coded as ~7.2px for the\nfont we use).\n\n### Drag clamping\nOn mousemove during drag:\n\n```js\nconst canvas_rect = Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\nconst win_w = win.offsetWidth;\nconst win_h = win.offsetHeight;\nconst new_x = clamp(mouse_x - drag_offset_x, canvas_rect.left, canvas_rect.right - win_w);\nconst new_y = clamp(mouse_y - drag_offset_y, canvas_rect.top,  canvas_rect.bottom - win_h);\n```\n\nSame idea for resize: the new size cannot push the window past the\ncanvas edges given its current position.\n\n### Multiple windows\n\nEach window is a separately-tracked DOM node. A small registry\n(`open_source_windows[]`) tracks them so they can all be closed when\nthe map is switched, and so a click on a window brings it to the\nfront (z-index increment).\n\n### CSS\n\nFloating window styles are scoped under a class like\n`.source-view-window`. Header bar uses the project's existing accent\ncolor. The `<pre>` body uses the same monospace font as the\ninspector's existing port labels.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/008-source-view.js` (new) — module exposing\n   `open_source_view(box, ref, anchor_box?)`. Handles fetch, default\n   sizing, window creation, drag/resize bindings, close.\n2. `assets/index.html` — add `.source-view-window`,\n   `.source-view-header`, `.source-view-body` CSS.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add a \"view source\" button next\n   to the ref field; clicks call into the new module.\n4. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas\n   right-click context menu when a box is selected; clicks call the\n   same module with the selected box as `anchor_box`.\n5. Test: open the same source from two boxes (or twice from one\n   box) — verify two independent windows. Drag both around. Resize\n   both. Confirm clamping at canvas edges.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Bring-to-front on click: standard expectation, easy to implement\n  via a global z-counter. Worth doing.\n- Edit support: explicitly out of scope for now. Read-only. Editing\n  source files happens in the user's preferred editor on disk; the\n  viewer just shows what's there. (A future \"edit in editor\" issue\n  could add a \"save back\" capability with conflict warnings against\n  on-disk mtime.)\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_src_file, get_extra_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for the floating window\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — canvas bounding rect for clamping\n"
  },

      "content":"// Camera state and canvas management.\n// Owns pan/zoom, the render loop, and coordinate conversion.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  const cam = { x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 };\n  let dirty = true;\n  let dragging_cam = false;\n  let drag_start   = null;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return {\n      x: (wx + cam.x) * cam.zoom,\n      y: (wy + cam.y) * cam.zoom,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return {\n      x: sx / cam.zoom - cam.x,\n      y: sy / cam.zoom - cam.y,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Called by the render loop; returns true if a redraw is needed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.scale(cam.zoom, cam.zoom);\n    ctx.translate(cam.x, cam.y);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore(); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Panning via middle-mouse or space+drag\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true; });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      dragging_cam = true;\n      drag_start   = { x: e.clientX - cam.x * cam.zoom,\n                       y: e.clientY - cam.y * cam.zoom };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (dragging_cam && drag_start) {\n      cam.x = (e.clientX - drag_start.x) / cam.zoom;\n      cam.y = (e.clientY - drag_start.y) / cam.zoom;\n      mark_dirty();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || e.button === 0) dragging_cam = false;\n  });\n\n  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  return { el, ctx, cam, world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\n           start_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos };\n})();\n"

color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n"
    }
  },

' danger' : '');\n      el.textContent = item.label;\n      el.onclick = () => { hide_ctx_menu(); item.action(); };\n      ctx_menu.appendChild(el);\n    });\n    ctx_menu.style.display = 'block';\n    ctx_menu.style.left = screen_x + 'px';\n    ctx_menu.style.top  = screen_y + 'px';\n    // keep on screen\n    const r = ctx_menu.getBoundingClientRect();\n    if (r.right  > window.innerWidth)  ctx_menu.style.left = (screen_x - r.width)  + 'px';\n    if (r.bottom > window.innerHeight) ctx_menu.style.top  = (screen_y - r.height) + 'px';\n  }\n\n  function hide_ctx_menu() { ctx_menu.style.display = 'none'; }\n\n  // hide context menu on any click or scroll\n  document.addEventListener('click',    hide_ctx_menu);\n  document.addEventListener('keydown',  e => { if (e.key === 'Escape') hide_ctx_menu(); });\n\n  // {{{ status_msg\n  window.status_msg = function(msg, level = 'info') {\n    status_el.textContent = msg;\n    status_el.className   = 'status ' + level;\n  };\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ wire_sig\n  // Stable string key for a connection record, used to prevent double-erase.\n  function wire_sig(c) {\n    return c.from_box + '|' + (c.from_branch || '') + '|' + c.to_box + '|' + c.to_input;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ set_tool_mode\n  function set_tool_mode(mode) {\n    tool_mode = mode;\n    const era_btn = document.getElementById('tool-erase-wire');\n    if (era_btn) era_btn.classList.toggle('active', mode === 'erase-wire');\n    if (mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      Canvas.el.style.cursor = 'cell';\n      status_msg('click and drag to erase wires');\n    } else {\n      Canvas.el.style.cursor = '';\n      status_msg('');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ load_map\n  async function load_map() {\n    status_msg('loading…');\n    try {\n      const ids = await API.list_boxes();\n      const fetches = ids.map(id => API.get_box(id));\n      const all = await Promise.all(fetches);\n      // mutate the existing object so the draw_all closure sees the new boxes\n      Object.keys(Boxes.boxes).forEach(k => delete Boxes.boxes[k]);\n      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ new_box_at\n  async function new_box_at(wx, wy) {\n    const id = 'box-' + Date.now().toString(36);"
    }

Empty map resets to origin/zoom 1.\n  function fit_to_view() {\n    const ids = Object.keys(Boxes.boxes);\n    if (ids.length === 0) {\n      Canvas.cam.x = 0;\n      Canvas.cam.y = 0;\n      Canvas.cam.zoom = 1;\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let min_x =  Infinity, min_y =  Infinity;\n    let max_x = -Infinity, max_y = -Infinity;\n    for (const id of ids) {\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0;\n      const y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      const w = Boxes.BOX_W;\n      const h = Boxes.box_height(b);\n      if (x      < min_x) min_x = x;\n      if (y      < min_y) min_y = y;\n      if (x + w  > max_x) max_x = x + w;\n      if (y + h  > max_y) max_y = y + h;\n    }\n\n    const margin   = 60;\n    const cw       = Canvas.el.width;\n    const ch       = Canvas.el.height;\n    const bb_w     = max_x - min_x;\n    const bb_h     = max_y - min_y;\n\n    // Pick zoom that fits the bounding box with margin on each side.\n    // A zero-sized bb (single box at zero size somehow) falls back to 1.\n    let zoom = 1;\n    if (bb_w > 0 && bb_h > 0) {\n      const zx = (cw - 2 * margin) / bb_w;\n      const zy = (ch - 2 * margin) / bb_h;\n      zoom = Math.max(0.25, Math.min(1.5, Math.min(zx, zy)));\n    }\n\n    // Center the bounding box on the canvas.\n    // world_to_screen does sx = (wx + cam.x) * zoom, so to put the bb center\n    // at the canvas center we set cam.{x,y} = canvas_half / zoom - bb_center.\n    const center_wx = min_x + bb_w / 2;\n    const center_wy = min_y + bb_h / 2;\n    Canvas.cam.zoom = zoom;\n    Canvas.cam.x    = cw / (2 * zoom) - center_wx;\n    Canvas.cam.y    = ch / (2 * zoom) - center_wy;\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "oldString":"  // {{{ load_map\n  async function load_map() {\n    status_msg('loading…');\n    try {\n      const ids = await API.list_boxes();\n      const fetches = ids.map(id => API.get_box(id));\n      const all = await Promise.all(fetches);\n      // mutate the existing object so the draw_all closure sees the new boxes\n      Object.keys(Boxes.boxes).forEach(k => delete Boxes.boxes[k]);\n      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "newString":"  // {{{ load_map\n  async function load_map() {\n    status_msg('loading…');\n    try {\n      const ids = await API.list_boxes();\n      const fetches = ids.map(id => API.get_box(id));\n      const all = await Promise.all(fetches);\n      // mutate the existing object so the draw_all closure sees the new boxes\n      Object.keys(Boxes.boxes).forEach(k => delete Boxes.boxes[k]);\n      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });\n      fit_to_view();\n      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ fit_to_view\n  // Center the camera on the bounding box of all boxes, picking a zoom\n  // that fits everything with a margin. Empty map resets to origin/zoom 1.\n  function fit_to_view() {\n    const ids = Object.keys(Boxes.boxes);\n    if (ids.length === 0) {\n      Canvas.cam.x = 0;\n      Canvas.cam.y = 0;\n      Canvas.cam.zoom = 1;\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let min_x =  Infinity, min_y =  Infinity;\n    let max_x = -Infinity, max_y = -Infinity;\n    for (const id of ids) {\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0;\n      const y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      const w = Boxes.BOX_W;\n      const h = Boxes.box_height(b);\n      if (x      < min_x) min_x = x;\n      if (y      < min_y) min_y = y;\n      if (x + w  > max_x) max_x = x + w;\n      if (y + h  > max_y) max_y = y + h;\n    }\n\n    const margin   = 60;\n    const cw       = Canvas.el.width;\n    const ch       = Canvas.el.height;\n    const bb_w     = max_x - min_x;\n    const bb_h     = max_y - min_y;\n\n    // Pick zoom that fits the bounding box with margin on each side.\n    // A zero-sized bb (single box at zero size somehow) falls back to 1.\n    let zoom = 1;\n    if (bb_w > 0 && bb_h > 0) {\n      const zx = (cw - 2 * margin) / bb_w;\n      const zy = (ch - 2 * margin) / bb_h;\n      zoom = Math.max(0.25, Math.min(1.5, Math.min(zx, zy)));\n    }\n\n    // Center the bounding box on the canvas.\n    // world_to_screen does sx = (wx + cam.x) * zoom, so to put the bb center\n    // at the canvas center we set cam.{x,y} = canvas_half / zoom - bb_center.\n    const center_wx = min_x + bb_w / 2;\n    const center_wy = min_y + bb_h / 2;\n    Canvas.cam.zoom = zoom;\n    Canvas.cam.x    = cw / (2 * zoom) - center_wx;\n    Canvas.cam.y    = ch / (2 * zoom) - center_wy;\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "userModified":false

    "originalFile":"// Camera state and canvas management.\n// Owns pan/zoom, the render loop, and coordinate conversion.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  const cam = { x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 };\n  let dirty = true;\n  let dragging_cam = false;\n  let drag_start   = null;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return {\n      x: (wx + cam.x) * cam.zoom,\n      y: (wy + cam.y) * cam.zoom,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return {\n      x: sx / cam.zoom - cam.x,\n      y: sy / cam.zoom - cam.y,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Called by the render loop; returns true if a redraw is needed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.scale(cam.zoom, cam.zoom);\n    ctx.translate(cam.x, cam.y);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore(); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Panning via middle-mouse or space+drag\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true; });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      dragging_cam = true;\n      drag_start   = { x: e.clientX - cam.x * cam.zoom,\n                       y: e.clientY - cam.y * cam.zoom };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (dragging_cam && drag_start) {\n      cam.x = (e.clientX - drag_start.x) / cam.zoom;\n      cam.y = (e.clientY - drag_start.y) / cam.zoom;\n      mark_dirty();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || e.button === 0) dragging_cam = false;\n  });\n\n  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  return { el, ctx, cam, world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\n           start_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos };\n})();\n",

      "content":"  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (tool_mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      erasing    = true;\n      erase_seen = new Set();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // select mode: existing port / box / deselect logic\n    const port = Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y);\n    if (port && port.side === 'output') {\n      drawing_wire = { from_box: port.box_id, from_port: port.port_name,\n                       cur_x: w.x, cur_y: w.y };\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const box_id = Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y);\n    if (box_id) {\n      selected_id = box_id;\n      drag_box_id = box_id;\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[box_id];\n      drag_offset = { x: w.x - (b.ui?.x ?? 0), y: w.y - (b.ui?.y ?? 0) };\n      Inspector.show(b, () => Canvas.mark_dirty(), () => delete_box(box_id));\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    selected_id = null;\n    Inspector.hide();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (erasing && tool_mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      const wire = Wires.hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n      if (wire) {\n        const sig = wire_sig(wire);\n        if (!erase_seen.has(sig)) {\n          erase_seen.add(sig);\n          // remove from local cache immediately for instant visual feedback\n          [wire.from_box, wire.to_box].forEach(id => {\n            if (Boxes.boxes[id]) {\n              Boxes.boxes[id].connections = (Boxes.boxes[id].connections || []).filter(\n                c => wire_sig(c) !== sig\n              );\n            }\n          });\n          Canvas.mark_dirty();\n          Wires.delete_connection(wire).catch(e2 =>\n            status_msg('erase error: ' + e2.message, 'error'));\n        }\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (drawing_wire) {\n      drawing_wire.cur_x = w.x;\n      drawing_wire.cur_y = w.y;\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (drag_box_id) {\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[drag_box_id];\n      if (b) {\n        b.ui = b.ui || {};\n        b.ui.x = Math.round(w.x - drag_offset.x);\n        b.ui.y = Math.round(w.y - drag_offset.y);\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();"
    }
  },

    "originalFile":"// Camera state and canvas management.\n// Owns pan/zoom, the render loop, and coordinate conversion.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  const cam = { x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 };\n  let dirty = true;\n  let dragging_cam = false;\n  let drag_start   = null;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return {\n      x: (wx + cam.x) * cam.zoom,\n      y: (wy + cam.y) * cam.zoom,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return {\n      x: sx / cam.zoom - cam.x,\n      y: sy / cam.zoom - cam.y,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Called by the render loop; returns true if a redraw is needed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.scale(cam.zoom, cam.zoom);\n    ctx.translate(cam.x, cam.y);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore(); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Panning via middle-mouse or space+drag\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true; });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      dragging_cam = true;\n      drag_start   = { x: e.clientX - cam.x * cam.zoom,\n                       y: e.clientY - cam.y * cam.zoom };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (dragging_cam && drag_start) {\n      cam.x = (e.clientX - drag_start.x) / cam.zoom;\n      cam.y = (e.clientY - drag_start.y) / cam.zoom;\n      mark_dirty();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || e.button === 0) dragging_cam = false;\n  });\n\n  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    console.log('[wheel] deltaY=', e.deltaY, ' deltaMode=', e.deltaMode, ' ctrlKey=', e.ctrlKey, ' shiftKey=', e.shiftKey);\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  return { el, ctx, cam, world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\n           start_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos };\n})();\n",
    "oldString":"  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    console.log('[wheel] deltaY=', e.deltaY, ' deltaMode=', e.deltaMode, ' ctrlKey=', e.ctrlKey, ' shiftKey=', e.shiftKey);\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });",
    "newString":"  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    const old_zoom = cam.zoom;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    console.log('[wheel] deltaY=', e.deltaY, ' factor=', factor, ' zoom:', old_zoom, '→', cam.zoom);\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  // DEBUG: trap any other writer of cam.zoom by replacing cam with a Proxy\n  const _cam_inner = cam;\n  // No proxy approach — instead, install a read-only check that warns if zoom changes outside the wheel/fit_to_view paths.\n  // We wrap with Object.defineProperty descriptors so any write logs the stack.\n  let _zoom_val = _cam_inner.zoom;\n  Object.defineProperty(_cam_inner, 'zoom', {\n    get() { return _zoom_val; },\n    set(v) {\n      if (v !== _zoom_val) {\n        console.log('[zoom set]', _zoom_val, '→', v, 'stack:', new Error().stack.split('\\n').slice(1, 5).join(' | '));\n      }\n      _zoom_val = v;\n    },\n    configurable: true,\n  });",

Then test:\n\n- Scroll up over canvas — does it zoom in (boxes get bigger)?\n- Scroll down — does it zoom out?\n- Click and drag empty canvas — does it pan? Or does nothing happen?\n- Middle-click drag, or space+left-click drag — does that pan?\n\nTell me what works and what doesn't with the rolled-back state. Once I know what yesterday's actual behavior was, I can plan fit-to-view properly without disturbing it.\n\nAlso: I'm sorry about the chaos. The defineProperty trap I added was probably what broke dragging — putting a getter/setter on a property of an object that's used in tight loops can have weird timing effects in some browsers, and it's a debugging tool I shouldn't have reached for here. I'll be more methodical next round."

    "originalFile":"// Camera state and canvas management.\n// Owns pan/zoom, the render loop, and coordinate conversion.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  const cam = { x: 0, y: 0, zoom: 1 };\n  let dirty = true;\n  let dragging_cam = false;\n  let drag_start   = null;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return {\n      x: (wx + cam.x) * cam.zoom,\n      y: (wy + cam.y) * cam.zoom,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return {\n      x: sx / cam.zoom - cam.x,\n      y: sy / cam.zoom - cam.y,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Called by the render loop; returns true if a redraw is needed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.scale(cam.zoom, cam.zoom);\n    ctx.translate(cam.x, cam.y);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore(); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Panning via middle-mouse or space+drag\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true; });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      dragging_cam = true;\n      drag_start   = { x: e.clientX - cam.x * cam.zoom,\n                       y: e.clientY - cam.y * cam.zoom };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (dragging_cam && drag_start) {\n      cam.x = (e.clientX - drag_start.x) / cam.zoom;\n      cam.y = (e.clientY - drag_start.y) / cam.zoom;\n      mark_dirty();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || e.button === 0) dragging_cam = false;\n  });\n\n  // Zoom via scroll wheel\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m   = mouse_pos(e);\n    const wbefore = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    const factor  = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    cam.zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, cam.zoom * factor));\n    const wafter = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n    cam.x += wafter.x - wbefore.x;\n    cam.y += wafter.y - wbefore.y;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  return { el, ctx, cam, world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\n           start_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos };\n})();\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/001-canvas.js",
    "content":"// Canvas viewport: pan + zoom, and the per-frame draw transform.\n//\n// Coordinate model\n//   screen pixel (sx, sy)  ←→  world point (wx, wy)\n//     sx = wx * zoom + pan_x\n//     wx = (sx - pan_x) / zoom\n//\n// `pan_x` / `pan_y` are screen-pixel offsets passed to ctx.translate\n// AFTER scaling: the world is scaled around its origin first, then the\n// result is shifted on screen. This is simpler than a world-space camera\n// because every operation is either pure-screen-pixel arithmetic\n// (panning, mouse positions) or pure-world arithmetic (drawing). They\n// only meet in two functions: world_to_screen and screen_to_world.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  let zoom  = 1;\n  let pan_x = 0;\n  let pan_y = 0;\n\n  let dirty = true;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return { x: wx * zoom + pan_x, y: wy * zoom + pan_y };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return { x: (sx - pan_x) / zoom, y: (sy - pan_y) / zoom };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Reset the transform, clear, then set up the world-drawing transform.\n  // The explicit setTransform reset is defensive — guarantees no leftover\n  // matrix state can affect this frame even if a previous restore was missed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.translate(pan_x, pan_y);\n    ctx.scale(zoom, zoom);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore();  });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      panning          = true;\n      pan_anchor_mouse = mouse_pos(e);\n      pan_anchor_pan   = { x: pan_x, y: pan_y };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (!panning) return;\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    pan_x = pan_anchor_pan.x + (m.x - pan_anchor_mouse.x);\n    pan_y = pan_anchor_pan.y + (m.y - pan_anchor_mouse.y);\n    mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { panning = false; });\n\n  // -- Zoom: scroll wheel, anchored on the cursor.\n  // The world point under the cursor stays under the cursor across zoom\n  // changes. After updating zoom we solve the screen-equation for the\n  // new pan offset:\n  //     m.x = w.x * zoom + pan_x   →   pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n\n    // Direction by sign of deltaY: up (negative) zooms in, down zooms out.\n    const factor   = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    const new_zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, zoom * factor));\n    zoom = new_zoom;\n\n    pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom;\n    pan_y = m.y - w.y * zoom;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  // Backward-compatible `cam` accessor.           "command":"git add assets/js/001-canvas.js && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nRewrite canvas viewport with screen-pixel pan and direct zoom math\n\nThe previous implementation used a world-space camera position, which\nproduced inconsistent zoom and drag behavior on at least one input\nconfiguration — scrolling could appear to invert direction, and\nnon-modifier left-click drags had been observed to perturb the zoom\nstate through a path that was hard to track down.\n\nThe replacement uses screen-pixel pan offsets and explicit\nscale-then-translate canvas transform setup. Every operation is now\neither pure screen-pixel arithmetic (panning, mouse positions, hit\ntesting) or pure world arithmetic (drawing); the two coordinate\nsystems only meet in two small conversion functions. Pan also uses\nan anchor-and-delta model so drag error cannot accumulate.\n\nPublic API is unchanged: world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\nstart_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos, and a backward-compatible cam\naccessor whose .zoom reads work as before. The .x and .y on cam now\nexpose screen-pixel pan offsets rather than the prior world-space\ncamera position, but no consumer outside this module reads those.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit canvas rewrite"
        },
        "id":"toolu_017bckzjJHtsR6FozcEDDcWW"
      }]
  },
