        "text":"Committed.\n\n**Where we are:** the canvas viewport is on a clean foundation now. Yesterday's bug is gone. Pan and zoom both behave as expected.\n\n**What this means for the UX issues:**\n- The toolbar is unchanged, so adding new buttons (fit-to-view, compile placeholder) is straightforward.\n- `Canvas.cam.zoom` still works for hit-test consumers.\n- `fit_to_view` can now be implemented cleanly in the new model: zoom+pan derived from the bounding box, no risk of creating an inconsistent camera state.\n\nWant me to take another run at **202 (fit-to-view)** with this clean foundation? Same plan as before — toolbar button, called automatically after `load_map()` — but now with simpler math: `zoom = min((cw - margin*2)/bb_w, (ch - margin*2)/bb_h)` and pan derived directly from screen-center placement, no awkward `cam.x = canvas_half/zoom - center_wx` formula.\n\nOr would you rather start with a different one to keep momentum? 222 (compile button placeholder) is even simpler — literally one button that logs \"compile clicked.\" Could land in 30 seconds."
      }]
  },

          "new_string":"  // {{{ load_map\n  async function load_map() {\n    status_msg('loading…');\n    try {\n      const ids = await API.list_boxes();\n      const fetches = ids.map(id => API.get_box(id));\n      const all = await Promise.all(fetches);\n      // mutate the existing object so the draw_all closure sees the new boxes\n      Object.keys(Boxes.boxes).forEach(k => delete Boxes.boxes[k]);\n      all.forEach(b => { Boxes.boxes[b.id] = b; });\n      fit_to_view();\n      status_msg('loaded ' + ids.length + ' boxes');\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('load error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ fit_to_view\n  // Center the camera on the bounding box of all boxes, picking a zoom\n  // that fits the whole graph with a screen-pixel margin. Empty map\n  // resets to origin / zoom 1.\n  //\n  // The new canvas viewport (001-canvas.js) uses screen-pixel pan\n  // offsets, so the math here is one-to-one with what's drawn:\n  //   sx = wx * zoom + pan_x\n  // Solve for pan so the bounding-box center lands at the canvas center.\n  function fit_to_view() {\n    const ids = Object.keys(Boxes.boxes);\n    if (ids.length === 0) {\n      Canvas.cam.zoom = 1;\n      Canvas.cam.x    = 0;\n      Canvas.cam.y    = 0;\n      return;\n    }\n\n    let min_x =  Infinity, min_y =  Infinity;\n    let max_x = -Infinity, max_y = -Infinity;\n    for (const id of ids) {\n      const b = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0;\n      const y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      const w = Boxes.BOX_W;\n      const h = Boxes.box_height(b);\n      if (x     < min_x) min_x = x;\n      if (y     < min_y) min_y = y;\n      if (x + w > max_x) max_x = x + w;\n      if (y + h > max_y) max_y = y + h;\n    }\n\n    const margin = 60;\n    const cw     = Canvas.el.width;\n    const ch     = Canvas.el.height;\n    const bb_w   = max_x - min_x;\n    const bb_h   = max_y - min_y;\n\n    // Pick the largest zoom that fits the bounding box with margin on\n    // each side. Clamp to a comfortable range.\n    let zoom = 1;\n    if (bb_w > 0 && bb_h > 0) {\n      const zx = (cw - 2 * margin) / bb_w;\n      const zy = (ch - 2 * margin) / bb_h;\n      zoom = Math.max(0.25, Math.min(1.5, Math.min(zx, zy)));\n    }\n\n    // Center the bounding box: canvas_center = bb_center * zoom + pan\n    const center_wx = min_x + bb_w / 2;\n    const center_wy = min_y + bb_h / 2;\n    Canvas.cam.zoom = zoom;\n    Canvas.cam.x    = cw / 2 - center_wx * zoom;\n    Canvas.cam.y    = ch / 2 - center_wy * zoom;\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Different code paths, different blast radius.\n\n**top-left \"switch map\"** — `onclick=\"localStorage.clear(); location.reload()\"` — wipes ALL localStorage (server URL, current map, history, whatever else) and hard-reloads the page. That drops you to the first-load flow, which currently is `prompt()` for server URL and `prompt()` for map name (the bare browser dialogs). Nuclear option.\n\n**top-right map name click** — calls `show_map_picker()`, an in-app sidebar panel that lets you pick from a list of maps without wiping anything else. Server URL and history stay intact.\n\nSo the toolbar one exists as the \"escape hatch when stuck\" — if the in-app picker breaks, you can always click the toolbar one and start fresh. But day-to-day, clicking the map name on the right is the cleaner path.\n\nThis is also exactly the territory **issue 203 (map picker panel)** is supposed to clean up. Right now: first-time load is still `prompt()`, switch-map (top-left) is `prompt()` again. 203's intent is to make even the first-time load show the same in-app panel that map-name-click shows, and at that point the top-left \"switch map\" button becomes redundant and can probably go.\n\nWant me to do 203 next? It's a natural follow-on — it kills the `prompt()` calls entirely and removes the redundant toolbar button. After that, only **204 (interaction hints)**, **208 (port literals)**, **215 (source viewer window)**, and **222 (compile button placeholder)** remain in the UX batch.\n\nOr commit 202 first and then decide?"
      }]
  },

      "numLines":40,
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":40,
      "content":"# 202 — Fit-to-view on map load\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 201 (boxes must render before fit-to-view can be tested)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen a map loads, the camera stays at its default position (origin, zoom 1).\nIf boxes were placed at coordinates far from (0,0), they are off-screen and\nthe user has no way to know where to look.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nAfter `load_map()` completes, the camera is moved and zoomed so that all\nloaded boxes are visible with a small margin. If the map is empty, the camera\nresets to the origin.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js`, after populating `Boxes.boxes`, compute the bounding box\n   of all box positions (using `box.ui.x`, `box.ui.y`, and `Boxes.box_height`).\n2. Compute the center of the bounding box and set `cam.x` / `cam.y` to center\n   it in the canvas.\n3. Compute zoom so the bounding box fits within the canvas with ~60px margin\n   on each side. Clamp zoom to [0.25, 1.5].\n4. Call `Canvas.mark_dirty()`.\n5. Expose a `fit_to_view()` function from App and wire it to a toolbar button\n   so the user can re-center at any time.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — cam, mark_dirty\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — box_height, BOX_W\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map\n"
    }

    "originalFile":"# 202 — Fit-to-view on map load\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 201 (boxes must render before fit-to-view can be tested)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen a map loads, the camera stays at its default position (origin, zoom 1).\nIf boxes were placed at coordinates far from (0,0), they are off-screen and\nthe user has no way to know where to look.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nAfter `load_map()` completes, the camera is moved and zoomed so that all\nloaded boxes are visible with a small margin. If the map is empty, the camera\nresets to the origin.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js`, after populating `Boxes.boxes`, compute the bounding box\n   of all box positions (using `box.ui.x`, `box.ui.y`, and `Boxes.box_height`).\n2. Compute the center of the bounding box and set `cam.x` / `cam.y` to center\n   it in the canvas.\n3. Compute zoom so the bounding box fits within the canvas with ~60px margin\n   on each side. Clamp zoom to [0.25, 1.5].\n4. Call `Canvas.mark_dirty()`.\n5. Expose a `fit_to_view()` function from App and wire it to a toolbar button\n   so the user can re-center at any time.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — cam, mark_dirty\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — box_height, BOX_W\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map\n",
    "oldString":"# 202 — Fit-to-view on map load\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Blockers\n\n- 201 (boxes must render before fit-to-view can be tested)\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen a map loads, the camera stays at its default position (origin, zoom 1).\nIf boxes were placed at coordinates far from (0,0), they are off-screen and\nthe user has no way to know where to look.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nAfter `load_map()` completes, the camera is moved and zoomed so that all\nloaded boxes are visible with a small margin. If the map is empty, the camera\nresets to the origin.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In `005-app.js`, after populating `Boxes.boxes`, compute the bounding box\n   of all box positions (using `box.ui.x`, `box.ui.y`, and `Boxes.box_height`).\n2. Compute the center of the bounding box and set `cam.x` / `cam.y` to center\n   it in the canvas.\n3. Compute zoom so the bounding box fits within the canvas with ~60px margin\n   on each side. Clamp zoom to [0.25, 1.5].\n4. Call `Canvas.mark_dirty()`.\n5. Expose a `fit_to_view()` function from App and wire it to a toolbar button\n   so the user can re-center at any time.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — cam, mark_dirty\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — box_height, BOX_W\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map",
    "newString":"# 202 — Fit-to-view on map load\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen a map loads, the camera stays at its default position (origin, zoom 1).\nIf boxes were placed at coordinates far from (0,0), they are off-screen and\nthe user has no way to know where to look.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nAfter `load_map()` completes, the camera is moved and zoomed so that all\nloaded boxes are visible with a small margin. If the map is empty, the camera\nresets to the origin.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`App.fit_to_view()` in `assets/js/005-app.js`:\n\n1. Walks `Boxes.boxes` to compute the bounding box (using `box.ui.x`,\n   `box.ui.y`, `Boxes.BOX_W`, `Boxes.box_height`).\n2. Picks the largest zoom that fits the bounding box with a 60px margin\n   on each side, clamped to `[0.25, 1.5]`.\n3. Sets `Canvas.cam.zoom`, `Canvas.cam.x`, `Canvas.cam.y` directly. The\n   new canvas viewport (post the rewrite at commit 8fbcbcb) uses\n   screen-pixel pan offsets, so the centering math is one line:\n   `pan = canvas_center - bb_center * zoom`.\n\n`load_map()` calls `fit_to_view()` after populating boxes. A toolbar\n\"⊡ fit\" button calls it directly so the user can re-center at any time.\n\nEmpty-map case (no boxes): resets to origin / zoom 1.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/001-canvas.js — viewport, cam getters, mark_dirty\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — BOX_W, box_height\n- assets/js/005-app.js — load_map, fit_to_view\n- assets/index.html — toolbar button",

The only way to switch maps\n11\tis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\n12\tagain with bare text inputs.\n13\t\n14\tThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n15\t\n16\t## Intended behavior\n17\t\n18\tOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\n19\tbrowser prompt) with:\n20\t- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n21\t- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n22\t- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n23\t\n24\tThe \"switch map\" button opens this panel again without clearing all of\n25\tlocalStorage (so the server URL is remembered).\n26\t\n27\tThe panel should be rendered in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content\n28\twhile open.       "content":"# 203 — Map picker panel\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nOn first load, the editor shows a browser `prompt()` asking for a server URL\nand map name. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe \"switch map\" button opens this panel again without clearing all of\nlocalStorage (so the server URL is remembered).\n\nThe panel should be rendered in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content\nwhile open. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. On `DOMContentLoaded`, if `soramech_map` is not in localStorage, show the\n   picker panel instead of loading immediately.\n2. The picker panel: server URL text input + \"connect\" button. On connect,\n   call `API.list_maps()` and render a clickable list of map names.\n3. On map name click: store URL + name in localStorage, call `API.init()`,\n   close the picker, call `load_map()`.\n4. \"switch map\" button opens the picker panel without wiping the server URL.\n5. If the server is unreachable, show an error in the panel with a retry\n   option.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps()\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init(), load_map()\n- assets/index.html — sidebar and inspector panel\n"
    }

'▶' : '▼';\n          body.style.display = collapsed ? su : null;\n          g.body.appendChild(mk_map_row(mn, sub, () => switch_to_map(su, mn)));\n        });\n        container.appendChild(g.wrap);\n      }\n\n      // available on this server\n      if (available.length > 0) {\n        const g = mk_group('on this server');\n        available.forEach(mn => {\n          g.body.appendChild(mk_map_row(mn, null, () => switch_to_map(null, mn)));\n        });\n        container.appendChild(g.wrap);\n      }\n\n      if (recent.length === 0 && available.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = 'no maps found';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n      }\n\n      // new / connect section\n      const sep = document.createElement('div');\n      sep.className   = 'section-label';\n      sep.textContent = 'open map by name';\n      sep.style.marginTop = '10px';\n      container.appendChild(sep);\n\n      const new_wrap = document.createElement('div');\n      new_wrap.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;';\n      const new_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      new_inp.type        = 'text';\n      new_inp.placeholder = 'map name';\n      new_inp.style.cssText = 'flex:1;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      const new_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      new_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n      new_btn.textContent = 'open';\n      new_btn.onclick = () => {\n        const name = new_inp.value.trim();\n        if (name) switch_to_map(null, name);\n      };\n      new_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') new_btn.click(); });\n      new_wrap.appendChild(new_inp);\n      new_wrap.appendChild(new_btn);\n      container.appendChild(new_wrap);\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}"

    "newString":"  // {{{ show_map_picker\n  // Renders the map picker into the inspector sidebar. Used for both\n  // first-time load (no map stored yet) and switching maps later. The\n  // picker carries its own server-URL input so it works before any\n  // server has been configured; nothing here reads from API state.\n  function show_map_picker() {\n    Inspector.show_content('maps', (container) => {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // -- helper: collapsible group with a body element\n      function mk_group(label) {\n        let collapsed = false;\n        const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n        const hdr  = document.createElement('div');\n        hdr.className = 'fb-group-hdr';\n        const toggle = document.createElement('span');\n        toggle.className   = 'fb-group-toggle';\n        toggle.textContent = '▼';\n        hdr.appendChild(toggle);\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n        lbl.textContent = label;\n        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n        const body = document.createElement('div');\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          collapsed = !collapsed;\n          toggle.textContent = collapsed ? '▶' : '▼';\n          body.style.display = collapsed ? 'none' : '';\n        };\n        wrap.appendChild(hdr);\n        wrap.appendChild(body);\n        return { wrap, body };\n      }\n\n      // -- helper: clickable map row\n      function mk_map_row(name, subtitle, onclick) {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.textContent = name;\n        if (subtitle) {\n          const s = document.createElement('span');\n          s.style.cssText = 'font-size:9px;color:#3a3f55;margin-left:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n          s.textContent   = subtitle;\n          row.appendChild(s);\n        }\n        row.onclick = onclick;\n        return row;\n      }\n\n      // -- server URL input row at the top.\n      // The input is the source of truth for \"which server are we\n      // talking to right now\". All map-row click handlers read from it.\n      const stored_server = localStorage.getItem('soramech_server') || 'http://localhost:7700';\n\n      const server_label = document.createElement('div');\n      server_label.className   = 'section-label';\n      server_label.textContent = 'server';\n      container.appendChild(server_label);\n\n      const server_row = document.createElement('div');\n      server_row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:4px;margin-bottom:10px;';\n      const server_inp = document.createElement('input');\n      server_inp.type        = 'text';\n      server_inp.value       = stored_server;\n      server_inp.placeholder = 'http://host:port';\n      server_inp.style.cssText = 'flex:1;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n        'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n      const connect_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      connect_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n      connect_btn.textContent = '→';\n      server_row.appendChild(server_inp);\n      server_row.appendChild(connect_btn);\n      container.appendChild(server_row);\n\n      // -- maps list section: re-renders on connect.\n      const maps_section = document.createElement('div');\n      container.appendChild(maps_section);\n\n      function current_server() { return server_inp.value.trim().replace(/\\/$/, ''); }\n\n      async function refresh_maps() {\n        maps_section.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n        const recent = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('soramech_maps_history') || '[]');\n        const url    = current_server();\n\n        let available = [];\n        let err = null;\n        if (url) {\n          try {\n            const r = await fetch(url + '/maps');\n            if (r.ok) available = await r.json();\n            else      err = 'server returned ' + r.status;\n          } catch(e) {\n            err = e.message || 'unreachable';\n          }\n        } else {\n          err = 'enter a server URL';\n        }\n\n        maps_section.innerHTML = '';\n\n        // recent group: shows every distinct (server, map) pair from\n        // history. Subtitle shows the server URL when it differs from\n        // the current picker URL.\n        if (recent.length > 0) {\n          const g = mk_group('recent');\n          recent.forEach(({ server_url: su, map_name: mn }) => {\n            const sub = su !== url ? su : null;\n            g.body.appendChild(mk_map_row(mn, sub, () => switch_to_map(su, mn)));\n          });\n          maps_section.appendChild(g.wrap);\n        }\n\n        // available group / error: maps fetched from the picker URL.\n        if (err) {\n          const note = document.createElement('div');\n          note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n          note.textContent = 'cannot reach server: ' + err;\n          maps_section.appendChild(note);\n        } else if (available.length > 0) {\n          const g = mk_group('on this server');\n          available.forEach(mn => {\n            g.body.appendChild(mk_map_row(mn, null, () => switch_to_map(url, mn)));\n          });\n          maps_section.appendChild(g.wrap);\n        } else if (recent.length === 0) {\n          const note = document.createElement('div');\n          note.className   = 'fb-note';\n          note.textContent new_inp.placeholder = 'map name';\n        new_inp.style.cssText = 'flex:1;background:#0f1117;border:1px solid #2a2f45;' +\n          'border-radius:3px;color:#e8eaf6;font-family:monospace;font-size:11px;padding:4px 6px;';\n        const new_btn = document.createElement('button');\n        new_btn.className   = 'toolbar-btn';\n        new_btn.textContent = 'open';\n        new_btn.onclick = () => {\n          const name = new_inp.value.trim();\n          if (name) switch_to_map(current_server(), name);\n        };\n        new_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter') new_btn.click(); });\n        new_wrap.appendChild(new_inp);\n        new_wrap.appendChild(new_btn);\n        maps_section.appendChild(new_wrap);\n      }\n\n      connect_btn.onclick = refresh_maps;\n      server_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n        if (e.key === 'Enter') refresh_maps();\n      });\n\n      refresh_maps();\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "snippet":"1\t- all scripts should be written assuming they are to be run from any directory. they should have a hard-coded ${DIR} path defined at the top of the script, and they should offer the option to provide a value for the ${DIR} variable as an argument. All paths in the program should be relative to the ${DIR} variable.\n2\t-are paid all functions should use vimfolds to collapse functionality. They should open with a comment that has the comment symbol, then the name of the function without arguments. On the next line, the function should be defined with arguments. Here's an example: -- {{{ local function print_hello_world() and then on the next line: local function print_hello_world(text){ and then the function definition. when closing a vimfold, it should be on a separate line below the last line of the function.\n3\t- to create a project, mkdir docs notes src libs assets issues\n4\t- to initialize a project, read the vision document located in prj-dir/notes/vision - then create documentation related to it in prj-dir/docs/ - then repeat, then repeat. Ensure there is a roadmap document split into phases. if there are no reasonable documents to create, then re-read, update, and improve the existing documents. Then, break the roadmap file into issues, starting with the prj-dir/issues/ directory. be as specific as need be. ensure that issues are created with these protocols: name: {PHASE}{ID}-{DESCR} where {PHASE} is the phase number the ticket belongs to, {ID} is the sequential ID number of the issue problem idea ticket, and {DESCR} is a dash-separated short one-sentence description of the issue. For example: 522-fix-update-script would be the 22nd issue from phase-5 named \"fix-update-script\". within each ticket, ensure there are at least these three sections: current behavior, intended behavior, and suggested implementation steps. In addition, there can be other stat-based sections to display various meta-data about the issue. There may also be a related documents or tools section. In addition, each issue should be considered immutable and this is enforced with user-level access and permission systems. It is necessary to preserve consent of access to imagination. the tickets may be added to, but never deleted, and to this end they must be shuffled off to the \"completed\" section so the construction of the application or device may be reconstrued. Ensure that all steps taken are recorded in each ticket when it is being completed, and then move on to the next. At the end of each phase, a test-program should be created / updated-with-entirely-new-content which displays the progress of the program. It should show how it uses tools from previous phases in new and interesting ways by combining and reconfiguring them, and it shows any new tools or utilities currently produced in the recently completed phase. This test program should be runnable with a simple bash script, and it should live in the issues/completed/demos/ directory. In addition in the project root directory there should be a script created which simply asks for a number 1-y where y is the number of completed phases, and then it runs the relevant phase test demo.\n5\t- mono-repo utilities can be found in the docs/ directory. If not found, create a symlink to ../delta-version/docs/delta-guide.md in the docs/ directory.\n6\t- when working on a large feature, the issue ticket may be broken into sub-issues. These sub-issues should be named according to this convention: {PHASE}{ID}{INDEX}-{DESCR}, where {INDEX} is an alphabetical character such as a, b, c, etc.\n7\t- for every implemented change to the project, there must always be an issue file. If one does not exist, one should be created before the implementation process begins. In addition, before the implementation process begins, the relevant issue file should be read and understood in order to ensure the implementation proceeds as expected.\n8\t- prefer error messages and breaking functionality over fallbacks. Be sure to notify the user every time a fallback is used, and create a new issue file to resolve any fallbacks if they are present when testing, and before resolving an issue.\n9\t- every time an issue file is completed, the /issues/phase-X-progress.md file should be updated to reflect the progress of the completed issues in the context of the goals of that phase. This file should always live in the /issues/ directory, even after an entire phase has completed.\n10\t- when an issue is completed, all relevant issues should be updated to reflect the new current behavior and lessons learned if necessary. The completed issue should be moved to the /issues/completed/ directory.\n11\t- when an issue is completed, any version control systems present should be updated with a new commit.\n12\t- every time a new document is created, it should be added to the tree-hierarchy structure present in /docs/table-of-contents.md. Issue files and source code don't need to be included in the table of contents, only files in docs/ and notes/ and other similar directories.\n13\t- phase demos should focus on demonstrating relevant statistics or datapoints, and less on describing the functionality. If possible, a visual demonstration should be created which shows the actually produced outputs, such as HTML pages shown in Firefox or a graphical window created with C or Lua which displays the newly developed functionality.\n14\t- all script files should have a comment at the top which explains what they are and a general description of how they do it. \"general description\" meaning, fit for a CEO or general.\n15\t- after completing an issue file, a git commit should be made.\n16\t- if you need to diagnose a git-style memory bug, complete with change history (primarily stored through issue notes) first look to the delta version project. you will find it in the list of projects.\n17\t- if you need to write a long test script, write a temporary script. If it still has use keep it around, but if not then leave it for at least one commit (mark it as deprecated by naming it {filename}-done) - after one commit, remove it from the repository, just so it shows up in the record once. But only if there's no anticipated future use. Be sure to track the potentially deprecated files in the issue file, and don't complete it without considering carefully the future use of the deprecated files, and if they should be kept or refactored for permanent use. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe map-name label in the sidebar header opens the same panel for switching\nmaps without clearing localStorage. The redundant top-left \"switch map\"\ntoolbar button (which used to wipe localStorage and reload) is removed.\n\nThe panel renders in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content while\nopen. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`show_map_picker` in `assets/js/005-app.js`:\n- Carries its own server-URL `<input>` at the top of the panel — the picker\n  reads from this input rather than from API state, so it works on\n  first-time load when nothing is stored yet.\n- `→` button next to the URL input (and the Enter key in the input) refreshes\n  the maps list.\n- Maps fetched via direct `fetch(url + '/maps')`, bypassing `API.list_maps`\n  so it works before `API.init()` has been called.\n- Recent maps come from `localStorage.soramech_maps_history`. Each row's\n  click handler captures its own `(server_url, map_name)` so users can jump\n  back to a different server entirely.\n- \"On this server\" group lists what the picker URL serves. Click handlers\n  pass the picker URL into `switch_to_map`.\n- \"Open map by name\" input/button at the bottom for typing a name directly.\n- Errors (server unreachable, non-200) render inline as `cannot reach\n  server: <reason>`.\n\n`init` in `assets/js/005-app.js`:\n- If `soramech_server` and `soramech_map` are both in localStorage, the\n  normal flow runs (`API.init` + `load_map`).\n- Otherwise, the picker is shown immediately. Selection inside the picker\n  saves to localStorage and calls `switch_to_map`, which then calls\n  `load_map`. No `prompt()` anywhere.\n- The `requestAnimationFrame(render)` loop starts in either case so the\n  canvas is live the moment the picker is up.\n\nThe top-left `switch map` toolbar button is removed. The map-label in the\nsidebar header is the only switch-maps entry point now.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps (no longer used for first-time fetch)\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init, load_map, show_map_picker, switch_to_map\n- assets/index.html — sidebar, inspector panel, toolbar",

          "old_string":"# 203 — Map picker panel\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nOn first load, the editor shows a browser `prompt()` asking for a server URL\nand map name. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe \"switch map\" button opens this panel again without clearing all of\nlocalStorage (so the server URL is remembered).\n\nThe panel should be rendered in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content\nwhile open. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. On map name click: store URL + name in localStorage, call `API.init()`,\n   close the picker, call `load_map()`.\n4. \"switch map\" button opens the picker panel without wiping the server URL.\n5. If the server is unreachable, show an error in the panel with a retry\n   option.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps()\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init(), load_map()\n- assets/index.html — sidebar and inspector panel"

On map name click: store URL + name in localStorage, call `API.init()`,\n   close the picker, call `load_map()`.\n4. \"switch map\" button opens the picker panel without wiping the server URL.\n5. If the server is unreachable, show an error in the panel with a retry\n   option.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps()\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init(), load_map()\n- assets/index.html — sidebar and inspector panel\n",
    "oldString":"# 203 — Map picker panel\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nOn first load, the editor shows a browser `prompt()` asking for a server URL\nand map name. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe \"switch map\" button opens this panel again without clearing all of\nlocalStorage (so the server URL is remembered).\n\nThe panel should be rendered in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content\nwhile open. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. On `DOMContentLoaded`, if `soramech_map` is not in localStorage, show the\n   picker panel instead of loading immediately.\n2. The picker panel: server URL text input + \"connect\" button. On connect,\n   call `API.list_maps()` and render a clickable list of map names.\n3. On map name click: store URL + name in localStorage, call `API.init()`,\n   close the picker, call `load_map()`.\n4. \"switch map\" button opens the picker panel without wiping the server URL.\n5. If the server is unreachable, show an error in the panel with a retry\n   option.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps()\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init(), load_map()\n- assets/index.html — sidebar and inspector panel",
    "newString":"# 203 — Map picker panel\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\n\nOn first load, the editor shows a browser `prompt()` asking for a server URL\nand map name. These are stored in localStorage. The only way to switch maps\nis to click \"switch map\", which clears localStorage and reloads — prompting\nagain with bare text inputs.\n\nThis is friction every time you want to work on a different map.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nOn load, if no server URL or map name is stored, show a proper panel (not a\nbrowser prompt) with:\n- A text input for the server URL (default: http://localhost:7700)\n- A list of available maps fetched from GET /maps on the server\n- Clicking a map name connects to it and loads the editor\n\nThe map-name label in the sidebar header opens the same panel for switching\nmaps without clearing localStorage. The redundant top-left \"switch map\"\ntoolbar button (which used to wipe localStorage and reload) is removed.\n\nThe panel renders in the sidebar, replacing the inspector content while\nopen. Once a map is selected, the normal editor state resumes.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`show_map_picker` in `assets/js/005-app.js`:\n- Carries its own server-URL `<input>` at the top of the panel — the picker\n  reads from this input rather than from API state, so it works on\n  first-time load when nothing is stored yet.\n- `→` button next to the URL input (and the Enter key in the input) refreshes\n  the maps list.\n- Maps fetched via direct `fetch(url + '/maps')`, bypassing `API.list_maps`\n  so it works before `API.init()` has been called.\n- Recent maps come from `localStorage.soramech_maps_history`. Each row's\n  click handler captures its own `(server_url, map_name)` so users can jump\n  back to a different server entirely.\n- \"On this server\" group lists what the picker URL serves. Click handlers\n  pass the picker URL into `switch_to_map`.\n- \"Open map by name\" input/button at the bottom for typing a name directly.\n- Errors (server unreachable, non-200) render inline as `cannot reach\n  server: <reason>`.\n\n`init` in `assets/js/005-app.js`:\n- If `soramech_server` and `soramech_map` are both in localStorage, the\n  normal flow runs (`API.init` + `load_map`).\n- Otherwise, the picker is shown immediately. Selection inside the picker\n  saves to localStorage and calls `switch_to_map`, which then calls\n  `load_map`. No `prompt()` anywhere.\n- The `requestAnimationFrame(render)` loop starts in either case so the\n  canvas is live the moment the picker is up.\n\nThe top-left `switch map` toolbar button is removed. The map-label in the\nsidebar header is the only switch-maps entry point now.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/003-api.js — list_maps (no longer used for first-time fetch)\n- assets/js/005-app.js — init, load_map, show_map_picker, switch_to_map\n- assets/index.html — sidebar, inspector panel, toolbar",

    "originalFile":"# 222 — Compile button and assets directory\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nThe editor has no mechanism to trigger compilation of a map. Maps are only\nrunnable via the synchronous interpreter path (`src/007-runner-main.lua`).\nThere is no compiled artifact, no assets directory, and no binary output.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### UI: compile button\nA \"Compile\" button appears in the editor toolbar. Clicking it does nothing\nyet — it is a placeholder for the compilation pipeline (issue 219). The\nbutton is present so the UI layout is established before the backend is wired\nin.\n\nThe button label is \"Compile\". It has no loading state, no progress\nindicator, and no output for now. It simply exists in the toolbar next to\nthe existing controls.\n\n### Compiled artifacts: assets directory\nWhen compilation is eventually wired in, pressing the button triggers a\nbuild that produces a self-contained output directory alongside the map:\n\n```\nmaps/<map-name>/compiled/\n    pool-runner          ← the compiled C entry point (008-pool-runner.c)\n    src/                 ← copy of all source files used by the map\n    bin/                 ← compiled per-box binaries (C boxes → .so or binary)\n    manifest.json        ← list of every box, its language, and its binary path\n```\n\nThe compiled directory is the map's deployment artifact. Each box's language\ndetermines which invocation wrapper is selected at compile time. The same\nbuild path handles a Lua box, a C box, and a Bash box without branching on\nthe language at the top level. Iterators have no `ref` / `fn`.\n- **Connection schema**: `from_branch` field replaces the old\n  `from_output` / `from_port` dual-field design.\n",

      "totalLines":53,
      "content":"# 204 — Visible interaction hints\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe editor has no visible instructions. A new user sees a blank canvas with\ntwo toolbar buttons (\"reload\", \"switch map\") and no indication of what to do.\nAll interactions are undiscoverable:\n- Double-click to create a box\n- Drag an output port to draw a wire\n- Click a wire then Delete to remove it\n- Space+drag or middle-mouse to pan\n- Scroll to zoom\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe canvas shows a short hint overlay when the map is empty or when nothing\nis selected. The hint disappears once the user has at least one box on the\ncanvas. It should not reappear after that.\n\nSuggested hint text (monospace, centered, dim):\n```\ndouble-click  create box\ndrag port →   draw wire\nspace+drag    pan\nscroll        zoom\n```\n\nAdditionally, the status bar at the bottom-left should reflect the current\ninteraction state:\n- Idle with boxes: \"N boxes loaded  —  double-click to create\"\n- Wire drawing in progress: \"drawing wire — release on an input port\"\n- Box selected: \"selected: <box-id>\"\n- Wire selected: \"wire selected — Delete to remove\"\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. In the render loop (`005-app.js`), if `Boxes.boxes` is empty, draw the\n   hint text centered on the canvas using the canvas 2D context (not a DOM\n   overlay, so it transforms with the camera only for pan/zoom-invariant\n   display use `ctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0)` before drawing).\n2. Update `status_msg` calls in mouse handlers to reflect interaction state.\n3.     "content":"// Floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source viewer.\n//\n// open_source_view(ref, anchor_box?) creates an absolutely-positioned\n// window over the canvas showing the file's content. Multiple windows\n// can be open simultaneously; each is independently positioned and\n// closes only when its × button is clicked.\n//\n// The window is confined to the canvas's bounding box: drag and resize\n// operations clamp position and dimensions so the window can't leave\n// the canvas area.\n//\n// Default sizing (per issue 215):\n//   width  = (average line length + 3 chars) × monospace char width\n//   height = canvas height / 2\n\nconst SourceView = (() => {\n  // Track open windows so we can bring-to-front on click and so a future\n  // close-all (e.g. on map switch) can find them. Each entry is the\n  // outer DOM element.\n  const open_windows = [];\n  let z_top = 100;\n\n  // {{{ measure_char_w\n  // Measure the width of a single 12px-monospace character once at module\n  // load. Used for translating \"characters\" into pixels for default sizing.\n  // The measurement node is removed after use; no DOM clutter.\n  function measure_char_w() {\n    const probe = document.createElement('span');\n    probe.style.cssText =\n      'visibility:hidden;position:absolute;font:12px monospace;' +\n      'white-space:pre;left:-9999px;top:-9999px;';\n    probe.textContent = 'M'.repeat(50);\n    document.body.appendChild(probe);\n    const w = probe.getBoundingClientRect().width / 50;\n    probe.remove();\n    return w;\n  }\n  const CHAR_W = measure_char_w();\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ fetch_source\n  // Resolve a box's `ref` to file content. The ref is just a filename or a\n  // path relative to the map; we try the map's main src/ first (stripping\n  // a leading \"src/\" that older boxes sometimes carry), then walk through\n  // any extra source directories the server has registered. Throws if\n  // nothing matches.\n  async function fetch_source(ref) {\n    if (!ref) throw new Error('no ref set on this box');\n\n    const stripped = ref.replace(/^src\\//, '');\n\n    try { return await API.get_src_file(stripped); } catch (e) { /* fall through */ }\n\n    let extras = [];\n    try { extras = await API.list_extra_src(); } catch (e) {}\n    for (let i = 0; i < (extras || []).length; i++) {\n      try { return await API.get_extra_src_file(i, stripped); } catch (e) {}\n    }\n\n    throw new Error('source not found: ' + ref);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ canvas_rect\n  // Bounding box of the canvas in viewport coordinates. Used as the clamp\n  // region for the floating window.\n  function canvas_rect() {\n    return Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ default_size\n  // Returns the default { w, h } for a window showing the given source\n  // text, sized per issue 215 spec.\n  function default_size(text) {\n    const lines = (text || '').split('\\n');\n    const total = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0);\n    const avg   = lines.length ? total / lines.length : 40;\n    const w     = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(avg) + 3) * CHAR_W + 20;  // +20 for padding\n    const h     = canvas_rect().height / 2;\n    return { w: Math.round(w), h: Math.round(h) };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ clamp_position\n  // Clamp a candidate (left, top, width, height) so the window stays\n  // fully inside the canvas's bounding box.\n  function clamp_position(left, top, width, height) {\n    const r = canvas_rect();\n    const max_left = r.right  - width;\n    const max_top  = r.bottom - height;\n    return {\n      left: Math.min(Math.max(left, r.left), Math.max(r.left, max_left)),\n      top:  Math.min(Math.max(top,  r.top),  Math.max(r.top,  max_top)),\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bring_to_front\n  function bring_to_front(win) {\n    z_top += 1;\n    win.style.zIndex = String(z_top);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ make_window\n  // Create the outer DOM structure for a source window with the given\n  // title and body text. Wires up the drag-from-header behavior and the\n  // close button. Returns the outer element; caller positions and sizes\n  // it.\n  function make_window(title, body_text) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'source-view-window';\n\n    const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n    hdr.className = 'source-view-header';\n\n    const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n    lbl.className   = 'source-view-title';\n    lbl.textContent = title;\n    hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n    const close_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    close_btn.className   = 'source-view-close';\n    close_btn.textContent = '×';\n    close_btn.title       = 'close';\n    close_btn.onclick     = () => {\n      const i = open_windows.indexOf(wrap);\n      if (i >= 0) open_windows.splice(i, 1);\n      wrap.remove();\n    };\n    hdr.appendChild(close_btn);\n\n    wrap.appendChild(hdr);\n\n    const body = document.createElement('pre');\n    body.className   = 'source-view-body';\n    body.textContent = body_text;\n    wrap.appendChild(body);\n\n    // Drag-from-header: anchor at mousedown, every mousemove computes\n    // from the anchor to avoid accumulating error over a long drag.\n    let drag_anchor_mouse = null;\n    let drag_anchor_pos   = null;\n\n    hdr.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n      // Don't start a drag from the close button.\n      if (e.target === close_btn) return;\n      drag_anchor_mouse = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };\n      const r = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      drag_anchor_pos   = { left: r.left, top: r.top };\n      bring_to_front(wrap);\n      e.preventDefault();\n    });\n\n    window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n      if (!drag_anchor_mouse) return;\n      const cand_left = drag_anchor_pos.left + (e.clientX - drag_anchor_mouse.x);\n      const cand_top  = drag_anchor_pos.top  + (e.clientY - drag_anchor_mouse.y);\n      const r         = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      const clamped   = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, r.width, r.height);\n      wrap.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n      wrap.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n    });\n\n    window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { drag_anchor_mouse = null; });\n\n    // Click anywhere on the window brings it to the front.\n    wrap.addEventListener('mousedown', () => bring_to_front(wrap));\n\n    // Resize handle: native CSS resize=both, but we observe size changes\n    // and re-clamp position so the window doesn't grow off-canvas.\n    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {\n      const r = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      const c = clamp_position(r.left, r.top, r.width, r.height);\n      // Cap maximum size at the canvas bounds.\n      const cr = canvas_rect();\n      const max_w = cr.width;\n      const max_h = cr.height;\n      if (r.width  > max_w) wrap.style.width  = max_w + 'px';\n      if (r.height > max_h) wrap.style.height = max_h + 'px';\n      wrap.style.left = c.left + 'px';\n      wrap.style.top  = c.top  + 'px';\n    });\n    ro.observe(wrap);\n\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_source_view\n  // Public entry point. Fetches the source for `ref` and opens a floating\n  // window. If `anchor_box` is given, the window is centered over that\n  // box's screen position; otherwise it's centered on the canvas.\n  async function open_source_view(ref, anchor_box) {\n    let text;\n    try {\n      text = await fetch_source(ref);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('view source: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const win  = make_window(ref, text);\n    const size = default_size(text);\n\n    document.body.appendChild(win);\n    win.style.width  = size.w + 'px';\n    win.style.height = size.h + 'px';\n\n    // Default position: centered over anchor_box (if provided) or canvas.\n    const cr = canvas_rect();\n    let cand_left, cand_top;\n    if (anchor_box && anchor_box.ui) {\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(anchor_box.ui.x + Boxes.BOX_W / 2,\n                                       anchor_box.ui.y + Boxes.box_height(anchor_box) / 2);\n      cand_left = cr.left + s.x - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + s.y - size.h / 2;\n    } else {\n      cand_left = cr.left + cr.width  / 2 - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + cr.height / 2 - size.h / 2;\n    }\n    const clamped = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, size.w, size.h);\n    win.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n    win.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n\n    bring_to_front(win);\n    open_windows.push(win);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { open_source_view };\n})();\n"
  },

        "type":"text",
        "text":"You're right — average gets pulled down by all the blank lines, closing braces, and single-keyword lines, so the window ends up too narrow for the lines you actually need to read.\n\nThree reasonable options:\n\n1. **Max line length, clamped to [80, 120]**: fits everything in the file, but never absurdly wide and never absurdly narrow. One line of code, adaptive — a tiny helper file gets a smaller window, a long file caps at a sane upper bound. My favorite.\n\n2. **Hardcoded 100 chars**: predictable, simple, matches common code-style limits. Doesn't adapt at all, which is fine — the user can resize.\n\n3. **Some high percentile (e.g. 90th)**: fits 90% of lines, ignores extreme outliers. More clever but more code, and overkill for this.\n\nI'd go with **(1)** — same code complexity as a hardcoded number, but adapts when the file is short. Something like:\n\n```js\nconst max_len  = lines.reduce((m, l) => Math.max(m, l.length), 0);\nconst w_chars  = Math.max(80, Math.min(120, max_len));\nconst w        = w_chars * CHAR_W + 20;  // +20 for padding\n```\n\nIf you'd rather just go with hardcoded 100, that's fine too — it's a reasonable place to land and we can revisit if it ever feels wrong. Which way?"

    "originalFile":"// Floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source viewer.\n//\n// open_source_view(ref, anchor_box?) creates an absolutely-positioned\n// window over the canvas showing the file's content. Multiple windows\n// can be open simultaneously; each is independently positioned and\n// closes only when its × button is clicked.\n//\n// The window is confined to the canvas's bounding box: drag and resize\n// operations clamp position and dimensions so the window can't leave\n// the canvas area.\n//\n// Default sizing (per issue 215):\n//   width  = (average line length + 3 chars) × monospace char width\n//   height = canvas height / 2\n\nconst SourceView = (() => {\n  // Track open windows so we can bring-to-front on click and so a future\n  // close-all (e.g. on map switch) can find them. Each entry is the\n  // outer DOM element.\n  const open_windows = [];\n  let z_top = 100;\n\n  // {{{ measure_char_w\n  // Measure the width of a single 12px-monospace character once at module\n  // load. Used for translating \"characters\" into pixels for default sizing.\n  // The measurement node is removed after use; no DOM clutter.\n  function measure_char_w() {\n    const probe = document.createElement('span');\n    probe.style.cssText =\n      'visibility:hidden;position:absolute;font:12px monospace;' +\n      'white-space:pre;left:-9999px;top:-9999px;';\n    probe.textContent = 'M'.repeat(50);\n    document.body.appendChild(probe);\n    const w = probe.getBoundingClientRect().width / 50;\n    probe.remove();\n    return w;\n  }\n  const CHAR_W = measure_char_w();\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ fetch_source\n  // Resolve a box's `ref` to file content. The ref is just a filename or a\n  // path relative to the map; we try the map's main src/ first (stripping\n  // a leading \"src/\" that older boxes sometimes carry), then walk through\n  // any extra source directories the server has registered. Throws if\n  // nothing matches.\n  async function fetch_source(ref) {\n    if (!ref) throw new Error('no ref set on this box');\n\n    const stripped = ref.replace(/^src\\//, '');\n\n    try { return await API.get_src_file(stripped); } catch (e) { /* fall through */ }\n\n    let extras = [];\n    try { extras = await API.list_extra_src(); } catch (e) {}\n    for (let i = 0; i < (extras || []).length; i++) {\n      try { return await API.get_extra_src_file(i, stripped); } catch (e) {}\n    }\n\n    throw new Error('source not found: ' + ref);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ canvas_rect\n  // Bounding box of the canvas in viewport coordinates. Used as the clamp\n  // region for the floating window.\n  function canvas_rect() {\n    return Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ default_size\n  // Returns the default { w, h } for a window showing the given source\n  // text, sized per issue 215 spec.\n  function default_size(text) {\n    const lines = (text || '').split('\\n');\n    const total = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0);\n    const avg   = lines.length ? total / lines.length : 40;\n    const w     = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(avg) + 3) * CHAR_W + 20;  // +20 for padding\n    const h     = canvas_rect().height / 2;\n    return { w: Math.round(w), h: Math.round(h) };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ clamp_position\n  // Clamp a candidate (left, top, width, height) so the window stays\n  // fully inside the canvas's bounding box.\n  function clamp_position(left, top, width, height) {\n    const r = canvas_rect();\n    const max_left = r.right  - width;\n    const max_top  = r.bottom - height;\n    return {\n      left: Math.min(Math.max(left, r.left), Math.max(r.left, max_left)),\n      top:  Math.min(Math.max(top,  r.top),  Math.max(r.top,  max_top)),\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bring_to_front\n  function bring_to_front(win) {\n    z_top += 1;\n    win.style.zIndex = String(z_top);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ make_window\n  // Create the outer DOM structure for a source window with the given\n  // title and body text. Wires up the drag-from-header behavior and the\n  // close button. Returns the outer element; caller positions and sizes\n  // it.\n  function make_window(title, body_text) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'source-view-window';\n\n    const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n    hdr.className = 'source-view-header';\n\n    const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n    lbl.className   = 'source-view-title';\n    lbl.textContent = title;\n    hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n    const close_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    close_btn.className   = 'source-view-close';\n    close_btn.textContent = '×';\n    close_btn.title       = 'close';\n    close_btn.onclick     = () => {\n      const i = open_windows.indexOf(wrap);\n      if (i >= 0) open_windows.splice(i, 1);\n      wrap.remove();\n    };\n    hdr.appendChild(close_btn);\n\n    wrap.appendChild(hdr);\n\n    const body = document.createElement('pre');\n    body.className   = 'source-view-body';\n    body.textContent = body_text;\n    wrap.appendChild(body);\n\n    // Drag-from-header: anchor at mousedown, every mousemove computes\n    // from the anchor to avoid accumulating error over a long drag.\n    let drag_anchor_mouse = null;\n    let drag_anchor_pos   = null;\n\n    hdr.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n      // Don't start a drag from the close button.\n      if (e.target === close_btn) return;\n      drag_anchor_mouse = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };\n      const r = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      drag_anchor_pos   = { left: r.left, top: r.top };\n      bring_to_front(wrap);\n      e.preventDefault();\n    });\n\n    window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n      if (!drag_anchor_mouse) return;\n      const cand_left = drag_anchor_pos.left + (e.clientX - drag_anchor_mouse.x);\n      const cand_top  = drag_anchor_pos.top  + (e.clientY - drag_anchor_mouse.y);\n      const r         = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      const clamped   = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, r.width, r.height);\n      wrap.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n      wrap.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n    });\n\n    window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { drag_anchor_mouse = null; });\n\n    // Click anywhere on the window brings it to the front.\n    wrap.addEventListener('mousedown', () => bring_to_front(wrap));\n\n    // Resize handle: native CSS resize=both, but we observe size changes\n    // and re-clamp position so the window doesn't grow off-canvas.\n    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {\n      const r = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      const c = clamp_position(r.left, r.top, r.width, r.height);\n      // Cap maximum size at the canvas bounds.\n      const cr = canvas_rect();\n      const max_w = cr.width;\n      const max_h = cr.height;\n      if (r.width  > max_w) wrap.style.width  = max_w + 'px';\n      if (r.height > max_h) wrap.style.height = max_h + 'px';\n      wrap.style.left = c.left + 'px';\n      wrap.style.top  = c.top  + 'px';\n    });\n    ro.observe(wrap);\n\n    return wrap;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ open_source_view\n  // Public entry point. Fetches the source for `ref` and opens a floating\n  // window. If `anchor_box` is given, the window is centered over that\n  // box's screen position; otherwise it's centered on the canvas.\n  async function open_source_view(ref, anchor_box) {\n    let text;\n    try {\n      text = await fetch_source(ref);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('view source: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const win  = make_window(ref, text);\n    const size = default_size(text);\n\n    document.body.appendChild(win);\n    win.style.width  = size.w + 'px';\n    win.style.height = size.h + 'px';\n\n    // Default position: centered over anchor_box (if provided) or canvas.\n    const cr = canvas_rect();\n    let cand_left, cand_top;\n    if (anchor_box && anchor_box.ui) {\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(anchor_box.ui.x + Boxes.BOX_W / 2,\n                                       anchor_box.ui.y + Boxes.box_height(anchor_box) / 2);\n      cand_left = cr.left + s.x - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + s.y - size.h / 2;\n    } else {\n      cand_left = cr.left + cr.width  / 2 - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + cr.height / 2 - size.h / 2;\n    }\n    const clamped = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, size.w, size.h);\n    win.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n    win.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n\n    bring_to_front(win);\n    open_windows.push(win);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { open_source_view };\n})();\n",
    "oldString":"  // {{{ default_size\n  // Returns the default { w, h } for a window showing the given source\n  // text, sized per issue 215 spec.\n  function default_size(text) {\n    const lines = (text || '').split('\\n');\n    const total = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0);\n    const avg   = lines.length ? total / lines.length : 40;\n    const w     = Math.max(20, Math.ceil(avg) + 3) * CHAR_W + 20;  // +20 for padding\n    const h     = canvas_rect().height / 2;\n    return { w: Math.round(w), h: Math.round(h) };\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "newString":"  // {{{ default_size\n  // Returns the default { w, h } for a window showing the given source\n  // text. Width is the file's longest line clamped to [80, 120] chars —\n  // tiny files don't get pointlessly small windows, big files don't get\n  // pointlessly huge ones, and the user never sees horizontal scroll\n  // for content that already fits in 120 columns. Height is half the\n  // canvas height; the user resizes if they want more.\n  //\n  // Average line length was the first attempt and got pulled way down\n  // by blank lines and short single-keyword lines, so most files\n  // opened too narrow.\n  function default_size(text) {\n    const lines   = (text || '').split('\\n');\n    const max_len = lines.reduce((m, l) => Math.max(m, l.length), 0);\n    const w_chars = Math.max(80, Math.min(120, max_len));\n    const w       = w_chars * CHAR_W + 20;  // +20 for padding\n    const h       = canvas_rect().height / 2;\n    return { w: Math.round(w), h: Math.round(h) };\n  }\n  // }}}",

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Good question — syntax highlighting is a real feature. Here's the landscape, tersely:\n\n**The four common approaches**, simplest to most accurate:\n\n1. **Regex-pattern lists** — TextMate / VS Code / Sublime grammar files. Per-language file is a list of `{ pattern, className }` rules. Tokenize line-by-line, wrap matches in spans, style spans with CSS. Loose accuracy (regex can't truly parse code), but cheap, fast, and very easy to write or modify. The de-facto standard for editor-class highlighting.\n2. **Hand-rolled lexers** — Write a small tokenizer per language. Better accuracy than regex, but you write one per language and they grow.\n3. **Tree-sitter** — Real incremental parser per language compiled from a grammar. Best accuracy, used by GitHub / Neovim / Atom. Heavy: each grammar is a `.wasm` blob, tens of KB to MB.\n4. **Library** — Prism.js or highlight.js, ~50 KB gzipped, covers ~200 languages out of the box. Drop in, done. No per-language work for anything common.\n\n**For SoraMech specifically**, the natural fit is a hybrid that mirrors the language-spec architecture:\n\n- **Default**: highlight.js for instant coverage of Lua / C / Bash / Python / Rust / anything common. Pick the language by file extension, which we already have on `lang_spec_t.file_ext` (issue 303).\n- **Per-language override**: each `langs/<name>/` directory can optionally include a `syntax.json` that the viewer prefers over highlight.js when present. Format is simple — just a list of regex rules with CSS class names. Lets users style their custom-language boxes the way they want without depending on highlight.js shipping a definition.\n- **Fallback**: plain text if neither a syntax file nor a highlight.js definition matches.\n\nThat's three layers, each one optional. Most users get good highlighting from layer 1 with zero work; advanced users override per language; edge cases degrade gracefully.\n\nA `syntax.json` for, say, Lua would look like:\n\n```json\n[\n  { \"pattern\": \"--\\\\[\\\\[[\\\\s\\\\S]*?\\\\]\\\\]\", \"class\": \"syntax-comment\" },\n  { \"pattern\": \"--.*\",                       \"class\": \"syntax-comment\" },\n  { \"pattern\": \"\\\"(?:\\\\\\\\.|[^\\\"])*\\\"\",       \"class\": \"syntax-string\" },\n  { \"pattern\": \"\\\\b(local|function|end|if|then|else|elseif|return|do|while|for|in|nil|true|false)\\\\b\",\n    \"class\": \"syntax-keyword\" },\n  { \"pattern\": \"\\\\b\\\\d+(?:\\\\.\\\\d+)?\\\\b\",     \"class\": \"syntax-number\" }\n]\n```\n\nCSS:\n```css\n.syntax-comment { color: #6c72a0; }\n.syntax-keyword { color: #4a9eff; }\n.syntax-string  { color: #4caf7d; }\n.syntax-number  { color: #ff8c42; }\n```\n\n**My take**: this is worth doing, but it's its own issue, not a 215 add-on. Want me to:\n\n1. Close 215 as-is (no highlighting yet — viewer is functional plain-text)\n2. Open a new issue (216-something — actually 216 is taken; next free is 223 or so) speccing out the highlighting design above\n3. Move on to 208 (the last UX issue in the batch)\n4. Then come back to highlighting whenever\n\nOr do you want to go after highlighting now while this code is fresh?"
      }]

## [2262]

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T19:19:43.283Z",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01DXxU3QC9ov2bwdM3maVkHU",

        "type":"tool_result"
      }],
    "role":"user"
  },
  "slug":"snug-booping-dove",
  "gitBranch":"master",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "userType":"external",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/223-syntax-highlighting-via-user-lexers.md",
    "content":"# 223 — Syntax highlighting in the source viewer via user-written lexers\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe source viewer (issue 215, complete) shows file content as plain\nmonospace text. Every box source — Lua, C, Bash, anything else —\nrenders the same: white text on dark background, no syntax cues.\nReading a function in the editor is harder than it should be.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach language has its own small JavaScript lexer that turns raw text\ninto a list of typed tokens. The source viewer asks the lexer for the\nfile's tokens, then wraps each token in a span with a CSS class per\ntoken type. Styling is done purely in CSS, so themes are independent\nof lexers.\n\nThis mirrors the runtime language-spec architecture (issue 303):\neach language is responsible for its own concerns, the editor /\nrunner only knows how to call into a shared interface. No\nSoraMech-internal language list, no transpiling. Users add a new\nlanguage by writing a small JS file.\n\n### Lexer interface\n\nEach lexer is a JS module exporting a single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/lexer.js\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  // Returns an ordered array of tokens covering the entire input.\n  // Tokens must not overlap and together must cover [0, text.length).\n  return [\n    { type: 'keyword', start: 0,  end: 5  },\n    { type: 'plain',   start: 5,  end: 6  },\n    { type: 'string',  start: 6,  end: 17 },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nToken types are convention-only — the viewer applies a CSS class\nnamed `syntax-<type>` to each span. The standard set is:\n\n| type        | typical use                                        |\n|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `keyword`   | language keywords (`function`, `if`, `local`, …)   |\n| `comment`   | line and block comments                            |\n| `string`    | quoted strings, char literals, here-docs           |\n| `number`    | numeric literals                                   |\n| `operator`  | `+`, `-`, `==`, `=`, `:`, …                        |\n| `identifier`| variable / function names                          |\n| `plain`     | everything not classified                          |\n\nA lexer is free to introduce its own token types (`regex`,\n`annotation`, `decorator`, etc.) — the viewer just renders unknown\ntypes with a default `syntax-default` style.\n\n### File location\n\nLexers live next to the language they belong to. For shipped\nlanguages this is `langs/<name>/lexer.js`. The runner doesn't read\nthem — the editor server serves them as static JS files alongside\nthe `spec.c` and `spec.so` files used by the phase 3 runner.\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c          ← runtime spec (issue 306, phase 3)\n    lexer.js        ← editor lexer (this issue)\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/c/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    soramech-c.h\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/bash/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    bash-server.sh\n    Makefile\n```\n\nFor a language whose runtime spec hasn't been written (still in phase\n2), there's no `spec.c` yet — but the editor lexer can land first\nand live in `langs/<name>/lexer.js` waiting for the runtime work.\n\n### Loading\n\nThe source viewer determines a file's language by its extension and\nloads the corresponding lexer on demand. [[...]]), numbers, identifiers, operators\n    // ...\n  }\n  return tokens;\n}\n\nexport { tokenize };\n```\n\nHand-rolled, ~150 lines. The user resizes if\n56\t  they want more or less.\n57\t\n58\tIf the file is empty, fall back to a sensible default (e.g. 40\n59\tcharacters wide, half-canvas tall).\n60\t\n61\t### Default position\n62\t\n63\tCentered over the box that the user opened the source for, when\n64\topened from the canvas context menu. The existing browser does this distinction\n93\talready; the source viewer reuses it.\n94\t\n95\t### Average line length\n96\t\n97\t```js\n98\tconst lines = text.split('\\n');\n99\tconst avg = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0) / lines.length;\n100\tconst width_chars = Math.ceil(avg) + 3;\n101\t```\n102\t\n103\tMultiply by the monospace character width (computed once via a\n104\thidden `<span>` measurement at load, or hard-coded as ~7.2px for the\n105\tfont we use).\n106\t\n107\t### Drag clamping\n108\tOn mousemove during drag:\n109\t\n110\t```js\n111\tconst canvas_rect = Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\n112\tconst win_w = win.offsetWidth;\n113\tconst win_h = win.offsetHeight;\n114\tconst new_x = clamp(mouse_x - drag_offset_x, canvas_rect.left, canvas_rect.right - win_w);\n115\tconst new_y = clamp(mouse_y - drag_offset_y, canvas_rect.top,  canvas_rect.bottom - win_h);\n116\t```\n117\t\n118\tSame idea for resize: the new size cannot push the window past the\n119\tcanvas edges given its current position.\n120\t\n121\t### Multiple windows\n122\t\n123\tEach window is a separately-tracked DOM node.     "originalFile":"# 215 — View source code of a box in a draggable canvas window\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\nWhen a box isn't working as expected, the user has no way to inspect\nits source file from within the editor. They must find the file path\nin the inspector's `ref` field and open it manually in a separate\neditor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source-code\nwindow that appears over the canvas. Two entry points open it:\n\n1. **Inspector** — a \"view source\" button next to the `ref` field.\n2. **Canvas right-click context menu** — a \"view source\" item when\n   a box is selected.\n\nBoth call into the same window-creation helper. Multiple source\nwindows can be open at once (one per box the user opens), each\nindependently positioned.\n\n### Window behavior\n\n- **Floating**: rendered as an absolutely-positioned DOM element\n  layered above the canvas (not drawn into the canvas 2D context).\n  This makes scroll, text selection, and resize the browser's\n  native behavior — no per-frame redraw needed.\n- **Draggable**: a header bar at the top of the window is the drag\n  handle. Mousedown on the header initiates drag; mousemove updates\n  the window's `left` / `top`; mouseup releases.\n- **Confined to the canvas area**: the window cannot be dragged\n  outside the canvas's bounding box. The drag handler clamps\n  position so the window stays fully inside (drag stops at edges).\n  Resize is similarly clamped — the window cannot extend past the\n  canvas boundary.\n- **Resizable**: standard CSS `resize: both` on the inner pre or a\n  custom resize grip in the bottom-right corner. Either way, the\n  resize is constrained to keep the window inside the canvas.\n- **Scrollable**: the inner content area scrolls when the file\n  exceeds the window's dimensions. Standard browser scrolling, both\n  axes if needed.\n- **Closeable**: an `×` button in the header closes the window.\n\n### Default size\n\nComputed from the file content when the window opens:\n\n- **Width**: the average line length of the file (in characters)\n  plus three, multiplied by the monospace character width. Three\n  extra characters of breathing room past the average. Lines longer\n  than the window scroll horizontally.\n- **Height**: half the canvas's current height. The user resizes if\n  they want more or less.\n\nIf the file is empty, fall back to a sensible default (e.g. 40\ncharacters wide, half-canvas tall).\n\n### Default position\n\nCentered over the box that the user opened the source for, when\nopened from the canvas context menu. Centered on the canvas when\nopened from the inspector. If the default position would push the\nwindow outside the canvas, clamp to the nearest edge.\n\n### Window structure\n\n```\n┌─ classify.lua ──────────────────────────── × ┐  ← drag handle\n│ local M = {}                                  │\n│                                               │\n│ function M.classify(text)                     │  ← <pre> with file content\n│   if text:match(\"^%d+$\") then ...             │\n│   ...                                         │\n│ end                                           │\n│                                               │\n│ return M                                      │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                              ↘ ← resize grip\n```\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### File text fetch\nThe same API call as the existing file-browser preview (issue 207's\n`API.get_src_file`). The `ref` field on the box is the file path\nrelative to the map. Some refs may be in `libs/` (vendored or\nshipped), some in the map's `src/` — the fetch routes appropriately\n(via `API.get_src_file` for the map's source, `API.get_extra_src_file`\nfor libs/extra dirs). The existing browser does this distinction\nalready; the source viewer reuses it.\n\n### Average line length\n\n```js\nconst lines = text.split('\\n');\nconst avg = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0) / lines.length;\nconst width_chars = Math.ceil(avg) + 3;\n```\n\nMultiply by the monospace character width (computed once via a\nhidden `<span>` measurement at load, or hard-coded as ~7.2px for the\nfont we use).\n\n### Drag clamping\nOn mousemove during drag:\n\n```js\nconst canvas_rect = Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\nconst win_w = win.offsetWidth;\nconst win_h = win.offsetHeight;\nconst new_x = clamp(mouse_x - drag_offset_x, canvas_rect.left, canvas_rect.right - win_w);\nconst new_y = clamp(mouse_y - drag_offset_y, canvas_rect.top,  canvas_rect.bottom - win_h);\n```\n\nSame idea for resize: the new size cannot push the window past the\ncanvas edges given its current position.\n\n### Multiple windows\n\nEach window is a separately-tracked DOM node. A small registry\n(`open_source_windows[]`) tracks them so they can all be closed when\nthe map is switched, and so a click on a window brings it to the\nfront (z-index increment).\n\n### CSS\n\nFloating window styles are scoped under a class like\n`.source-view-window`. Header bar uses the project's existing accent\ncolor. The `<pre>` body uses the same monospace font as the\ninspector's existing port labels.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/008-source-view.js` (new) — module exposing\n   `open_source_view(box, ref, anchor_box?)`. Handles fetch, default\n   sizing, window creation, drag/resize bindings, close.\n2. `assets/index.html` — add `.source-view-window`,\n   `.source-view-header`, `.source-view-body` CSS.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add a \"view source\" button next\n   to the ref field; clicks call into the new module.\n4. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas\n   right-click context menu when a box is selected; clicks call the\n   same module with the selected box as `anchor_box`.\n5. Test: open the same source from two boxes (or twice from one\n   box) — verify two independent windows. Drag both around. Resize\n   both. Confirm clamping at canvas edges.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Bring-to-front on click: standard expectation, easy to implement\n  via a global z-counter. Worth doing.\n- Edit support: explicitly out of scope for now. Read-only. Editing\n  source files happens in the user's preferred editor on disk; the\n  viewer just shows what's there. (A future \"edit in editor\" issue\n  could add a \"save back\" capability with conflict warnings against\n  on-disk mtime.)\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_src_file, get_extra_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for the floating window\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — canvas bounding rect for clamping\n",
