    "originalFile":"# 215 — View source code of a box in a draggable canvas window\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Current behavior\nWhen a box isn't working as expected, the user has no way to inspect\nits source file from within the editor. They must find the file path\nin the inspector's `ref` field and open it manually in a separate\neditor.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source-code\nwindow that appears over the canvas. Two entry points open it:\n\n1. **Inspector** — a \"view source\" button next to the `ref` field.\n2. **Canvas right-click context menu** — a \"view source\" item when\n   a box is selected.\n\nBoth call into the same window-creation helper. Multiple source\nwindows can be open at once (one per box the user opens), each\nindependently positioned.\n\n### Window behavior\n\n- **Floating**: rendered as an absolutely-positioned DOM element\n  layered above the canvas (not drawn into the canvas 2D context).\n  This makes scroll, text selection, and resize the browser's\n  native behavior — no per-frame redraw needed.\n- **Draggable**: a header bar at the top of the window is the drag\n  handle. Mousedown on the header initiates drag; mousemove updates\n  the window's `left` / `top`; mouseup releases.\n- **Confined to the canvas area**: the window cannot be dragged\n  outside the canvas's bounding box. The drag handler clamps\n  position so the window stays fully inside (drag stops at edges).\n  Resize is similarly clamped — the window cannot extend past the\n  canvas boundary.\n- **Resizable**: standard CSS `resize: both` on the inner pre or a\n  custom resize grip in the bottom-right corner. Either way, the\n  resize is constrained to keep the window inside the canvas.\n- **Scrollable**: the inner content area scrolls when the file\n  exceeds the window's dimensions. Standard browser scrolling, both\n  axes if needed.\n- **Closeable**: an `×` button in the header closes the window.\n\n### Default size\n\nComputed from the file content when the window opens:\n\n- **Width**: the file's longest line clamped to `[80, 120]`\n  characters, multiplied by the monospace character width. Tiny\n  files don't get pointlessly small windows; very long lines don't\n  get pointlessly wide ones. Lines past 120 chars scroll\n  horizontally; the user resizes the window if they want more.\n  *(Earlier draft used average line length, but the average is\n  pulled way down by blank lines and short single-keyword lines, so\n  most files opened too narrow.)*\n- **Height**: half the canvas's current height.\n\n### Default position\n\nCentered over the box that the user opened the source for, when\nopened from the canvas context menu. Centered on the canvas when\nopened from the inspector. If the default position would push the\nwindow outside the canvas, clamp to the nearest edge.\n\n### Window structure\n\n```\n┌─ classify.lua ──────────────────────────── × ┐  ← drag handle\n│ local M = {}                                  │\n│                                               │\n│ function M.classify(text)                     │  ← <pre> with file content\n│   if text:match(\"^%d+$\") then ...             │\n│   ...                                         │\n│ end                                           │\n│                                               │\n│ return M                                      │\n└───────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                                              ↘ ← resize grip\n```\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n### File text fetch\nThe same API call as the existing file-browser preview (issue 207's\n`API.get_src_file`). The `ref` field on the box is the file path\nrelative to the map. Some refs may be in `libs/` (vendored or\nshipped), some in the map's `src/` — the fetch routes appropriately\n(via `API.get_src_file` for the map's source, `API.get_extra_src_file`\nfor libs/extra dirs). The existing browser does this distinction\nalready; the source viewer reuses it.\n\n### Average line length\n\n```js\nconst lines = text.split('\\n');\nconst avg = lines.reduce((a, l) => a + l.length, 0) / lines.length;\nconst width_chars = Math.ceil(avg) + 3;\n```\n\nMultiply by the monospace character width (computed once via a\nhidden `<span>` measurement at load, or hard-coded as ~7.2px for the\nfont we use).\n\n### Drag clamping\nOn mousemove during drag:\n\n```js\nconst canvas_rect = Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\nconst win_w = win.offsetWidth;\nconst win_h = win.offsetHeight;\nconst new_x = clamp(mouse_x - drag_offset_x, canvas_rect.left, canvas_rect.right - win_w);\nconst new_y = clamp(mouse_y - drag_offset_y, canvas_rect.top,  canvas_rect.bottom - win_h);\n```\n\nSame idea for resize: the new size cannot push the window past the\ncanvas edges given its current position.\n\n### Multiple windows\n\nEach window is a separately-tracked DOM node. A small registry\n(`open_source_windows[]`) tracks them so they can all be closed when\nthe map is switched, and so a click on a window brings it to the\nfront (z-index increment).\n\n### CSS\n\nFloating window styles are scoped under a class like\n`.source-view-window`. Header bar uses the project's existing accent\ncolor. The `<pre>` body uses the same monospace font as the\ninspector's existing port labels.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/008-source-view.js` (new) — module exposing\n   `open_source_view(box, ref, anchor_box?)`. Handles fetch, default\n   sizing, window creation, drag/resize bindings, close.\n2. `assets/index.html` — add `.source-view-window`,\n   `.source-view-header`, `.source-view-body` CSS.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — add a \"view source\" button next\n   to the ref field; clicks call into the new module.\n4. `assets/js/005-app.js` — add \"view source\" item to the canvas\n   right-click context menu when a box is selected; clicks call the\n   same module with the selected box as `anchor_box`.\n5. Test: open the same source from two boxes (or twice from one\n   box) — verify two independent windows. Drag both around. Resize\n   both. Confirm clamping at canvas edges.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Bring-to-front on click: standard expectation, easy to implement\n  via a global z-counter. Worth doing.\n- Edit support: explicitly out of scope for now. Read-only. Editing\n  source files happens in the user's preferred editor on disk; the\n  viewer just shows what's there. (A future \"edit in editor\" issue\n  could add a \"save back\" capability with conflict warnings against\n  on-disk mtime.)\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_src_file, get_extra_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for the floating window\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — canvas bounding rect for clamping\n",

    "newString":"## Implementation notes\n\nThe viewer is `assets/js/008-source-view.js`, a new module exposing\none public function — `SourceView.open_source_view(ref, anchor_box?)`.\nEach call creates an absolutely-positioned DOM window, populates it\nwith the fetched file content, and lets the user drag it around.\n\n### File text fetch\n`fetch_source(ref)` strips a leading `src/` prefix and tries\n`API.get_src_file` first; on failure it walks every directory\nreturned by `API.list_extra_src` and tries `API.get_extra_src_file`\nin order. Returns the first hit; throws if nothing matches. Plain\ntext — no JSON parsing.\n\n### Default size\nWidth derived from the file's longest line, clamped to\n`[80, 120]` characters and converted to pixels via a one-time\nmonospace-character measurement (`measure_char_w` runs at module\nload using a hidden probe span). Height is `canvas_rect().height /\n2`. Both rounded to integers.\n\n### Drag clamping\nThe header captures `mousedown` and records anchor positions for\nthe mouse and the window. `mousemove` computes a candidate\n`(left, top)` from the anchor delta and runs it through\n`clamp_position(left, top, w, h)` — which restricts the window to\n`canvas_rect()`'s bounds — before applying. Test: open the same source from two boxes (or twice from one\n   box) — verify two independent windows. Drag both around. Resize\n   both. Confirm clamping at canvas edges.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Bring-to-front on click: standard expectation, easy to implement\n  via a global z-counter. (A future \"edit in editor\" issue\n  could add a \"save back\" capability with conflict warnings against\n  on-disk mtime.)\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field rendering, inspector panel\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — canvas context menu, show_ctx_menu\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — get_src_file, get_extra_src_file\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for the floating window\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — canvas bounding rect for clamping\n",

Default\nheight is half the canvas. Drag uses an anchor-and-delta model so\nno error accumulates over a long drag; resize is clamped via a\nResizeObserver so the window can't grow off-canvas.\n\nCloses 215. Opens 223 (syntax highlighting via user-written\nlexers), specced as a follow-on: each language ships a small JS\ntokenizer in langs/<name>/lexer.js producing typed tokens that the\nviewer wraps in CSS-classed spans.       "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
    }

        "text":"Looking at the actual state — 208 turns out to be **already implemented**. The work happened across several sibling issues (207, 210, 218):\n\n- ✅ Input port names are read-only — `mk_port_display` in `004-inspector.js` uses a `<span>`, not an `<input>`\n- ✅ Per-port literal `value` field in the inspector with sever-wire-on-set semantics — same function\n- ✅ Output port section gone from inspector — only the comparator toggle remains in the output area\n- ✅ File browser doesn't set `box.outputs` — the on-select handler in `004-inspector.js` line 161 explicitly skips it\n- ✅ Schema doesn't require `outputs` — `001-schema.lua` validates `inputs` and `comparand` only\n- ✅ Executor pre-seeds literal values — `004-executor.lua` lines 208–215 seed `port.value` into the store before the run; wires overwrite at runtime\n\nLet me just close the issue with implementation notes pointing at where each piece landed:"

If no wire\n10\tis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\n11\tskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\n12\tthe editor.\n13\t\n14\tPort names on both input and output ports are editable text fields in the\n15\tinspector. This is fragile — the names must match the actual function signature\n16\texactly or the box silently misfires at runtime.\n17\t\n18\t## Intended behavior\n19\t\n20\t**Input port names are read-only.** They are derived from the function's\n21\tparameter names when the user selects a function via the file browser (issue\n22\t207). The inspector displays them as non-editable labels. Only the literal\n23\tvalue field is editable per input port.\n24\t\n25\t**Literal values:** Each input port has an optional literal value editable\n26\tdirectly in the inspector panel. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\n32\tif that fails, the raw string is used.\n33\t\n34\t**Output ports are gone.** Every call box has exactly one output wire carrying\n35\tthe raw return value (see issue 210). The output section of the inspector is\n36\treplaced by the comparator toggle (see issue 210). `box.outputs` is removed\n37\tfrom the call box schema.\n38\t\n39\tThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\n40\tdedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant, and eliminates the class\n41\tof runtime failures caused by mistyped port names.\n42\t\n43\t## Suggested implementation steps\n44\t\n45\t1. **Data model** — `box.inputs` port objects gain an optional `value` string\n46\t   field. `box.outputs` is removed from call box schema (not needed; see\n47\t   issue 210 for the single-wire model).\n48\t\n49\t2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)**:\n50\t   - `mk_port_display()` renders input port names as non-editable labels\n51\t     (remove the name input). Each row shows the type label and a value input.\n52\t   - On value change, update `ports[i].value` and call `save()`.\n53\t   - Remove the output port section for call boxes entirely.\n54\t\n55\t3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the\n56\t   main execution loop: for every box, for every input port with a non-empty\n57\t   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n58\t   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n59\t   because they only read from the store.\n60\t\n61\t## Related documents\n62\t\n63\t- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n64\t- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n65\t- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n66\t- issues/210 — single output wire and comparator (replaces box.outputs)\n67\t- issues/207 — file browser sets input names from function signature\n68\t",

      "content":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\nPort names on both input and output ports are editable text fields in the\ninspector. This is fragile — the names must match the actual function signature\nexactly or the box silently misfires at runtime.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n**Input port names are read-only.** They are derived from the function's\nparameter names when the user selects a function via the file browser (issue\n207). The inspector displays them as non-editable labels. Only the literal\nvalue field is editable per input port.\n\n**Literal values:** Each input port has an optional literal value editable\ndirectly in the inspector panel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is\nconnected to that port, the literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS\nconnected, the wire's value overwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\n**Output ports are gone.** Every call box has exactly one output wire carrying\nthe raw return value (see issue 210). The output section of the inspector is\nreplaced by the comparator toggle (see issue 210). `box.outputs` is removed\nfrom the call box schema.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant, and eliminates the class\nof runtime failures caused by mistyped port names.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — `box.inputs` port objects gain an optional `value` string\n   field. `box.outputs` is removed from call box schema (not needed; see\n   issue 210 for the single-wire model).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - `mk_port_display()` renders input port names as non-editable labels\n     (remove the name input). Each row shows the type label and a value input.\n   - On value change, update `ports[i].value` and call `save()`.\n   - Remove the output port section for call boxes entirely.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the\n   main execution loop: for every box, for every input port with a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n- issues/210 — single output wire and comparator (replaces box.outputs)\n- issues/207 — file browser sets input names from function signature\n"
    }
  },

    "originalFile":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput ports on a box can only receive values from wired connections. If no wire\nis connected to an input port, the box never becomes \"ready\" and the runner\nskips it silently. There is no way to supply a constant value to an input from\nthe editor.\n\nPort names on both input and output ports are editable text fields in the\ninspector. This is fragile — the names must match the actual function signature\nexactly or the box silently misfires at runtime.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n**Input port names are read-only.** They are derived from the function's\nparameter names when the user selects a function via the file browser (issue\n207). The inspector displays them as non-editable labels. Only the literal\nvalue field is editable per input port.\n\n**Literal values:** Each input port has an optional literal value editable\ndirectly in the inspector panel. If the value field is non-empty and no wire is\nconnected to that port, the literal value is used at runtime. If a wire IS\nconnected, the wire's value overwrites the literal at runtime — wires always win.\n\nThe value field accepts JSON notation (numbers, strings with quotes, arrays,\nobjects) or bare strings for convenience. The executor tries JSON.decode first;\nif that fails, the raw string is used.\n\n**Output ports are gone.** Every call box has exactly one output wire carrying\nthe raw return value (see issue 210). The output section of the inspector is\nreplaced by the comparator toggle (see issue 210). `box.outputs` is removed\nfrom the call box schema.\n\nThis lets a box be fully configured from the inspector without needing a\ndedicated \"data\" box wired to it for every constant, and eliminates the class\nof runtime failures caused by mistyped port names.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Data model** — `box.inputs` port objects gain an optional `value` string\n   field. `box.outputs` is removed from call box schema (not needed; see\n   issue 210 for the single-wire model).\n\n2. **Inspector (`004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - `mk_port_display()` renders input port names as non-editable labels\n     (remove the name input). Each row shows the type label and a value input.\n   - On value change, update `ports[i].value` and call `save()`.\n   - Remove the output port section for call boxes entirely.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)** — add a pre-seeding pass before the\n   main execution loop: for every box, for every input port with a non-empty\n   `value`, write `store[box_id..\".\"..port.name]` with the parsed value.\n   Existing `inputs_satisfied` and `collect_inputs` logic requires no changes\n   because they only read from the store.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — mk_port_display, show\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n- issues/210 — single output wire and comparator (replaces box.outputs)\n- issues/207 — file browser sets input names from function signature\n",
    "oldString":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\nopen",
    "newString":"# 208 — Port literal values\n\n## Status\n\ncomplete (work landed across 207, 210, 218)",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

          "new_string":"## Implementation notes\n\nThis issue was implemented incrementally as part of the related\nwork in 207 (file browser sets input names from function\nsignatures), 210 (comparator-based branching replaces named output\nports), and 218 (single-output driver contract). By the time those\nissues finished, every piece of 208 was in place. The current code\nis:\n\n### Inspector — `assets/js/004-inspector.js`\n`mk_port_display(ports)` renders each input port as a row with:\n- A read-only `<span>` for the port name (derived from the function\n  signature via the file browser).\n- A `:type` label when the type is more specific than `any`.\n- A `<input>` for the literal value, placeholder `value…`, persisted\n  to `ports[i].value` on input.\n\nSetting a literal value also severs any incoming wires to that port\n(walks `box.connections`, removes matches from this box's connections\nand from each upstream box's connections, persists via the API).\nThis keeps \"literal vs wire\" from having two competing sources of\ntruth at the editor level.\n\nThe output side renders only the comparator toggle (issue 210) — no\noutput port list. Call-box schema does not include `outputs` and the\ninspector never iterates `box.outputs`.\n\n### Executor — `src/004-executor.lua`\nBefore the main run loop, every input port's `value` (if present\nand non-empty) is JSON-decoded and seeded into the wire-value\nstore at `<box_id>.<port_name>`. Wires fired during the run\noverwrite the seed with the producer's output, so wires win at\nruntime — exactly the spec in this issue.\n\n### File browser — `assets/js/004-inspector.js::open_browser`\nOn function selection, sets `current_box.ref`, `current_box.fn`, and\n`current_box.inputs` from the parsed signature. Does not set\n`current_box.outputs`. Comment in the source explicitly notes the\nsingle-output rule.\n\n### Schema — `src/001-schema.lua`\n`validate_box` checks `inputs` (must be a table when present) and\n`comparand` (must be a string when present). It does not require,\nmention, or reject `outputs`. Existing box JSONs that still carry\nan `outputs` field from before the cleanup are tolerated as\nharmless leftover data — the runner ignores them.\n\n### Notes\n- The \"wire wins at runtime\" semantics are achieved by the\n  pre-seed-then-overwrite ordering in the executor. Editor-side, the\n  redundant case of \"literal AND wire on the same port\" is avoided\n  by severing wires on literal entry. Either route to a value works.\n- Existing maps may still have `outputs` arrays in their box JSONs.\n  Loading and editing them works fine; the leftover is invisible\n  unless you `cat` the file. A future cleanup could strip them, but\n  that's not required by this issue.",

features so much as model corrections that shape\nwhat phase 3 will consume:\n\n- **Single-output rule** (218, complete): every box has exactly one\n  output wire.     "originalFile":"# 210 — Comparator wire branching\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Supersedes\n\nThe original design of this issue described an `llm-route` box kind that used an\nOllama call to route between named output ports. That design has been removed:\nthe `llm-route` box kind, the executor's `llm_route_call` helper, and all\nrelated inspector and wire rendering code should be reverted. The problem it was\nsolving — conditional routing — is handled instead by the comparator mechanism\ndescribed here, which works on any box.\n\nSimilarly, the `branch` box kind (issue 108) is removed in favour of this mechanism.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEvery box has named output ports. Routing is done either by:\n- `branch` boxes with named ports and hard-coded predicates, or\n- `llm-route` boxes with named ports and an Ollama routing call.\n\nBoth approaches require a dedicated box kind. The connection schema uses\n`from_port` for these boxes and `from_output` for call boxes — two parallel\nfields, only one ever set.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEvery box has exactly **one output wire** carrying whatever the function\nreturned (raw, as a single value). There are no named output ports.\n\nA box may optionally have a **comparator** configured. When a comparator is\nactive, the single output wire splits into three wires: `lt`, `eq`, and `gt`.\nThe executor compares the output value against a literal number. If the output\nis not a strict number, the executor halts with an error — there is no fallback.\n\nThe comparator is configured per box via a `comparand` string field (the\nliteral number to compare against) stored in the box file. The inspector shows:\n- A toggle button labelled **compare** next to the output section.\n- When active, a text input for the comparand value.\n\nConnection schema changes:\n- Old: `{from_box, from_output|from_port, to_box, to_input}`\n- New: `{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`\n  where `from_branch` is `null` (no comparator, one wire) or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`.\n\nThe canvas renders one output dot per box by default. When a comparator is\nactive, it renders three stacked dots labelled lt / eq / gt.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Box schema** — add optional `comparand` string to the box file format.\n   Remove `outputs` array from call box schema. Remove `ports` array and\n   predicate fields.\n\n2. **Connection schema** — replace `from_output`/`from_port` with `from_branch`\n   (`null` or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`). Update `src/001-schema.lua` validation\n   and `src/003-loader.lua` connection loading.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind handling from the execute loop.\n   - Remove `fire_connections` named-port logic for both kinds.\n   - After a call box runs: if `box.comparand` is set, parse it as number,\n     compare against the output value (`lt`/`eq`/`gt`), and fire only the\n     connection whose `from_branch` matches. If value is not a number, halt\n     with error. If no comparator, fire the one connection whose `from_branch`\n     is null.\n\n4. **Canvas rendering (`assets/js/002-boxes.js`)** — one output dot per box;\n   if `box.comparand` is set, render three stacked dots with labels.\n\n5. **Wire drawing (`assets/js/006-wires.js`)**:\n   - Remove `from_port`/`from_output` dual-field logic.\n   - Use `from_branch` to identify which dot a wire originates from.\n   - Color lt/eq/gt wires distinctly if desired.\n\n6. **Inspector (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind options from dropdown.\n   - Remove output port list for call boxes.\n   - Add compare toggle button and comparand input field.\n   - Input port names are read-only (derived from parsing); only literal values\n     are editable (see issue 208).\n\n7. **File browser (`assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)** — on function select, set\n   `box.inputs` from parsed argument names; do NOT set `box.outputs` (no named\n   outputs).\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — canvas dot rendering\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — compare toggle, comparand field\n- assets/js/006-wires.js — connection drawing, from_branch field\n- src/001-schema.lua — box and connection validation\n- src/003-loader.lua — connection loading\n- src/004-executor.lua — fire_connections, comparator evaluation\n- docs/001-architecture.md — box and connection file format\n",
    "oldString":"# 210 — Comparator wire branching\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Supersedes\n\nThe original design of this issue described an `llm-route` box kind that used an\nOllama call to route between named output ports. The problem it was\nsolving — conditional routing — is handled instead by the comparator mechanism\ndescribed here, which works on any box.\n\nSimilarly, the `branch` box kind (issue 108) is removed in favour of this mechanism.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEvery box has named output ports. Routing is done either by:\n- `branch` boxes with named ports and hard-coded predicates, or\n- `llm-route` boxes with named ports and an Ollama routing call.\n\nBoth approaches require a dedicated box kind. The connection schema uses\n`from_port` for these boxes and `from_output` for call boxes — two parallel\nfields, only one ever set.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEvery box has exactly **one output wire** carrying whatever the function\nreturned (raw, as a single value). There are no named output ports.\n\nA box may optionally have a **comparator** configured. When a comparator is\nactive, the single output wire splits into three wires: `lt`, `eq`, and `gt`.\nThe executor compares the output value against a literal number. If the output\nis not a strict number, the executor halts with an error — there is no fallback.\n\nThe comparator is configured per box via a `comparand` string field (the\nliteral number to compare against) stored in the box file. The inspector shows:\n- A toggle button labelled **compare** next to the output section.\n- When active, a text input for the comparand value.\n\nConnection schema changes:\n- Old: `{from_box, from_output|from_port, to_box, to_input}`\n- New: `{from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input}`\n  where `from_branch` is `null` (no comparator, one wire) or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`.\n\nThe canvas renders one output dot per box by default. When a comparator is\nactive, it renders three stacked dots labelled lt / eq / gt.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Box schema** — add optional `comparand` string to the box file format.\n   Remove `outputs` array from call box schema. Remove `ports` array and\n   predicate fields.\n\n2. **Connection schema** — replace `from_output`/`from_port` with `from_branch`\n   (`null` or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`). Update `src/001-schema.lua` validation\n   and `src/003-loader.lua` connection loading.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind handling from the execute loop.\n   - Remove `fire_connections` named-port logic for both kinds.\n   - After a call box runs: if `box.comparand` is set, parse it as number,\n     compare against the output value (`lt`/`eq`/`gt`), and fire only the\n     connection whose `from_branch` matches. If value is not a number, halt\n     with error. If no comparator, fire the one connection whose `from_branch`\n     is null.\n\n4. **Canvas rendering (`assets/js/002-boxes.js`)** — one output dot per box;\n   if `box.comparand` is set, render three stacked dots with labels.\n\n5. **Wire drawing (`assets/js/006-wires.js`)**:\n   - Remove `from_port`/`from_output` dual-field logic.\n   - Use `from_branch` to identify which dot a wire originates from.\n   - Color lt/eq/gt wires distinctly if desired.\n\n6. **Inspector (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind options from dropdown.\n   - Remove output port list for call boxes.\n   - Add compare toggle button and comparand input field.\n   - Input port names are read-only (derived from parsing); only literal values\n     are editable (see issue 208).\n\n7. **File browser (`assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)** — on function select, set\n   `box.inputs` from parsed argument names; do NOT set `box.outputs` (no named\n   outputs).\n\n## Related documents\n\n- assets/js/002-boxes.js — canvas dot rendering\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — compare toggle, comparand field\n- assets/js/006-wires.js — connection drawing, from_branch field\n- src/001-schema.lua — box and connection validation\n- src/003-loader.lua — connection loading\n- src/004-executor.lua — fire_connections, comparator evaluation\n- docs/001-architecture.md — box and connection file format\n",
    "oldString":"## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **Box schema** — add optional `comparand` string to the box file format.\n   Remove `outputs` array from call box schema. Remove `ports` array and\n   predicate fields.\n\n2. **Connection schema** — replace `from_output`/`from_port` with `from_branch`\n   (`null` or `\"lt\"`/`\"eq\"`/`\"gt\"`). Update `src/001-schema.lua` validation\n   and `src/003-loader.lua` connection loading.\n\n3. **Executor (`src/004-executor.lua`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind handling from the execute loop.\n   - Remove `fire_connections` named-port logic for both kinds.\n   - After a call box runs: if `box.comparand` is set, parse it as number,\n     compare against the output value (`lt`/`eq`/`gt`), and fire only the\n     connection whose `from_branch` matches. If value is not a number, halt\n     with error. If no comparator, fire the one connection whose `from_branch`\n     is null.\n\n4. **Canvas rendering (`assets/js/002-boxes.js`)** — one output dot per box;\n   if `box.comparand` is set, render three stacked dots with labels.\n\n5. **Wire drawing (`assets/js/006-wires.js`)**:\n   - Remove `from_port`/`from_output` dual-field logic.\n   - Use `from_branch` to identify which dot a wire originates from.\n   - Color lt/eq/gt wires distinctly if desired.\n\n6. **Inspector (`assets/js/004-inspector.js`)**:\n   - Remove `branch` and `llm-route` kind options from dropdown.\n   - Remove output port list for call boxes.\n   - Add compare toggle button and comparand input field.\n   - Input port names are read-only (derived from parsing); only literal values\n     are editable (see issue 208).\n\n7. **File browser (`assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)** — on function select, set\n   `box.inputs` from parsed argument names; do NOT set `box.outputs` (no named\n   outputs).",
    "newString":"## Implementation notes\n\nThe whole pipeline is in place across schema, loader, executor,\ncanvas rendering, wires, inspector, and file browser:\n\n### Box schema — `src/001-schema.lua`\n`comparand` is an optional string field validated by `validate_box`.\nThe `outputs` array is not part of the schema (no validation, not\nrequired, ignored if present in legacy box JSONs). Branch box kind\nand predicate-port fields are gone.\n\n### Connection schema — `src/001-schema.lua` + `src/003-loader.lua`\nConnection records use `from_branch`, validated by `validate_box`\nagainst `valid_branches = { lt, eq, gt }` plus `nil` (single-wire\nmode). The loader loads connections without any `from_port` /\n`from_output` handling.\n\n### Executor — `src/004-executor.lua`\nAfter a box runs, `fire_connections` checks `box.comparand`:\n- If set: parse as number (halt with error if it isn't), compare\n  against the output (also must be number-coercible), classify as\n  `lt` / `eq` / `gt`, fire only the connection whose `from_branch`\n  matches.\n- If unset: fire every connection whose `from_branch` is nil.\n\nThere's no remaining `branch` kind handling or `llm_route_call`\nhelper.\n\n### Canvas rendering — `assets/js/002-boxes.js`\n`port_positions` returns three output dots (`lt` / `eq` / `gt`)\nwhen `box.comparand` is set, otherwise a single centered dot.\n`draw_box` uses `BRANCH_COLOR = { lt, eq, gt }` to color each\ncomparator dot and labels them next to the dots.\n\n### Wire drawing — `assets/js/006-wires.js`\nConnections use `c.from_branch` exclusively. Plain wires use a dim\ndefault color; comparator branches get distinct colors per branch\nvia `BRANCH_COLOR`. `create_connection` takes a `from_branch`\nparameter (null for plain).\n\n### Inspector — `assets/js/004-inspector.js`\n- Read-only port names rendered via `mk_port_display`.\n- Compare toggle button and comparand input field in the output\n  section. No output port list, no branch/llm-route kinds.\n\n### File browser — `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` (called from\n`004-inspector.js::open_browser`)\nOn function select: sets `current_box.ref`, `current_box.fn`, and\n`current_box.inputs` from the parsed signature. Does not set\n`current_box.outputs`.",

          "content":"-- Text manipulation — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"text\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ to use\n-- it directly as a call box via the file browser.\n-- No external dependencies.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.concat\n-- Join N text values with a separator. The signature is variadic so the\n-- box can grow its `text` input without modifying this source — see\n-- issue 217 part B for the editor-side variadic-input mechanics.\nfunction M.concat(sep, ...)\n    return table.concat({ ... }, sep or \"\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.split\n-- Split a text into parts on a literal (non-pattern) separator. Returns\n-- a Lua array of the parts; the driver shim encodes it as JSON for\n-- transport on the single output wire. The downstream box decodes the\n-- array — there is no fan-out into multiple wires (that would require\n-- knowing the part count at design time, which we don't).\n--\n-- Plain-string match: the separator is escaped before being passed to\n-- string.find so users don't have to think about Lua patterns.\nfunction M.split(text, sep)\n    if text == nil then return {} end\n    if sep == nil or sep == \"\" then\n        -- splitting on empty separator: return a single-element array\n        -- with the whole input. Avoids an infinite loop and matches\n        -- common library behavior for split-on-empty.\n        return { text }\n    end\n\n    local parts = {}\n    local plain = true   -- treat sep as a literal string, not a pattern\n    local pos   = 1\n\n    while true do\n        local s, e = string.find(text, sep, pos, plain)\n        if s == nil then\n            parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos)\n            break\n        end\n        parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos, s - 1)\n        pos = e + 1\n    end\n\n    return parts\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/text.lua"

    "content":"-- Text manipulation — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"text\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ to use\n-- it directly as a call box via the file browser.\n-- No external dependencies.\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.concat\n-- Join N text values with a separator. The signature is variadic so the\n-- box can grow its `text` input without modifying this source — see\n-- issue 217 part B for the editor-side variadic-input mechanics.\nfunction M.concat(sep, ...)\n    return table.concat({ ... }, sep or \"\")\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.split\n-- Split a text into parts on a literal (non-pattern) separator. Returns\n-- a Lua array of the parts; the driver shim encodes it as JSON for\n-- transport on the single output wire. The downstream box decodes the\n-- array — there is no fan-out into multiple wires (that would require\n-- knowing the part count at design time, which we don't).\n--\n-- Plain-string match: the separator is escaped before being passed to\n-- string.find so users don't have to think about Lua patterns.\nfunction M.split(text, sep)\n    if text == nil then return {} end\n    if sep == nil or sep == \"\" then\n        -- splitting on empty separator: return a single-element array\n        -- with the whole input. Avoids an infinite loop and matches\n        -- common library behavior for split-on-empty.\n        return { text }\n    end\n\n    local parts = {}\n    local plain = true   -- treat sep as a literal string, not a pattern\n    local pos   = 1\n\n    while true do\n        local s, e = string.find(text, sep, pos, plain)\n        if s == nil then\n            parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos)\n            break\n        end\n        parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos, s - 1)\n        pos = e + 1\n    end\n\n    return parts\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
  },

    "content":"# text.lua\n\nText manipulation helpers — concat and split. Pure Lua, no external\ndependencies. Use as `require(\"text\")` from another Lua function, or\ncopy into a map's `src/` and pick the function via the file browser.\n\nBoth functions output a single value on the box's output wire (per\nthe single-output rule, issue 218).\n\n---\n\n## M.concat(sep, ...) → string\n\nJoins the variadic text arguments with the given separator.\n\n| param | type    | description                                          |\n|-------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| sep   | string  | separator inserted between every pair of values     |\n| ...   | strings | any number of text values to join                    |\n\nReturns: a single string with all values concatenated.\n\nThe signature is variadic so the box's `text` input can be marked\nvariadic in the inspector and grown to any number of slots — see\nissue 217 part B for the editor mechanics.\n\nEdge cases: `sep` may be an empty string. Zero-arg call returns the\nempty string.\n\n---\n\n## M.split(text, sep) → table\n\nSplits `text` into parts on a literal (non-pattern) separator. Returns\na Lua array; the driver shim JSON-encodes it for transport on the\nsingle output wire. The downstream box decodes the array.\n\n| param | type   | description                                          |\n|-------|--------|------------------------------------------------------|\n| text  | string | the input string                                     |\n| sep   | string | the separator to split on (literal — no pattern matching) |\n\nReturns: an array (Lua table with integer keys) of the parts.\n\nEdge cases:\n- `nil` text → empty array\n- `nil` or empty `sep` → single-element array containing the whole input\n  (avoids an infinite loop and matches common library behavior)\n- Separator characters that are also Lua-pattern metacharacters (`.`,\n  `*`, `[`, etc.) are matched literally — `string.find` is called with\n  `plain = true`.\n"
  },
  "uuid":"4754bcee-d1d5-4ebb-ad65-a20cba7bbe61",

    "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
    "oldString":"    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end",
    "newString":"    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end",

        "content":"1\t// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n2\t// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n3\t\n4\tconst Wires = (() => {\n5\t  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n6\t  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n7\t  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n8\t\n9\t  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n10\t  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n11\t\n12\t  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n13\t\n14\t  // {{{ selected_wire\n15\t  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n16\t  // }}}\n17\t\n18\t  // {{{ bezier_point\n19\t  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n20\t    const mt = 1 - t;\n21\t    return {\n22\t      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n23\t      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n24\t    };\n25\t  }\n26\t  // }}}\n27\t\n28\t  // {{{ draw_bezier\n29\t  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n30\t    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n31\t    const cy0 = y0;\n32\t    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n33\t    const cy1 = y1;\n34\t\n35\t    ctx.beginPath();\n36\t    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n37\t    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n38\t    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n39\t    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n40\t    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n41\t    ctx.stroke();\n42\t  }\n43\t  // }}}\n44\t\n45\t  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n46\t  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n47\t  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n48\t  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n49\t    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n50\t    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n51\t      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n52\t      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n53\t        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n54\t\n55\t        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n56\t        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n57\t        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n58\t\n59\t        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n60\t        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n61\t\n62\t        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n63\t          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n64\t          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n65\t          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n66\t          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n67\t        }\n68\t      }\n69\t    }\n70\t    return null;\n71\t  }\n72\t  // }}}\n73\t\n74\t  // {{{ draw_all\n75\t  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n76\t    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n77\t      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n78\t      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n79\t        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n80\t\n81\t        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n82\t        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n83\t        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n84\t\n85\t        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n86\t        const color = c.from_branch ?       "content":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ?         "text":"Hard reload and test. Open a box that has inputs (e.g. one of the boxes in the hello map). In the inspector:\n\n1. **`var` button** on the right of each input port — click it on a plain port (e.g. `text`). The port should rename to `text_0` and the button should change to `var ×` (active state). `text` should now be in `box.variadic_inputs`.\n2. **`+` button** on the last variadic slot — click to add `text_1`, `text_2`, etc.\n3. **`×` button** on non-first slots — click to remove that slot. Higher-indexed slots in the same group rename down by one.\n4. **`var ×` button** on slot 0 — click to collapse the whole variadic group back to a single non-variadic port. Higher slots and their wires get dropped.\n\nIf a wire is connected to a slot that gets renamed, the connection on both endpoints (this box and the upstream box) should update. If a wire is connected to a slot that gets removed, the connection on both endpoints should disappear.\n\nTell me how it behaves. Auto-grow on wire-connect and auto-shrink on wire-disconnect are not yet implemented — for now slot count is fully controlled by the `+`/`×` buttons. We can add the wire-driven auto-behavior in a follow-up if you want."

  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T19:45:52.822Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"pushing the + button adds the slot in the inspector, but not in the visual box. There's no additional ports to connect wires to.\n\nIf a function has more than one variadic input argument, it's typically the case that we're inputting like, an array or a table or something. So we should expect more than one to be possible, but they should be grouped together as well.\n\npushing the X button should disconnect any wires going to that port. But that might be part of the fact that adding new variadic slots doesn't provide more input ports.\n\nWe shouldn't need the + button really at all. It should auto-grow when we provide a value for one of them. Connecting a wire or inputting a specific value should auto-grow, and snipping a wire or deleting a value SHOULDN'T remove a slot. It should only be removed if the X button is clicked. I think?\n\nAm I right in that assessment?\n\nAlso, when I click \"compare\" to return it to a normal, non comparison output, it restores a wire link that was present before turning it into a comparison. This tells me that connection is stored somewhere. I don't want to maintain that stale data, we should clear any wire connections on the output port when switching to and from \"compare\" mode.\n\nOh, it seems like pushing the + button now adds the input ports correctly. I wonder what I was doing wrong before? Weird.\n\nOkay I just connected three wires of different colors (so I could keep track) to a box with 1 input, variadic'd to 3 input ports. I pushed X in the second slot, and the inspector updated, but the box display still has 3 ports while the inspector only has 2. When I add more inputs in the inspector, it doesn't modify the box anymore.\n\nwe should be able to change the names of input fields if we want. Right now it doesn't let us. Can we move the text input field to the box display? The inspector is a little crowded. We should have more room for the text input there, with the names being on the box.",

    "oldString":"  // Toggle a non-variadic input ON: rename `text` → `text_0`, add base\n  // to box.variadic_inputs, update incoming connections.\n  // Special case: a port literally named `...` (Lua variadic that the\n  // file-browser parser left in place) gets renamed to `args_0` with\n  // base `args` — there's no other sensible name we can derive.\n  async function make_variadic(port_name) {\n    const idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === port_name);\n    if (idx < 0) return;\n\n    const base     = port_name === '...' ? 'args' : port_name;\n    const new_name = base + '_0';\n    const old_name = port_name;\n\n    current_box.inputs[idx].name = new_name;\n    current_box.variadic_inputs  = current_box.variadic_inputs || [];\n    if (!current_box.variadic_inputs.includes(base)) {\n      current_box.variadic_inputs.push(base);\n    }\n\n    await update_target_connections([old_name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: new_name }));\n    await save();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Higher-indexed slots are deleted along with their incoming wires.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Drop higher slots from box.inputs.\n    const drop_names = slots.slice(1).map(s => s.port.name);\n    const keep_idx   = slots[0].idx;\n\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    // Re-resolve slot 0's index after the filter, then rename it.\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slots[0].port.name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    // Rename slot-0 connections, drop higher-slot connections.\n    await update_target_connections([slots[0].port.name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: base }));\n    if (drop_names.length > 0) {\n      await update_target_connections(drop_names, () => null);\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append `<base>_<last+1>` to box.inputs.\n  async function add_variadic_slot(base) {\n    const next = last_variadic_index(current_box, base) + 1;\n    current_box.inputs.push({ name: base + '_' + next, type: 'any' });\n    await save();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Higher slots in the\n  // same group rename down by one. Connections targeting the removed\n  // slot are dropped; connections targeting renamed slots get their\n  // to_input rewritten on both endpoints.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Drop the slot.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n\n    // Rename higher slots down by one.\n    const renames = [];  // [{ old: 'text_3', new: 'text_2' }, ...]\n    current_box.inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const ppv = parse_variadic_name(p.name);\n      if (ppv && ppv.base === pv.base && ppv.index > pv.index) {\n        const new_name = pv.base + '_' + (ppv.index - 1);\n        renames.push({ old: p.name, new: new_name });\n        current_box.inputs[i].name = new_name;\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Drop connections to the removed slot. Renames go in ascending\n    // order so we never collide with an existing slot's name (we just\n    // freed it up by the previous rename).\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n    renames.sort((a, b) => parse_variadic_name(a.old).index - parse_variadic_name(b.old).index);\n    for (const r of renames) {\n      await update_target_connections([r.old], c => ({ ...c, to_input: r.new }));\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}",
    "newString":"  // Toggle a non-variadic input ON: rename `text` → `text_0`, add base\n  // to box.variadic_inputs, update incoming connections.\n  // Special case: a port literally named `...` (Lua variadic that the\n  // file-browser parser left in place) gets renamed to `args_0` with\n  // base `args` — there's no other sensible name we can derive.\n  async function make_variadic(port_name) {\n    const idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === port_name);\n    if (idx < 0) return;\n\n    const base     = port_name === '...' ? 'args' : port_name;\n    const new_name = base + '_0';\n    const old_name = port_name;\n\n    current_box.inputs[idx].name = new_name;\n    current_box.variadic_inputs  = current_box.variadic_inputs || [];\n    if (!current_box.variadic_inputs.includes(base)) {\n      current_box.variadic_inputs.push(base);\n    }\n\n    await update_target_connections([old_name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: new_name }));\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Higher-indexed slots are deleted along with their incoming wires.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Drop higher slots from box.inputs.\n    const drop_names = slots.slice(1).map(s => s.port.name);\n\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    // Re-resolve slot 0's index after the filter, then rename it.\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slots[0].port.name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    // Rename slot-0 connections, drop higher-slot connections.\n    await update_target_connections([slots[0].port.name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: base }));\n    if (drop_names.length > 0) {\n      await update_target_connections(drop_names, () => null);\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append `<base>_<last+1>` to box.inputs. Idempotent if no slot grows\n  // would be needed (caller checks). Used by the wire-connect and\n  // value-set auto-grow paths and by sibling code in the wires module.\n  async function add_variadic_slot(base) {\n    const next = last_variadic_index(current_box, base) + 1;\n    current_box.inputs.push({ name: base + '_' + next, type: 'any' });\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Higher slots in the\n  // same group rename down by one. Connections targeting the removed\n  // slot are dropped; connections targeting renamed slots get their\n  // to_input rewritten on both endpoints.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Drop the slot.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n\n    // Rename higher slots down by one.\n    const renames = [];  // [{ old: 'text_3', new: 'text_2' }, ...]\n    current_box.inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const ppv = parse_variadic_name(p.name);\n      if (ppv && ppv.base === pv.base && ppv.index > pv.index) {\n        const new_name = pv.base + '_' + (ppv.index - 1);\n        renames.push({ old: p.name, new: new_name });\n        current_box.inputs[i].name = new_name;\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Drop connections to the removed slot. Renames go in ascending\n    // order so we never collide with an existing slot's name (we just\n    // freed it up by the previous rename).\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n    renames.sort((a, b) => parse_variadic_name(a.old).index - parse_variadic_name(b.old).index);\n    for (const r of renames) {\n      await update_target_connections([r.old], c => ({ ...c, to_input: r.new }));\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Sever every outgoing wire from this box. Used when toggling the\n  // comparator on/off — wires from null-output and lt/eq/gt outputs\n  // can't all be valid at once, so we wipe the slate on either toggle\n  // direction. Also clears any selected wire if it pointed at one of\n  // the removed connections.\n  async function sever_output_wires() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const out   = (current_box.connections || []).filter(c => c.from_box === my_id);\n    if (out.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Collect destinations whose connection records also need cleaning.\n    const dest_ids = new Set();\n    out.forEach(c => dest_ids.add(c.to_box));\n\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => c.from_box !== my_id);\n\n    await Promise.all(Array.from(dest_ids).map(async dst_id => {\n      try {\n        const dst = await API.get_box(dst_id);\n        dst.connections = (dst.connections || []).filter(c => c.from_box !== my_id);\n        await API.put_box(dst_id, dst);\n        Boxes.boxes[dst_id] = dst;\n      } catch (e) {\n        console.error('failed to sever wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message);\n      }\n    }));\n\n    status_msg('cleared ' + out.length + ' outgoing wire(s)');\n  }\n\n  // Auto-grow check used by the wire-connect path and the value-set\n  // path. If `slot_name` is the LAST slot of a variadic group on\n  // `box`, append a new empty slot and persist. Idempotent — calling\n  // again on the same slot is a no-op because it's no longer last.\n  // Exported via the Inspector return so other modules (Wires) can call\n  // it after creating a connection.\n  async function auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n    if (!(box.variadic_inputs || []).includes(pv.base)) return;\n    if (pv.index !== last_variadic_index(box, pv.base)) return;\n\n    box.inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    box.inputs.push({ name: pv.base + '_' + (pv.index + 1), type: 'any' });\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(box.id, box);\n      Boxes.boxes[box.id] = box;\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      // If this was the currently-shown box, refresh the inspector too.\n      if (current_box && current_box.id === box.id) {\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('auto-grow failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",

They sit in the connections array invisibly. = btn_style;\n            x_btn.textContent   = '×';\n            x_btn.title         = 'remove this slot';\n            x_btn.onclick       = () => remove_variadic_slot(p.name);\n            row.appendChild(x_btn);\n          }\n          if (pv.index === group_last) {\n            // Last slot offers the \"+\" to grow the group.\n            const plus_btn = document.createElement('button');\n            plus_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n            plus_btn.textContent   = '+';\n            plus_btn.title         = 'add another slot to this variadic input';\n            plus_btn.onclick       = () => add_variadic_slot(pv.base);\n            row.appendChild(plus_btn);\n          }\n        }",
    "newString":"          // Auto-grow the variadic group when a value lands on its last\n          // slot. Idempotent — once the group has grown, this slot is\n          // no longer the last and the call is a no-op.\n          if (new_val !== undefined && current_box && in_var_group &&\n              pv.index === last_variadic_index(current_box, pv.base)) {\n            await auto_grow_after_set(current_box, p.name);\n          }\n\n          save();\n        });\n        row.appendChild(val_inp);\n\n        // Variadic control buttons. Two states a port row can be in:\n        //   1. Plain port (not variadic): show a \"var\" toggle that turns it on.\n        //   2. First slot of a variadic group (index 0): show \"var ×\"\n        //      to collapse the group back to a single port.\n        //   3. Non-first slot in a variadic group: show \"×\" to remove it.\n        //\n        // No \"+\" button — slots auto-grow when wired or when a value is\n        // set on the last slot.\n        const btn_style = 'background:none;border:1px solid #2a2f45;border-radius:3px;' +\n          'color:#6c72a0;cursor:pointer;font-family:monospace;font-size:9px;' +\n          'padding:1px 5px;line-height:1.4;';\n\n        if (!in_var_group) {\n          // Plain port — offer the variadic toggle.\n          const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n          var_btn.textContent   = 'var';\n          var_btn.title         = 'mark this input as variadic (grows to N slots)';\n          var_btn.onclick       = () => make_variadic(p.name);\n          row.appendChild(var_btn);\n        } else if (pv.index === 0) {\n          // First slot of a variadic group: collapse-back toggle.\n          const var_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          var_btn.style.cssText = btn_style + 'border-color:#4a9eff;color:#4a9eff;';\n          var_btn.textContent   = 'var ×';\n          var_btn.title         = 'collapse back to a single non-variadic input';\n          var_btn.onclick       = () => unmake_variadic(pv.base);\n          row.appendChild(var_btn);\n        } else {\n          // Non-first variadic slot: remove this slot.\n          const x_btn = document.createElement('button');\n          x_btn.style.cssText = btn_style;\n          x_btn.textContent   = '×';\n          x_btn.title         = 'remove this slot';\n          x_btn.onclick       = () => remove_variadic_slot(p.name);\n          row.appendChild(x_btn);\n        }",
    "userModified":false
