    "originalFile":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n      const branch_str = wire.from_branch ? '.' + wire.from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('wire ' + wire.from_box + branch_str + ' → ' + wire.to_box + '.' +\n        wire.to_input + ' — press Delete to remove');\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(from_box_id),\n        API.get_box(to_box_id),\n      ]);\n\n      const conn = {\n        from_box:    from_box_id,\n        from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n        to_box:      to_box_id,\n        to_input:    to_input,\n      };\n\n      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n      // avoid duplicates\n      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n      );\n      if (dup) return;\n\n      src_box.connections.push(conn);\n      dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      // update local cache\n      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;\n\n      const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(conn.from_box),\n        API.get_box(conn.to_box),\n      ]);\n\n      const match = c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;\n\n      _selected_wire = null;\n      status_msg('deleted connection');\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

      }],

  },

  "userType":"external",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/224-editable-port-names-and-canvas-value-edit.md",
    "content":"# 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput port names are read-only labels in the inspector — derived from\nthe function's parameter names when the file browser populates the\nbox (issue 207, 208). Each port row in the inspector also carries a\nliteral value input. With variadic inputs (issue 217), a box with\nseveral slots produces a tall, narrow list of name+type+value rows\nthat crowds the sidebar.\n\nThe canvas already renders port names next to their dots, so the\nname appears twice — once on the canvas (read-only label) and once\nin the inspector (read-only label).\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nMove both the port name and the literal value input out of the\ninspector and onto the canvas next to the port dot. The inspector\nkeeps only the variadic toggle / remove-slot buttons and any\nnon-port box-level fields (ref / fn / comparator).\n\n### Why\n\n- The inspector is crowded with redundant data (the canvas already\n  shows port names).\n- Literal values often need more horizontal room than a 72px input\n  field allows, especially for prompts, paths, or JSON snippets.\n- Reading the box's full configuration without clicking through the\n  inspector becomes possible — every input's name and value is\n  visible directly on the canvas.\n- 208's \"read-only port names\" decision was about preventing typo\n  drift between source code and box JSON; the file browser still\n  populates names from the parsed signature, but the user should be\n  free to override them after the fact.\n\n### Reverses 208's read-only-name decision\n\nIssue 208 made input port names non-editable on the principle that\nthey should match the parsed function signature exactly. This issue\nflips that — names become editable again, with the trade-off that a\ntypo can desynchronize the editor's record from the function the box\ncalls. The cost is a per-box runtime error rather than a hidden\nsilent skip, so it surfaces clearly. The benefit is that users can\nrename inputs freely (renaming a Lua function's parameter and then\nupdating the box does not require re-browsing).\n\n### Layout\n\nEach input port row on the canvas becomes:\n\n```\n●  text_0    ┌──────────────────┐\n             │ \"hello world\"    │\n             └──────────────────┘\n```\n\n- The port dot stays on the box's left edge (unchanged).\n- The port name is an editable text field, rendered as an HTML\n  overlay positioned next to the dot. Pan and zoom adjust the\n  overlay's transform to match the canvas.\n- The literal value field is another HTML overlay below or to the\n  right of the name.\n\n### HTML overlays over the canvas\n\nCanvas 2D doesn't do native text inputs, so the editable fields are\nDOM `<input>` elements absolutely positioned over the canvas. A\nsmall per-box overlay container holds them, transforms with the\ncamera (CSS transform applied on every render frame), and updates\nthe underlying `box.inputs[i]` on input.\n\nThis is the same pattern as the source viewer (issue 215) — DOM\nelements layered over the canvas, with positions computed from\n`Canvas.world_to_screen`. The complexity is keeping overlay state\nin sync with the canvas: they need to be created when a box is\nloaded, destroyed when a box is deleted, repositioned every frame\n(or when pan/zoom changes), and hidden when off-screen.\n\n### Inspector becomes lighter\n\nAfter this change the inspector shows:\n- Box label (editable)\n- ref / fn (with browse / view buttons)\n- For each input: the variadic toggle (`var` / `var ×` / `×`) only.\n  No name field, no value field — those live on the canvas.\n- Output: the comparator toggle and comparand input (unchanged).\n- Delete-box button (unchanged).\n\nRoughly half the height the current inspector takes for variadic\nboxes.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Overlay performance**: dozens of overlays multiplied by frequent\n  pan/zoom updates is a real cost. Tests are needed; a bounding-box\n  cull (only render overlays for visible boxes) is the obvious\n  optimization if it matters.\n- **Value-input width**: the field grows with the input's content, or\n  is a fixed width with horizontal scroll? Probably grow-on-content\n  with a max width clamp, similar to what monospace text does.\n- **Editing port names while wires are connected**: renaming a port\n  while a wire is attached should rename the wire's `to_input` /\n  `from_branch` on both endpoints atomically — same bilateral-update\n  pattern the variadic ops use.\n- **Name validation**: what's a valid port name? Probably `[A-Za-z_][\\w]*`\n  (a Lua / C / shell-compatible identifier). Reject names that start\n  with digits, contain spaces, etc. Reject duplicates within a box.\n- **Backward compat**: existing maps with the current layout work as\n  before — no migration needed. The change is purely UI.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Create `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` (new module) responsible\n   for per-box DOM overlays. Public API: `update_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   to create / refresh overlays for a box, `remove_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   on box deletion, `redraw_overlays()` on pan/zoom.\n2. Wire the overlays into the render loop: after `Boxes.draw_all`,\n   call `redraw_overlays()` to reposition the overlays for the\n   current camera. The overlays themselves don't redraw — only their\n   `style.left` / `style.top` / `style.transform` updates.\n3. Remove the name + value rendering from `mk_port_display` in\n   `004-inspector.js`. Leave only the variadic controls.\n4. Remove the canvas-side port name labels from `002-boxes.js::draw_box`\n   (the overlay's editable input replaces it).\n5. Wire validation: name must be a valid identifier and unique\n   within the box's `inputs`. Validate in the input's `oninput`\n   handler; revert to the previous valid name on rejection.\n6. Test against `maps/hello`, `maps/classify-demo`, and a fresh map\n   with variadic inputs (e.g. via `libs/text.lua`'s concat).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — port name labels move out\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `mk_port_display` simplified\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — pan/zoom triggers overlay reposition\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — render loop calls overlay redraw\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire-connect/rename touches names\n- `issues/completed/208-port-literal-values.md` — the read-only-names\n  decision that this issue flips\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — variadic UI that\n  drove the inspector-crowding observation\n"
  },
  "uuid":"bc4c29dc-a379-4b62-b661-c6e4c483c818",
  "parentUuid":"b3f0e001-5083-4bd1-8d07-c94117e766b1",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "sourceToolAssistantUUID":"b3f0e001-5083-4bd1-8d07-c94117e766b1",

  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

    "originalFile":"# Phase 2 Progress\n\nGoal: an editor you can actually use to build maps, plus the graph\nmodel the phase 3 runtime will consume.\n\n## Issues\n\n| ID   | Title                                          | Status   |\n|------|------------------------------------------------|----------|\n| 201  | fix box rendering closure bug                  | complete |\n| 202  | fit-to-view on map load                        | complete |\n| 203  | map picker panel                               | complete |\n| 204  | visible interaction hints                      | complete |\n| 206  | entry box designation                          | won't implement |\n| 207  | source file browser and port auto-population   | complete |\n| 208  | port literal values                            | complete |\n| 209  | ollama query library                           | complete |\n| 210  | comparator wire branching                      | complete |\n| 211  | file browser library directories               | complete |\n| 211a | unify src/ into same directory pipeline        | complete |\n| 212  | editor interaction modes                       | complete |\n| 213  | queued inputs and task model                   | open     |\n| 214  | tmp symlink recreation on reboot               | complete |\n| 215  | view source button                             | complete |\n| 223  | syntax highlighting via user-written lexers    | open     |\n| 216  | read-file box                                  | open     |\n| 217  | concat box and dynamic inputs                  | open     |\n| 218  | enforce single-output driver contract          | complete |\n| 219  | map compiler                                   | open     |\n| 220  | root run script and entry point cleanup        | complete |\n| 221  | iterator box                                   | open     |\n| 222  | compile button and assets directory            | complete |\n\n## Phase goal checklist\n\n- [x] Boxes render on map load\n- [x] Clicking a box opens the inspector\n- [x] Ref/fn set by browsing src/ files; ports auto-derived\n- [x] Map loads centered on screen (fit-to-view)\n- [x] Map can be switched from a list, not a text prompt\n- [x] Empty canvas shows interaction hints\n- [—] Entry box marker (won't implement — phase 3 auto-detects, see 305)\n- [ ] Comparator routing replaces the old branch box (issue 210)\n- [ ] Iterator box with auto-grow output slots (issue 221)\n- [x] Compile button (issue 222) — placeholder UI for the phase 3 build\n\n## Notes on graph model changes during phase 2\n\nThese are not new features so much as model corrections that shape\nwhat phase 3 will consume:\n\n- **Single-output rule** (218, complete): every box has exactly one\n  output wire. The driver contract emits one JSON value, not an\n  array.\n- **Comparator-based branching** (210, complete): the old `branch`\n  box kind with named ports is removed. A box may carry a\n  `comparand`; the dispatch layer fires the connection whose\n  `from_branch` matches `lt` / `eq` / `gt`.\n- **Iterator routing** (221): a box with `iterator_outputs` is a\n  pure routing primitive; the dispatch layer rotates through the\n  declared output names. Iterators have no `ref` / `fn`.\n- **Connection schema**: `from_branch` field replaces the old\n  `from_output` / `from_port` dual-field design.\n",

      "content":"  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, path?, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n    // collapsed state: set of group labels\n    const collapsed = new Set();\n\n    // all browseable dirs come from one endpoint — src/ is no longer a special case\n    let src_dirs = [];\n    try {\n      src_dirs = await API.list_extra_src().catch(() => []);\n    } catch (e) {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">load error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // build group list — every entry has a path; no exceptions\n    const groups = [];\n    (src_dirs || []).forEach(d => {\n      if (d.files && d.files.length > 0) {\n        groups.push({\n          label:      d.label + '/',\n          path:       d.path,\n          files:      d.files,\n          fetch_file: f => API.get_extra_src_file(d.index, f),\n        });\n      }\n    });\n\n    const show_file_list = () => {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // add-library-dir button\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ library dir';\n      add_btn.className   = 'fb-add-dir-btn';\n      add_btn.onclick = () => {\n        // open picker at parent of last known dir so the user lands near recent work\n        const last = groups.length > 0 ? groups[groups.length - 1].path : null;\n        const initial = last ? (last.replace(/\\/[^/]+$/, '') || '/') : '/home';\n        show_dir_picker(container,\n          async (path) => {\n            try {\n              const meta = await API.get_meta();\n              // derive current list from groups, not meta.src_dirs:\n              // groups already reflects the server-migrated state (extra_src_dirs + src/),\n              // whereas meta.src_dirs is absent on old maps and would discard prior entries\n              const current = groups.map(g => g.path);\n              if (!current.includes(path)) {\n                current.push(path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: current });\n              }\n              render(container, on_select);\n            } catch(e) {\n              show_file_list();\n              const note = document.createElement('div');\n              note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n              note.textContent = 'could not save dir: ' + e.message;\n              container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n            }\n          },\n          () => show_file_list(),\n          initial\n        );\n      };\n      container.appendChild(add_btn);\n\n      if (groups.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = 'src/ is empty — add source files or a library dir';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      groups.forEach(group => {\n        // use full path as the collapse key for extra dirs so same-named dirs don't share state\n        const collapse_key = group.path || group.label;\n        const is_collapsed = collapsed.has(collapse_key);\n\n        // group header row with toggle\n        const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n        hdr.className = 'fb-group-hdr';\n\n        const toggle = document.createElement('span');\n        toggle.className   = 'fb-group-toggle';\n        toggle.textContent = is_collapsed ? '▶' : '▼';\n        hdr.appendChild(toggle);\n\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n        lbl.textContent = group.label;\n        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(collapse_key)) collapsed.delete(collapse_key);\n          else collapsed.add(collapse_key);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n\n        // right-click on any dir header: offer \"hide directory\"\n        hdr.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => {\n          e.preventDefault();\n          show_fb_ctx_menu(e.clientX, e.clientY, [{\n            label:  'hide directory',\n            danger: true,\n            action: async () => {\n              try {\n                const meta = await API.get_meta();\n                // same migration rationale as add: use groups as source of truth\n                const dirs = groups.map(g => g.path).filter(p => p !== group.path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: dirs });\n                render(container, on_select);\n              } catch (err) {\n                show_file_list();\n                const note = document.createElement('div');\n                note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n                note.textContent = 'could not hide dir: ' + err.message;\n                container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n              }\n            },\n          }]);\n        });\n\n        container.appendChild(hdr);\n\n        if (is_collapsed) return;\n\n        group.files.forEach(filename => {\n          const row = document.createElement('div');\n          row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n          row.textContent = filename;\n          row.onclick     = async () => {\n            row.textContent = filename + ' …';\n            let content;\n            try {\n              content = await group.fetch_file(filename);\n            } catch (e) {\n              container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">could not read ' + filename + ': ' + e.message + '</div>';\n              show_file_list();\n              return;\n            }\n            const fns = parse_functions(content, filename);\n            render_fn_list(container, group.label + filename, fns,\n              (f, fn) => on_select(f, fn),\n              show_file_list\n            );\n          };\n          container.appendChild(row);\n        });\n      });\n    };\n\n    show_file_list();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { parse_functions, render };\n})();\n"

      "content":"Middle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires.           "new_string":"## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Future development ideas\n\n### Language-spec-driven variadic detection\n\nCurrently the editor uses hard-coded heuristics per language to find\nvariadic indicators in a function signature (Lua: literal `...`, Bash:\n`$@` after `shift`). The cleaner architecture mirrors the phase 3\nlanguage-spec model (issue 303): each language declares its own way\nto recognize and surface variadic parameters, and the file-browser\nparser asks the language spec rather than embedding the rules.\n\nConcretely, the editor side of a language spec\n(`langs/<name>/lexer.js` or a sibling `parser.js`) could expose:\n\n```js\n// Returns { name, inputs: [\"sep\", \"text\"], variadic_inputs: [\"text\"] }\n// for `function M.concat(sep, ...)` in Lua, or\n// `concat() { local sep=\"$1\"; shift; ... \"$@\" }` in Bash.\nfunction parse_function_signature(source, fn_name) { ... }\n```\n\nThe editor still calls the same on-select handler; the language spec\nis responsible for deciding how to translate native variadic syntax\ninto the editor's `(inputs, variadic_inputs)` model.\n\n### Variadic shapes that don't map cleanly to an array\n\nThe current model assumes variadic = an ordered series of positional\nslots. That fits Lua `...`, C `va_list`, Bash `\"$@\"`, JavaScript rest\nparams, etc. It does not fit:\n\n- **Keyword arguments** (Python `**kwargs`, Ruby keyword splats) —\n  these are key/value pairs, not positional. A box would need\n  named-slot pairs the user labels per slot, not auto-numbered\n  `_0` / `_1` / `_2`.\n- **Tagged unions / discriminated lists** (Rust enum lists, Haskell\n  variadic via heterogeneous lists) — each entry has a type tag in\n  addition to a value. Two-field slots, or per-slot type metadata.\n- **Streaming inputs** (generators, channels, iterators) — the\n  consumer doesn't know in advance how many values arrive. This is\n  closer to issue 213's queued-input model than to variadic.\n\nA future revision of the editor's variadic UI could let language\nspecs choose between several \"variadic shapes\":\n\n| shape           | slot model                          | example use      |\n|-----------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|\n| `positional`    | `<base>_<index>` ordered (current)  | Lua `...`        |\n| `keyed`         | per-slot `(key, value)` pairs       | Python `**kwargs`|\n| `tagged`        | per-slot `(tag, value)` pairs       | discriminated unions |\n| `stream`        | one slot, queued (issue 213)        | iterators        |\n\nEach shape would have its own auto-grow rule and inspector controls.\nThe language spec declares which shape applies to a given variadic\nparameter, and the editor renders accordingly.\n\nThis is speculative — the positional shape covers every shipped\nlanguage so far. Capturing it here so the design door stays open.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md",

Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`."

    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\nNote: one output wire per box is a deliberate design constraint, not a missing\nfeature. Positional multi-output was explicitly rejected as fragile (multiple\nreturn statements with the same tuple width are indistinguishable). The\ncomparator (lt/eq/gt branching) is the only multi-path mechanism. Whatever the\nfunction returns goes down the single output wire as one value — arrays or JSON\nobjects if multiple values need to travel together.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding side on the source box (connections are stored in both\n     endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.",
    "newString":"## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Future development ideas\n\n### Language-spec-driven variadic detection\n\nCurrently the editor uses hard-coded heuristics per language to find\nvariadic indicators in a function signature (Lua: literal `...`, Bash:\n`$@` after `shift`). The cleaner architecture mirrors the phase 3\nlanguage-spec model (issue 303): each language declares its own way\nto recognize and surface variadic parameters, and the file-browser\nparser asks the language spec rather than embedding the rules.\n\nConcretely, the editor side of a language spec\n(`langs/<name>/lexer.js` or a sibling `parser.js`) could expose:\n\n```js\n// Returns { name, inputs: [\"sep\", \"text\"], variadic_inputs: [\"text\"] }\n// for `function M.concat(sep, ...)` in Lua, or\n// `concat() { local sep=\"$1\"; shift; ... \"$@\" }` in Bash.\nfunction parse_function_signature(source, fn_name) { ... }\n```\n\nThe editor still calls the same on-select handler; the language spec\nis responsible for deciding how to translate native variadic syntax\ninto the editor's `(inputs, variadic_inputs)` model.\n\n### Variadic shapes that don't map cleanly to an array\n\nThe current model assumes variadic = an ordered series of positional\nslots. That fits Lua `...`, C `va_list`, Bash `\"$@\"`, JavaScript rest\nparams, etc. It does not fit:\n\n- **Keyword arguments** (Python `**kwargs`, Ruby keyword splats) —\n  these are key/value pairs, not positional. A box would need\n  named-slot pairs the user labels per slot, not auto-numbered\n  `_0` / `_1` / `_2`.\n- **Tagged unions / discriminated lists** (Rust enum lists, Haskell\n  variadic via heterogeneous lists) — each entry has a type tag in\n  addition to a value. Two-field slots, or per-slot type metadata.\n- **Streaming inputs** (generators, channels, iterators) — the\n  consumer doesn't know in advance how many values arrive. This is\n  closer to issue 213's queued-input model than to variadic.\n\nA future revision of the editor's variadic UI could let language\nspecs choose between several \"variadic shapes\":\n\n| shape           | slot model                          | example use      |\n|-----------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|\n| `positional`    | `<base>_<index>` ordered (current)  | Lua `...`        |\n| `keyed`         | per-slot `(key, value)` pairs       | Python `**kwargs`|\n| `tagged`        | per-slot `(tag, value)` pairs       | discriminated unions |\n| `stream`        | one slot, queued (issue 213)        | iterators        |\n\nEach shape would have its own auto-grow rule and inspector controls.\nThe language spec declares which shape applies to a given variadic\nparameter, and the editor renders accordingly.\n\nThis is speculative — the positional shape covers every shipped\nlanguage so far. Capturing it here so the design door stays open.",

    "userModified":false
  },

    "content":"# 225 — Directory picker: show files alongside dirs, distinguish them visually\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the user clicks \"+ library dir\" in the file browser, the\ndirectory picker (`show_dir_picker` in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)\nfetches the directory contents via `API.list_dirs(path)`, which\nreturns `{ path, dirs }`. Only the subdirectories are rendered; any\nsource files in the current directory are invisible.\n\nThis makes navigation harder than it should be — there's no visible\nconfirmation that you've reached the right directory until you click\n\"use this directory\" and the file list re-renders.\n\nThe list itself uses the `.fb-file-row` class for both dirs and the\nparent-directory `..` row, so dirs and the (currently absent) files\nwould render identically. There's no visual cue distinguishing\n\"this is a directory I can enter\" from \"this is a file I'd see if I\npicked this directory.\"\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe directory picker shows both subdirectories and source files in\nthe current directory.\n\n- **Directories**: clickable, navigate into them on click, render\n  with a visual marker (icon, prefix, color, underline, or\n  combination — see \"Visual differentiation\" below).\n- **Files**: shown as a read-only list — they can't be picked\n  individually here (this is a directory picker), but their\n  presence tells the user what they'd be importing if they picked\n  this directory.\n\n### Visual differentiation: dir vs file\n\nThree approaches; pick one or layer them.\n\n1. **Icon prefix** — a small character before the name. `📁` for\n   dirs and `📄` for files, or pure-text alternatives like `▸ /`\n   and `· `. Friendly to colorblind users.\n2. **Color** — directories in the editor's blue accent\n   (`#4a9eff`), files in dim gray (`#6c72a0`). Easy to do but\n   inaccessible alone.\n3. **Underline** — directories underlined to suggest \"clickable\n   link\". Already a familiar web idiom. Pairs well with color.\n\nRecommendation: layer (1) and (2) — icon prefix for accessibility,\ncolor for at-a-glance identification. The icon doesn't have to be\nemoji; ASCII glyphs like `>` for dirs and `·` for files are\nunambiguous and font-portable.\n\n### Implementation notes\n\nThe server endpoint `/fs/dirs` currently returns `{ path, dirs }`.\nEither:\n\n- Extend the response to `{ path, dirs, files }`, where `files` is\n  an array of source-file basenames in the current directory. The\n  server filters by extension to avoid listing every file (only\n  show `.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`, etc., matching what the language specs\n  declare).\n- Or add a sibling endpoint `/fs/files?path=…` and call both in\n  parallel from the picker.\n\nExtending the existing endpoint is simpler. The filter\n(file-extensions to include) lives server-side and references\n`langs/*/spec.so`'s `file_ext` field at startup once phase 3\nships; in phase 2 we hard-code the current set\n(`.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/006-server-main.lua` — extend the `/fs/dirs` handler to also\n   return matching source files. Filter by a small allowlist of\n   extensions for now.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js::list_dirs` — already returns the response\n   verbatim, so just consume the new `files` field.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::show_dir_picker` — render files\n   below the directory list, in dim color, non-clickable.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add CSS classes `.fb-dir-row` and\n   `.fb-file-row-readonly` (or reuse the existing `.fb-file-row`\n   with a modifier class). Icon prefix added via a `::before`\n   pseudo-element or a leading span.\n5. The same icon/color treatment optionally applies to the main\n   file list (`render` function), which currently uses\n   `.fb-file-row` for clickable file entries — they'd get the file\n   icon + dim color while keeping their click behavior.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should files in the dir picker be clickable to \"preview\" their\n  contents (open the source viewer from issue 215)? Probably not —\n  it adds a click target where there shouldn't be one. The user is\n  picking a directory, not a file. Defer.\n- Which icon set: ASCII (`>`, `·`) or unicode glyphs (`▸`, `·`) or\n  emoji (`📁`, `📄`)? ASCII / unicode for portability; emoji\n  rendering varies wildly across systems.\n- Should the file list hide when collapsed (collapsible group\n  header)? Probably not necessary for the picker — the file list\n  is informational, and short.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — `show_dir_picker`, file rendering\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — `/fs/dirs` handler\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — `list_dirs` API call\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for `.fb-file-row` etc.\n- `issues/completed/207-source-file-browser-and-port-population.md`\n  — original file browser issue\n"
  },

    "content":[{
        "type":"tool_use",
        "name":"Write",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 226 — Hide output port and inspector output section when the function returns nothing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the file browser parses a function that has no return values\n(e.g. `function M.write_result(text) print(text) end` — sink, no\nreturns), the on-select handler sets `box.inputs` from the parsed\nsignature but doesn't carry through any \"this function has no\noutput\" signal. The inspector then renders the output section\n(comparator toggle + comparand input) for every call box,\nunconditionally, and the canvas draws an output port dot.\n\nThe UI implies you can wire from the output, but at runtime the\nfunction returns nil and the wire just propagates a nil value.\nVisually noisy; conceptually misleading.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box whose function has no return values:\n- Has no output port dot on the canvas.\n- Has no output section in the inspector (no compare toggle, no\n  comparand input, no output area at all).\n- Cannot have outgoing wires drawn from it. The wire-drawing\n  interaction in `005-app.js` skips it because there's no output\n  port to grab.\n\nThe single-output-wire-per-box rule from issue 218 still holds for\nboxes with return values; this issue carves out the explicit \"no\noutput\" case.\n\n## Where the signal comes from\n\nThe Lua and Bash parsers in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` already\nreturn a `fn.outputs` array — empty when the function has no\nreturn statements. The on-select handler currently does not store\nthis on the box. The fix is to persist a boolean flag (or the\nempty `outputs` array itself) so the inspector and canvas can\ncheck it.\n\nTwo options:\n\n1. **Persist `box.has_output: false`** when the parser detects no\n   return values. The inspector and canvas check this field. New\n   field, but unambiguous.\n2. **Persist `box.outputs: []`** (the empty array). The inspector\n   and canvas treat `box.outputs === []` as \"no output.\" Reuses\n   the legacy field that was previously used for named output\n   ports (issue 210 superseded it; this gives it a new\n   single-purpose meaning).\n\nOption 1 is cleaner because the name says exactly what it means.\nOption 2 reuses an existing-but-stale field, which has the\nadvantage of zero schema churn but the disadvantage of overloading\nthe field's meaning. Lean toward option 1.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- **Manually-added boxes** that haven't been wired through the\n  file browser: no information about return values exists. Default\n  to `has_output: true` (current behavior). The user can flip it\n  manually if they want a sink box without going through the file\n  browser.\n- **Functions whose return value depends on a branch** (some\n  return, some don't): the parser already lists every distinct\n  return shape. As long as ANY return statement exists, treat the\n  function as having an output. `has_output: false` only when\n  zero return statements.\n- **Comparator toggle**: if the user activates the comparator on\n  a non-output box, that's nonsensical (there's no value to\n  compare). The comparator UI only renders when the box has an\n  output anyway, so this falls out naturally.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::on_select` (in\n   `004-inspector.js`) — when `fn.outputs.length === 0`, set\n   `current_box.has_output = false`. Otherwise delete the field\n   (treat absence as `true`).\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — wrap the entire output\n   section render in `if (box.has_output !== false) { ... }`.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — when\n   `box.has_output === false`, return an empty `outputs` array.\n   `draw_box` already iterates `outputs` and draws nothing for an\n   empty array.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — early-out if the\n   `from_box` has `has_output === false` (defensive — the canvas\n   wouldn't have a port to grab from, but cover the edge case).\n5. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `has_output` as an optional\n   boolean field. No validation beyond type-check.\n6. Test: open the hello map, look at `write-result` (which is a\n   sink). After re-browsing it through the file browser, output\n   port should disappear. Existing wires from a now-output-less\n   box are dropped on save (preferable to dangling).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should existing wires from a box that flips to `has_output:\n  false` be dropped automatically, or should the flip be rejected\n  if any outgoing wires exist? Auto-drop with a status-bar\n  warning is the smoother path.\n- Should the file browser do this automatically on every re-pick,\n  or only the first time a function is selected? Doing it every\n  time matches what we do for `box.inputs` (always overwritten on\n  re-select), and keeps the box's `has_output` flag in sync with\n  the actual function.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show` (output section render),\n  `open_browser` (on-select handler that sets the flag)\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — parsers that detect zero returns\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `port_positions`, `draw_box`\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `create_connection` (defensive check)\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts `has_output`\n- `issues/completed/218-enforce-single-output-driver-contract.md`\n  — single-wire rule that this issue qualifies\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/226-hide-output-controls-for-no-return-functions.md"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01X96bSzHGpXwKwVrYVhndhG"

  "toolUseResult":{

    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/226-hide-output-controls-for-no-return-functions.md",
    "content":"# 226 — Hide output port and inspector output section when the function returns nothing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the file browser parses a function that has no return values\n(e.g. `function M.write_result(text) print(text) end` — sink, no\nreturns), the on-select handler sets `box.inputs` from the parsed\nsignature but doesn't carry through any \"this function has no\noutput\" signal. The inspector then renders the output section\n(comparator toggle + comparand input) for every call box,\nunconditionally, and the canvas draws an output port dot.\n\nThe UI implies you can wire from the output, but at runtime the\nfunction returns nil and the wire just propagates a nil value.\nVisually noisy; conceptually misleading.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box whose function has no return values:\n- Has no output port dot on the canvas.\n- Has no output section in the inspector (no compare toggle, no\n  comparand input, no output area at all).\n- Cannot have outgoing wires drawn from it. The wire-drawing\n  interaction in `005-app.js` skips it because there's no output\n  port to grab.\n\nThe single-output-wire-per-box rule from issue 218 still holds for\nboxes with return values; this issue carves out the explicit \"no\noutput\" case.\n\n## Where the signal comes from\n\nThe Lua and Bash parsers in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` already\nreturn a `fn.outputs` array — empty when the function has no\nreturn statements. The on-select handler currently does not store\nthis on the box. The fix is to persist a boolean flag (or the\nempty `outputs` array itself) so the inspector and canvas can\ncheck it.\n\nTwo options:\n\n1. **Persist `box.has_output: false`** when the parser detects no\n   return values. The inspector and canvas check this field. New\n   field, but unambiguous.\n2. **Persist `box.outputs: []`** (the empty array). The inspector\n   and canvas treat `box.outputs === []` as \"no output.\" Reuses\n   the legacy field that was previously used for named output\n   ports (issue 210 superseded it; this gives it a new\n   single-purpose meaning).\n\nOption 1 is cleaner because the name says exactly what it means.\nOption 2 reuses an existing-but-stale field, which has the\nadvantage of zero schema churn but the disadvantage of overloading\nthe field's meaning. Lean toward option 1.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- **Manually-added boxes** that haven't been wired through the\n  file browser: no information about return values exists. Default\n  to `has_output: true` (current behavior). The user can flip it\n  manually if they want a sink box without going through the file\n  browser.\n- **Functions whose return value depends on a branch** (some\n  return, some don't): the parser already lists every distinct\n  return shape. As long as ANY return statement exists, treat the\n  function as having an output. `has_output: false` only when\n  zero return statements.\n- **Comparator toggle**: if the user activates the comparator on\n  a non-output box, that's nonsensical (there's no value to\n  compare). The comparator UI only renders when the box has an\n  output anyway, so this falls out naturally.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::on_select` (in\n   `004-inspector.js`) — when `fn.outputs.length === 0`, set\n   `current_box.has_output = false`. Otherwise delete the field\n   (treat absence as `true`).\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — wrap the entire output\n   section render in `if (box.has_output !== false) { ... }`.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — when\n   `box.has_output === false`, return an empty `outputs` array.\n   `draw_box` already iterates `outputs` and draws nothing for an\n   empty array.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — early-out if the\n   `from_box` has `has_output === false` (defensive — the canvas\n   wouldn't have a port to grab from, but cover the edge case).\n5. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `has_output` as an optional\n   boolean field. No validation beyond type-check.\n6. Test: open the hello map, look at `write-result` (which is a\n   sink). After re-browsing it through the file browser, output\n   port should disappear. Existing wires from a now-output-less\n   box are dropped on save (preferable to dangling).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should existing wires from a box that flips to `has_output:\n  false` be dropped automatically, or should the flip be rejected\n  if any outgoing wires exist? Auto-drop with a status-bar\n  warning is the smoother path.\n- Should the file browser do this automatically on every re-pick,\n  or only the first time a function is selected? Doing it every\n  time matches what we do for `box.inputs` (always overwritten on\n  re-select), and keeps the box's `has_output` flag in sync with\n  the actual function.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show` (output section render),\n  `open_browser` (on-select handler that sets the flag)\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — parsers that detect zero returns\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `port_positions`, `draw_box`\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `create_connection` (defensive check)\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts `has_output`\n- `issues/completed/218-enforce-single-output-driver-contract.md`\n  — single-wire rule that this issue qualifies\n"
  },

          "new_string":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n**Part A** — `libs/text.lua` ships `M.concat(sep, ...)` and\n`M.split(text, sep)`. Concat is variadic to match the editor's\nvariadic-input model. Split returns a Lua array; the driver shim\nJSON-encodes for the single output wire. The accompanying\n`libs/text.lua.info.md` documents both functions.\n\n**Part B** — Variadic UI lives in `assets/js/004-inspector.js`:\n\n- Helpers (`parse_variadic_name`, `is_variadic_slot`,\n  `variadic_slots_for`, `last_variadic_index`) parse and query the\n  `<base>_<index>` naming convention for variadic slots.\n- `make_variadic(port_name)` toggles a non-variadic port into a\n  one-slot variadic group (rename `text` → `text_0`, add base to\n  `box.variadic_inputs`, update connection records on this box and\n  every upstream box).\n- `unmake_variadic(base)` collapses a group back to a single port\n  (drop higher slots and their wires, rename slot 0 back to base).\n- `add_variadic_slot(base)` appends `<base>_<last+1>`. Used by the\n  auto-grow path; also reachable directly when needed.\n- `remove_variadic_slot(slot_name)` drops a single slot and renames\n  higher slots down by one, updating connections atomically per\n  slot.\n- `auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name)` is the public-from-Inspector\n  helper. If `slot_name` is the last slot of its variadic group, it\n  appends a new empty slot. Idempotent — calling again on the same\n  slot is a no-op once the slot is no longer last.\n\nThe wire-create path (`006-wires.js::create_connection`) calls\n`Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input)` after a\nsuccessful PUT. The inspector's per-port value-input handler also\ncalls it when a non-empty literal value is set on a slot. Together\nthese cover both growth triggers — wire-connect and value-set.\n\nPer-port UI (`mk_port_display`):\n\n- Plain port → `var` toggle (turn variadic on).\n- First slot of a variadic group → `var ×` toggle (collapse back).\n- Non-first variadic slot → `×` (remove this slot only; higher\n  slots rename down).\n- No `+` button — slots auto-grow. Wire-disconnect and\n  value-clear do NOT shrink (only `×` removes structure).\n\nSchema accepts `variadic_inputs` as an optional array of strings\n(`src/001-schema.lua`).\n\nComparator toggle (`004-inspector.js::cmp_btn.onclick`) now severs\nall outgoing wires on either toggle direction, fixing the prior\nbehavior where lt/eq/gt wires from a previous comparator state\nsilently re-appeared when the user re-enabled it.\n\n## Deliberate omissions / follow-ups\n\n- **Auto-shrink on wire-disconnect** is intentionally not done —\n  the user explicitly chose \"explicit `×` is the only way to shrink\"\n  so transient editing doesn't lose structure.\n- **Editable port names** and **value editing on the canvas\n  itself** belong in issue 224 — bigger redesign than 217 covers.\n- **Future ideas** (language-spec-driven variadic detection,\n  alternative variadic shapes for keyword args / streams /\n  discriminated unions) are captured below.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md",

    "originalFile":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard concat box exists. No mechanism exists for a box to have a variable\nnumber of input wires on a single logical port.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### Part A — text library box\n`libs/text.lua` exposes two functions:\n\n`M.concat(sep, ...)` — join N strings:\n- `sep` — separator string (e.g. `\"\\n\\n\"`)\n- `...` — any number of text values to join (variadic)\n- returns a single `result` port\n\nThe function is variadic so its `text` input can expand to any count without\nmodifying the source file.\n\n`M.split(text, sep)` — split one string into parts:\n- `text` — the input string\n- `sep` — the separator to split on (plain string, not a pattern)\n- returns a single `result` port containing a JSON-encoded array of the parts\n\nOutput ports are named at wire-design time, so a variable number of runtime\nparts cannot map to separate wires. A JSON array on one port is the only\nconsistent design — the downstream box decodes it.\n\nNote: one output wire per box is a deliberate design constraint, not a missing\nfeature. Positional multi-output was explicitly rejected as fragile (multiple\nreturn statements with the same tuple width are indistinguishable). The\ncomparator (lt/eq/gt branching) is the only multi-path mechanism. Whatever the\nfunction returns goes down the single output wire as one value — arrays or JSON\nobjects if multiple values need to travel together.\n\n### Part B — per-input variadic flag\n\nVariadic is a property of a specific input port, not the box as a whole. A box\ncould have `sep` (fixed) and `text` (variadic). The inspector shows a toggle on\neach input to mark it variadic.\n\n#### Data model\n\nThe box JSON gains a `variadic_inputs` set (array of base names):\n```json\n{\n  \"inputs\": [\"sep\", \"text_0\", \"text_1\", \"text_2\"],\n  \"variadic_inputs\": [\"text\"]\n}\n```\n\nSlots of a variadic input are stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array.\nThe executor already passes all inputs positionally — no executor changes needed.\nConnections reference slots by their indexed name (`\"text_0\"`, `\"text_1\"`, etc.).\n\nThe parser (Lua: detects `...`, bash: detects `$@` after shift) can auto-populate\n`variadic_inputs` when a file is selected via the file browser. For other languages\n(C, etc.) the user sets the toggle manually in the inspector — the executor contract\nalready supports N positional args via `arg_count`, so C functions reading `argv[]`\nin a loop work without any changes.\n\n#### Auto-grow\nWhen a wire is connected to the LAST slot of a variadic input, the editor appends\na new empty slot (`text_N+1`) to `box.inputs` and saves the box. The new slot\nappears immediately as an open port.\n\n#### Auto-shrink\nWhen a wire is disconnected from any slot of a variadic input:\n1. Remove that slot from `box.inputs`.\n2. Rename all subsequent slots down by one (`text_2` → `text_1`, etc.).\n3. Update every connection that referenced a renamed slot:\n   - `to_input` in the connection record on this box\n   - The corresponding side on the source box (connections are stored in both\n     endpoint files; both must be updated atomically).\n4. Keep at least one slot for the variadic input (never shrink below `text_0`).\n\nMiddle-port removal is handled by the same rename-and-compact step: remove the cut\nslot, shift all higher-indexed slots down, update their wires. The user always sees\na dense, gap-free list of ports.\n\n## Open questions before implementing Part B\n- Rename atomicity: the server's `PUT /maps/:name/boxes/:id` writes one box at a\n  time. Updating the connection in the source box requires a second PUT. These are\n  two separate writes — consider whether a partial failure leaves the map in an\n  inconsistent state, and whether a `PUT /maps/:name/connections` batch endpoint\n  is worth adding first.\n- Should the file browser parser set `variadic_inputs` automatically when it\n  detects `...` in a Lua signature, and if so, which argument specifically?\n\n  -- nah let's just make the user set the variadic property manually. Unless we can put it in the language driver\n     somehow? but I don't think that's really possible in the design. Thoughts?\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. Part A: implement `libs/text.lua` with `M.concat(sep, ...)`.\n2. Part B schema: add `variadic_inputs` to box schema and validator.\n3. Part B editor: auto-grow on wire connect; auto-shrink + rename on wire disconnect.\n4. Part B inspector: variadic toggle per input port.\n5. Part B parser: auto-detect `...` in Lua and set `variadic_inputs`.\n\n## Future development ideas\n\n### Language-spec-driven variadic detection\n\nCurrently the editor uses hard-coded heuristics per language to find\nvariadic indicators in a function signature (Lua: literal `...`, Bash:\n`$@` after `shift`). The cleaner architecture mirrors the phase 3\nlanguage-spec model (issue 303): each language declares its own way\nto recognize and surface variadic parameters, and the file-browser\nparser asks the language spec rather than embedding the rules.\n\nConcretely, the editor side of a language spec\n(`langs/<name>/lexer.js` or a sibling `parser.js`) could expose:\n\n```js\n// Returns { name, inputs: [\"sep\", \"text\"], variadic_inputs: [\"text\"] }\n// for `function M.concat(sep, ...)` in Lua, or\n// `concat() { local sep=\"$1\"; shift; ... \"$@\" }` in Bash.\nfunction parse_function_signature(source, fn_name) { ... }\n```\n\nThe editor still calls the same on-select handler; the language spec\nis responsible for deciding how to translate native variadic syntax\ninto the editor's `(inputs, variadic_inputs)` model.\n\n### Variadic shapes that don't map cleanly to an array\n\nThe current model assumes variadic = an ordered series of positional\nslots. That fits Lua `...`, C `va_list`, Bash `\"$@\"`, JavaScript rest\nparams, etc. It does not fit:\n\n- **Keyword arguments** (Python `**kwargs`, Ruby keyword splats) —\n  these are key/value pairs, not positional. A box would need\n  named-slot pairs the user labels per slot, not auto-numbered\n  `_0` / `_1` / `_2`.\n- **Tagged unions / discriminated lists** (Rust enum lists, Haskell\n  variadic via heterogeneous lists) — each entry has a type tag in\n  addition to a value. Two-field slots, or per-slot type metadata.\n- **Streaming inputs** (generators, channels, iterators) — the\n  consumer doesn't know in advance how many values arrive. This is\n  closer to issue 213's queued-input model than to variadic.\n\nA future revision of the editor's variadic UI could let language\nspecs choose between several \"variadic shapes\":\n\n| shape           | slot model                          | example use      |\n|-----------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|\n| `positional`    | `<base>_<index>` ordered (current)  | Lua `...`        |\n| `keyed`         | per-slot `(key, value)` pairs       | Python `**kwargs`|\n| `tagged`        | per-slot `(tag, value)` pairs       | discriminated unions |\n| `stream`        | one slot, queued (issue 213)        | iterators        |\n\nEach shape would have its own auto-grow rule and inspector controls.\nThe language spec declares which shape applies to a given variadic\nparameter, and the editor renders accordingly.\n\nThis is speculative — the positional shape covers every shipped\nlanguage so far. Capturing it here so the design door stays open.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire connect/disconnect events\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — input port list, toggle rendering\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`variadic_inputs` field)\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT box endpoint (rename propagation)\n- `issues/208-port-literal-values.md` — `sep` will likely use literal port values\n",
    "oldString":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"# 217 — Concat box with per-input variadic ports and auto-grow/shrink\n\n## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n**Part A** — `libs/text.lua` ships `M.concat(sep, ...)` and\n`M.split(text, sep)`. Concat is variadic to match the editor's\nvariadic-input model. Split returns a Lua array; the driver shim\nJSON-encodes for the single output wire. The accompanying\n`libs/text.lua.info.md` documents both functions.\n\n**Part B** — Variadic UI lives in `assets/js/004-inspector.js`:\n\n- Helpers (`parse_variadic_name`, `is_variadic_slot`,\n  `variadic_slots_for`, `last_variadic_index`) parse and query the\n  `<base>_<index>` naming convention for variadic slots.\n- `make_variadic(port_name)` toggles a non-variadic port into a\n  one-slot variadic group (rename `text` → `text_0`, add base to\n  `box.variadic_inputs`, update connection records on this box and\n  every upstream box).\n- `unmake_variadic(base)` collapses a group back to a single port\n  (drop higher slots and their wires, rename slot 0 back to base).\n- `add_variadic_slot(base)` appends `<base>_<last+1>`. Used by the\n  auto-grow path; also reachable directly when needed.\n- `remove_variadic_slot(slot_name)` drops a single slot and renames\n  higher slots down by one, updating connections atomically per\n  slot.\n- `auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name)` is the public-from-Inspector\n  helper. If `slot_name` is the last slot of its variadic group, it\n  appends a new empty slot. Idempotent — calling again on the same\n  slot is a no-op once the slot is no longer last.\n\nThe wire-create path (`006-wires.js::create_connection`) calls\n`Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input)` after a\nsuccessful PUT. The inspector's per-port value-input handler also\ncalls it when a non-empty literal value is set on a slot. Together\nthese cover both growth triggers — wire-connect and value-set.\n\nPer-port UI (`mk_port_display`):\n\n- Plain port → `var` toggle (turn variadic on).\n- First slot of a variadic group → `var ×` toggle (collapse back).\n- Non-first variadic slot → `×` (remove this slot only; higher\n  slots rename down).\n- No `+` button — slots auto-grow. Wire-disconnect and\n  value-clear do NOT shrink (only `×` removes structure).\n\nSchema accepts `variadic_inputs` as an optional array of strings\n(`src/001-schema.lua`).\n\nComparator toggle (`004-inspector.js::cmp_btn.onclick`) now severs\nall outgoing wires on either toggle direction, fixing the prior\nbehavior where lt/eq/gt wires from a previous comparator state\nsilently re-appeared when the user re-enabled it.\n\n## Deliberate omissions / follow-ups\n\n- **Auto-shrink on wire-disconnect** is intentionally not done —\n  the user explicitly chose \"explicit `×` is the only way to shrink\"\n  so transient editing doesn't lose structure.\n- **Editable port names** and **value editing on the canvas\n  itself** belong in issue 224 — bigger redesign than 217 covers.\n- **Future ideas** (language-spec-driven variadic detection,\n  alternative variadic shapes for keyword args / streams /\n  discriminated unions) are captured below.",

It's the phase-2 implementation of the queue-per-port model that phase 3 already assumes (issues 302/304). Likely real work — touches the executor — and would close out the last graph-model correction in my earlier suggested sequence.\n\nOr if you want a smaller breather: **216 (read-file box)** is just `libs/files.lua` with two functions, like `libs/text.lua` from earlier. Quick.\n\nOr take a break — we've done a lot today. Up to you."

    "replaceAll":false,
    "oldString":"  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Higher-indexed slots are deleted along with their incoming wires.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Drop higher slots from box.inputs.\n    const drop_names = slots.slice(1).map(s => s.port.name);\n\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    // Re-resolve slot 0's index after the filter, then rename it.\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slots[0].port.name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    // Rename slot-0 connections, drop higher-slot connections.\n    await update_target_connections([slots[0].port.name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: base }));\n    if (drop_names.length > 0) {\n      await update_target_connections(drop_names, () => null);\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
    "newString":"  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Higher-indexed slots are deleted along with their incoming wires.\n  //\n  // Order matters: connection updates run FIRST, while port objects\n  // still carry their old names. If we rename the port objects before\n  // updating connections, the second update reads `slots[0].port.name`\n  // post-mutation and ends up looking for connections targeting the\n  // already-renamed slot — finds none, leaves a stale `text_0`-pointing\n  // connection record behind, which reappears as a \"ghost\" wire when\n  // the user toggles variadic back on.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Capture old names BEFORE any mutation. drop_names are the higher\n    // slots' names (text_1, text_2, ...); slot_0_old_name is the first\n    // slot's name (text_0) which we'll rename to `base` (text).\n    const slot_0_old_name = slots[0].port.name;\n    const drop_names      = slots.slice(1).map(s => s.port.name);\n\n    // 1. Update connections targeting the old slot-0 name → rename to base.\n    await update_target_connections([slot_0_old_name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: base }));\n    // 2. Drop connections targeting any higher slot.\n    if (drop_names.length > 0) {\n      await update_target_connections(drop_names, () => null);\n    }\n\n    // 3. Now safe to rename / drop the port objects on this box.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slot_0_old_name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
    "userModified":false
  },

          "command":"git add assets/js/004-inspector.js && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nFix unmake_variadic leaving stale connections to old slot-0 name\n\nThe slot-0 rename (text_0 → text) ran in two phases: mutate the port\nobject's name, then call update_target_connections to update wires.\nThe second phase read the slot-0 name from the port object — which\nhad already been mutated — and so looked for connections whose\nto_input was the new name (text), not the old (text_0). No connection\nmatched; the rename quietly did nothing. The text_0-pointing\nconnection record stayed in both the box's connections array and the\nupstream box's connections array. Visually the wire disappeared\n(no port named text_0 to anchor it), but the moment the user\nre-toggled variadic on, the slot text_0 reappeared and the orphan\nrecord found its target again — a ghost wire restored from stale\ndata.\n\nFix: capture the pre-mutation slot-0 name before any port-object\nchanges, run all connection updates first using captured names, then\nmutate the port objects.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit the bug fix"
        },
        "id":"toolu_01K4JMAM3TU8tsdpehiTMgbj"
      }]

        "text":"Hard reload and verify the fix:\n\n1. Wire up a port → variadic on → wire to all three slots → variadic off → variadic on. The text_1, text_2 wires should NOT come back.\n2. Wire up a port → variadic on → variadic off → variadic on. The original wire should still be there (it survives both round-trips because it gets renamed correctly each step).\n\nI also confirmed the same bug pattern doesn't exist in `make_variadic` (it captures `old_name` before mutating) or `remove_variadic_slot` (it captures `r.old` from `p.name` before assigning `p.name = new_name`). Just `unmake_variadic` had the order flipped."
      }]

    "content":"Does 213 affect things that are modified by phase 3? Should we defer it, or mark it as \"will-not-implement\" because we're just going to replace it later?\n\nThe \"view\" button next to the \"browse\" button shouldn't exist if a function isn't selected yet, and there's nothing to view. Can you put that in an issue file?\n\nOkay so. Creating a new box, connecting a wire, then switching to variadic mode doesn't snip the wires. In-fact, it doesn't even auto-grow the input ports. It also doesn't rename the port connection. However, when I connect a second wire to the first port, it DOES snip the original, doesn't connect the second, and it does rename the input port. From that point on, when I connect wires, it does auto-grow correctly.\n\nAlso, sometimes, when clicking the \"snip wire\" tool, then clicking on the canvas and dragging over the wire to the other side of the wire, it doesn't seem to register. Not sure why. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Maybe the pointer is skipping over it? Maybe we need to add some sort of interpolation or whatever?\n\nwhen I create a new box, don't connect any wires, but do turn on variadic mode, it does correctly auto-grow upon connecting a wire. If I connect 2+ wires, when switching OUT of variadic mode, it maintains the first position wire connection. Intended behavior is to snip all input wires.",
