    "originalFile":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n      const branch_str = wire.from_branch ? '.' + wire.from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('wire ' + wire.from_box + branch_str + ' → ' + wire.to_box + '.' +\n        wire.to_input + ' — press Delete to remove');\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  // Fetch-before-PUT: read both boxes, add the connection record, write both.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(from_box_id),\n        API.get_box(to_box_id),\n      ]);\n\n      const conn = {\n        from_box:    from_box_id,\n        from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n        to_box:      to_box_id,\n        to_input:    to_input,\n      };\n\n      src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n      dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n      // avoid duplicates\n      const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n      );\n      if (dup) return;\n\n      src_box.connections.push(conn);\n      dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      // update local cache\n      Boxes.boxes[from_box_id] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[to_box_id]   = dst_box;\n\n      const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n\n      // Auto-grow the destination box's variadic group when the wire\n      // landed on its last slot (issue 217 part B). Idempotent — the\n      // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n      // group and exits if not.\n      if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n        await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n      }\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    try {\n      const [src_box, dst_box] = await Promise.all([\n        API.get_box(conn.from_box),\n        API.get_box(conn.to_box),\n      ]);\n\n      const match = c =>\n        c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n        (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n        c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n        c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n      src_box.connections = (src_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n      dst_box.connections = (dst_box.connections || []).filter(c => !match(c));\n\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box] = src_box;\n      Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box]   = dst_box;\n\n      _selected_wire = null;\n      status_msg('deleted connection');\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    } catch(e) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

Mutating in place keeps every reference\n  // valid.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const conn = {\n      from_box:    from_box_id,\n      from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n      to_box:      to_box_id,\n      to_input:    to_input,\n    };\n\n    src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n    dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n    // avoid exact duplicates (same source, branch, dest, input)\n    const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n    );\n    if (dup) return;\n\n    src_box.connections.push(conn);\n    dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back the push so the in-memory state matches the server\n      src_box.connections.pop();\n      dst_box.connections.pop();\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n    status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n\n    // Auto-grow the destination box's variadic group when the wire\n    // landed on its last slot (issue 217 part B). Idempotent — the\n    // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n    // group and exits if not.\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  // Same in-place mutation pattern as create_connection — never\n  // replace the cached references.\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const match = c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n    const src_before = src_box.connections || [];\n    const dst_before = dst_box.connections || [];\n    src_box.connections = src_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n    dst_box.connections = dst_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back\n      src_box.connections = src_before;\n      dst_box.connections = dst_before;\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    _selected_wire = null;\n    status_msg('deleted connection');\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}",

        "text":"Several real issues here. Let me work through them:\n\n**213 deferral**: yes, defer it. Phase 3 (issue 302) implements the queue-per-port model directly in C; the phase 2 Lua executor's queue work is throwaway. I'll mark 213 as won't-implement.\n\n**Variadic toggle bug** — root cause: when a wire is created, `create_connection` does `API.get_box` (fresh fetch) → mutate → `Boxes.boxes[id] = freshly_fetched`. This **replaces the reference**. The inspector's `current_box` was set when the user clicked the box and now points at the stale pre-fetch object. So `make_variadic` walks `current_box.connections`, finds nothing (no wire there), and the rename does nothing. Then `save()` overwrites the server with stale data, dropping the wire silently. The rename \"works\" only after a second wire-create because by then the inspector has been re-shown via `auto_grow_after_set`'s `show(box)` call.\n\nFix: never replace cache references. Mutate `Boxes.boxes[id]` in place. `current_box === Boxes.boxes[id]` stays true.\n\n**Variadic toggle should snip all wires** (per your spec): both directions clear wires. Cleaner, less corner-cases.\n\n**Other**: I'll write up the wire-erase pointer-skip bug and the \"view\" button condition as new issues.\n\nLet me fix the stale-reference bug first:"
      }]

      "totalLines":652,
      "content":"    const out   = (current_box.connections || []).filter(c => c.from_box === my_id);\n    if (out.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Collect destinations whose connection records also need cleaning.\n    const dest_ids = new Set();\n    out.forEach(c => dest_ids.add(c.to_box));\n\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => c.from_box !== my_id);\n\n    await Promise.all(Array.from(dest_ids).map(async dst_id => {\n      try {\n        const dst = await API.get_box(dst_id);\n        dst.connections = (dst.connections || []).filter(c => c.from_box !== my_id);\n        await API.put_box(dst_id, dst);\n        Boxes.boxes[dst_id] = dst;\n      } catch (e) {\n        console.error('failed to sever wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message);\n      }\n    }));\n\n    status_msg('cleared ' + out.length + ' outgoing wire(s)');\n  }\n\n  // Auto-grow check used by the wire-connect path and the value-set\n  // path. If `slot_name` is the LAST slot of a variadic group on\n  // `box`, append a new empty slot and persist. Idempotent — calling\n  // again on the same slot is a no-op because it's no longer last.\n  // Exported via the Inspector return so other modules (Wires) can call\n  // it after creating a connection.\n  async function auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n    if (!(box.variadic_inputs || []).includes(pv.base)) return;\n    if (pv.index !== last_variadic_index(box, pv.base)) return;\n\n    box.inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    box.inputs.push({ name: pv.base + '_' + (pv.index + 1), type: 'any' });\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(box.id, box);"
    }
  },

'args' : port_name;\n    const new_name = base + '_0';\n    const old_name = port_name;\n\n    current_box.inputs[idx].name = new_name;\n    current_box.variadic_inputs  = current_box.variadic_inputs || [];\n    if (!current_box.variadic_inputs.includes(base)) {\n      current_box.variadic_inputs.push(base);\n    }\n\n    await update_target_connections([old_name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: new_name }));\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
    "newString":"  // Toggle a non-variadic input ON: snip every wire targeting the\n  // port, rename the port `text` → `text_0`, add base to\n  // box.variadic_inputs.\n  //\n  // Snipping (rather than renaming the wire to point at `text_0`)\n  // matches the user's mental model: variadic-on and variadic-off\n  // are different input shapes; switching shapes clears the wires.\n  // The user reconnects after the toggle. This avoids a class of\n  // edge cases where rename + wire-create + auto-grow have to\n  // coordinate.\n  //\n  // Special case: a port literally named `...` (Lua variadic that\n  // the file-browser parser left in place) gets renamed to `args_0`\n  // with base `args` — there's no other sensible name we can derive.\n  async function make_variadic(port_name) {\n    const idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === port_name);\n    if (idx < 0) return;\n\n    const base     = port_name === '...' ? 'args' : port_name;\n    const new_name = base + '_0';\n\n    // 1. Drop any wires currently targeting this port.\n    await update_target_connections([port_name], () => null);\n\n    // 2. Rename the port and add base to variadic_inputs.\n    current_box.inputs[idx].name = new_name;\n    current_box.variadic_inputs  = current_box.variadic_inputs || [];\n    if (!current_box.variadic_inputs.includes(base)) {\n      current_box.variadic_inputs.push(base);\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",

          "new_string":"  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Snips every wire targeting any slot in the group, drops higher\n  // slots from box.inputs, renames slot 0 back to base, removes the\n  // base from box.variadic_inputs.\n  //\n  // Snipping (rather than keeping slot-0's wire) matches the same\n  // \"shape change clears wires\" rule as make_variadic. Symmetric.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Capture all slot names BEFORE mutating port objects.\n    const all_names = slots.map(s => s.port.name);\n\n    // 1. Drop every wire targeting any slot in the group.\n    await update_target_connections(all_names, () => null);\n\n    // 2. Drop higher slots from box.inputs and rename slot 0 to base.\n    const slot_0_old_name = slots[0].port.name;\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slot_0_old_name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    // 3. Remove base from variadic_inputs.\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"  // Toggle a variadic group OFF (collapse to single port `<base>`).\n  // Higher-indexed slots are deleted along with their incoming wires.\n  //\n  // Order matters: connection updates run FIRST, while port objects\n  // still carry their old names. If we rename the port objects before\n  // updating connections, the second update reads `slots[0].port.name`\n  // post-mutation and ends up looking for connections targeting the\n  // already-renamed slot — finds none, leaves a stale `text_0`-pointing\n  // connection record behind, which reappears as a \"ghost\" wire when\n  // the user toggles variadic back on.\n  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // Capture old names BEFORE any mutation. drop_names are the higher\n    // slots' names (text_1, text_2, ...); slot_0_old_name is the first\n    // slot's name (text_0) which we'll rename to `base` (text).\n    const slot_0_old_name = slots[0].port.name;\n    const drop_names      = slots.slice(1).map(s => s.port.name);\n\n    // 1. Update connections targeting the old slot-0 name → rename to base.\n    await update_target_connections([slot_0_old_name], c => ({ ...c, to_input: base }));\n    // 2. Drop connections targeting any higher slot.\n    if (drop_names.length > 0) {\n      await update_target_connections(drop_names, () => null);\n    }\n\n    // 3. Now safe to rename / drop the port objects on this box.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter((_, i) =>\n      !slots.slice(1).some(s => s.idx === i));\n    const new_keep_idx = current_box.inputs.findIndex(p => p.name === slot_0_old_name);\n    if (new_keep_idx >= 0) current_box.inputs[new_keep_idx].name = base;\n\n    current_box.variadic_inputs = (current_box.variadic_inputs || [])\n      .filter(n => n !== base);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }"

    "originalFile":"# 213 — Queued inputs and synchronous task model\n\n## Status\n\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nEach input port in the executor store holds exactly one value. When an upstream\nbox fires a connection, it overwrites whatever was previously in that slot. A box\nonly runs once (the `visited` guard prevents re-execution). This means:\n\n- A box with two upstream feeders only processes the last-arriving value.\n- Fan-in patterns (many outputs converging on one input) silently drop values.\n- There is no way to process a stream of values through a box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach input port has a **queue** (ordered list) of waiting values instead of a\nsingle slot. A box becomes \"ready\" when all of its required input ports have at\nleast one value in their queue. When a box runs, it pops one value from the\nfront of each required input queue, then runs the task with those values. After\nthe task completes, the box is checked again — if all required queues are still\nnon-empty, it runs again immediately, consuming the next set of inputs.\n\nOptional ports (marked with `\"optional\": true` in the input object) do not gate\nreadiness. If a value is present in an optional port's queue when the task runs,\nit is consumed; otherwise the task receives nil for that port.\n\nThis model enables:\n- Fan-in: A collects 10 values, B collects 1. Each new value to B creates one\n  task that consumes one A-value and the new B-value.\n- Pipelines: output of one box feeds into the next, which re-runs for each\n  arriving value.\n- Broadcast: one box fans out to two boxes, both of which process that one value.\n\nThe executor stays **synchronous** in this phase. Coroutines are not required\nfor the synchronous model — the simple approach is: after each box run, re-check\nall boxes (not just directly connected ones) for readiness and enqueue any that\nare ready. Run until the queue is empty or an error occurs.\n\n## Data model changes\n\n**Store**: `store[\"box_id.port_name\"]` changes from a single value to an array\nof values (a queue). All reads pop from the front; all writes push to the back.\n\n**Inputs satisfied**: `inputs_satisfied(box, store)` — a port is satisfied when\n`#store[key] > 0`. Optional ports are always considered satisfied.\n\n**Collect inputs**: `collect_inputs(box, store)` — shifts (pops front) one value\nfrom each port's queue and returns the map of port-name → value.\n\n**Visited guard**: remove the `visited` flag. Instead, enqueue a box whenever its\ninputs become satisfied (even if it has run before). This is safe because\nsatisfaction requires queue entries, and collect_inputs consumes them.\n\n**Literal values**: pre-seeded literal values are still pushed once into the\nqueue at startup. They are consumed on first run. A wire can push additional\nvalues on top of the literal.\n\n## Optional port convention\n\nIn the box file:\n```json\n{ \"name\": \"temperature\", \"type\": \"any\", \"optional\": true, \"value\": \"0.7\" }\n```\n\n`optional: true` means this port does not block readiness. The literal `value`\n(if present) is still pre-seeded into the queue as a default. Wires can push\nadditional values.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — change store values to arrays. Update\n   `inputs_satisfied` (check array length, skip optional ports). Update\n   `collect_inputs` (table.remove from front). Remove `visited` table.\n   After each `fire_connections`, re-scan all boxes for satisfaction and\n   enqueue the newly ready ones.\n\n2. **`src/001-schema.lua`** — add optional `\"optional\"` boolean to port objects.\n\n3. **`src/004-executor.lua`** — pre-seeding: push literal values into arrays\n   (`store[key] = { parsed_val }`) instead of assigning directly.\n\n4. **`assets/js/004-inspector.js`** — add an \"optional\" checkbox per input port\n   row. On change, update `port.optional` and save.\n\n## Future: thread pool\n\nWhen the synchronous model is replaced by a thread pool, the queue-per-port\ndesign maps directly: a worker thread pops one value from each input queue,\nruns the task, and pushes outputs to the connected ports' queues. The\nsatisfaction check becomes a condition variable or semaphore per port. The\nsynchronous executor described here is the reference implementation.\n\n## Related documents\n\n- src/004-executor.lua — execute, inputs_satisfied, collect_inputs, fire_connections\n- src/001-schema.lua — port schema, optional field\n- assets/js/004-inspector.js — optional port checkbox\n- docs/001-architecture.md — store model, box.inputs schema\n",
    "oldString":"# 213 — Queued inputs and synchronous task model\n\n## Status\n\nopen",
    "newString":"# 213 — Queued inputs and synchronous task model\n\n## Status\n\nwon't implement (in phase 2 — superseded by phase 3 issue 302)\n\n## Resolution\n\nThe queue-per-port model described here is the right model. The\nphase 2 implementation in `src/004-executor.lua` would be throwaway\nwork because phase 3 (issues 301–311) replaces the synchronous\nruntime wholesale: the C pool runner uses ring-buffer slots in\nshared memory (issue 302) for exactly the queue semantics this\nissue describes.\n\nPhase 3 already incorporates this issue's design — fan-in,\nqueue-drain, optional ports, and the \"many wires into one input\nport\" model. See:\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — slots are ring buffers;\n  N-cell rings handle queued inputs natively.\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — the dispatch action drains\n  one value per input from each port queue.\n\nClosing this issue without implementing it in the phase 2 Lua\nruntime. Maps that rely on fan-in (multiple wires to one input\nport) will produce undefined behavior under the phase 2 runner —\nlast-wire-wins, with no queue.   "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/227-hide-view-button-without-ref.md",
    "content":"# 227 — Hide the inspector \"view\" button when the box has no ref\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe inspector renders three buttons next to the `ref` field on every\ncall box: `browse` (open the file browser), `view` (open the\nfloating source viewer, issue 215), and the inputs/outputs sections.\nThe `view` button shows up for every call box regardless of whether\n`box.ref` has been set yet.\n\nClicking `view` on a box with no ref calls\n`SourceView.open_source_view(current_box.ref, current_box)`, which\nfalls through to `fetch_source(ref)` returning the error \"no ref\nset on this box.\" A status-bar error appears. The button is\nnon-functional until a ref is set; it shouldn't be visible until\nthen.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe `view` button is rendered only when `box.ref` is non-empty. When\nthe user creates a fresh box and hasn't yet picked a function via the\nfile browser, the button is absent. After picking a function, the\nbutton appears. After clearing the ref (manual edit of the input\nfield), the button disappears again.\n\nThe `browse` button stays visible at all times — that's the entry\npoint to actually setting a ref.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show`, in the block that builds the\nref row:\n\n```js\nconst view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n// ... existing setup ...\nref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\nref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\nif (box.ref && box.ref !== '') {\n  ref_wrap.appendChild(view_btn);\n}\n```\n\nThe button should also appear/disappear in response to the user\ntyping into the ref input. Easiest way: re-render the ref row on\ninput. Or: keep the button always in the DOM but toggle its\n`hidden` attribute on input.\n\nToggle-on-input is simpler:\n\n```js\nref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n  current_box.ref = ref_inp.value;\n  view_btn.hidden = !ref_inp.value;\n  save();\n});\n```\n\nAdd `view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at button creation time so the\ninitial render is correct.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field row, `view_btn` setup\n- `issues/completed/215-view-box-source.md` — the source viewer\n  this button opens\n"
  },
  "uuid":"829c0cb2-b650-4cff-8233-439d6bfc8bf1",

After clearing the ref (manual edit of the input\nfield), the button disappears again.\n\nThe `browse` button stays visible at all times — that's the entry\npoint to actually setting a ref.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show`, in the block that builds the\nref row:\n\n```js\nconst view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n// ... existing setup ...\nref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\nref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\nif (box.ref && box.ref !== '') {\n  ref_wrap.appendChild(view_btn);\n}\n```\n\nThe button should also appear/disappear in response to the user\ntyping into the ref input. Easiest way: re-render the ref row on\ninput. Or: keep the button always in the DOM but toggle its\n`hidden` attribute on input.\n\nToggle-on-input is simpler:\n\n```js\nref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n  current_box.ref = ref_inp.value;\n  view_btn.hidden = !ref_inp.value;\n  save();\n});\n```\n\nAdd `view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at button creation time so the\ninitial render is correct.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field row, `view_btn` setup\n- `issues/completed/215-view-box-source.md` — the source viewer\n  this button opens\n",

        "input":{
          "new_string":"  // last_erase_pos: world-coord of the previous mousemove during an\n  // erase-wire drag. Used to interpolate between events when the user\n  // drags fast enough that the pointer skips over a thin wire between\n  // browser-throttled mousemove ticks.\n  let last_erase_pos = null;\n\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (erasing && tool_mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      // Sample several points along the line from the previous cursor\n      // position to the current one; hit-test each against every wire.\n      // Without interpolation a fast drag misses thin wires entirely\n      // because mousemove only fires every ~16ms.\n      const erase_at = (px, py) => {\n        const wire = Wires.hit_test_wire(px, py, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n        if (!wire) return;\n        const sig = wire_sig(wire);\n        if (erase_seen.has(sig)) return;\n        erase_seen.add(sig);\n        // remove from local cache immediately for instant visual feedback\n        [wire.from_box, wire.to_box].forEach(id => {\n          if (Boxes.boxes[id]) {\n            Boxes.boxes[id].connections = (Boxes.boxes[id].connections || []).filter(\n              c => wire_sig(c) !== sig\n            );\n          }\n        });\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();\n        Wires.delete_connection(wire).catch(e2 =>\n          status_msg('erase error: ' + e2.message, 'error'));\n      };\n\n      if (last_erase_pos) {\n        // Sample density: one sample every HIT_THRESHOLD-ish world units\n        // along the segment. Length is in world units; threshold is also.\n        const dx = w.x - last_erase_pos.x;\n        const dy = w.y - last_erase_pos.y;\n        const dist = Math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy);\n        const n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(dist / 4));   // ~one sample per 4 world units\n        for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n          const t = i / n;\n          erase_at(last_erase_pos.x + dx * t, last_erase_pos.y + dy * t);\n        }\n      } else {\n        erase_at(w.x, w.y);\n      }\n      last_erase_pos = w;\n      return;\n    } else {\n      last_erase_pos = null;\n    }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/005-app.js",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (erasing && tool_mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      const wire = Wires.hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n      if (wire) {\n        const sig = wire_sig(wire);\n        if (!erase_seen.has(sig)) {\n          erase_seen.add(sig);\n          // remove from local cache immediately for instant visual feedback\n          [wire.from_box, wire.to_box].forEach(id => {\n            if (Boxes.boxes[id]) {\n              Boxes.boxes[id].connections = (Boxes.boxes[id].connections || []).filter(\n                c => wire_sig(c) !== sig\n              );\n            }\n          });\n          Canvas.mark_dirty();\n          Wires.delete_connection(wire).catch(e2 =>\n            status_msg('erase error: ' + e2.message, 'error'));\n        }\n      }\n      return;\n    }"

Used to interpolate between events when the user\n  // drags fast enough that the pointer skips over a thin wire between\n  // browser-throttled mousemove ticks.\n  let last_erase_pos = null;\n\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    if (erasing && tool_mode === 'erase-wire') {\n      // Sample several points along the line from the previous cursor\n      // position to the current one; hit-test each against every wire.\n      // Without interpolation a fast drag misses thin wires entirely\n      // because mousemove only fires every ~16ms.\n      const erase_at = (px, py) => {\n        const wire = Wires.hit_test_wire(px, py, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n        if (!wire) return;\n        const sig = wire_sig(wire);\n        if (erase_seen.has(sig)) return;\n        erase_seen.add(sig);\n        // remove from local cache immediately for instant visual feedback\n        [wire.from_box, wire.to_box].forEach(id => {\n          if (Boxes.boxes[id]) {\n            Boxes.boxes[id].connections = (Boxes.boxes[id].connections || []).filter(\n              c => wire_sig(c) !== sig\n            );\n          }\n        });\n        Canvas.mark_dirty();\n        Wires.delete_connection(wire).catch(e2 =>\n          status_msg('erase error: ' + e2.message, 'error'));\n      };\n\n      if (last_erase_pos) {\n        // Sample density: one sample every HIT_THRESHOLD-ish world units\n        // along the segment. Length is in world units; threshold is also.\n        const dx = w.x - last_erase_pos.x;\n        const dy = w.y - last_erase_pos.y;\n        const dist = Math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy);\n        const n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(dist / 4));   // ~one sample per 4 world units\n        for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n          const t = i / n;\n          erase_at(last_erase_pos.x + dx * t, last_erase_pos.y + dy * t);\n        }\n      } else {\n        erase_at(w.x, w.y);\n      }\n      last_erase_pos = w;\n      return;\n    } else {\n      last_erase_pos = null;\n    }",
    "userModified":false
  },

          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nFix stale-cache bug; variadic toggle snips wires; close 213 and 227\n\nThe root cause of several recent bugs (variadic toggle not renaming\nwires, ghost wires reappearing on toggle, save() clobbering recent\nchanges) was the wire / inspector code replacing cached box\nreferences with freshly-fetched copies after a server PUT. The\ninspector's current_box reference would then silently diverge from\nthe cache, and operations on it ran on out-of-date data. The fix is\nto mutate cached box objects in place — every reference holder\n(canvas, inspector, wires) sees updates immediately. Applied to\ncreate_connection, delete_connection, sever_output_wires,\nupdate_target_connections, and the literal-value-severs-wires path.\n\nVariadic toggle now snips every wire targeting the affected port\n(or port group, on un-variadic) rather than trying to rename or\npreserve them. Switching the input shape between non-variadic and\nvariadic groups is a \"fresh slate\" operation; the user reconnects\nafterwards. This eliminates a cluster of edge cases where rename +\nauto-grow + wire-create had to coordinate.\n\nWire-erase tool now interpolates between consecutive cursor\npositions during drag — fast drags across thin wires were missing\nbecause mousemove only fires every ~16ms. Samples one hit-test per\n4 world units along the segment.\n\nCloses 213 (won't implement; phase 3 issue 302 implements the\nqueue-per-port model directly in C and supersedes the phase 2 Lua\nwork). Opens 227 (the inspector \"view\" button shouldn't appear when\nthe box has no ref set).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit bug fixes + 213 close + 227 open"
        },
        "id":"toolu_018umzPMmt4cZ1TAqfy3zJb8"
      }]

  "toolUseResult":{
    "type":"create",
    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md",
    "content":"# 228 — Self-loop wires: connect a box's output to its own input, routed around the body\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe connection model permits a wire whose `from_box` and `to_box`\nare the same — `create_connection` checks for exact duplicates but\ndoes not reject self-loops. The wire renderer in\n`assets/js/006-wires.js::draw_all` then draws a cubic Bézier from\nthe output dot (right edge of the box) to the input dot (left edge\nof the box), with control points fixed at\n`±BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80px` horizontally. For a self-loop, both\nendpoints sit on opposite sides of the same body and the curve cuts\nstraight through the middle of the box — visually unreadable, and\nclipped by the box rectangle.\n\nHit-testing samples the same Bézier path and inherits the same\nproblem: clicks land in the wrong place because the wire sits\nunderneath the box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nSelf-loops are allowed and render as a wire that loops *around*\nthe box body, not through it. The user can wire a box's output to\nits own input the same way as any other connection (drag from\noutput port, release on input port).\n\n### Why this matters\n\nSelf-loops are useful with iterator boxes (issue 221): an\niterator's output feeds back into its own queued input, building\nan accumulator or polling-state pattern. The comparator (issue\n210) routes one branch to the input on a self-loop, the other\nbranch downstream. With queued inputs (phase 3 issue 302) the\nloop terminates naturally when the queue empties.\n\nThe runtime semantics differ between phase 2 and phase 3:\n- **Phase 2 (current)**: the synchronous executor walks dependency\n  order. A self-loop on a non-iterator box never resolves and\n  hangs the run. The user is responsible for not shipping such\n  maps. The editor allows constructing them; the runner errors\n  cleanly (or hangs, which is also a clear signal).\n- **Phase 3**: the C graph loader (issue 305) rejects non-iterator\n  cycles at load time and accepts iterator cycles. The editor\n  doesn't need to know which is which; the loader catches misuse.\n\nEither way, the editor's job is just to draw the wire correctly.\n\n### Routing\n\nThe wire path for a self-loop goes out the right side from the\noutput dot, around either the top or the bottom of the box body\n(pick deterministically — say, always the bottom), and back to\nthe input dot on the left side.\n\nTwo reasonable shapes:\n\n1. **Cubic Bézier with off-axis control points** — keep the same\n   `draw_bezier` machinery but pick control points that pull the\n   curve out, down, and around. For a box at world-(x, y) with\n   width W and height H, output dot at (x+W, oy) and input dot at\n   (x, iy):\n\n   ```\n   src = (x+W, oy)\n   dst = (x,   iy)\n   cp1 = (x+W + LOOP_OFFSET, oy + H)\n   cp2 = (x   - LOOP_OFFSET, iy + H)\n   ```\n\n   `LOOP_OFFSET` ~ 60–80px gives a smooth horseshoe under the box.\n\n2. **Polyline** — straight segments: right from output dot,\n   down past the box bottom, left past the box left edge, up to\n   input dot. Visually crisper, easier to hit-test, but stylistically\n   inconsistent with every other wire being a Bézier.\n\nRecommendation: option 1. Reuses `draw_bezier` with different\ncontrol-point math, no new rendering primitive needed.\n\n### Hit-testing\n\n`hit_test_wire` samples the Bézier path at `HIT_SAMPLES = 20`\npoints. With the same machinery and routed-around control points,\nthe samples sit on the curved path under the box, not behind the\nbody. Clicks register correctly.\n\nThe wire-erase pointer-interpolation fix (commit 899f35d) walks\nthe *cursor* path, not the wire's path. It already works for any\nwire shape `hit_test_wire` can match. No additional change needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/006-wires.js`:\n\n1. Detect self-loop where the wire is being computed:\n   `c.from_box === c.to_box`.\n2. When self-loop, compute `cp1` and `cp2` with the looped offsets\n   above. The offset is in world units, so it scales with zoom\n   correctly.\n3. Pass `cp1` / `cp2` into `draw_bezier` (refactor to accept\n   explicit control points, or add a sibling `draw_loop_bezier`).\n4. `hit_test_wire` does the same self-loop check and uses the\n   same `bezier_point` sampling with the looped control points.\n\n```js\nfunction endpoint_controls(c, src, dst, box) {\n  if (c.from_box === c.to_box && box) {\n    const h = Boxes.box_height(box);\n    return {\n      cp1: { x: src.x + LOOP_OFFSET,        y: src.y + h * 0.7 },\n      cp2: { x: dst.x - LOOP_OFFSET,        y: dst.y + h * 0.7 },\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    cp1: { x: src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: src.y },\n    cp2: { x: dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: dst.y },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Box height changes** while a self-loop wire exists (variadic\n  slot added → box grows): the wire's control points are derived\n  per-frame from current `box_height`, so it adapts automatically.\n- **Output is a comparator branch** (`from_branch` is `lt`/`eq`/`gt`):\n  the loop renders the same way; the branch coloring still applies.\n  A user can wire `lt` back to the same box's input, which is a\n  legitimate self-loop pattern for \"while less than X, keep going.\"\n- **Multiple self-loops on one box** (different output → different\n  inputs, or comparator branches): each renders independently.\n  They will overlap; visual cleanup if it ever matters in\n  practice.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Top vs bottom routing**: always-below is simplest. Always-above\n  is also fine. Configurable per-wire (right-click → \"route around\n  top\") is overkill until someone asks for it.\n- **Self-loop validation in the schema**: the phase 2 schema\n  doesn't reject self-loops, and the phase 3 loader handles cycle\n  detection at load time (issue 305). Editor-side validation is\n  unnecessary; the wire-draw machinery just needs to render it.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `draw_all`, `hit_test_wire`,\n  `draw_bezier`, control-point math\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `box_height`, `BOX_W`, port positions\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — wire-create flow (no change needed; the\n  existing flow already permits self-loop construction)\n- `issues/221-iterator-box.md` — iterator self-re-spawn pattern\n  that motivates this\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — phase 3 loader's cycle\n  validation policy\n"
  },

    "id":"msg_0142EJVuDLbSsczMa9xEmczE",
    "model":"claude-opus-4-7",
    "stop_reason":"tool_use",
    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Let me explain the bug, then write up the self-loop issue.\n\n**The bug:** It was a classic JavaScript-reference-vs-mutation issue. Two pieces of code were holding references to \"the same box\" but those references could silently get out of sync.\n\nWhen you click a box, the inspector grabs the box object as `current_box`. The canvas-side cache, `Boxes.boxes[id]`, is the same object — same reference, both names point to the same JS object in memory.\n\nWhen you then connect a wire, `create_connection` did this:\n```js\nconst dst_box = await API.get_box(to_box_id);   // fetch a *fresh* object from server\ndst_box.connections.push(conn);                 // mutate the fresh one\nawait API.put_box(to_box_id, dst_box);          // PUT\nBoxes.boxes[to_box_id] = dst_box;               // replace cache\n```\n\nThat last line was the culprit. `Boxes.boxes[id]` now points at a **different object** than `current_box` does. The canvas reads `Boxes.boxes[id]` and sees the new wire. The inspector reads `current_box` and doesn't.\n\nSo when you clicked the variadic toggle, `make_variadic` walked `current_box.connections` looking for a wire to rename — found nothing (the wire is on the *new* `dst_box` object, not on `current_box`). The rename did nothing. Then `save()` PUT the stale `current_box` to the server, which silently dropped the wire because the stale object had no record of it.\n\nThe reason connecting a *second* wire seemed to \"fix\" things: `auto_grow_after_set` had a fallback line — `if (current_box.id === box.id) show(box, ...)` — that adopted the new `box` as the new `current_box`. After the second wire, the inspector was finally pointing at the same object as the cache, and subsequent operations worked.\n\n**The fix:** mutate the cached objects in place instead of replacing the reference. Every place that used to do `Boxes.boxes[id] = freshly_fetched` now does `cached.connections = ...` directly on the existing object. Both `current_box` and `Boxes.boxes[id]` keep pointing at the same object, and there's no way for them to drift. Plus, on PUT failure, we roll back the in-memory mutation so the state stays consistent with the server.\n\nThe variadic-toggle \"snip all wires\" change was a separate decision — it makes the toggle behave as \"shape change clears wires\" so the rename + auto-grow corner cases stop existing in the first place. Easier to reason about than the previous \"rename slot 0's wire, drop higher slots' wires\" asymmetry.\n\nNow writing the self-loop issue:"
      }]
  },

The wire renderer in\n`assets/js/006-wires.js::draw_all` then draws a cubic Bézier from\nthe output dot (right edge of the box) to the input dot (left edge\nof the box), with control points fixed at\n`±BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80px` horizontally. For a self-loop, both\nendpoints sit on opposite sides of the same body and the curve cuts\nstraight through the middle of the box — visually unreadable, and\nclipped by the box rectangle.\n\nHit-testing samples the same Bézier path and inherits the same\nproblem: clicks land in the wrong place because the wire sits\nunderneath the box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nSelf-loops are allowed and render as a wire that loops *around*\nthe box body, not through it. The user can wire a box's output to\nits own input the same way as any other connection (drag from\noutput port, release on input port).\n\n### Why this matters\n\nSelf-loops are useful with iterator boxes (issue 221): an\niterator's output feeds back into its own queued input, building\nan accumulator or polling-state pattern. The comparator (issue\n210) routes one branch to the input on a self-loop, the other\nbranch downstream. With queued inputs (phase 3 issue 302) the\nloop terminates naturally when the queue empties.\n\nThe runtime semantics differ between phase 2 and phase 3:\n- **Phase 2 (current)**: the synchronous executor walks dependency\n  order. A self-loop on a non-iterator box never resolves and\n  hangs the run. The user is responsible for not shipping such\n  maps. The editor allows constructing them; the runner errors\n  cleanly (or hangs, which is also a clear signal).\n- **Phase 3**: the C graph loader (issue 305) rejects non-iterator\n  cycles at load time and accepts iterator cycles. The editor\n  doesn't need to know which is which; the loader catches misuse.\n\nEither way, the editor's job is just to draw the wire correctly.\n\n### Routing\n\nThe wire path for a self-loop goes out the right side from the\noutput dot, around either the top or the bottom of the box body\n(pick deterministically — say, always the bottom), and back to\nthe input dot on the left side.\n\nTwo reasonable shapes:\n\n1. **Cubic Bézier with off-axis control points** — keep the same\n   `draw_bezier` machinery but pick control points that pull the\n   curve out, down, and around. For a box at world-(x, y) with\n   width W and height H, output dot at (x+W, oy) and input dot at\n   (x, iy):\n\n   ```\n   src = (x+W, oy)\n   dst = (x,   iy)\n   cp1 = (x+W + LOOP_OFFSET, oy + H)\n   cp2 = (x   - LOOP_OFFSET, iy + H)\n   ```\n\n   `LOOP_OFFSET` ~ 60–80px gives a smooth horseshoe under the box.\n\n2. **Polyline** — straight segments: right from output dot,\n   down past the box bottom, left past the box left edge, up to\n   input dot. Visually crisper, easier to hit-test, but stylistically\n   inconsistent with every other wire being a Bézier.\n\nRecommendation: option 1. Reuses `draw_bezier` with different\ncontrol-point math, no new rendering primitive needed.\n\n### Hit-testing\n\n`hit_test_wire` samples the Bézier path at `HIT_SAMPLES = 20`\npoints. With the same machinery and routed-around control points,\nthe samples sit on the curved path under the box, not behind the\nbody. Clicks register correctly.\n\nThe wire-erase pointer-interpolation fix (commit 899f35d) walks\nthe *cursor* path, not the wire's path. It already works for any\nwire shape `hit_test_wire` can match. No additional change needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/006-wires.js`:\n\n1. Detect self-loop where the wire is being computed:\n   `c.from_box === c.to_box`.\n2. When self-loop, compute `cp1` and `cp2` with the looped offsets\n   above. The offset is in world units, so it scales with zoom\n   correctly.\n3. Pass `cp1` / `cp2` into `draw_bezier` (refactor to accept\n   explicit control points, or add a sibling `draw_loop_bezier`).\n4. `hit_test_wire` does the same self-loop check and uses the\n   same `bezier_point` sampling with the looped control points.\n\n```js\nfunction endpoint_controls(c, src, dst, box) {\n  if (c.from_box === c.to_box && box) {\n    const h = Boxes.box_height(box);\n    return {\n      cp1: { x: src.x + LOOP_OFFSET,        y: src.y + h * 0.7 },\n      cp2: { x: dst.x - LOOP_OFFSET,        y: dst.y + h * 0.7 },\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    cp1: { x: src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: src.y },\n    cp2: { x: dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: dst.y },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Box height changes** while a self-loop wire exists (variadic\n  slot added → box grows): the wire's control points are derived\n  per-frame from current `box_height`, so it adapts automatically.\n- **Output is a comparator branch** (`from_branch` is `lt`/`eq`/`gt`):\n  the loop renders the same way; the branch coloring still applies.\n  A user can wire `lt` back to the same box's input, which is a\n  legitimate self-loop pattern for \"while less than X, keep going.\"\n- **Multiple self-loops on one box** (different output → different\n  inputs, or comparator branches): each renders independently.\n  They will overlap; visual cleanup if it ever matters in\n  practice.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Top vs bottom routing**: always-below is simplest. Always-above\n  is also fine. Configurable per-wire (right-click → \"route around\n  top\") is overkill until someone asks for it.\n- **Self-loop validation in the schema**: the phase 2 schema\n  doesn't reject self-loops, and the phase 3 loader handles cycle\n  detection at load time (issue 305). Editor-side validation is\n  unnecessary; the wire-draw machinery just needs to render it.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `draw_all`, `hit_test_wire`,\n  `draw_bezier`, control-point math\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `box_height`, `BOX_W`, port positions\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — wire-create flow (no change needed; the\n  existing flow already permits self-loop construction)\n- `issues/221-iterator-box.md` — iterator self-re-spawn pattern\n  that motivates this\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — phase 3 loader's cycle\n  validation policy\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md"
        },
        "id":"toolu_011rUb5DzDZodtd7ro2SA8XV"
      }]

          "command":"git add issues/ docs/ && git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nOpen 228: self-loop wires routed around the box body\n\nA wire whose from_box and to_box are the same box currently renders\nas a Bézier straight through the body — the curve clips into the\nrectangle and is unreadable. Allowing self-loops is useful with\niterator boxes (the natural pattern for accumulators, polling, and\n\"keep going while X\" loops via a comparator branch) so the editor\nshould render them clearly. The fix is a different control-point\ncalculation when from_box === to_box: pull the curve out, down, and\naround the box body in a horseshoe.\n\nPhase 3's graph loader already accepts iterator-cycles and rejects\nnon-iterator-cycles at load (issue 305). The editor doesn't need to\nknow which is which; it just needs to draw the wire correctly.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Open 228"

    "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"228 is open. Let me also clarify the bug-explanation point you asked about — three takeaways worth keeping in mind:\n\n**1. JavaScript reference identity matters when state is shared.** Two modules holding \"the same box\" need to literally hold the same object. The moment one of them does `Boxes.boxes[id] = newObject`, anyone else holding the old reference is stuck with stale data. That's true for any mutable shared state in JS.\n\n**2. The \"fetch fresh, mutate, replace cache\" pattern looks safe but isn't.** It's a reasonable pattern when nobody else holds references to the cached object. The instant a second module retains a reference (the inspector's `current_box`), the pattern silently breaks consistency. The fix — mutate in place — keeps every reference pointing at the same object, but it gives up concurrency safety (other tabs can't have edited the box). For this project that trade is fine.\n\n**3. The cascade was self-reinforcing.** The auto-grow path's \"if current_box.id matches, show(box)\" line was acting as a delayed reconciliation — it eventually fixed `current_box` but only on the next wire-create. So the bug appeared \"intermittent\": first wire-create after a fresh box looked broken, the second one quietly fixed everything. That kind of \"second action fixes the first action's leftovers\" pattern is a strong signal of stale-reference bugs.\n\nWant to keep going? Remaining open: 216 (read-file box, small lib like `text.lua`), 219 (map compiler — phase 3 work), 221 (iterator box), and the new follow-ups (223–228). 221 is the next one I'd expect from your earlier sequence (210 → 217 → 213 → 221, and 213 is closed-as-superseded)."
      }]
  },

{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T21:56:35.731Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.\n\nSummary:\n1. Primary Request and Intent:\n   The user wanted to work through Phase 2 UX issues in the SoraMech project (a visual FSM/dataflow editor at `/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/`). The session built on prior work that had specified Phase 3 issues 301-311. Specific user requests through the day:\n   - Implement Phase 2 UX issues in sequence\n   - Fix the canvas zoom direction bug (\"zoom out works but zoom in is broken\")\n   - Rewrite canvas pan/zoom from scratch when bug persisted\n   - Implement fit-to-view (202) cleanly with new canvas model\n   - Replace prompt() with map picker panel (203), remove redundant \"switch map\" toolbar button\n   - Add interaction hints overlay (204)\n   - Add compile button placeholder (222)\n   - Add floating draggable source viewer (215) with width = max line clamped to [80,120] chars\n   - Implement variadic input UX (217 part B): `+/×` buttons, then auto-grow on wire-connect/value-set, no auto-shrink, var toggle snips wires\n   - Defer 213 as superseded by phase 3 issue 302\n   - Fix variadic toggle bug where wires don't snip and slots don't auto-grow when toggling on with existing wire\n   - Fix wire-erase tool sometimes missing wires (pointer skipping)\n   - Open follow-up issues for syntax highlighting (223), editable names + canvas value-edit (224), dir picker improvements (225), hide output for no-return functions (226), hide view button without ref (227), self-loop wire routing (228)\n   - Explain the stale cache bug after fix worked\n   - Open issue for self-loop wire connections\n\n2. Key Technical Concepts:\n   - JavaScript object reference identity vs mutation\n   - In-place mutation pattern for shared cache state (avoid replacing references)\n   - Canvas 2D transform math: scale-then-translate with screen-pixel pan offsets\n   - Anchor-and-delta drag pattern (avoids accumulating error)\n   - Bezier curve hit-testing with sample points\n   - HTML overlays positioned over canvas (source viewer)\n   - Variadic input naming convention: `<base>_<index>` slots\n   - Idempotent auto-grow (check \"is last slot of variadic group\")\n   - JSON Lines format (mentioned for phase 3 issue 311)\n   - SoraMech architecture: editor + runner + server, three independent programs\n   - Single-output-wire-per-box rule\n   - Comparator branching (lt/eq/gt) replaces named output ports\n   - Phase 3 thread pool runtime (specced in issues 301-311)\n\n3. Files and Code Sections:\n\n   - **`assets/js/001-canvas.js`** - Rewritten with screen-pixel pan model\n     - Important because the original world-space camera math was causing zoom-direction confusion\n     - Final pattern:\n     ```js\n     // sx = wx * zoom + pan_x\n     function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n       return { x: wx * zoom + pan_x, y: wy * zoom + pan_y };\n     }\n     function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n       return { x: (sx - pan_x) / zoom, y: (sy - pan_y) / zoom };\n     }\n     // start_frame uses translate(pan_x, pan_y); scale(zoom, zoom)\n     // Wheel zoom: pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom (zoom about cursor)\n     // Backward-compatible cam getter exposes x/y/zoom\n     ```\n\n   - **`assets/js/004-inspector.js`** - Major changes for variadic UI and bug fixes\n     - Added variadic helpers: `parse_variadic_name`, `is_variadic_slot`, `variadic_slots_for`, `last_variadic_index`\n     - Operations: `make_variadic`, `unmake_variadic`, `add_variadic_slot`, `remove_variadic_slot`\n     - `auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name)` - exported for wires module\n     - `update_target_connections` - bilateral connection updates with rollback\n     - `sever_output_wires` - clears outgoing wires on comparator toggle\n     - Critical fix: variadic toggle now snips all wires:\n     ```js\n     // make_variadic: snip wires, then rename\n     await update_target_connections([port_name], () => null);\n     current_box.inputs[idx].name = new_name;\n     current_box.variadic_inputs.push(base);\n     ```\n     - View button added next to ref field\n\n   - **`assets/js/005-app.js`** - Multiple feature additions\n     - `fit_to_view()` - centers camera on box bounding box\n     - `draw_empty_hint(ctx)` - canvas hint overlay when empty\n     - `compile_map()` - placeholder for phase 3 compile pipeline\n     - `show_map_picker` - rewritten with server URL input\n     - `init()` - removed prompt(), shows picker on first load\n     - Wire-erase pointer interpolation:\n     ```js\n     let last_erase_pos = null;\n     // interpolate between cursor positions during drag\n     const n = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(dist / 4));\n     for (let i = 1; i <= n; i++) {\n       const t = i / n;\n       erase_at(last_erase_pos.x + dx * t, last_erase_pos.y + dy * t);\n     }\n     ```\n     - Canvas right-click context menu has \"view source\" item\n\n   - **`assets/js/006-wires.js`** - Stale reference bug fix\n     - `create_connection` and `delete_connection` rewritten to mutate cached objects in place:\n     ```js\n     // OLD (broken): Boxes.boxes[id] = freshly_fetched\n     // NEW: const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id]; mutate in place\n     src_box.connections.push(conn);\n     await API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box);\n     // No reference replacement\n     ```\n     - Auto-grow integration: `await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);`\n\n   - **`assets/js/008-source-view.js`** (NEW) - Floating source viewer\n     - `open_source_view(ref, anchor_box?)` public API\n     - Width = max line length clamped to [80, 120] chars × monospace width\n     - Height = canvas height / 2\n     - Drag from header with anchor-and-delta math\n     - ResizeObserver clamps size to canvas bounds\n     - Multiple windows tracked in `open_windows[]` with z-counter\n\n   - **`assets/index.html`** - Toolbar buttons, source viewer CSS, removed switch-map button\n\n   - **`libs/text.lua`** (NEW) - `M.concat(sep, ...)` and `M.split(text, sep)`\n   \n   - **`libs/text.lua.info.md`** (NEW) - Documentation\n\n   - **`src/001-schema.lua`** - Added `variadic_inputs` validation\n\n   - **Issue files**: Created 223, 224, 225, 226, 227, 228;   "parentUuid":"6900df6c-9ce5-41b9-aa15-34b80a14d449",
  "version":"2.1.121",
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "entrypoint":"cli",
  "type":"attachment",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "attachment":{
    "type":"file",
    "content":{
      "type":"text",
      "file":{
        "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md",
        "numLines":159,
        "startLine":1,
        "totalLines":159,
        "content":"# 228 — Self-loop wires: connect a box's output to its own input, routed around the body\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe connection model permits a wire whose `from_box` and `to_box`\nare the same — `create_connection` checks for exact duplicates but\ndoes not reject self-loops. The wire renderer in\n`assets/js/006-wires.js::draw_all` then draws a cubic Bézier from\nthe output dot (right edge of the box) to the input dot (left edge\nof the box), with control points fixed at\n`±BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80px` horizontally. For a self-loop, both\nendpoints sit on opposite sides of the same body and the curve cuts\nstraight through the middle of the box — visually unreadable, and\nclipped by the box rectangle.\n\nHit-testing samples the same Bézier path and inherits the same\nproblem: clicks land in the wrong place because the wire sits\nunderneath the box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nSelf-loops are allowed and render as a wire that loops *around*\nthe box body, not through it. The user can wire a box's output to\nits own input the same way as any other connection (drag from\noutput port, release on input port).\n\n### Why this matters\n\nSelf-loops are useful with iterator boxes (issue 221): an\niterator's output feeds back into its own queued input, building\nan accumulator or polling-state pattern. The comparator (issue\n210) routes one branch to the input on a self-loop, the other\nbranch downstream. With queued inputs (phase 3 issue 302) the\nloop terminates naturally when the queue empties.\n\nThe runtime semantics differ between phase 2 and phase 3:\n- **Phase 2 (current)**: the synchronous executor walks dependency\n  order. A self-loop on a non-iterator box never resolves and\n  hangs the run. The user is responsible for not shipping such\n  maps. The editor allows constructing them; the runner errors\n  cleanly (or hangs, which is also a clear signal).\n- **Phase 3**: the C graph loader (issue 305) rejects non-iterator\n  cycles at load time and accepts iterator cycles. The editor\n  doesn't need to know which is which; the loader catches misuse.\n\nEither way, the editor's job is just to draw the wire correctly.\n\n### Routing\n\nThe wire path for a self-loop goes out the right side from the\noutput dot, around either the top or the bottom of the box body\n(pick deterministically — say, always the bottom), and back to\nthe input dot on the left side.\n\nTwo reasonable shapes:\n\n1. **Cubic Bézier with off-axis control points** — keep the same\n   `draw_bezier` machinery but pick control points that pull the\n   curve out, down, and around. For a box at world-(x, y) with\n   width W and height H, output dot at (x+W, oy) and input dot at\n   (x, iy):\n\n   ```\n   src = (x+W, oy)\n   dst = (x,   iy)\n   cp1 = (x+W + LOOP_OFFSET, oy + H)\n   cp2 = (x   - LOOP_OFFSET, iy + H)\n   ```\n\n   `LOOP_OFFSET` ~ 60–80px gives a smooth horseshoe under the box.\n\n2. **Polyline** — straight segments: right from output dot,\n   down past the box bottom, left past the box left edge, up to\n   input dot. Visually crisper, easier to hit-test, but stylistically\n   inconsistent with every other wire being a Bézier.\n\nRecommendation: option 1. Reuses `draw_bezier` with different\ncontrol-point math, no new rendering primitive needed.\n\n### Hit-testing\n\n`hit_test_wire` samples the Bézier path at `HIT_SAMPLES = 20`\npoints. With the same machinery and routed-around control points,\nthe samples sit on the curved path under the box, not behind the\nbody. Clicks register correctly.\n\nThe wire-erase pointer-interpolation fix (commit 899f35d) walks\nthe *cursor* path, not the wire's path. It already works for any\nwire shape `hit_test_wire` can match. No additional change needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/006-wires.js`:\n\n1. Detect self-loop where the wire is being computed:\n   `c.from_box === c.to_box`.\n2. When self-loop, compute `cp1` and `cp2` with the looped offsets\n   above. The offset is in world units, so it scales with zoom\n   correctly.\n3. Pass `cp1` / `cp2` into `draw_bezier` (refactor to accept\n   explicit control points, or add a sibling `draw_loop_bezier`).\n4. `hit_test_wire` does the same self-loop check and uses the\n   same `bezier_point` sampling with the looped control points.\n\n```js\nfunction endpoint_controls(c, src, dst, box) {\n  if (c.from_box === c.to_box && box) {\n    const h = Boxes.box_height(box);\n    return {\n      cp1: { x: src.x + LOOP_OFFSET,        y: src.y + h * 0.7 },\n      cp2: { x: dst.x - LOOP_OFFSET,        y: dst.y + h * 0.7 },\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    cp1: { x: src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: src.y },\n    cp2: { x: dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: dst.y },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Box height changes** while a self-loop wire exists (variadic\n  slot added → box grows): the wire's control points are derived\n  per-frame from current `box_height`, so it adapts automatically.\n- **Output is a comparator branch** (`from_branch` is `lt`/`eq`/`gt`):\n  the loop renders the same way; the branch coloring still applies.\n  A user can wire `lt` back to the same box's input, which is a\n  legitimate self-loop pattern for \"while less than X, keep going.\"\n- **Multiple self-loops on one box** (different output → different\n  inputs, or comparator branches): each renders independently.\n  They will overlap; visual cleanup if it ever matters in\n  practice.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Top vs bottom routing**: always-below is simplest. Always-above\n  is also fine. Configurable per-wire (right-click → \"route around\n  top\") is overkill until someone asks for it.\n- **Self-loop validation in the schema**: the phase 2 schema\n  doesn't reject self-loops, and the phase 3 loader handles cycle\n  detection at load time (issue 305). Editor-side validation is\n  unnecessary; the wire-draw machinery just needs to render it.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `draw_all`, `hit_test_wire`,\n  `draw_bezier`, control-point math\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `box_height`, `BOX_W`, port positions\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — wire-create flow (no change needed; the\n  existing flow already permits self-loop construction)\n- `issues/221-iterator-box.md` — iterator self-re-spawn pattern\n  that motivates this\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — phase 3 loader's cycle\n  validation policy\n"
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md"
  },
  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

      "type":"text",
      "file":{
        "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/227-hide-view-button-without-ref.md",
        "numLines":70,
        "startLine":1,
        "totalLines":70,
        "content":"# 227 — Hide the inspector \"view\" button when the box has no ref\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe inspector renders three buttons next to the `ref` field on every\ncall box: `browse` (open the file browser), `view` (open the\nfloating source viewer, issue 215), and the inputs/outputs sections.\nThe `view` button shows up for every call box regardless of whether\n`box.ref` has been set yet.\n\nClicking `view` on a box with no ref calls\n`SourceView.open_source_view(current_box.ref, current_box)`, which\nfalls through to `fetch_source(ref)` returning the error \"no ref\nset on this box.\" A status-bar error appears. The button is\nnon-functional until a ref is set; it shouldn't be visible until\nthen.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe `view` button is rendered only when `box.ref` is non-empty. When\nthe user creates a fresh box and hasn't yet picked a function via the\nfile browser, the button is absent. After picking a function, the\nbutton appears. After clearing the ref (manual edit of the input\nfield), the button disappears again.\n\nThe `browse` button stays visible at all times — that's the entry\npoint to actually setting a ref.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show`, in the block that builds the\nref row:\n\n```js\nconst view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n// ... existing setup ...\nref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\nref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\nif (box.ref && box.ref !== '') {\n  ref_wrap.appendChild(view_btn);\n}\n```\n\nThe button should also appear/disappear in response to the user\ntyping into the ref input. Easiest way: re-render the ref row on\ninput. Or: keep the button always in the DOM but toggle its\n`hidden` attribute on input.\n\nToggle-on-input is simpler:\n\n```js\nref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n  current_box.ref = ref_inp.value;\n  view_btn.hidden = !ref_inp.value;\n  save();\n});\n```\n\nAdd `view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at button creation time so the\ninitial render is correct.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field row, `view_btn` setup\n- `issues/completed/215-view-box-source.md` — the source viewer\n  this button opens\n"
      }
    },
    "displayPath":"issues/227-hide-view-button-without-ref.md",
    "filename":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/227-hide-view-button-without-ref.md"
  },
  "sessionId":"579d58b3-7452-44f3-983a-80ff5821082a"
}

The C\n   spec generates a wrapper from the box's declared signature and\n   produces a `.so` in `compiled/bin/` (issue 307). Lua and Bash\n   specs have no compile step; their files are copied verbatim.\n4. **Copy spec libraries.** The `langs/<name>/spec.so` files for\n   every language used in the map are copied to\n   `compiled/langs/<name>/spec.so`. The pool runner discovers\n   specs relative to its binary location, so this co-location is\n   what makes the deployment self-contained.\n5. **Copy the runner binary.** `soramech-pool` is copied to\n   `compiled/pool-runner`. (A symlink works too, for development.)\n6. **Write the manifest.** `compiled/manifest.json` lists every\n   box, its language, the path of its compiled artifact (or source\n   file for interpreted languages), and the SoraMech build version\n   the deployment was compiled against.\n\n### What stays in the box JSON\nCanvas positions, labels, wire layout — everything the editor needs\nto display and edit the graph. The JSON is the editor's\nrepresentation of the graph. The compiled directory is the\ndeliverable. Useful for CI and headless deployment.\n\n## Design constraints\n\n- The editor still has no conception of *running* maps — only\n  compiling them. Run is a separate concern (the user invokes the\n  pool-runner binary themselves).\n- Compile is incremental: mtime comparison on each artifact. Walk the map graph using the C loader (issue 305) — the same\n   code the runtime uses. Emit a list of (box, language, files).\n2. Implement the source-copy step. Every `box.ref` file plus any\n   `require`/`source`/`#include` dependencies (resolvable via\n   static analysis or just-copy-the-whole-libs/-directory).\n3. For C boxes: invoke the C spec's `compile` callback (issue 307)\n   per box. Outputs land in `compiled/bin/`.\n4. Copy `langs/<name>/spec.so` for every language present.\n5. Copy or symlink `soramech-pool`.\n6. Write `manifest.json`.\n7. Wire `POST /maps/<name>/compile` in the server (issue 222\n   button calls this).\n8. Smoke test: compile `maps/hello`, run\n   `./maps/hello/compiled/pool-runner`, verify result matches\n   the phase 2 run.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — the runner binary that gets copied in\n- `langs/<name>/spec.so` — language specs that get copied in\n- `langs/<name>/spec.c::compile` — per-language compile callback\n- `issues/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` — UI button\n  that triggers this\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — `compile` interface\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — graph-walk logic shared with\n  the runtime\n- `issues/307-c-language-spec.md` — C wrapper generation\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — describes the `compiled/` directory\n  layout\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — phase 2\n  driver model (historical reference)\n"

{

        "content":"1\t# 226 — Hide output port and inspector output section when the function returns nothing\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\t\n8\tWhen the file browser parses a function that has no return values\n9\t(e.g. `function M.write_result(text) print(text) end` — sink, no\n10\treturns), the on-select handler sets `box.inputs` from the parsed\n11\tsignature but doesn't carry through any \"this function has no\n12\toutput\" signal. The inspector then renders the output section\n13\t(comparator toggle + comparand input) for every call box,\n14\tunconditionally, and the canvas draws an output port dot.\n15\t\n16\tThe UI implies you can wire from the output, but at runtime the\n17\tfunction returns nil and the wire just propagates a nil value.\n18\tVisually noisy; conceptually misleading.\n19\t\n20\t## Intended behavior\n21\t\n22\tA box whose function has no return values:\n23\t- Has no output port dot on the canvas.\n24\t- Has no output section in the inspector (no compare toggle, no\n25\t  comparand input, no output area at all).\n26\t- Cannot have outgoing wires drawn from it. The wire-drawing\n27\t  interaction in `005-app.js` skips it because there's no output\n28\t  port to grab.\n29\t\n30\tThe single-output-wire-per-box rule from issue 218 still holds for\n31\tboxes with return values; this issue carves out the explicit \"no\n32\toutput\" case.\n33\t\n34\t## Where the signal comes from\n35\t\n36\tThe Lua and Bash parsers in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` already\n37\treturn a `fn.outputs` array — empty when the function has no\n38\treturn statements. The on-select handler currently does not store\n39\tthis on the box. The fix is to persist a boolean flag (or the\n40\tempty `outputs` array itself) so the inspector and canvas can\n41\tcheck it.\n42\t\n43\tTwo options:\n44\t\n45\t1. **Persist `box.has_output: false`** when the parser detects no\n46\t   return values. The inspector and canvas check this field. New\n47\t   field, but unambiguous.\n48\t2. **Persist `box.outputs: []`** (the empty array). The inspector\n49\t   and canvas treat `box.outputs === []` as \"no output.\" Reuses\n50\t   the legacy field that was previously used for named output\n51\t   ports (issue 210 superseded it; this gives it a new\n52\t   single-purpose meaning).\n53\t\n54\tOption 1 is cleaner because the name says exactly what it means.\n55\tOption 2 reuses an existing-but-stale field, which has the\n56\tadvantage of zero schema churn but the disadvantage of overloading\n57\tthe field's meaning. Lean toward option 1.\n58\t\n59\t## Edge cases\n60\t\n61\t- **Manually-added boxes** that haven't been wired through the\n62\t  file browser: no information about return values exists. Default\n63\t  to `has_output: true` (current behavior). The user can flip it\n64\t  manually if they want a sink box without going through the file\n65\t  browser.\n66\t- **Functions whose return value depends on a branch** (some\n67\t  return, some don't): the parser already lists every distinct\n68\t  return shape. As long as ANY return statement exists, treat the\n69\t  function as having an output. `has_output: false` only when\n70\t  zero return statements.\n71\t- **Comparator toggle**: if the user activates the comparator on\n72\t  a non-output box, that's nonsensical (there's no value to\n73\t  compare). The comparator UI only renders when the box has an\n74\t  output anyway, so this falls out naturally.\n75\t\n76\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n77\t\n78\t1. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::on_select` (in\n79\t   `004-inspector.js`) — when `fn.outputs.length === 0`, set\n80\t   `current_box.has_output = false`. Otherwise delete the field\n81\t   (treat absence as `true`).\n82\t2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — wrap the entire output\n83\t   section render in `if (box.has_output !== false) { ... }`.\n84\t3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — when\n85\t   `box.has_output === false`, return an empty `outputs` array.\n86\t   `draw_box` already iterates `outputs` and draws nothing for an\n87\t   empty array.\n88\t4. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — early-out if the\n89\t   `from_box` has `has_output === false` (defensive — the canvas\n90\t   wouldn't have a port to grab from, but cover the edge case).\n91\t5. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `has_output` as an optional\n92\t   boolean field. No validation beyond type-check.\n93\t6. Test: open the hello map, look at `write-result` (which is a\n94\t   sink). After re-browsing it through the file browser, output\n95\t   port should disappear. Existing wires from a now-output-less\n96\t   box are dropped on save (preferable to dangling).\n97\t\n98\t## Open questions\n99\t\n100\t- Should existing wires from a box that flips to `has_output:\n101\t  false` be dropped automatically, or should the flip be rejected\n102\t  if any outgoing wires exist? Auto-drop with a status-bar\n103\t  warning is the smoother path.\n104\t- Should the file browser do this automatically on every re-pick,\n105\t  or only the first time a function is selected? Doing it every\n106\t  time matches what we do for `box.inputs` (always overwritten on\n107\t  re-select), and keeps the box's `has_output` flag in sync with\n108\t  the actual function.\n109\t\n110\t## Relevant files\n111\t\n112\t- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show` (output section render),\n113\t  `open_browser` (on-select handler that sets the flag)\n114\t- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — parsers that detect zero returns\n115\t- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `port_positions`, `draw_box`\n116\t- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `create_connection` (defensive check)\n117\t- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts `has_output`\n118\t- `issues/completed/218-enforce-single-output-driver-contract.md`\n119\t  — single-wire rule that this issue qualifies\n120\t",
