      "content":"# 226 — Hide output port and inspector output section when the function returns nothing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the file browser parses a function that has no return values\n(e.g. `function M.write_result(text) print(text) end` — sink, no\nreturns), the on-select handler sets `box.inputs` from the parsed\nsignature but doesn't carry through any \"this function has no\noutput\" signal. The inspector then renders the output section\n(comparator toggle + comparand input) for every call box,\nunconditionally, and the canvas draws an output port dot.\n\nThe UI implies you can wire from the output, but at runtime the\nfunction returns nil and the wire just propagates a nil value.\nVisually noisy; conceptually misleading.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box whose function has no return values:\n- Has no output port dot on the canvas.\n- Has no output section in the inspector (no compare toggle, no\n  comparand input, no output area at all).\n- Cannot have outgoing wires drawn from it. The wire-drawing\n  interaction in `005-app.js` skips it because there's no output\n  port to grab.\n\nThe single-output-wire-per-box rule from issue 218 still holds for\nboxes with return values; this issue carves out the explicit \"no\noutput\" case.\n\n## Where the signal comes from\n\nThe Lua and Bash parsers in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` already\nreturn a `fn.outputs` array — empty when the function has no\nreturn statements. The on-select handler currently does not store\nthis on the box. The fix is to persist a boolean flag (or the\nempty `outputs` array itself) so the inspector and canvas can\ncheck it.\n\nTwo options:\n\n1. **Persist `box.has_output: false`** when the parser detects no\n   return values. The inspector and canvas check this field. New\n   field, but unambiguous.\n2. **Persist `box.outputs: []`** (the empty array). The inspector\n   and canvas treat `box.outputs === []` as \"no output.\" Reuses\n   the legacy field that was previously used for named output\n   ports (issue 210 superseded it; this gives it a new\n   single-purpose meaning).\n\nOption 1 is cleaner because the name says exactly what it means.\nOption 2 reuses an existing-but-stale field, which has the\nadvantage of zero schema churn but the disadvantage of overloading\nthe field's meaning. Lean toward option 1.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- **Manually-added boxes** that haven't been wired through the\n  file browser: no information about return values exists. Default\n  to `has_output: true` (current behavior). The user can flip it\n  manually if they want a sink box without going through the file\n  browser.\n- **Functions whose return value depends on a branch** (some\n  return, some don't): the parser already lists every distinct\n  return shape. As long as ANY return statement exists, treat the\n  function as having an output. `has_output: false` only when\n  zero return statements.\n- **Comparator toggle**: if the user activates the comparator on\n  a non-output box, that's nonsensical (there's no value to\n  compare). The comparator UI only renders when the box has an\n  output anyway, so this falls out naturally.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::on_select` (in\n   `004-inspector.js`) — when `fn.outputs.length === 0`, set\n   `current_box.has_output = false`. Otherwise delete the field\n   (treat absence as `true`).\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — wrap the entire output\n   section render in `if (box.has_output !== false) { ... }`.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — when\n   `box.has_output === false`, return an empty `outputs` array.\n   `draw_box` already iterates `outputs` and draws nothing for an\n   empty array.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — early-out if the\n   `from_box` has `has_output === false` (defensive — the canvas\n   wouldn't have a port to grab from, but cover the edge case).\n5. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `has_output` as an optional\n   boolean field. No validation beyond type-check.\n6. Test: open the hello map, look at `write-result` (which is a\n   sink). After re-browsing it through the file browser, output\n   port should disappear. Existing wires from a now-output-less\n   box are dropped on save (preferable to dangling).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should existing wires from a box that flips to `has_output:\n  false` be dropped automatically, or should the flip be rejected\n  if any outgoing wires exist? Auto-drop with a status-bar\n  warning is the smoother path.\n- Should the file browser do this automatically on every re-pick,\n  or only the first time a function is selected? Doing it every\n  time matches what we do for `box.inputs` (always overwritten on\n  re-select), and keeps the box's `has_output` flag in sync with\n  the actual function.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show` (output section render),\n  `open_browser` (on-select handler that sets the flag)\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — parsers that detect zero returns\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `port_positions`, `draw_box`\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `create_connection` (defensive check)\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts `has_output`\n- `issues/completed/218-enforce-single-output-driver-contract.md`\n  — single-wire rule that this issue qualifies\n"

Every box source — Lua, C, Bash, anything else —\nrenders the same: white text on dark background, no syntax cues.\nReading a function in the editor is harder than it should be.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach language has its own small JavaScript lexer that turns raw text\ninto a list of typed tokens. The source viewer asks the lexer for the\nfile's tokens, then wraps each token in a span with a CSS class per\ntoken type. Styling is done purely in CSS, so themes are independent\nof lexers.\n\nThis mirrors the runtime language-spec architecture (issue 303):\neach language is responsible for its own concerns, the editor /\nrunner only knows how to call into a shared interface. No\nSoraMech-internal language list, no transpiling. Users add a new\nlanguage by writing a small JS file.\n\n### Lexer interface\n\nEach lexer is a JS module exporting a single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/lexer.js\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  // Returns an ordered array of tokens covering the entire input.\n  // Tokens must not overlap and together must cover [0, text.length).\n  return [\n    { type: 'keyword', start: 0,  end: 5  },\n    { type: 'plain',   start: 5,  end: 6  },\n    { type: 'string',  start: 6,  end: 17 },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nToken types are convention-only — the viewer applies a CSS class\nnamed `syntax-<type>` to each span. The standard set is:\n\n| type        | typical use                                        |\n|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `keyword`   | language keywords (`function`, `if`, `local`, …)   |\n\n==> /mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/224-editable-port-names-and-canvas-value-edit.md <==\n# 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput port names are read-only labels in the inspector — derived from\nthe function's parameter names when the file browser populates the\nbox (issue 207, 208). Each port row in the inspector also carries a\nliteral value input. With variadic inputs (issue 217), a box with\nseveral slots produces a tall, narrow list of name+type+value rows\nthat crowds the sidebar.\n\nThe canvas already renders port names next to their dots, so the\nname appears twice — once on the canvas (read-only label) and once\nin the inspector (read-only label).\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nMove both the port name and the literal value input out of the\ninspector and onto the canvas next to the port dot. The inspector\nkeeps only the variadic toggle / remove-slot buttons and any\nnon-port box-level fields (ref / fn / comparator).\n\n### Why\n\n- The inspector is crowded with redundant data (the canvas already\n  shows port names).\n- Literal values often need more horizontal room than a 72px input\n  field allows, especially for prompts, paths, or JSON snippets.\n- Reading the box's full configuration without clicking through the\n  inspector becomes possible — every input's name and value is\n  visible directly on the canvas.\n- 208's \"read-only port names\" decision was about preventing typo\n  drift between source code and box JSON; the file browser still\n  populates names from the parsed signature, but the user should be\n  free to override them after the fact.\n\n### Reverses 208's read-only-name decision\n\nIssue 208 made input port names non-editable on the principle that\nthey should match the parsed function signature exactly. This issue\nflips that — names become editable again, with the trade-off that a\ntypo can desynchronize the editor's record from the function the box\ncalls. The cost is a per-box runtime error rather than a hidden\nsilent skip, so it surfaces clearly. Only the subdirectories are rendered; any\nsource files in the current directory are invisible.\n\nThis makes navigation harder than it should be — there's no visible\nconfirmation that you've reached the right directory until you click\n\"use this directory\" and the file list re-renders.\n\nThe list itself uses the `.fb-file-row` class for both dirs and the\nparent-directory `..` row, so dirs and the (currently absent) files\nwould render identically. Easy to do but\n   inaccessible alone.\n3. **Underline** — directories underlined to suggest \"clickable\n   link\". Already a familiar web idiom. Pairs well with color.\n\nRecommendation: layer (1) and (2) — icon prefix for accessibility,",

      "content":"# SoraMech — Roadmap\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation (complete)\n\nGoal: a map you can edit in the browser and execute from the\nterminal.\n\nAt the end of phase 1, the user can:\n- Open the editor at `http://localhost:7700/`, see a canvas, create\n  boxes, set their `ref` / `fn` / `inputs`, wire them together\n- Save edits as box files on disk via the HTTP file CRUD server\n- Run `luajit src/007-runner-main.lua <map-dir>` to execute the map\n- Add a custom language driver and have the runner use it\n\nIssues 101–110, all complete and moved to `issues/completed/`.\n\nDemo: `issues/completed/demos/phase-1/`.\n\n## Phase 2 — Editor & graph model (current)\n\nGoal: an editor you can actually use to build maps, and the graph\nmodel the phase 3 runtime will consume.\n\nThis phase is editor-focused with some graph-model cleanup:\n- Map picker, fit-to-view, interaction hints, entry-box marking\n- Source file browser with auto-populated input ports\n- File browser library directories\n- Single-output driver contract (issue 218)\n- Comparator-based branching replaces the old `branch` box kind with\n  named ports (issue 210)\n- Comparator + iterator are the two routing primitives (issues 210,\n  221)\n- Variadic / queued inputs (issues 213, 217)\n- Map compiler (issue 219) and compile button (issue 222) — ties\n  the editor into the phase 3 build path\n- Ollama / LLM library (issue 209)\n\nPhase 2 runs on the synchronous Lua interpreter\n(`src/007-runner-main.lua`). No threading. Drivers per phase 1.\n\nSee `issues/phase-2-progress.md` for the live status.\n\n## Phase 3 — Thread pool runtime (planned, fully designed)\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel, with persistent per-worker\nlanguage runtimes and proper inter-task value plumbing.\n\nDesigned across issues 301–311:\n\n- 301 — pool lifecycle and per-worker init\n- 302 — wire value slot store (per-task ring buffers, refcount,\n  large-value heap)\n- 303 — language runtime spec (`lang_spec_t` interface)\n- 304 — task dispatch layer\n- 305 — C graph loader (replaces `src/003-loader.lua`)\n- 306 — Lua language spec (in-process via `lua_State`)\n- 307 — C language spec (in-process via `dlopen`, with compile)\n- 308 — Bash language spec (out-of-process via Unix domain socket)\n- 309 — build system & Makefile orchestration\n- 310 — priority queue (wired in, no-op behaviorally)\n- 311 — integration tests & run output (`last-run.jsonl`)\n\nWhen phase 3 lands, the synchronous Lua runner retires. The editor\nand the map directory format do not change — the runtime mechanism\nbeneath the box is what changes. See `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`\nfor the design discussion.\n\n## Phase 4 — SoraMind integration\n\nGoal: boxes that call SoraMind inference endpoints on the Alpine\ncluster.\n\n- LLM call box type — sends a prompt, receives a completion string\n- Prompt assembly: text values wired from upstream boxes, data file\n  sections explicitly loaded into prompt context\n- Comparator-routed classifiers (\"rogue / wizard / else\" via lt/eq/gt\n  on a hashed-class score)\n- Streaming output from SoraMind inference back to the runner\n\nBuilt on the phase 3 runtime — the LLM call is a regular box function,\njust one whose backing service is a network endpoint.\n\n## Phase 5 — Map-to-map calls\n\nGoal: a box that invokes another map as a subroutine.\n\n- Map call box type: specifies another map directory, passes inputs,\n  receives outputs\n- Maps run concurrently with each other (sub-pool per map)\n- Entry/exit contracts defined in `meta.json`\n\n## Phase 6 — Remote runner\n\nGoal: run a map on the Alpine cluster, edit it from a laptop.\n\n- Pool runner on a remote machine\n- File-CRUD server on the same machine exposes map files over HTTP\n- Browser editor on the laptop connects to the remote server\n- Results written to remote `last-run.jsonl`, accessible via server\n\nPhases 4, 5, and 6 are scoped only briefly here — concrete planning\nhappens once phase 3 is done.\n"

Lean toward","+  static analysis with a fallback whole-tree copy if analysis fails.","+"," ## Open questions"," "," - macOS: `.so` becomes `.dylib`, and there's no `/proc/self/exe`."],

    "originalFile":"# 309 — Build system & Makefile orchestration\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nPhase 2 has no compiled binary. The runner is a Lua script\n(`src/007-runner-main.lua`) invoked via `luajit`. Drivers are shell\nscripts that compile per-box C source on demand. There is no\ntop-level Makefile, no vendoring of C dependencies, no link step\nbeyond per-driver compile.\n\nPhase 3 introduces a real C binary (the pool runner) plus a set of\nlanguage spec `.so` files. They need to compile in the right order\nwith the right flags, and the build needs to be reproducible from a\nclean checkout.\n\n## Concept\n\nA top-level `Makefile` at the project root orchestrates the entire\nphase 3 build. It builds:\n\n1. The pool runner binary: `soramech-pool` (statically links the\n   3d-rts task pool, the vendored JSON parser, the slot store, the\n   graph loader, the dispatch layer, the spec registry).\n2. Each language spec: `langs/<name>/spec.so`, built by a small\n   per-spec Makefile.\n3. (Optional) Unit test binaries.\n\nEach component has its own Makefile if it has non-trivial build\nrules. The top-level Makefile delegates to them via `$(MAKE) -C\n<dir>`. A clean checkout becomes a working build with `make`.\n\n## Directory layout\n\n```\nsoramech/\n├── Makefile                       ← top-level orchestration\n├── soramech-pool                  ← built binary (gitignored)\n├── src/\n│   ├── 008-pool-runner.c          ← main entry, pool lifecycle (issue 301)\n│   ├── slot-store.c / .h          ← per-task slot allocator (issue 302)\n│   ├── graph-loader.c / .h        ← C loader, replaces 003-loader.lua (issue 305)\n│   ├── dispatch.c / .h            ← dispatch action (issue 304)\n│   └── spec-registry.c / .h       ← spec dlopen/registry (issue 303)\n├── libs/\n│   ├── task-pool/                 ← vendored 3d-rts pool\n│   │   ├── 900-task-pool.h\n│   │   └── 900-task-pool.c\n│   └── json/                      ← vendored JSON parser (cJSON, jsmn, etc.)\n│       ├── cjson.h\n│       └── cjson.c\n├── langs/\n│   ├── lua/\n│   │   ├── Makefile               ← builds spec.so\n│   │   ├── spec.c\n│   │   └── spec.so                ← built (gitignored)\n│   ├── c/\n│   │   ├── Makefile\n│   │   ├── spec.c\n│   │   ├── soramech-c.h           ← user-facing helper header\n│   │   └── spec.so\n│   └── bash/\n│       ├── Makefile\n│       ├── spec.c\n│       ├── bash-server.sh\n│       └── spec.so\n└── build/                         ← intermediate object files (gitignored)\n```\n\n`build/` holds intermediate `.o` files; binaries land alongside their\nsources or at the project root. `.so` and `.o` files are gitignored;\n`make clean` removes them.\n\n## Top-level targets\n\n```make\n.PHONY: all runner specs clean test\n\nall: runner specs\n\nrunner: soramech-pool\n\nsoramech-pool: $(POOL_OBJECTS)\n\t$(CC) -O2 -Wall -pthread -o $@ $^ -ldl\n\nspecs:\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/lua\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/c\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/bash\n\nclean:\n\trm -f soramech-pool\n\trm -rf build/\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/lua clean\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/c clean\n\t$(MAKE) -C langs/bash clean\n\ntest: all\n\t./scripts/run-tests.sh\n```\n\n`POOL_OBJECTS` resolves to the `.o` files for every `src/*.c`,\n`libs/task-pool/*.c`, and `libs/json/*.c`. A pattern rule compiles\neach source into `build/`.\n\n## Per-language spec Makefiles\n\nEach `langs/<name>/Makefile` follows the same shape. Lua's:\n\n```make\nLUA_INCLUDE ?= /usr/include/luajit-2.1\nLUA_LIB    ?= /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu\n\nCFLAGS  = -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -I$(LUA_INCLUDE)\nLDFLAGS = -L$(LUA_LIB) -lluajit-5.1\n\nspec.so: spec.c\n\t$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -o $@ $< $(LDFLAGS)\n\nclean:\n\trm -f spec.so\n```\n\nC's spec links `-ldl`. Bash's links nothing beyond libc. The pattern\nis uniform.\n\nLuaJIT's include and lib paths are set via environment variables so\nthe build works on systems where they live elsewhere (macOS via\nhomebrew, Alpine, etc.). Defaults match Debian/Ubuntu.\n\n## Build modes\n\n```\nmake                  ← release: -O2 -Wall\nmake DEBUG=1          ← debug:   -O0 -g -DDEBUG -Wall -Wextra\nmake STRICT=1         ← strict:  release + -Werror -Wextra -Wpedantic\n```\n\n`DEBUG=1` adds `-g` for symbols and `-DDEBUG` for opt-in debug\nprints in the C sources. `STRICT=1` fails the build on any warning;\nuseful in CI.\n\n## Vendoring\n\nVendored libraries live under `libs/` and are checked into the repo\nas plain source — no submodules, no fetches at build time. To\nupdate a vendored library, copy the new sources in and commit. The\nvendored directory carries a small `VENDOR.md` noting the upstream\nsource and the version that was copied.\n\nInitial vendored libraries:\n- `libs/task-pool/` — 3d-rts task pool (issue 301)\n- `libs/json/` — JSON parser (issue 305 picks cJSON or similar)\n\nFuture additions land alongside these.\n\n## Spec discovery at runtime\n\nThe pool runner finds language specs by scanning the `langs/`\ndirectory at startup, opening each `langs/<name>/spec.so` via\n`dlopen`, and reading the `soramech_lang_spec` symbol via `dlsym`\n(per issue 303). The path to `langs/` is resolved relative to the\nrunner binary's location: the runner reads `/proc/self/exe`\n(Linux), follows the symlink, and looks for `langs/` next to it.\n\nThis means the binary is location-flexible: the user can drop the\nproject tree anywhere, and `./soramech-pool` finds its specs\nwithout a config file.\n\nIf the user wants to override (custom spec dirs for development),\n`SORAMECH_LANGS_DIR=/path/to/langs ./soramech-pool` overrides the\nauto-detected location.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- macOS: `.so` becomes `.dylib`, and there's no `/proc/self/exe`.\n  Use `_NSGetExecutablePath`. Cross-platform spec discovery is a\n  small platform-#ifdef. Fold into the spec registry implementation.\n- Out-of-tree build (a separate `build/` directory holding all\n  artifacts): nice-to-have, not blocking. Current layout uses\n  in-tree `.o` files in `build/` already — full out-of-tree means\n  the `.so`s live in `build/langs/lua/spec.so` instead of next to\n  the source. Defer.\n- Static vs dynamic linking of vendored libs: vendored sources\n  compile straight into the runner binary. No separate `.so` for\n  the task pool or JSON parser. Right call given how small they are.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Write the top-level Makefile with empty `runner`, `specs`,\n   `clean` targets. Verify `make` succeeds against an empty source\n   tree.\n2. Vendor the 3d-rts task pool into `libs/task-pool/`. Add a\n   `VENDOR.md`.\n3. Vendor cJSON (or chosen JSON parser) into `libs/json/`. Add a\n   `VENDOR.md`.\n4. Add the pool-runner build rule. Compiles `src/*.c` plus vendored\n   libs into `soramech-pool`. Initially the runner is just `int\n   main() { return 0; }` to verify the link.\n5. Add `langs/lua/Makefile`. Build `spec.so` from a stub `spec.c`.\n6. Add `langs/c/Makefile`. Same shape.\n7. Add `langs/bash/Makefile`. Same shape.\n8. Add `make DEBUG=1` and `make STRICT=1` modes.\n9. Wire `make test` into a placeholder script (real tests come from\n   issue 311).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `Makefile` — top-level (to be created)\n- `langs/lua/Makefile`, `langs/c/Makefile`, `langs/bash/Makefile`\n  — per-spec (to be created)\n- `libs/task-pool/`, `libs/json/` — vendored sources (to be added)\n- `issues/301-pool-lifecycle-and-worker-init.md` — pool runner this\n  builds\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — spec discovery uses\n  `dlopen`/`dlsym`\n- `issues/306-lua-language-spec.md`, `307-c-language-spec.md`,\n  `308-bash-language-spec.md` — per-spec build details\n- `issues/311-integration-tests-and-run-output.md` — `make test`\n  consumers\n",
    "oldString":"## Open questions",
    "newString":"## Compile and package a map for standalone execution\n\nFolded in from issue 219 (closed). The build system also handles the\n\"package a map for deployment\" step that the editor's Compile button\n(issue 222) and a CLI tool both invoke.\n\nThe compile step turns an editable map directory into a self-contained\ndeployable directory:\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/compiled/\n    pool-runner          ← copy (or symlink) of soramech-pool\n    src/                 ← every source file the map uses\n    bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n    langs/               ← copy of language spec .so files used\n    manifest.json        ← every box, its language, artifact path, build version\n```\n\nRunning `./compiled/pool-runner` executes the map without reference to\nthe editor, the live `src/` outside `compiled/`, or any external\nSoraMech installation.\n\n### Steps the compile step performs\n\n1. **Walk the graph.** Reuse the C loader (issue 305) to enumerate\n   boxes, languages, and source files.\n2. **Copy source.** Every file referenced by `box.ref` plus\n   transitively-required libs lands in `compiled/src/`. The map's\n   local `src/` is the only path `package.path` searches at runtime\n   (issue 306), so all dependencies must be present.\n3. **Compile per-box artifacts.** For each language present, invoke\n   that spec's `compile` callback (issue 303). The C spec emits a\n   wrapper from the box's signature into `compiled/bin/` (issue 307).\n   Lua and Bash have no compile step; their files are copied verbatim.\n4. **Copy spec libraries.** `langs/<name>/spec.so` for every language\n   used in the map is copied to `compiled/langs/<name>/spec.so`. The\n   pool runner's spec discovery (above) finds them relative to the\n   binary location.\n5. **Copy or symlink the runner binary.** `--portable` copies; the\n   default symlinks to save disk on the dev machine.\n6. **Write the manifest.** `compiled/manifest.json` lists every box,\n   its language, its compiled artifact path (or source file for\n   interpreted languages), and the SoraMech build version.\n\n### Incremental compile\n\nmtime comparison per artifact: if the source is newer than the\ncompiled output, recompile that one; otherwise skip. The C spec's\n`compile` callback (issue 307) implements this per-box; the package\nstep inherits it.\n\n### Editor invocation (issue 222)\n\nThe Compile button calls `POST /maps/<name>/compile`. The server\nshells out to a `soramech-compile` CLI (or invokes the same code\nin-process). Output streams back to the editor for display. The\neditor itself never runs the compiled output; the user invokes\n`./compiled/pool-runner` from a terminal.\n\n### CLI invocation\n\nStandalone `soramech-compile <map-dir>` runs the same pipeline\nwithout the server. Used in CI and headless deployment.\n\n### Errors\n\nAny failure aborts the compile and surfaces a precise message:\nwhich box, which file, what failed. Partial output is left in\n`compiled/` for inspection but the manifest is not written, so the\ndeployment is recognizably broken until a clean compile succeeds.\n\n### Open questions (compile step)\n\n- **Multi-architecture**: a directory built on x86_64 won't run on\n  arm64. Out of scope — users compile on the target. Could later\n  add cross-compile if the SoraMind cluster goes mixed-arch.\n- **Source-copy granularity**: copy the file referenced by `box.ref`\n  plus a static-analysis sweep for `require` / `source` /\n  `#include`, or just copy the entire `libs/` tree. Lean toward\n  static analysis with a fallback whole-tree copy if analysis fails.\n\n## Open questions",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

    "originalFile":"# 219 — Map compiler: package a map for standalone execution\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nPhase 2's synchronous runner interprets the box graph at runtime,\nshelling out to a language driver per box. The runner is a Lua\nscript (`src/007-runner-main.lua`); to run a map, the user must have\nSoraMech installed.\n\nPhase 3 introduces the C pool runner (`soramech-pool`, issues\n301–311) plus per-language specs under `langs/`. The runner is a\nreal binary, but it still reads the map directory at startup. The\n\"compile\" step bridges from \"an editable map directory\" to \"a\nself-contained deployable directory\" that includes the binary, all\nsource files, all compiled `.so`s, and a manifest.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe compile step (triggered by the editor's Compile button, issue\n222, or by the CLI) walks a map and produces a `compiled/`\nsubdirectory:\n\n```\nmaps/<name>/compiled/\n    pool-runner          ← the soramech-pool binary, copied here\n    src/                 ← copy of every source file the map uses\n    bin/                 ← per-box compiled .so files (C boxes)\n    langs/               ← copy of language spec .so files needed\n    manifest.json        ← every box, its language, its compiled artifact path\n```\n\nThe `compiled/` directory is the deployment artifact. Running\n`./compiled/pool-runner` executes the map without any reference to\nthe editor, the live `src/` outside `compiled/`, or any external\nSoraMech installation. Ship the directory to someone else and it\nruns.\n\n### What the compile step does\n\n1. **Walk the graph.** Use the same loader logic the runtime uses\n   (issue 305) to enumerate boxes, languages, and source files.\n2. **Copy source.** Every file referenced by `box.ref` is copied\n   into `compiled/src/`. The map's local `src/` is the only place\n   `package.path` searches at runtime (per issue 306), so all\n   dependencies must land here. This includes vendored libraries\n   the user wired in (`libs/json.lua`, `libs/ollama.lua`, etc.).\n3. **Compile per-box artifacts.** For each language present in the\n   map, invoke that spec's `compile` callback (issue 303). The C\n   spec generates a wrapper from the box's declared signature and\n   produces a `.so` in `compiled/bin/` (issue 307). Lua and Bash\n   specs have no compile step; their files are copied verbatim.\n4. **Copy spec libraries.** The `langs/<name>/spec.so` files for\n   every language used in the map are copied to\n   `compiled/langs/<name>/spec.so`. The pool runner discovers\n   specs relative to its binary location, so this co-location is\n   what makes the deployment self-contained.\n5. **Copy the runner binary.** `soramech-pool` is copied to\n   `compiled/pool-runner`. (A symlink works too, for development.)\n6. **Write the manifest.** `compiled/manifest.json` lists every\n   box, its language, the path of its compiled artifact (or source\n   file for interpreted languages), and the SoraMech build version\n   the deployment was compiled against.\n\n### What stays in the box JSON\nCanvas positions, labels, wire layout — everything the editor needs\nto display and edit the graph. The JSON is the editor's\nrepresentation of the graph. The compiled directory is the\ndeliverable. The two never need to be in sync after compile —\nthe compiled output is frozen at compile time.\n\n### Editor invocation (issue 222)\nThe Compile button in the editor triggers the same compile step via\na new server endpoint `POST /maps/<name>/compile`. The server\nshells out to a `soramech-compile` CLI (or invokes the same code\nin-process — implementation detail). Output / errors stream back to\nthe editor for display. The editor itself does not run the\ncompiled output; the user invokes `./compiled/pool-runner` from a\nterminal.\n\nThis supersedes the earlier \"no compile button in the editor\" stance\nin the original issue text — issue 222 is the formal addition of\nthe button.\n\n### CLI invocation\nA standalone CLI tool `soramech-compile <map-dir>` runs the same\npipeline without the server. Useful for CI and headless deployment.\n\n## Design constraints\n\n- The editor still has no conception of *running* maps — only\n  compiling them. Run is a separate concern (the user invokes the\n  pool-runner binary themselves).\n- Compile is incremental: mtime comparison on each artifact. If a\n  source file is newer than its compiled output, re-compile that\n  one. Otherwise skip. (Per the C spec, issue 307.)\n- Errors at any stage abort the compile and surface a precise\n  message (which box, which file, what failed).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Whether the compiled directory bundles a copy of `soramech-pool`\n  or a symlink. Bundling makes the directory portable across\n  machines; symlinking saves disk on the dev machine. Configurable\n  via a `--portable` flag.\n- Multi-architecture: a compiled directory built on x86_64 won't\n  run on arm64. Out of scope — users compile on the target\n  architecture. Could later add a cross-compile mode if the SoraMind\n  cluster is mixed-arch.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Walk the map graph using the C loader (issue 305) — the same\n   code the runtime uses. Emit a list of (box, language, files).\n2. Implement the source-copy step. Every `box.ref` file plus any\n   `require`/`source`/`#include` dependencies (resolvable via\n   static analysis or just-copy-the-whole-libs/-directory).\n3. For C boxes: invoke the C spec's `compile` callback (issue 307)\n   per box. Outputs land in `compiled/bin/`.\n4. Copy `langs/<name>/spec.so` for every language present.\n5. Copy or symlink `soramech-pool`.\n6. Write `manifest.json`.\n7. Wire `POST /maps/<name>/compile` in the server (issue 222\n   button calls this).\n8. Smoke test: compile `maps/hello`, run\n   `./maps/hello/compiled/pool-runner`, verify result matches\n   the phase 2 run.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/008-pool-runner.c` — the runner binary that gets copied in\n- `langs/<name>/spec.so` — language specs that get copied in\n- `langs/<name>/spec.c::compile` — per-language compile callback\n- `issues/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` — UI button\n  that triggers this\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — `compile` interface\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — graph-walk logic shared with\n  the runtime\n- `issues/307-c-language-spec.md` — C wrapper generation\n- `docs/001-architecture.md` — describes the `compiled/` directory\n  layout\n- `issues/completed/102-language-driver-interface.md` — phase 2\n  driver model (historical reference)\n",
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/219-map-compiler.md",
    "content":"# 219 — Map compiler\n\n## Status\nwon't implement (folded into issue 309)\n\n## Resolution\n\nThe original 219 specified a \"package a map for standalone execution\"\nstep that produces `maps/<name>/compiled/` containing the pool runner\nbinary, all source files, per-box compiled `.so`s, language spec\n`.so`s, and a manifest.\n\nEvery dependency of that work lives in phase 3:\n- 305 — graph loader (reused to walk the map)\n- 307 — C compile callback (produces per-box `.so`)\n- 303 — language spec interface (`compile` hook)\n- 309 — build system & Makefile orchestration\n\nThere is nothing to do in phase 2 — the artifacts being packaged\ndon't yet exist. The substantive content (compiled directory layout,\nmanifest format, mtime incremental compile, editor `POST\n/maps/<name>/compile` endpoint, `soramech-compile` CLI) is folded\ninto issue 309 under the \"Compile and package a map for standalone\nexecution\" section.\n\nThe editor's Compile button (issue 222, complete) is a placeholder\nuntil 309 ships the backing endpoint.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `issues/309-build-system.md` — the new home for compile/package\n- `issues/completed/222-compile-button-and-assets-directory.md` —\n  editor button that will trigger the compile step\n"
  },

        "input":{
          "content":"# 221 — Iterator box: editor surface for round-robin output routing\n\n## Status\nopen (editor surface only)\n\n## Scope\n\nThis issue covers the **editor side** of the iterator box: schema\nfield, inspector toggle, wires auto-grow, canvas rendering. The\nruntime semantics (counter on `dispatch_task_t`, successor task\nre-spawn, copy-input-to-output without invoking a language spec) are\nspecified in issue 304 and implemented as part of phase 3.\n\nThe phase 2 synchronous executor (`src/004-executor.lua`) does not\nget an interim iterator implementation — the executor is being\nretired by the phase 3 pool runner, so adding throwaway support\nhere is wasted work. Maps with iterator boxes can be authored in\nphase 2 and run in phase 3.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo mechanism exists for a box to distribute output across multiple\ndownstream paths in sequence. The comparator (issue 210) routes\nbased on a value threshold; the iterator routes based on a counter\nthat advances each call.\n\n## Intended behavior (editor)\n\n### What it is\n\nAn iterator box has no `ref` / `fn`. It declares an ordered list of\noutput names in `iterator_outputs`. The runtime (issue 304) routes\ninput → one output per call, advancing a per-instance counter mod\n`#iterator_outputs`. Pure routing primitive: there is no language\nfunction being invoked.\n\n### Data model\n\nBox JSON has an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\nuser-defined output path names. Iterator boxes do not carry `ref` or\n`fn`; those fields are absent (or, if present, ignored):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"inputs\": [{\"name\": \"data\", \"type\": \"any\"}],\n  \"iterator_outputs\": [\"path_a\", \"path_b\", \"path_c\"],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_a\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-a\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_b\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-b\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_c\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-c\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`from_branch` is reused for iterator output names — the same field\nthat holds `lt` / `eq` / `gt` for comparators. The dispatch layer\n(issue 304) checks whether the box has `iterator_outputs`; if so, it\nroutes by counter.\n\n### Inspector\n\n- An \"iterator\" toggle per box (mirrors the variadic toggle on\n  inputs).\n- When toggled on: the output side of the box renders named slots\n  instead of a single dot; a `+` row at the bottom adds a new slot.\n- Each slot name is editable inline.\n- The `ref` / `fn` / comparator controls hide while the iterator\n  toggle is on (mutually exclusive with a function-backed box).\n- Toggling iterator off restores `ref` / `fn` controls and snips all\n  output wires (same all-wires-snipped behavior as the variadic\n  toggle, per the stale-cache lesson from issue 217).\n\n### Auto-grow output slots\n\nConnecting a wire to the last output slot appends a new empty named\nslot — identical to variadic input auto-grow (issue 217).\nConnecting to the last slot generates a placeholder name (`output_N`)\nand grows the list immediately, no prompt. Disconnecting removes the\nslot and compacts (rename-and-compact mirror of variadic input\nlogic).\n\n### Canvas rendering\n\nWhen `iterator_outputs` is set, the box renders N named output dots\ndown the right edge instead of a single dot. Box height grows to\naccommodate. Wire dragging starts from the dot whose slot the cursor\nis over.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `iterator_outputs` (array of\n   strings) on call boxes; when present, `ref` and `fn` are not\n   required.\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle; editable output\n   slot list; mutual-exclusion with ref/fn/comparator controls;\n   snip-all-wires behavior on toggle (both directions).\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render N named output dots when\n   `iterator_outputs` is set; box height accommodates the slot\n   count; `port_positions` returns N output positions.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow output slots on connect;\n   auto-shrink + rename on disconnect (mirror of variadic input).\n\n## Runtime\n\nSee issue 304 (task dispatch layer) for the full runtime flow:\ncounter on the dispatch task, copy-input-to-output, fire the\nrouting connection, increment counter, re-spawn successor task. No\nlanguage driver, no function call, no executor-state table.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Counter exposed as a readable data port: no. Adds complexity most\n  users won't need.\n- Auto-grow naming: placeholder (`output_N`) on connect, user\n  renames afterward if they care. No prompt.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`iterator_outputs` field)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle, slot editor\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow/shrink for output slots\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box rendering, port positions\n- `issues/completed/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` —\n  variadic input model that auto-grow logic mirrors\n- `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md` —\n  comparator model that `from_branch` and routing pattern extend\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 runtime semantics\n- `issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md` — self-loop\n  routing that pairs naturally with iterators\n",

    "originalFile":"# 221 — Iterator box: round-robin output routing with per-instance counter\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo mechanism exists for a box to distribute output across multiple\ndownstream paths in sequence. The comparator routes based on a value\nthreshold; the iterator routes based on a counter that advances each call.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\n### What it does\nAn iterator box receives one input value and routes it to one of N named\noutput wires. Which wire fires is determined by an internal counter that\nincrements each call and wraps back to 0 after the last output. There is\nno function — the dispatch layer copies input directly to output, no\nlanguage spec is invoked. The iterator is a pure routing primitive.\n\nUseful for distributing work across parallel paths, cycling through a\nlist of consumers, or producing round-robin load balancing in the graph.\n\n### Counter model\nThe counter is per-box-instance, stored in the executor's in-memory\nstate (keyed by box ID). It resets to 0 at the start of each run.\nPersistence across runs is not in scope; that is a separate issue.\n\nIn the compiler output (issue 219), the counter becomes a local variable\nin a generated closure — same reset-per-program-start behavior.\n\nWrap-around: `counter = (counter + 1) % #iterator_outputs`\n\n### No function — pure dispatch primitive\nThere is no iterator function in any language. There are no\n`libs/iterator.lua` / `iterator.sh` / `iterator.c` files. The dispatch\nlayer (issue 304) recognizes iterator boxes by the presence of\n`iterator_outputs` in the box JSON and handles routing itself:\n\n1. Read the input value from the input slot.\n2. Copy it directly into the output slot.\n3. Fire the connection whose `from_branch` matches\n   `iterator_outputs[counter]`.\n4. Increment counter mod `n_iter_outputs`.\n5. Re-spawn a successor dispatch task with the new counter value.\n\nThis replaces the earlier \"passthrough function\" design. The function\nwas always identity, so there was nothing to invoke — the dispatch\nlayer does the copy directly and skips the language spec entirely.\n\n### Data model\nBox JSON has an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\nuser-defined output path names. Iterator boxes do not carry `ref` or\n`fn`; those fields are absent (or, if present, ignored):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"inputs\": [{\"name\": \"data\", \"type\": \"any\"}],\n  \"iterator_outputs\": [\"path_a\", \"path_b\", \"path_c\"],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_a\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-a\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_b\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-b\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_c\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-c\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`from_branch` is reused for iterator output names — the same field\nthat holds \"lt\" / \"eq\" / \"gt\" for comparators. The dispatch layer\nchecks whether the box has `iterator_outputs`; if so, it routes by\ncounter as described above.\n\n### Auto-grow output slots\nConnecting a wire to the last slot of the iterator's output side appends\na new empty named slot — identical to the auto-grow behavior for variadic\ninputs (issue 217). Connecting to the last slot generates a placeholder\nname (`output_N`) and grows the list immediately — no prompt. The user\ncan rename the slot in the inspector if they care, but the default\nflow does not interrupt them. Disconnecting removes the slot and\ncompacts (same rename-and-compact logic as variadic inputs).\n\n### Dispatch layer integration\nThe dispatch layer (issue 304) is where iterator semantics live. The\ncounter is stored on the `dispatch_task_t` for each iterator\ninvocation; successor tasks carry the next counter value. There is no\nlanguage driver, no function call, no executor-state table — just the\ncounter on the task struct.\n\nSee issue 304 for the full dispatch flow. The iterator-specific path\nis short: read input slot, copy to output slot, fire the routing\nconnection, increment counter, re-spawn.\n\n### Inspector changes\nThe inspector shows:\n- An \"iterator\" toggle per box (like the variadic toggle on inputs)\n- When toggled on: the output side of the box renders named slots instead\n  of a single dot; a \"+\" row at the bottom adds a new slot\n- Each slot name is editable inline\n- The current counter value is shown as a read-only display (useful for\n  debugging live runs)\n\n### Compiler output (issue 219 integration)\nFor an iterator box, the compiler emits a counter variable and a\nrouting function — no inner function call, since the iterator does\nnot invoke anything:\n\n```lua\nlocal router_counter = 0\nlocal function router(data)\n  local idx = router_counter\n  router_counter = (router_counter + 1) % 3\n  if     idx == 0 then worker_a(data)\n  elseif idx == 1 then worker_b(data)\n  else                 worker_c(data)\n  end\nend\n```\n\nNo iterator lib file is bundled — there is none.\n\n### Threading model\nIterator routing in the thread pool runner is fully described in issue\n304. Briefly: each invocation is a `dispatch_task_t` with the current\ncounter value; on completion the dispatch action fires the routing\nconnection, increments the counter, and submits a successor task. The\ninput slot is a queued (multi-cell) ring buffer that persists across\nre-spawns. See issues 302 (slot store) and 304 (dispatch layer) for\nthe full picture.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently — earlier questions resolved as follows:)\n\n- Counter exposed as a readable data port: no. Adds complexity most\n  users won't need.\n- Auto-grow naming: placeholder (`output_N`) on connect, user renames\n  afterward if they care. No prompt.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — add `iterator_outputs` to the box validator;\n   when present, `ref` and `fn` are not required.\n2. `src/004-executor.lua` (phase 2 path) — add per-box counter state;\n   extend `fire_connections` to route by `iterator_outputs[counter]`\n   and copy input → output without invoking a driver.\n3. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle; editable output slots.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow output slots on connect;\n   auto-shrink + rename on disconnect (mirrors variadic input logic).\n5. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render N named output dots when\n   `iterator_outputs` is set (replacing the single-wire dot).\n6. (Phase 3) Implement iterator dispatch in `src/008-pool-runner.c` per\n   issue 304 — counter on `dispatch_task_t`, successor re-spawn.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — phase 2 fire_connections / route-by-counter\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`iterator_outputs` field)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle, slot editor\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow/shrink for output slots\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box rendering\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — variadic input model\n  (auto-grow/shrink logic mirrors this)\n- `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md` — comparator\n  model that `from_branch` and the routing pattern extend from\n- `issues/219-map-compiler.md` — compiler integration\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 iterator dispatch (no\n  function invocation; routing only)\n",

    "content":"# 221 — Iterator box: editor surface for round-robin output routing\n\n## Status\nopen (editor surface only)\n\n## Scope\n\nThis issue covers the **editor side** of the iterator box: schema\nfield, inspector toggle, wires auto-grow, canvas rendering. The\nruntime semantics (counter on `dispatch_task_t`, successor task\nre-spawn, copy-input-to-output without invoking a language spec) are\nspecified in issue 304 and implemented as part of phase 3.\n\nThe phase 2 synchronous executor (`src/004-executor.lua`) does not\nget an interim iterator implementation — the executor is being\nretired by the phase 3 pool runner, so adding throwaway support\nhere is wasted work. Maps with iterator boxes can be authored in\nphase 2 and run in phase 3.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo mechanism exists for a box to distribute output across multiple\ndownstream paths in sequence. The comparator (issue 210) routes\nbased on a value threshold; the iterator routes based on a counter\nthat advances each call.\n\n## Intended behavior (editor)\n\n### What it is\n\nAn iterator box has no `ref` / `fn`. It declares an ordered list of\noutput names in `iterator_outputs`. The runtime (issue 304) routes\ninput → one output per call, advancing a per-instance counter mod\n`#iterator_outputs`. Pure routing primitive: there is no language\nfunction being invoked.\n\n### Data model\n\nBox JSON has an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\nuser-defined output path names. Iterator boxes do not carry `ref` or\n`fn`; those fields are absent (or, if present, ignored):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"inputs\": [{\"name\": \"data\", \"type\": \"any\"}],\n  \"iterator_outputs\": [\"path_a\", \"path_b\", \"path_c\"],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_a\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-a\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_b\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-b\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_c\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-c\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`from_branch` is reused for iterator output names — the same field\nthat holds `lt` / `eq` / `gt` for comparators. The dispatch layer\n(issue 304) checks whether the box has `iterator_outputs`; if so, it\nroutes by counter.\n\n### Inspector\n\n- An \"iterator\" toggle per box (mirrors the variadic toggle on\n  inputs).\n- When toggled on: the output side of the box renders named slots\n  instead of a single dot; a `+` row at the bottom adds a new slot.\n- Each slot name is editable inline.\n- The `ref` / `fn` / comparator controls hide while the iterator\n  toggle is on (mutually exclusive with a function-backed box).\n- Toggling iterator off restores `ref` / `fn` controls and snips all\n  output wires (same all-wires-snipped behavior as the variadic\n  toggle, per the stale-cache lesson from issue 217).\n\n### Auto-grow output slots\n\nConnecting a wire to the last output slot appends a new empty named\nslot — identical to variadic input auto-grow (issue 217).\nConnecting to the last slot generates a placeholder name (`output_N`)\nand grows the list immediately, no prompt. Disconnecting removes the\nslot and compacts (rename-and-compact mirror of variadic input\nlogic).\n\n### Canvas rendering\n\nWhen `iterator_outputs` is set, the box renders N named output dots\ndown the right edge instead of a single dot. Box height grows to\naccommodate. Wire dragging starts from the dot whose slot the cursor\nis over.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `iterator_outputs` (array of\n   strings) on call boxes; when present, `ref` and `fn` are not\n   required.\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle; editable output\n   slot list; mutual-exclusion with ref/fn/comparator controls;\n   snip-all-wires behavior on toggle (both directions).\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render N named output dots when\n   `iterator_outputs` is set; box height accommodates the slot\n   count; `port_positions` returns N output positions.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow output slots on connect;\n   auto-shrink + rename on disconnect (mirror of variadic input).\n\n## Runtime\n\nSee issue 304 (task dispatch layer) for the full runtime flow:\ncounter on the dispatch task, copy-input-to-output, fire the\nrouting connection, increment counter, re-spawn successor task. No\nlanguage driver, no function call, no executor-state table.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Counter exposed as a readable data port: no. Adds complexity most\n  users won't need.\n- Auto-grow naming: placeholder (`output_N`) on connect, user\n  renames afterward if they care. No prompt.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`iterator_outputs` field)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle, slot editor\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow/shrink for output slots\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box rendering, port positions\n- `issues/completed/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` —\n  variadic input model that auto-grow logic mirrors\n- `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md` —\n  comparator model that `from_branch` and routing pattern extend\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 runtime semantics\n- `issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md` — self-loop\n  routing that pairs naturally with iterators\n"
  },

        "lines":[" - Comparator + iterator are the two routing primitives (issues 210,","   221)"," - Variadic / queued inputs (issues 213, 217)","-- Map compiler (issue 219) and compile button (issue 222) — ties","-  the editor into the phase 3 build path","+- Compile button (issue 222) — placeholder until phase 3's build","+  system (issue 309) ships the backing endpoint"," - Ollama / LLM library (issue 209)"," "," Phase 2 runs on the synchronous Lua interpreter"],
        "oldStart":31,

      }],
    "originalFile":"# SoraMech — Roadmap\n\n## Phase 1 — Foundation (complete)\n\nGoal: a map you can edit in the browser and execute from the\nterminal.\n\nAt the end of phase 1, the user can:\n- Open the editor at `http://localhost:7700/`, see a canvas, create\n  boxes, set their `ref` / `fn` / `inputs`, wire them together\n- Save edits as box files on disk via the HTTP file CRUD server\n- Run `luajit src/007-runner-main.lua <map-dir>` to execute the map\n- Add a custom language driver and have the runner use it\n\nIssues 101–110, all complete and moved to `issues/completed/`.\n\nDemo: `issues/completed/demos/phase-1/`.\n\n## Phase 2 — Editor & graph model (current)\n\nGoal: an editor you can actually use to build maps, and the graph\nmodel the phase 3 runtime will consume.\n\nThis phase is editor-focused with some graph-model cleanup:\n- Map picker, fit-to-view, interaction hints, entry-box marking\n- Source file browser with auto-populated input ports\n- File browser library directories\n- Single-output driver contract (issue 218)\n- Comparator-based branching replaces the old `branch` box kind with\n  named ports (issue 210)\n- Comparator + iterator are the two routing primitives (issues 210,\n  221)\n- Variadic / queued inputs (issues 213, 217)\n- Map compiler (issue 219) and compile button (issue 222) — ties\n  the editor into the phase 3 build path\n- Ollama / LLM library (issue 209)\n\nPhase 2 runs on the synchronous Lua interpreter\n(`src/007-runner-main.lua`). No threading. Drivers per phase 1.\n\nSee `issues/phase-2-progress.md` for the live status.\n\n## Phase 3 — Thread pool runtime (planned, fully designed)\n\nGoal: replace the Lua synchronous runner with a C thread pool runner\nthat executes box graphs in parallel, with persistent per-worker\nlanguage runtimes and proper inter-task value plumbing.\n\nDesigned across issues 301–311:\n\n- 301 — pool lifecycle and per-worker init\n- 302 — wire value slot store (per-task ring buffers, refcount,\n  large-value heap)\n- 303 — language runtime spec (`lang_spec_t` interface)\n- 304 — task dispatch layer\n- 305 — C graph loader (replaces `src/003-loader.lua`)\n- 306 — Lua language spec (in-process via `lua_State`)\n- 307 — C language spec (in-process via `dlopen`, with compile)\n- 308 — Bash language spec (out-of-process via Unix domain socket)\n- 309 — build system & Makefile orchestration\n- 310 — priority queue (wired in, no-op behaviorally)\n- 311 — integration tests & run output (`last-run.jsonl`)\n\nWhen phase 3 lands, the synchronous Lua runner retires. The editor\nand the map directory format do not change — the runtime mechanism\nbeneath the box is what changes. See `docs/004-ipc-and-threading.md`\nfor the design discussion.\n\n## Phase 4 — SoraMind integration\n\nGoal: boxes that call SoraMind inference endpoints on the Alpine\ncluster.\n\n- LLM call box type — sends a prompt, receives a completion string\n- Prompt assembly: text values wired from upstream boxes, data file\n  sections explicitly loaded into prompt context\n- Comparator-routed classifiers (\"rogue / wizard / else\" via lt/eq/gt\n  on a hashed-class score)\n- Streaming output from SoraMind inference back to the runner\n\nBuilt on the phase 3 runtime — the LLM call is a regular box function,\njust one whose backing service is a network endpoint.\n\n## Phase 5 — Map-to-map calls\n\nGoal: a box that invokes another map as a subroutine.\n\n- Map call box type: specifies another map directory, passes inputs,\n  receives outputs\n- Maps run concurrently with each other (sub-pool per map)\n- Entry/exit contracts defined in `meta.json`\n\n## Phase 6 — Remote runner\n\nGoal: run a map on the Alpine cluster, edit it from a laptop.\n\n- Pool runner on a remote machine\n- File-CRUD server on the same machine exposes map files over HTTP\n- Browser editor on the laptop connects to the remote server\n- Results written to remote `last-run.jsonl`, accessible via server\n\nPhases 4, 5, and 6 are scoped only briefly here — concrete planning\nhappens once phase 3 is done.\n",
    "oldString":"- Map compiler (issue 219) and compile button (issue 222) — ties\n  the editor into the phase 3 build path",
    "newString":"- Compile button (issue 222) — placeholder until phase 3's build\n  system (issue 309) ships the backing endpoint",

    "userModified":false
  },

    "structuredPatch":[{
        "newStart":1,

        "lines":[" # 227 — Hide the inspector \"view\" button when the box has no ref"," "," ## Status","-open","+complete"," ","+## Implementation notes","+","+`assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — the view button now starts","+hidden when `box.ref` is empty (`view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at","+creation time), and the ref-input `input` listener flips","+`view_btn.hidden` on every keystroke. The file browser's on-select","+path was already re-rendering the inspector via `show(current_box)`","+so its ref-population path naturally takes the correct branch on","+the next render — no separate update needed there.","+","+The browse button stays visible at all times so the user always has","+a path to setting a ref.","+"," ## Current behavior"," "," The inspector renders three buttons next to the `ref` field on every"],
        "oldStart":1,
        "oldLines":8
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 227 — Hide the inspector \"view\" button when the box has no ref\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe inspector renders three buttons next to the `ref` field on every\ncall box: `browse` (open the file browser), `view` (open the\nfloating source viewer, issue 215), and the inputs/outputs sections.\nThe `view` button shows up for every call box regardless of whether\n`box.ref` has been set yet.\n\nClicking `view` on a box with no ref calls\n`SourceView.open_source_view(current_box.ref, current_box)`, which\nfalls through to `fetch_source(ref)` returning the error \"no ref\nset on this box.\" A status-bar error appears. The button is\nnon-functional until a ref is set; it shouldn't be visible until\nthen.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe `view` button is rendered only when `box.ref` is non-empty. When\nthe user creates a fresh box and hasn't yet picked a function via the\nfile browser, the button is absent. After picking a function, the\nbutton appears. After clearing the ref (manual edit of the input\nfield), the button disappears again.\n\nThe `browse` button stays visible at all times — that's the entry\npoint to actually setting a ref.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show`, in the block that builds the\nref row:\n\n```js\nconst view_btn = document.createElement('button');\n// ... existing setup ...\nref_wrap.appendChild(ref_inp);\nref_wrap.appendChild(browse_btn);\nif (box.ref && box.ref !== '') {\n  ref_wrap.appendChild(view_btn);\n}\n```\n\nThe button should also appear/disappear in response to the user\ntyping into the ref input. Easiest way: re-render the ref row on\ninput. Or: keep the button always in the DOM but toggle its\n`hidden` attribute on input.\n\nToggle-on-input is simpler:\n\n```js\nref_inp.addEventListener('input', () => {\n  current_box.ref = ref_inp.value;\n  view_btn.hidden = !ref_inp.value;\n  save();\n});\n```\n\nAdd `view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at button creation time so the\ninitial render is correct.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — ref field row, `view_btn` setup\n- `issues/completed/215-view-box-source.md` — the source viewer\n  this button opens\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — the view button now starts\nhidden when `box.ref` is empty (`view_btn.hidden = !box.ref` at\ncreation time), and the ref-input `input` listener flips\n`view_btn.hidden` on every keystroke. The file browser's on-select\npath was already re-rendering the inspector via `show(current_box)`\nso its ref-population path naturally takes the correct branch on\nthe next render — no separate update needed there.\n\nThe browse button stays visible at all times so the user always has\na path to setting a ref.",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

corrections that shape\nwhat phase 3 will consume:\n\n- **Single-output rule** (218, complete): every box has exactly one\n  output wire. The driver contract emits one JSON value, not an\n  array.\n- **Comparator-based branching** (210, complete): the old `branch`\n  box kind with named ports is removed. A box may carry a\n  `comparand`; the dispatch layer fires the connection whose\n  `from_branch` matches `lt` / `eq` / `gt`.\n- **Iterator routing** (221): a box with `iterator_outputs` is a\n  pure routing primitive; the dispatch layer rotates through the\n  declared output names. Iterators have no `ref` / `fn`.\n- **Connection schema**: `from_branch` field replaces the old\n  `from_output` / `from_port` dual-field design.\n",

      "content":"  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();"
    }
  },

    "newString":"  function open_browser() {\n    title.textContent = 'browse src/';\n    fields.innerHTML  = '';\n    FileBrowser.render(fields, async (filename, fn) => {\n      current_box.ref    = filename;\n      current_box.fn     = fn.name;\n      current_box.inputs = fn.inputs.map(n => ({ name: n, type: 'any' }));\n      // outputs are not set — all boxes have exactly one output wire.\n      // When the parsed function has zero return statements, mark the\n      // box as a sink (issue 226). Outgoing wires are dropped because\n      // the canvas would no longer have an output port to host them.\n      if (fn.outputs && fn.outputs.length === 0) {\n        current_box.has_output = false;\n        await sever_output_wires();\n      } else {\n        delete current_box.has_output;\n      }\n      await save();\n      show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    });\n  }",

    "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // comparator active: 3 output dots (lt/eq/gt); otherwise: 1 centered dot\n    const n_out = (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') ? 3 : 1;\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",

Mutating in place keeps every reference\n  // valid.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const conn = {\n      from_box:    from_box_id,\n      from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n      to_box:      to_box_id,\n      to_input:    to_input,\n    };\n\n    src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n    dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n    // avoid exact duplicates (same source, branch, dest, input)\n    const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n    );\n    if (dup) return;\n\n    src_box.connections.push(conn);\n    dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back the push so the in-memory state matches the server\n      src_box.connections.pop();\n      dst_box.connections.pop();\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const branch_str = from_branch ?     "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

        "content":"-- Writes the result text to data/state.json in the map directory.\n-- Uses dkjson directly (soramech-data is implemented in issue 109).\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ write_result\nfunction M.write_result(text)\n    -- SORAMECH_MAP_DIR is injected by the lua driver shim\n    local map_dir = SORAMECH_MAP_DIR or \".\"\n    local path = map_dir .. \"/data/state.json\"\n\n    local f_read = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f_read then error(\"write_result: cannot open \" .. path) end\n    local raw = f_read:read(\"*a\")\n    f_read:close()\n\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then error(\"write_result: JSON error in state.json: \" .. tostring(jerr)) end\n\n    obj.fields.result.value = text\n\n    local tmp_path = path .. \".tmp\"\n    local f_write = io.open(tmp_path, \"w\")\n    if not f_write then error(\"write_result: cannot write \" .. tmp_path) end\n    f_write:write(json.encode(obj, { indent = true }))\n    f_write:close()\n    os.rename(tmp_path, path)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M",

        "type":"tool_result"
      }],
