    "originalFile":"# 226 — Hide output port and inspector output section when the function returns nothing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the file browser parses a function that has no return values\n(e.g. `function M.write_result(text) print(text) end` — sink, no\nreturns), the on-select handler sets `box.inputs` from the parsed\nsignature but doesn't carry through any \"this function has no\noutput\" signal. The inspector then renders the output section\n(comparator toggle + comparand input) for every call box,\nunconditionally, and the canvas draws an output port dot.\n\nThe UI implies you can wire from the output, but at runtime the\nfunction returns nil and the wire just propagates a nil value.\nVisually noisy; conceptually misleading.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA box whose function has no return values:\n- Has no output port dot on the canvas.\n- Has no output section in the inspector (no compare toggle, no\n  comparand input, no output area at all).\n- Cannot have outgoing wires drawn from it. The wire-drawing\n  interaction in `005-app.js` skips it because there's no output\n  port to grab.\n\nThe single-output-wire-per-box rule from issue 218 still holds for\nboxes with return values; this issue carves out the explicit \"no\noutput\" case.\n\n## Where the signal comes from\n\nThe Lua and Bash parsers in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` already\nreturn a `fn.outputs` array — empty when the function has no\nreturn statements. The on-select handler currently does not store\nthis on the box. The fix is to persist a boolean flag (or the\nempty `outputs` array itself) so the inspector and canvas can\ncheck it.\n\nTwo options:\n\n1. **Persist `box.has_output: false`** when the parser detects no\n   return values. The inspector and canvas check this field. New\n   field, but unambiguous.\n2. **Persist `box.outputs: []`** (the empty array). The inspector\n   and canvas treat `box.outputs === []` as \"no output.\" Reuses\n   the legacy field that was previously used for named output\n   ports (issue 210 superseded it; this gives it a new\n   single-purpose meaning).\n\nOption 1 is cleaner because the name says exactly what it means.\nOption 2 reuses an existing-but-stale field, which has the\nadvantage of zero schema churn but the disadvantage of overloading\nthe field's meaning. Lean toward option 1.\n\n## Edge cases\n\n- **Manually-added boxes** that haven't been wired through the\n  file browser: no information about return values exists. Default\n  to `has_output: true` (current behavior). The user can flip it\n  manually if they want a sink box without going through the file\n  browser.\n- **Functions whose return value depends on a branch** (some\n  return, some don't): the parser already lists every distinct\n  return shape. As long as ANY return statement exists, treat the\n  function as having an output. `has_output: false` only when\n  zero return statements.\n- **Comparator toggle**: if the user activates the comparator on\n  a non-output box, that's nonsensical (there's no value to\n  compare). The comparator UI only renders when the box has an\n  output anyway, so this falls out naturally.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::on_select` (in\n   `004-inspector.js`) — when `fn.outputs.length === 0`, set\n   `current_box.has_output = false`. Otherwise delete the field\n   (treat absence as `true`).\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — wrap the entire output\n   section render in `if (box.has_output !== false) { ... }`.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — when\n   `box.has_output === false`, return an empty `outputs` array.\n   `draw_box` already iterates `outputs` and draws nothing for an\n   empty array.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — early-out if the\n   `from_box` has `has_output === false` (defensive — the canvas\n   wouldn't have a port to grab from, but cover the edge case).\n5. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `has_output` as an optional\n   boolean field. No validation beyond type-check.\n6. Test: open the hello map, look at `write-result` (which is a\n   sink). After re-browsing it through the file browser, output\n   port should disappear. Existing wires from a now-output-less\n   box are dropped on save (preferable to dangling).\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should existing wires from a box that flips to `has_output:\n  false` be dropped automatically, or should the flip be rejected\n  if any outgoing wires exist? Auto-drop with a status-bar\n  warning is the smoother path.\n- Should the file browser do this automatically on every re-pick,\n  or only the first time a function is selected? Doing it every\n  time matches what we do for `box.inputs` (always overwritten on\n  re-select), and keeps the box's `has_output` flag in sync with\n  the actual function.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `show` (output section render),\n  `open_browser` (on-select handler that sets the flag)\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — parsers that detect zero returns\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `port_positions`, `draw_box`\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `create_connection` (defensive check)\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts `has_output`\n- `issues/completed/218-enforce-single-output-driver-contract.md`\n  — single-wire rule that this issue qualifies\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nWent with option 1 (`box.has_output: false` field; absence means\n\"true\"). The signal flows from the Lua/Bash parsers in\n`007-filebrowser.js` (`fn.outputs.length === 0`) through the\ninspector's `open_browser` on-select handler, which sets the field\nand severs any pre-existing outgoing wires before saving. Re-picking\na function with returns deletes the field and the box returns to\nnormal output behavior.\n\nTouches:\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js::open_browser` — set/delete\n  `current_box.has_output`; await `sever_output_wires()` when\n  flipping false to drop wires the canvas would no longer host\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js::show` — early-return after the\n  inputs section when `box.has_output === false`, skipping the\n  comparator UI and output area entirely\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js::port_positions` — return `outputs: []`\n  when sink, so the canvas draws no output dot and wire-drag has\n  nothing to grab from\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — defensive early\n  return if a caller somehow tries to wire from a sink box's\n  (non-existent) output\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — accept the optional boolean field",

Mutating in place keeps every reference\n132\t  // valid.\n133\t  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n134\t    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n135\t    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n136\t    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n137\t      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n138\t      return;\n139\t    }\n140\t    // Defensive: a sink box has no output port (issue 226), so the\n141\t    // canvas wouldn't hand us a wire start from it.       "content":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n      const branch_str = wire.from_branch ? '.' + wire.from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('wire ' + wire.from_box + branch_str + ' → ' + wire.to_box + '.' +\n        wire.to_input + ' — press Delete to remove');\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  //\n  // Mutates the cached box objects in place. Replacing the reference\n  // (e.g. with a freshly-fetched copy from API.get_box) used to break\n  // any other module holding a reference to the box — most painfully\n  // the inspector, whose current_box reference would silently go\n  // stale after a wire was created, causing subsequent variadic\n  // operations to operate on out-of-date data and clobber the just-\n  // added wire on save. Mutating in place keeps every reference\n  // valid.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    // Defensive: a sink box has no output port (issue 226), so the\n    // canvas wouldn't hand us a wire start from it. Refuse anyway in\n    // case some other path tries to fabricate one.\n    if (src_box.has_output === false) {\n      status_msg('connect error: source box is a sink', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const conn = {\n      from_box:    from_box_id,\n      from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n      to_box:      to_box_id,\n      to_input:    to_input,\n    };\n\n    src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n    dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n    // avoid exact duplicates (same source, branch, dest, input)\n    const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n    );\n    if (dup) return;\n\n    src_box.connections.push(conn);\n    dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back the push so the in-memory state matches the server\n      src_box.connections.pop();\n      dst_box.connections.pop();\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n    status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n\n    // Auto-grow the destination box's variadic group when the wire\n    // landed on its last slot (issue 217 part B). Idempotent — the\n    // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n    // group and exits if not.\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  // Same in-place mutation pattern as create_connection — never\n  // replace the cached references.\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const match = c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n    const src_before = src_box.connections || [];\n    const dst_before = dst_box.connections || [];\n    src_box.connections = src_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n    dst_box.connections = dst_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back\n      src_box.connections = src_before;\n      dst_box.connections = dst_before;\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    _selected_wire = null;\n    status_msg('deleted connection');\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n"
    }

Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ?     "originalFile":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  // LOOP_OFFSET pulls a self-loop's control points further out and\n  // below the box body, so the curve sweeps around the bottom rather\n  // than cutting straight through the rectangle (issue 228).\n  const LOOP_OFFSET        = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        const cx0 = src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0 = src.y;\n        const cx1 = dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1 = dst.y;\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n      const branch_str = wire.from_branch ? '.' + wire.from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('wire ' + wire.from_box + branch_str + ' → ' + wire.to_box + '.' +\n        wire.to_input + ' — press Delete to remove');\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  //\n  // Mutates the cached box objects in place. Replacing the reference\n  // (e.g. with a freshly-fetched copy from API.get_box) used to break\n  // any other module holding a reference to the box — most painfully\n  // the inspector, whose current_box reference would silently go\n  // stale after a wire was created, causing subsequent variadic\n  // operations to operate on out-of-date data and clobber the just-\n  // added wire on save. Mutating in place keeps every reference\n  // valid.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    // Defensive: a sink box has no output port (issue 226), so the\n    // canvas wouldn't hand us a wire start from it. Refuse anyway in\n    // case some other path tries to fabricate one.\n    if (src_box.has_output === false) {\n      status_msg('connect error: source box is a sink', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const conn = {\n      from_box:    from_box_id,\n      from_branch: from_branch ?? null,\n      to_box:      to_box_id,\n      to_input:    to_input,\n    };\n\n    src_box.connections = src_box.connections || [];\n    dst_box.connections = dst_box.connections || [];\n\n    // avoid exact duplicates (same source, branch, dest, input)\n    const dup = src_box.connections.some(c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === conn.from_branch &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input\n    );\n    if (dup) return;\n\n    src_box.connections.push(conn);\n    dst_box.connections.push(conn);\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(from_box_id, src_box),\n        API.put_box(to_box_id,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back the push so the in-memory state matches the server\n      src_box.connections.pop();\n      dst_box.connections.pop();\n      status_msg('connect error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const branch_str = from_branch ? '.' + from_branch : '';\n    status_msg('connected ' + from_box_id + branch_str + ' → ' + to_box_id + '.' + to_input);\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n\n    // Auto-grow the destination box's variadic group when the wire\n    // landed on its last slot (issue 217 part B). Idempotent — the\n    // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n    // group and exits if not.\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  // Same in-place mutation pattern as create_connection — never\n  // replace the cached references.\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const match = c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n    const src_before = src_box.connections || [];\n    const dst_before = dst_box.connections || [];\n    src_box.connections = src_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n    dst_box.connections = dst_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back\n      src_box.connections = src_before;\n      dst_box.connections = dst_before;\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    _selected_wire = null;\n    status_msg('deleted connection');\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

    "originalFile":"// Wire rendering, hit testing, and connection management.\n// Wires are derived from box connection data — no separate wire store.\n\nconst Wires = (() => {\n  const BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80;\n  // LOOP_OFFSET pulls a self-loop's control points further out and\n  // below the box body, so the curve sweeps around the bottom rather\n  // than cutting straight through the rectangle (issue 228).\n  const LOOP_OFFSET        = 80;\n  const HIT_SAMPLES        = 20;\n  const HIT_THRESHOLD_PX   = 8;\n\n  // Colors for comparator branch wires; plain wire uses default\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  let _selected_wire = null;  // { from_box, from_branch, to_box, to_input }\n\n  // {{{ selected_wire\n  function selected_wire() { return _selected_wire; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ bezier_point\n  function bezier_point(t, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1) {\n    const mt = 1 - t;\n    return {\n      x: mt*mt*mt*x0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cx0 + 3*mt*t*t*cx1 + t*t*t*x1,\n      y: mt*mt*mt*y0 + 3*mt*mt*t*cy0 + 3*mt*t*t*cy1 + t*t*t*y1,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ endpoint_controls\n  // Returns the two cubic-Bezier control points for a wire from src to\n  // dst. For a normal wire the controls jut horizontally out of each\n  // port. For a self-loop (output and input on the same box body), the\n  // controls swing out and below so the curve routes around the\n  // rectangle instead of slicing through it (issue 228).\n  function endpoint_controls(src, dst, self_loop_box) {\n    if (self_loop_box) {\n      const h = Boxes.box_height(self_loop_box);\n      return {\n        cx0: src.x + LOOP_OFFSET, cy0: src.y + h * 0.7,\n        cx1: dst.x - LOOP_OFFSET, cy1: dst.y + h * 0.7,\n      };\n    }\n    return {\n      cx0: src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy0: src.y,\n      cx1: dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, cy1: dst.y,\n    };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier_cp\n  // Draws a cubic Bezier with explicit control points. The wrapper\n  // draw_bezier (kept for the in-progress wire-drag preview) calls\n  // this with the default straight-out controls.\n  function draw_bezier_cp(ctx, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.moveTo(x0, y0);\n    ctx.bezierCurveTo(cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1);\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? '#ffffff' : color;\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2.5 : 1.5;\n    ctx.setLineDash([]);\n    ctx.stroke();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_bezier\n  function draw_bezier(ctx, x0, y0, x1, y1, color, selected) {\n    const cx0 = x0 + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy0 = y0;\n    const cx1 = x1 - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET;\n    const cy1 = y1;\n    draw_bezier_cp(ctx, x0, y0, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, x1, y1, color, selected);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_wire\n  // Returns the connection record if cursor (wx,wy) is within HIT_THRESHOLD pixels\n  // of any wire, or null. Operates in world space; threshold is adjusted for zoom.\n  function hit_test_wire(wx, wy, zoom) {\n    const threshold = HIT_THRESHOLD_PX / zoom;\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst  = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // Self-loop wires use the looped control points, so sample\n        // along that same curve — clicks register on the visual wire\n        // path rather than on a phantom straight-through path.\n        const self_box = (c.from_box === c.to_box) ? Boxes.boxes[c.from_box] : null;\n        const { cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1 } = endpoint_controls(src, dst, self_box);\n\n        for (let i = 0; i <= HIT_SAMPLES; i++) {\n          const t = i / HIT_SAMPLES;\n          const p = bezier_point(t, src.x, src.y, cx0, cy0, cx1, cy1, dst.x, dst.y);\n          const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n          if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= threshold*threshold) return c;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_box_id) {\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      for (const c of box.connections || []) {\n        if (c.from_box !== id) continue;\n\n        const src = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.from_box, c.from_branch ?? null, 'output');\n        const dst = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(c.to_box,   c.to_input,            'input');\n        if (!src || !dst) continue;\n\n        // comparator branches get distinct colors; plain wire uses dim default\n        const color = c.from_branch ? (BRANCH_COLOR[c.from_branch] || '#4a6080') : '#4a6080';\n\n        const is_selected = _selected_wire &&\n          _selected_wire.from_box    === c.from_box &&\n          _selected_wire.from_branch === c.from_branch &&\n          _selected_wire.to_box      === c.to_box &&\n          _selected_wire.to_input    === c.to_input;\n\n        draw_bezier(ctx, src.x, src.y, dst.x, dst.y, color, is_selected);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Handle wire selection via click\n  Canvas.el.addEventListener('click', e => {\n    if (e.button !== 0) return;\n    const s = Canvas.mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = Canvas.screen_to_world(s.x, s.y);\n\n    // only try wire hit if no box was hit\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_box(w.x, w.y)) { _selected_wire = null; return; }\n    if (Boxes.hit_test_port(w.x, w.y)) return;\n\n    const wire = hit_test_wire(w.x, w.y, Canvas.cam.zoom);\n    if (wire) {\n      _selected_wire = wire;\n      const branch_str = wire.from_branch ? '.' + wire.from_branch : '';\n      status_msg('wire ' + wire.from_box + branch_str + ' → ' + wire.to_box + '.' +\n        wire.to_input + ' — press Delete to remove');\n    } else {\n      _selected_wire = null;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  // {{{ create_connection\n  // from_branch: null (no comparator) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt'.\n  //\n  // Mutates the cached box objects in place. Replacing the reference\n  // (e.g. with a freshly-fetched copy from API.get_box) used to break\n  // any other module holding a reference to the box — most painfully\n  // the inspector, whose current_box reference would silently go\n  // stale after a wire was created, causing subsequent variadic\n  // operations to operate on out-of-date data and clobber the just-\n  // added wire on save. Mutating in place keeps every reference\n  // valid.\n  async function create_connection(from_box_id, from_branch, to_box_id, to_input) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[from_box_id];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[to_box_id];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('connect error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    // Defensive: a sink box has no output port (issue 226), so the\n    // canvas wouldn't hand us a wire start from it. Idempotent — the\n    // helper checks first whether to_input is the last slot of its\n    // group and exits if not.\n    if (Inspector.auto_grow_after_set) {\n      await Inspector.auto_grow_after_set(dst_box, to_input);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ delete_connection\n  // Same in-place mutation pattern as create_connection — never\n  // replace the cached references.\n  async function delete_connection(conn) {\n    const src_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n    const dst_box = Boxes.boxes[conn.to_box];\n    if (!src_box || !dst_box) {\n      status_msg('delete wire error: box not in cache', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const match = c =>\n      c.from_box    === conn.from_box    &&\n      (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n      c.to_box      === conn.to_box      &&\n      c.to_input    === conn.to_input;\n\n    const src_before = src_box.connections || [];\n    const dst_before = dst_box.connections || [];\n    src_box.connections = src_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n    dst_box.connections = dst_before.filter(c => !match(c));\n\n    try {\n      await Promise.all([\n        API.put_box(conn.from_box, src_box),\n        API.put_box(conn.to_box,   dst_box),\n      ]);\n    } catch (e) {\n      // roll back\n      src_box.connections = src_before;\n      dst_box.connections = dst_before;\n      status_msg('delete wire error: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    _selected_wire = null;\n    status_msg('deleted connection');\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { draw_all, draw_bezier, hit_test_wire, create_connection,\n           delete_connection, selected_wire };\n})();\n",

          "new_string":"## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nWent with option 1 (cubic Bezier, off-axis control points). Removed.\n\n### Touches\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `endpoint_controls`, `draw_bezier_cp`,\n  `LOOP_OFFSET`, self-loop guards in create/delete\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — drop the wire-release self-loop block\n\n### Edge cases verified by inspection\n\n- **Box height changes** with a self-loop attached (e.g., variadic\n  slot added growing the box): control points use `box_height(box)`\n  per-frame, so the curve adapts.\n- **Multiple self-loops on a comparator box** (e.g., `lt` and `eq`\n  both routed back): each renders independently against its own\n  branch dot, with branch coloring preserved.\n- **Hit-test under the box body**: samples follow the looped curve,\n  so clicks near the visible wire register; clicks on the box body\n  itself are still consumed by `hit_test_box` first.",

Removed.","+","+### Touches","+","+- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `endpoint_controls`, `draw_bezier_cp`,","+  `LOOP_OFFSET`, self-loop guards in create/delete","+- `assets/js/005-app.js` — drop the wire-release self-loop block","+","+### Edge cases verified by inspection","+","+- **Box height changes** with a self-loop attached (e.g., variadic","+  slot added growing the box): control points use `box_height(box)`","+  per-frame, so the curve adapts.","+- **Multiple self-loops on a comparator box** (e.g., `lt` and `eq`","+  both routed back): each renders independently against its own","+  branch dot, with branch coloring preserved.","+- **Hit-test under the box body**: samples follow the looped curve,","+  so clicks near the visible wire register; clicks on the box body","+  itself are still consumed by `hit_test_box` first.","+"," ## Current behavior"," "," The connection model permits a wire whose `from_box` and `to_box`"],

    "originalFile":"# 228 — Self-loop wires: connect a box's output to its own input, routed around the body\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe connection model permits a wire whose `from_box` and `to_box`\nare the same — `create_connection` checks for exact duplicates but\ndoes not reject self-loops. The wire renderer in\n`assets/js/006-wires.js::draw_all` then draws a cubic Bézier from\nthe output dot (right edge of the box) to the input dot (left edge\nof the box), with control points fixed at\n`±BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET = 80px` horizontally. For a self-loop, both\nendpoints sit on opposite sides of the same body and the curve cuts\nstraight through the middle of the box — visually unreadable, and\nclipped by the box rectangle.\n\nHit-testing samples the same Bézier path and inherits the same\nproblem: clicks land in the wrong place because the wire sits\nunderneath the box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nSelf-loops are allowed and render as a wire that loops *around*\nthe box body, not through it. The user can wire a box's output to\nits own input the same way as any other connection (drag from\noutput port, release on input port).\n\n### Why this matters\n\nSelf-loops are useful with iterator boxes (issue 221): an\niterator's output feeds back into its own queued input, building\nan accumulator or polling-state pattern. The comparator (issue\n210) routes one branch to the input on a self-loop, the other\nbranch downstream. With queued inputs (phase 3 issue 302) the\nloop terminates naturally when the queue empties.\n\nThe runtime semantics differ between phase 2 and phase 3:\n- **Phase 2 (current)**: the synchronous executor walks dependency\n  order. A self-loop on a non-iterator box never resolves and\n  hangs the run. The user is responsible for not shipping such\n  maps. The editor allows constructing them; the runner errors\n  cleanly (or hangs, which is also a clear signal).\n- **Phase 3**: the C graph loader (issue 305) rejects non-iterator\n  cycles at load time and accepts iterator cycles. The editor\n  doesn't need to know which is which; the loader catches misuse.\n\nEither way, the editor's job is just to draw the wire correctly.\n\n### Routing\n\nThe wire path for a self-loop goes out the right side from the\noutput dot, around either the top or the bottom of the box body\n(pick deterministically — say, always the bottom), and back to\nthe input dot on the left side.\n\nTwo reasonable shapes:\n\n1. **Cubic Bézier with off-axis control points** — keep the same\n   `draw_bezier` machinery but pick control points that pull the\n   curve out, down, and around. For a box at world-(x, y) with\n   width W and height H, output dot at (x+W, oy) and input dot at\n   (x, iy):\n\n   ```\n   src = (x+W, oy)\n   dst = (x,   iy)\n   cp1 = (x+W + LOOP_OFFSET, oy + H)\n   cp2 = (x   - LOOP_OFFSET, iy + H)\n   ```\n\n   `LOOP_OFFSET` ~ 60–80px gives a smooth horseshoe under the box.\n\n2. **Polyline** — straight segments: right from output dot,\n   down past the box bottom, left past the box left edge, up to\n   input dot. Visually crisper, easier to hit-test, but stylistically\n   inconsistent with every other wire being a Bézier.\n\nRecommendation: option 1. Reuses `draw_bezier` with different\ncontrol-point math, no new rendering primitive needed.\n\n### Hit-testing\n\n`hit_test_wire` samples the Bézier path at `HIT_SAMPLES = 20`\npoints. With the same machinery and routed-around control points,\nthe samples sit on the curved path under the box, not behind the\nbody. Clicks register correctly.\n\nThe wire-erase pointer-interpolation fix (commit 899f35d) walks\nthe *cursor* path, not the wire's path. It already works for any\nwire shape `hit_test_wire` can match. No additional change needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation\n\nIn `assets/js/006-wires.js`:\n\n1. Detect self-loop where the wire is being computed:\n   `c.from_box === c.to_box`.\n2. When self-loop, compute `cp1` and `cp2` with the looped offsets\n   above. The offset is in world units, so it scales with zoom\n   correctly.\n3. Pass `cp1` / `cp2` into `draw_bezier` (refactor to accept\n   explicit control points, or add a sibling `draw_loop_bezier`).\n4. `hit_test_wire` does the same self-loop check and uses the\n   same `bezier_point` sampling with the looped control points.\n\n```js\nfunction endpoint_controls(c, src, dst, box) {\n  if (c.from_box === c.to_box && box) {\n    const h = Boxes.box_height(box);\n    return {\n      cp1: { x: src.x + LOOP_OFFSET,        y: src.y + h * 0.7 },\n      cp2: { x: dst.x - LOOP_OFFSET,        y: dst.y + h * 0.7 },\n    };\n  }\n  return {\n    cp1: { x: src.x + BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: src.y },\n    cp2: { x: dst.x - BEZIER_CTRL_OFFSET, y: dst.y },\n  };\n}\n```\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Box height changes** while a self-loop wire exists (variadic\n  slot added → box grows): the wire's control points are derived\n  per-frame from current `box_height`, so it adapts automatically.\n- **Output is a comparator branch** (`from_branch` is `lt`/`eq`/`gt`):\n  the loop renders the same way; the branch coloring still applies.\n  A user can wire `lt` back to the same box's input, which is a\n  legitimate self-loop pattern for \"while less than X, keep going.\"\n- **Multiple self-loops on one box** (different output → different\n  inputs, or comparator branches): each renders independently.\n  They will overlap; visual cleanup if it ever matters in\n  practice.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Top vs bottom routing**: always-below is simplest. Always-above\n  is also fine. Configurable per-wire (right-click → \"route around\n  top\") is overkill until someone asks for it.\n- **Self-loop validation in the schema**: the phase 2 schema\n  doesn't reject self-loops, and the phase 3 loader handles cycle\n  detection at load time (issue 305). Editor-side validation is\n  unnecessary; the wire-draw machinery just needs to render it.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `draw_all`, `hit_test_wire`,\n  `draw_bezier`, control-point math\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `box_height`, `BOX_W`, port positions\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — wire-create flow (no change needed; the\n  existing flow already permits self-loop construction)\n- `issues/221-iterator-box.md` — iterator self-re-spawn pattern\n  that motivates this\n- `issues/305-c-graph-loader.md` — phase 3 loader's cycle\n  validation policy\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nWent with option 1 (cubic Bezier, off-axis control points). A single\n`endpoint_controls(src, dst, self_loop_box)` helper returns the two\ncontrol points; `null` for the third arg gives the default\nstraight-out controls, a box reference gives the around-the-bottom\nloop. Both `draw_all` and `hit_test_wire` route through it, so the\nvisual wire and the click-detection curve always agree.\n\nTwo surprises I hadn't called out in the original write-up:\n\n1. **`src_box === dst_box` for self-loops.** `create_connection` and\n   `delete_connection` were pushing/filtering both sides of the\n   connection independently; with a self-loop, both sides are the\n   same array, so a wire would land in the array twice. Added a\n   `self_loop = src_box === dst_box` guard so the push and the PUT\n   happen once.\n2. **Wire-release blocked self-loops.** `005-app.js` had an explicit\n   `target_port.box_id !== drawing_wire.from_box` guard preventing\n   the user from ever releasing a wire on the same box. Removed.\n\n### Touches\n\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — `endpoint_controls`, `draw_bezier_cp`,\n  `LOOP_OFFSET`, self-loop guards in create/delete\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — drop the wire-release self-loop block\n\n### Edge cases verified by inspection\n\n- **Box height changes** with a self-loop attached (e.g., variadic\n  slot added growing the box): control points use `box_height(box)`\n  per-frame, so the curve adapts.\n- **Multiple self-loops on a comparator box** (e.g., `lt` and `eq`\n  both routed back): each renders independently against its own\n  branch dot, with branch coloring preserved.\n- **Hit-test under the box body**: samples follow the looped curve,\n  so clicks near the visible wire register; clicks on the box body\n  itself are still consumed by `hit_test_box` first.",

    }
  },

    "originalFile":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, data = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call' or 'data')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" or box.kind == \"data\" then\n        if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional;     "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // comparator active: 3 output dots (lt/eq/gt); otherwise: 1 centered dot\n    const n_out = (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') ? 3 : 1;\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226).     "newString":"  // {{{ Iterator helpers (issue 221)\n  // Iterator boxes are pure routing primitives: input copies straight\n  // to one output, the dispatch layer (phase 3, issue 304) advances a\n  // counter mod #iterator_outputs each call. No ref/fn — the box body\n  // is just the counter + slot list. Each slot has a user-renamable\n  // name; the slot name lands in a connection's `from_branch` field\n  // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n  //\n  // The inspector edits the slot list; the dispatch layer is what\n  // actually rotates between them at runtime.\n\n  function is_iterator(box) {\n    return Array.isArray(box && box.iterator_outputs);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle the box ON as an iterator. Ref/fn/comparand are mutually\n  // exclusive with iterator routing (a routing primitive has no\n  // function to invoke), so they are stripped. All outgoing wires are\n  // dropped because the output shape changes from a single dot (or\n  // lt/eq/gt) to N named slots — same shape-change-clears-wires rule\n  // as the variadic input toggle.\n  async function make_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n\n    delete current_box.ref;\n    delete current_box.fn;\n    delete current_box.comparand;\n    delete current_box.has_output;\n    current_box.iterator_outputs = ['output_0'];\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle iterator OFF. Drop the iterator_outputs field; sever\n  // outgoing wires (their from_branch values referenced slot names\n  // that no longer exist). The user re-picks a function via the\n  // browse button to restore ref/fn.\n  async function unmake_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    delete current_box.iterator_outputs;\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append a new slot with a placeholder name (`output_N`). The user\n  // can rename it after — placeholder is just to avoid prompting on\n  // every grow. Mirrors the variadic auto-grow pattern.\n  async function add_iterator_slot() {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    let n = slots.length;\n    // pick the lowest free `output_N` so renaming + adding doesn't\n    // collide with an existing user-named slot\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove the slot at index `idx`. Outgoing wires whose from_branch\n  // matched the removed slot get severed; remaining slots keep their\n  // names (no rename — slot names are user-defined and free-form, no\n  // need to compact like the variadic numeric indexes).\n  async function remove_iterator_slot(idx) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    if (slots.length <= 1) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove last slot — toggle iterator off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    const removed = slots[idx];\n\n    // Sever every outgoing wire on this branch.\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed) dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n    });\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    slots.splice(idx, 1);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Rename slot at index `idx` to `new_name`. Renames the slot itself\n  // and rewrites `from_branch` on every outgoing wire that used the\n  // old name (both the source-box record and the destination-box\n  // copy). No-op if the name is unchanged or already taken.\n  async function rename_iterator_slot(idx, new_name) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    const old_name = slots[idx];\n    if (old_name === new_name) return;\n    if (!new_name) {\n      status_msg('slot name cannot be empty', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (slots.includes(new_name)) {\n      status_msg('slot name already in use', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    slots[idx] = new_name;\n\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n        c.from_branch = new_name;\n        dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n      }\n    });\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      (dst.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n        if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n          c.from_branch = new_name;\n        }\n      });\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to rename wires on ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n\n  // Auto-grow check used by the wire-connect path. If `from_branch` is\n  // the LAST slot of an iterator box, append a new placeholder slot\n  // and persist. Idempotent — calling again on the same slot is a\n  // no-op once a newer slot exists below it. Mirrors the variadic\n  // input auto-grow.\n  async function auto_grow_iterator_after_connect(box, from_branch) {\n    if (!is_iterator(box)) return;\n    const slots = box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (slots[slots.length - 1] !== from_branch) return;\n\n    let n = slots.length;\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(box.id, box);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      if (current_box && current_box.id === box.id) {\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      slots.pop();\n      status_msg('iterator auto-grow failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // Sever every outgoing wire from this box. All outgoing wires are\n  // dropped because the output shape changes from a single dot (or\n  // lt/eq/gt) to N named slots — same shape-change-clears-wires rule\n  // as the variadic input toggle.\n  async function make_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n\n    delete current_box.ref;\n    delete current_box.fn;\n    delete current_box.comparand;\n    delete current_box.has_output;\n    current_box.iterator_outputs = ['output_0'];\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle iterator OFF. Drop the iterator_outputs field; sever\n  // outgoing wires (their from_branch values referenced slot names\n  // that no longer exist). The user re-picks a function via the\n  // browse button to restore ref/fn.\n  async function unmake_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    delete current_box.iterator_outputs;\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append a new slot with a placeholder name (`output_N`). Mirrors the variadic auto-grow pattern.\n  async function add_iterator_slot() {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    let n = slots.length;\n    // pick the lowest free `output_N` so renaming + adding doesn't\n    // collide with an existing user-named slot\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove the slot at index `idx`. Outgoing wires whose from_branch\n  // matched the removed slot get severed; remaining slots keep their\n  // names (no rename — slot names are user-defined and free-form, no\n  // need to compact like the variadic numeric indexes).\n  async function remove_iterator_slot(idx) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    if (slots.length <= 1) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove last slot — toggle iterator off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    const removed = slots[idx];\n\n    // Sever every outgoing wire on this branch.\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed) dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n    });\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    slots.splice(idx, 1);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Rename slot at index `idx` to `new_name`. Renames the slot itself\n  // and rewrites `from_branch` on every outgoing wire that used the\n  // old name (both the source-box record and the destination-box\n  // copy). No-op if the name is unchanged or already taken.\n  async function rename_iterator_slot(idx, new_name) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    const old_name = slots[idx];\n    if (old_name === new_name) return;\n    if (!new_name) {\n      status_msg('slot name cannot be empty', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (slots.includes(new_name)) {\n      status_msg('slot name already in use', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    slots[idx] = new_name;\n\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n        c.from_branch = new_name;\n        dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n      }\n    });\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      (dst.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n        if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n          c.from_branch = new_name;\n        }\n      });\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to rename wires on ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n\n  // Auto-grow check used by the wire-connect path. Last slot can't be removed — toggle iterator\n  off instead.\n- Renaming a slot rewrites `from_branch` on every outgoing wire on\n  both endpoints (source and destination boxes), so existing wires\n  follow the rename rather than going stale.\n\n### Edge cases verified by inspection\n\n- Self-loop wires (issue 228) on an iterator slot draw with the\n  looped control points: a self-feeding accumulator iterator is\n  the motivating use case.\n- The `data` kind also accepts `iterator_outputs` schema-wise.     "originalFile":"# 221 — Iterator box: editor surface for round-robin output routing\n\n## Status\nopen (editor surface only)\n\n## Scope\n\nThis issue covers the **editor side** of the iterator box: schema\nfield, inspector toggle, wires auto-grow, canvas rendering. The\nruntime semantics (counter on `dispatch_task_t`, successor task\nre-spawn, copy-input-to-output without invoking a language spec) are\nspecified in issue 304 and implemented as part of phase 3.\n\nThe phase 2 synchronous executor (`src/004-executor.lua`) does not\nget an interim iterator implementation — the executor is being\nretired by the phase 3 pool runner, so adding throwaway support\nhere is wasted work. Maps with iterator boxes can be authored in\nphase 2 and run in phase 3.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nNo mechanism exists for a box to distribute output across multiple\ndownstream paths in sequence. The comparator (issue 210) routes\nbased on a value threshold; the iterator routes based on a counter\nthat advances each call.\n\n## Intended behavior (editor)\n\n### What it is\n\nAn iterator box has no `ref` / `fn`. It declares an ordered list of\noutput names in `iterator_outputs`. The runtime (issue 304) routes\ninput → one output per call, advancing a per-instance counter mod\n`#iterator_outputs`. Pure routing primitive: there is no language\nfunction being invoked.\n\n### Data model\n\nBox JSON has an `iterator_outputs` field — an ordered array of\nuser-defined output path names. Iterator boxes do not carry `ref` or\n`fn`; those fields are absent (or, if present, ignored):\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"inputs\": [{\"name\": \"data\", \"type\": \"any\"}],\n  \"iterator_outputs\": [\"path_a\", \"path_b\", \"path_c\"],\n  \"connections\": [\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_a\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-a\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_b\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-b\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"from_box\": \"router\", \"from_branch\": \"path_c\",\n      \"to_box\": \"worker-c\", \"to_input\": \"data\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n`from_branch` is reused for iterator output names — the same field\nthat holds `lt` / `eq` / `gt` for comparators. The dispatch layer\n(issue 304) checks whether the box has `iterator_outputs`; if so, it\nroutes by counter.\n\n### Inspector\n\n- An \"iterator\" toggle per box (mirrors the variadic toggle on\n  inputs).\n- When toggled on: the output side of the box renders named slots\n  instead of a single dot; a `+` row at the bottom adds a new slot.\n- Each slot name is editable inline.\n- The `ref` / `fn` / comparator controls hide while the iterator\n  toggle is on (mutually exclusive with a function-backed box).\n- Toggling iterator off restores `ref` / `fn` controls and snips all\n  output wires (same all-wires-snipped behavior as the variadic\n  toggle, per the stale-cache lesson from issue 217).\n\n### Auto-grow output slots\n\nConnecting a wire to the last output slot appends a new empty named\nslot — identical to variadic input auto-grow (issue 217).\nConnecting to the last slot generates a placeholder name (`output_N`)\nand grows the list immediately, no prompt. Disconnecting removes the\nslot and compacts (rename-and-compact mirror of variadic input\nlogic).\n\n### Canvas rendering\n\nWhen `iterator_outputs` is set, the box renders N named output dots\ndown the right edge instead of a single dot. Box height grows to\naccommodate. Wire dragging starts from the dot whose slot the cursor\nis over.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `iterator_outputs` (array of\n   strings) on call boxes; when present, `ref` and `fn` are not\n   required.\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle; editable output\n   slot list; mutual-exclusion with ref/fn/comparator controls;\n   snip-all-wires behavior on toggle (both directions).\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — render N named output dots when\n   `iterator_outputs` is set; box height accommodates the slot\n   count; `port_positions` returns N output positions.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow output slots on connect;\n   auto-shrink + rename on disconnect (mirror of variadic input).\n\n## Runtime\n\nSee issue 304 (task dispatch layer) for the full runtime flow:\ncounter on the dispatch task, copy-input-to-output, fire the\nrouting connection, increment counter, re-spawn successor task. No\nlanguage driver, no function call, no executor-state table.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Counter exposed as a readable data port: no. Adds complexity most\n  users won't need.\n- Auto-grow naming: placeholder (`output_N`) on connect, user\n  renames afterward if they care. No prompt.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — box validator (`iterator_outputs` field)\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — iterator toggle, slot editor\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — auto-grow/shrink for output slots\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — box rendering, port positions\n- `issues/completed/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` —\n  variadic input model that auto-grow logic mirrors\n- `issues/completed/108-branch-box-and-predicate-routing.md` —\n  comparator model that `from_branch` and routing pattern extend\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — phase 3 runtime semantics\n- `issues/228-self-loop-wires-routed-around-box.md` — self-loop\n  routing that pairs naturally with iterators\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen (editor surface only)",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete (editor surface only — runtime in 304)\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nThe editor side of iterator boxes is in. Phase 3's dispatch layer\n(304) will read `iterator_outputs` and rotate the counter.\n\nTouches:\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — accept `iterator_outputs` (array of\n  strings); when present, `ref` is no longer required\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js::box_height`,`port_positions` — N output\n  rows when `iterator_outputs` is set; box grows vertically; each\n  slot's name lands on the dot exactly like a comparator branch\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `is_iterator`, `make_iterator`,\n  `unmake_iterator`, `add_iterator_slot`, `remove_iterator_slot`,\n  `rename_iterator_slot`, `auto_grow_iterator_after_connect`;\n  iterator toggle button next to kind dropdown; when active, the\n  ref/fn/comparator UI is replaced by an editable slot list with\n  per-slot remove and a \"+ slot\" button at the end\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection` — calls the iterator\n  auto-grow helper after a wire from any branch is created (it's a\n  no-op for non-iterators or non-last-slot connections)\n\n### Behavior decisions\n\n- Toggling on snips outgoing wires, strips ref/fn/comparand, seeds\n  one empty slot named `output_0`.\n- Toggling off snips outgoing wires, deletes `iterator_outputs`,\n  restores empty `ref`/`fn` so the schema (which requires ref on\n  non-iterator call boxes) accepts the save. User re-picks via\n  browse to populate.\n- Slot names are user-renamable — placeholder `output_N` only\n  applied on auto-grow / `+ slot`. Existing slots keep their names\n  on add/remove (no compaction; slot names are free-form, not\n  numeric indices like the variadic input pattern).\n- Removing a slot snips outgoing wires whose `from_branch` matched\n  the removed name. The downstream box decodes the\n-- array — there is no fan-out into multiple wires (that would require\n-- knowing the part count at design time, which we don't).\n--\n-- Plain-string match: the separator is escaped before being passed to\n-- string.find so users don't have to think about Lua patterns.\nfunction M.split(text, sep)\n    if text == nil then return {} end\n    if sep == nil or sep == \"\" then\n        -- splitting on empty separator: return a single-element array\n        -- with the whole input. Avoids an infinite loop and matches\n        -- common library behavior for split-on-empty.\n        return { text }\n    end\n\n    local parts = {}\n    local plain = true   -- treat sep as a literal string, not a pattern\n    local pos   = 1\n\n    while true do\n        local s, e = string.find(text, sep, pos, plain)\n        if s == nil then\n            parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos)\n            break\n        end\n        parts[#parts + 1] = string.sub(text, pos, s - 1)\n        pos = e + 1\n    end\n\n    return parts\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
    }

        "input":{
          "content":"-- File reading — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"files\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ to use\n-- it directly as a call box via the file browser. Both helpers emit a\n-- single string on the box's output wire (per the single-output rule,\n-- issue 218); errors go to stderr and the function returns nil so the\n-- executor surfaces an empty string downstream.\n--\n-- M.read_data depends on dkjson (already vendored under libs/ for the\n-- runtime's package.path).\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.read_text\n-- Reads a plain text file and returns its full contents as a string.\n-- Returns nil on any failure (file not found, read error). The error\n-- is written to stderr so the user sees it in the runner output.\nfunction M.read_text(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_text: cannot open \" .. tostring(path) ..\n                        \": \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    local content = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return content\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.read_data\n-- Reads a dkjson data file (the soramech-data format with `value` /\n-- `constant` fields) and returns the value at `key` as a string. If\n-- `key` is nil or empty, the full decoded JSON object is re-encoded\n-- and returned as a plain string — useful for piping a raw data file\n-- into a box that expects JSON text.\n--\n-- Strips metadata: when a key's record has a `.value` field, that\n-- value is returned (and only that value). Bare values without a\n-- wrapping record are returned as-is.\nfunction M.read_data(path, key)\n    local raw = M.read_text(path)\n    if not raw then return nil end\n\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_data: JSON decode failed for \" ..\n                        tostring(path) .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n\n    if key == nil or key == \"\" then\n        -- Whole-file mode: re-encode the parsed object so callers\n        -- receive a normalized JSON string regardless of the input\n        -- formatting. Uses indented form to match how soramech-data\n        -- writes its files on disk.\n        return json.encode(obj, { indent = true })\n    end\n\n    -- Soramech-data nests fields under `obj.fields[key]`; older\n    -- ad-hoc data files use a flat shape. Try the nested shape first,\n    -- fall back to the flat shape if no match.\n    local rec = (obj.fields and obj.fields[key]) or obj[key]\n    if rec == nil then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_data: key '\" .. tostring(key) ..\n                        \"' not found in \" .. tostring(path) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n\n    -- Strip metadata: if the record is itself an object with `.value`,\n    -- that's the user-facing value. Otherwise the bare record is the\n    -- value.\n    if type(rec) == \"table\" and rec.value ~= nil then\n        return tostring(rec.value)\n    end\n    return tostring(rec)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/files.lua"
        },

    "content":"-- File reading — shared library and ready-to-use box source.\n-- require(\"files\") from any Lua function, or copy to a map's src/ to use\n-- it directly as a call box via the file browser. Both helpers emit a\n-- single string on the box's output wire (per the single-output rule,\n-- issue 218); errors go to stderr and the function returns nil so the\n-- executor surfaces an empty string downstream.\n--\n-- M.read_data depends on dkjson (already vendored under libs/ for the\n-- runtime's package.path).\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ M.read_text\n-- Reads a plain text file and returns its full contents as a string.\n-- Returns nil on any failure (file not found, read error). The error\n-- is written to stderr so the user sees it in the runner output.\nfunction M.read_text(path)\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"r\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_text: cannot open \" .. tostring(path) ..\n                        \": \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n    local content = f:read(\"*a\")\n    f:close()\n    return content\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ M.read_data\n-- Reads a dkjson data file (the soramech-data format with `value` /\n-- `constant` fields) and returns the value at `key` as a string. If\n-- `key` is nil or empty, the full decoded JSON object is re-encoded\n-- and returned as a plain string — useful for piping a raw data file\n-- into a box that expects JSON text.\n--\n-- Strips metadata: when a key's record has a `.value` field, that\n-- value is returned (and only that value). Bare values without a\n-- wrapping record are returned as-is.\nfunction M.read_data(path, key)\n    local raw = M.read_text(path)\n    if not raw then return nil end\n\n    local obj, _, jerr = json.decode(raw)\n    if not obj then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_data: JSON decode failed for \" ..\n                        tostring(path) .. \": \" .. tostring(jerr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n\n    if key == nil or key == \"\" then\n        -- Whole-file mode: re-encode the parsed object so callers\n        -- receive a normalized JSON string regardless of the input\n        -- formatting. Uses indented form to match how soramech-data\n        -- writes its files on disk.\n        return json.encode(obj, { indent = true })\n    end\n\n    -- Soramech-data nests fields under `obj.fields[key]`; older\n    -- ad-hoc data files use a flat shape. Try the nested shape first,\n    -- fall back to the flat shape if no match.\n    local rec = (obj.fields and obj.fields[key]) or obj[key]\n    if rec == nil then\n        io.stderr:write(\"read_data: key '\" .. tostring(key) ..\n                        \"' not found in \" .. tostring(path) .. \"\\n\")\n        return nil\n    end\n\n    -- Strip metadata: if the record is itself an object with `.value`,\n    -- that's the user-facing value. Otherwise the bare record is the\n    -- value.\n    if type(rec) == \"table\" and rec.value ~= nil then\n        return tostring(rec.value)\n    end\n    return tostring(rec)\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n"
  },

          "content":"# files.lua\n\nFile-reading helpers — load text or soramech-data values from disk\ninto the wire graph. Pure Lua except for `read_data`, which depends\non dkjson (already vendored). Use as `require(\"files\")` from another\nLua function, or copy into a map's `src/` and pick a function via\nthe file browser.\n\nBoth functions emit a single string on the box's output wire (per the\nsingle-output rule, issue 218). On failure, the function writes to\nstderr and returns `nil`; the executor surfaces nil as an empty\nstring downstream.\n\n---\n\n## M.read_text(path) → string | nil\n\nReads a plain text file and returns its full contents as a string.\n\n| param | type   | description                  |\n|-------|--------|------------------------------|\n| path  | string | path to the text file        |\n\nReturns: the file contents as a string, or `nil` if the file can't\nbe opened (the error is written to stderr).\n\nUse cases: loading prompts, templates, configuration snippets, or\narbitrary text-shaped inputs into a downstream box.\n\n---\n\n## M.read_data(path, key) → string | nil\n\nReads a soramech-data JSON file and returns either a single field's\nvalue or the whole file re-encoded as JSON.\n\n| param | type   | description                                         |\n|-------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|\n| path  | string | path to the JSON data file                          |\n| key   | string | field name to extract; nil/empty returns whole file |\n\nReturns: the value at `key` (as a string), or — when `key` is nil or\nempty — the entire decoded object re-encoded as a JSON string. `nil`\non failure (file missing, JSON parse error, key not found), with the\nerror on stderr.\n\nStrips metadata: when the field has a wrapping record with a\n`.value` member (the soramech-data shape: `{ value, constant, ... }`),\nonly the `value` is returned. Bare values without a wrapping record\nare returned as-is. Falls back to a flat top-level lookup\n(`obj[key]`) when the file isn't in the soramech-data nested shape.\n\nEdge cases:\n- File missing or unreadable → nil + stderr message\n- JSON decode failure → nil + stderr message (the parser error is\n  included in the message)\n- Whole-file mode re-encodes with indentation, matching how\n  soramech-data writes its files to disk\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/files.lua.info.md"
