    "structuredPatch":[],
    "userModified":false,
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/libs/files.lua.info.md",
    "content":"# files.lua\n\nFile-reading helpers — load text or soramech-data values from disk\ninto the wire graph. Pure Lua except for `read_data`, which depends\non dkjson (already vendored). Use as `require(\"files\")` from another\nLua function, or copy into a map's `src/` and pick a function via\nthe file browser.\n\nBoth functions emit a single string on the box's output wire (per the\nsingle-output rule, issue 218). On failure, the function writes to\nstderr and returns `nil`; the executor surfaces nil as an empty\nstring downstream.\n\n---\n\n## M.read_text(path) → string | nil\n\nReads a plain text file and returns its full contents as a string.\n\n| param | type   | description                  |\n|-------|--------|------------------------------|\n| path  | string | path to the text file        |\n\nReturns: the file contents as a string, or `nil` if the file can't\nbe opened (the error is written to stderr).\n\nUse cases: loading prompts, templates, configuration snippets, or\narbitrary text-shaped inputs into a downstream box.\n\n---\n\n## M.read_data(path, key) → string | nil\n\nReads a soramech-data JSON file and returns either a single field's\nvalue or the whole file re-encoded as JSON.\n\n| param | type   | description                                         |\n|-------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|\n| path  | string | path to the JSON data file                          |\n| key   | string | field name to extract; nil/empty returns whole file |\n\nReturns: the value at `key` (as a string), or — when `key` is nil or\nempty — the entire decoded object re-encoded as a JSON string. `nil`\non failure (file missing, JSON parse error, key not found), with the\nerror on stderr.\n\nStrips metadata: when the field has a wrapping record with a\n`.value` member (the soramech-data shape: `{ value, constant, ... }`),\nonly the `value` is returned. Bare values without a wrapping record\nare returned as-is. Falls back to a flat top-level lookup\n(`obj[key]`) when the file isn't in the soramech-data nested shape.\n\nEdge cases:\n- File missing or unreadable → nil + stderr message\n- JSON decode failure → nil + stderr message (the parser error is\n  included in the message)\n- Whole-file mode re-encodes with indentation, matching how\n  soramech-data writes its files to disk\n"
  },
  "uuid":"0b0c9938-80a1-41f1-b91e-c25b24676a11",

    "originalFile":"# 216 — Read-file box: output contents of a text or data file\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\nNo standard box exists for loading text from disk into the wire graph. A user who\nwants to supply file contents as input to a downstream box must write a custom\nLua function from scratch.\n\n## Intended behavior\nA reusable source file (in `libs/` or a map's `src/`) that exposes two functions:\n- `M.read_text(path)` — reads a plain text file; returns its full contents as a string.\n- `M.read_data(path, key)` — reads a dkjson data file; returns the value at `key` as\n  a string (strips metadata fields like `constant`). If `key` is nil/empty, returns\n  the full JSON-decoded table encoded back to a plain string.\n\nBoth functions output a single port (`text`) carrying the file contents. Error cases\n(file not found, bad JSON) write to stderr and return nil — the executor surfaces nil\nas an empty string on downstream inputs.\n\nThe design follows the established pattern: a regular Lua file that the user picks\nvia the file browser and wires into their map. No executor changes needed.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n1. Create `libs/files.lua` with `M.read_text` and `M.read_data`.\n2. Add `libs/files.lua.info.md` listing the two public functions, their inputs, and\n   their single `text` output.\n\n## Relevant files\n- `libs/ollama.lua` — reference pattern for a library box source file\n- `libs/dkjson.lua` — used by `read_data` for JSON parsing\n- `src/004-executor.lua` — how call box outputs are threaded (no changes needed)\n",

Errors write to stderr and return nil per\nthe executor's nil-becomes-empty-string rule. `read_data` handles\nboth the soramech-data nested shape (`obj.fields[key].value`) and a\nflat fallback (`obj[key]`); whole-file mode (`key == nil or \"\"`)\nre-encodes the parsed object so callers always get a JSON string.\n\n`libs/files.lua.info.md` documents both helpers.",

[x] Map loads centered on screen (fit-to-view)\n- [x] Map can be switched from a list, not a text prompt\n- [x] Empty canvas shows interaction hints\n- [—] Entry box marker (won't implement — phase 3 (issue 222) — placeholder UI for the phase 3 build\n\n## Notes on graph model changes during phase 2\n\nThese are not new features so much as model corrections that shape\nwhat phase 3 will consume:\n\n- **Single-output rule** (218, complete): every box has exactly one\n  output wire. The driver contract emits one JSON value, not an\n  array.\n- **Comparator-based branching** (210, complete): the old `branch`\n  box kind with named ports is removed. A box may carry a\n  `comparand`; the dispatch layer fires the connection whose\n  `from_branch` matches `lt` / `eq` / `gt`.\n- **Iterator routing** (221): a box with `iterator_outputs` is a\n  pure routing primitive; the dispatch layer rotates through the\n  declared output names. Iterators have no `ref` / `fn`.\n- **Connection schema**: `from_branch` field replaces the old\n  `from_output` / `from_port` dual-field design.\n",

{

        "tool_use_id":"toolu_01HwRJ5cQTYkqbpqRKR5tv6o",
        "content":"1\t# 225 — Directory picker: show files alongside dirs, distinguish them visually\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\t\n8\tWhen the user clicks \"+ library dir\" in the file browser, the\n9\tdirectory picker (`show_dir_picker` in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)\n10\tfetches the directory contents via `API.list_dirs(path)`, which\n11\treturns `{ path, dirs }`. Only the subdirectories are rendered; any\n12\tsource files in the current directory are invisible.\n13\t\n14\tThis makes navigation harder than it should be — there's no visible\n15\tconfirmation that you've reached the right directory until you click\n16\t\"use this directory\" and the file list re-renders.\n17\t\n18\tThe list itself uses the `.fb-file-row` class for both dirs and the\n19\tparent-directory `..` row, so dirs and the (currently absent) files\n20\twould render identically. There's no visual cue distinguishing\n21\t\"this is a directory I can enter\" from \"this is a file I'd see if I\n22\tpicked this directory.\"\n23\t\n24\t## Intended behavior\n25\t\n26\tThe directory picker shows both subdirectories and source files in\n27\tthe current directory.\n28\t\n29\t- **Directories**: clickable, navigate into them on click, render\n30\t  with a visual marker (icon, prefix, color, underline, or\n31\t  combination — see \"Visual differentiation\" below).\n32\t- **Files**: shown as a read-only list — they can't be picked\n33\t  individually here (this is a directory picker), but their\n34\t  presence tells the user what they'd be importing if they picked\n35\t  this directory.\n36\t\n37\t### Visual differentiation: dir vs file\n38\t\n39\tThree approaches; pick one or layer them.\n40\t\n41\t1. **Icon prefix** — a small character before the name. `📁` for\n42\t   dirs and `📄` for files, or pure-text alternatives like `▸ /`\n43\t   and `· `. Friendly to colorblind users.\n44\t2. **Color** — directories in the editor's blue accent\n45\t   (`#4a9eff`), files in dim gray (`#6c72a0`). Easy to do but\n46\t   inaccessible alone.\n47\t3. **Underline** — directories underlined to suggest \"clickable\n48\t   link\". Already a familiar web idiom. Pairs well with color.\n49\t\n50\tRecommendation: layer (1) and (2) — icon prefix for accessibility,\n51\tcolor for at-a-glance identification. The icon doesn't have to be\n52\temoji; ASCII glyphs like `>` for dirs and `·` for files are\n53\tunambiguous and font-portable.\n54\t\n55\t### Implementation notes\n56\t\n57\tThe server endpoint `/fs/dirs` currently returns `{ path, dirs }`.\n58\tEither:\n59\t\n60\t- Extend the response to `{ path, dirs, files }`, where `files` is\n61\t  an array of source-file basenames in the current directory. The\n62\t  server filters by extension to avoid listing every file (only\n63\t  show `.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`, etc., matching what the language specs\n64\t  declare).\n65\t- Or add a sibling endpoint `/fs/files?path=…` and call both in\n66\t  parallel from the picker.\n67\t\n68\tExtending the existing endpoint is simpler. The filter\n69\t(file-extensions to include) lives server-side and references\n70\t`langs/*/spec.so`'s `file_ext` field at startup once phase 3\n71\tships; in phase 2 we hard-code the current set\n72\t(`.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`).\n73\t\n74\t## Suggested implementation sequence\n75\t\n76\t1. `src/006-server-main.lua` — extend the `/fs/dirs` handler to also\n77\t   return matching source files. Filter by a small allowlist of\n78\t   extensions for now.\n79\t2. `assets/js/003-api.js::list_dirs` — already returns the response\n80\t   verbatim, so just consume the new `files` field.\n81\t3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::show_dir_picker` — render files\n82\t   below the directory list, in dim color, non-clickable.\n83\t4. `assets/index.html` — add CSS classes `.fb-dir-row` and\n84\t   `.fb-file-row-readonly` (or reuse the existing `.fb-file-row`\n85\t   with a modifier class). Icon prefix added via a `::before`\n86\t   pseudo-element or a leading span.\n87\t5. The same icon/color treatment optionally applies to the main\n88\t   file list (`render` function), which currently uses\n89\t   `.fb-file-row` for clickable file entries — they'd get the file\n90\t   icon + dim color while keeping their click behavior.\n91\t\n92\t## Open questions\n93\t\n94\t- Should files in the dir picker be clickable to \"preview\" their\n95\t  contents (open the source viewer from issue 215)? Probably not —\n96\t  it adds a click target where there shouldn't be one. The user is\n97\t  picking a directory, not a file. Defer.\n98\t- Which icon set: ASCII (`>`, `·`) or unicode glyphs (`▸`, `·`) or\n99\t  emoji (`📁`, `📄`)? ASCII / unicode for portability; emoji\n100\t  rendering varies wildly across systems.\n101\t- Should the file list hide when collapsed (collapsible group\n102\t  header)? Probably not necessary for the picker — the file list\n103\t  is informational, and short.\n104\t\n105\t## Relevant files\n106\t\n107\t- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — `show_dir_picker`, file rendering\n108\t- `src/006-server-main.lua` — `/fs/dirs` handler\n109\t- `assets/js/003-api.js` — `list_dirs` API call\n110\t- `assets/index.html` — CSS for `.fb-file-row` etc.\n111\t- `issues/completed/207-source-file-browser-and-port-population.md`\n112\t  — original file browser issue\n113\t",

      "content":"# 225 — Directory picker: show files alongside dirs, distinguish them visually\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the user clicks \"+ library dir\" in the file browser, the\ndirectory picker (`show_dir_picker` in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)\nfetches the directory contents via `API.list_dirs(path)`, which\nreturns `{ path, dirs }`. Only the subdirectories are rendered; any\nsource files in the current directory are invisible.\n\nThis makes navigation harder than it should be — there's no visible\nconfirmation that you've reached the right directory until you click\n\"use this directory\" and the file list re-renders.\n\nThe list itself uses the `.fb-file-row` class for both dirs and the\nparent-directory `..` row, so dirs and the (currently absent) files\nwould render identically. There's no visual cue distinguishing\n\"this is a directory I can enter\" from \"this is a file I'd see if I\npicked this directory.\"\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe directory picker shows both subdirectories and source files in\nthe current directory.\n\n- **Directories**: clickable, navigate into them on click, render\n  with a visual marker (icon, prefix, color, underline, or\n  combination — see \"Visual differentiation\" below).\n- **Files**: shown as a read-only list — they can't be picked\n  individually here (this is a directory picker), but their\n  presence tells the user what they'd be importing if they picked\n  this directory.\n\n### Visual differentiation: dir vs file\n\nThree approaches; pick one or layer them.\n\n1. **Icon prefix** — a small character before the name. `📁` for\n   dirs and `📄` for files, or pure-text alternatives like `▸ /`\n   and `· `. Friendly to colorblind users.\n2. **Color** — directories in the editor's blue accent\n   (`#4a9eff`), files in dim gray (`#6c72a0`). Easy to do but\n   inaccessible alone.\n3. **Underline** — directories underlined to suggest \"clickable\n   link\". Already a familiar web idiom. Pairs well with color.\n\nRecommendation: layer (1) and (2) — icon prefix for accessibility,\ncolor for at-a-glance identification. The icon doesn't have to be\nemoji; ASCII glyphs like `>` for dirs and `·` for files are\nunambiguous and font-portable.\n\n### Implementation notes\n\nThe server endpoint `/fs/dirs` currently returns `{ path, dirs }`.\nEither:\n\n- Extend the response to `{ path, dirs, files }`, where `files` is\n  an array of source-file basenames in the current directory. The\n  server filters by extension to avoid listing every file (only\n  show `.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`, etc., matching what the language specs\n  declare).\n- Or add a sibling endpoint `/fs/files?path=…` and call both in\n  parallel from the picker.\n\nExtending the existing endpoint is simpler. The filter\n(file-extensions to include) lives server-side and references\n`langs/*/spec.so`'s `file_ext` field at startup once phase 3\nships; in phase 2 we hard-code the current set\n(`.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/006-server-main.lua` — extend the `/fs/dirs` handler to also\n   return matching source files. Filter by a small allowlist of\n   extensions for now.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js::list_dirs` — already returns the response\n   verbatim, so just consume the new `files` field.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::show_dir_picker` — render files\n   below the directory list, in dim color, non-clickable.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add CSS classes `.fb-dir-row` and\n   `.fb-file-row-readonly` (or reuse the existing `.fb-file-row`\n   with a modifier class). Icon prefix added via a `::before`\n   pseudo-element or a leading span.\n5. The same icon/color treatment optionally applies to the main\n   file list (`render` function), which currently uses\n   `.fb-file-row` for clickable file entries — they'd get the file\n   icon + dim color while keeping their click behavior.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should files in the dir picker be clickable to \"preview\" their\n  contents (open the source viewer from issue 215)? Probably not —\n  it adds a click target where there shouldn't be one. The user is\n  picking a directory, not a file. Defer.\n- Which icon set: ASCII (`>`, `·`) or unicode glyphs (`▸`, `·`) or\n  emoji (`📁`, `📄`)? ASCII / unicode for portability; emoji\n  rendering varies wildly across systems.\n- Should the file list hide when collapsed (collapsible group\n  header)? Probably not necessary for the picker — the file list\n  is informational, and short.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — `show_dir_picker`, file rendering\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — `/fs/dirs` handler\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — `list_dirs` API call\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for `.fb-file-row` etc.\n- `issues/completed/207-source-file-browser-and-port-population.md`\n  — original file browser issue\n"
    }
  },

      "content":"  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show_dir_picker\n  // Renders a directory browser into container, navigating the server filesystem.\n  // on_select(abs_path) called when the user confirms a directory.\n  // on_cancel() called when the user clicks back.\n  // initial_path: starting directory; defaults to /home if omitted.\n  async function show_dir_picker(container, on_select, on_cancel, initial_path) {\n    let current_path = initial_path || '/home';\n\n    const render_picker = async () => {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n      let result;\n      try {\n        result = await API.list_dirs(current_path);\n      } catch(e) {\n        container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n        return;\n      }\n\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // back button returns to file list without selecting\n      const cancel_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      cancel_btn.className   = 'fb-back';\n      cancel_btn.textContent = '← cancel';\n      cancel_btn.onclick     = on_cancel;\n      container.appendChild(cancel_btn);\n\n      // current path breadcrumb\n      const path_el = document.createElement('div');\n      path_el.style.cssText = 'font-size:10px;color:#4a9eff;word-break:break-all;' +\n        'margin-bottom:6px;font-family:monospace;';\n      path_el.textContent = result.path;\n      container.appendChild(path_el);\n\n      // \"use this directory\" confirmation button\n      const sel_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      sel_btn.className   = 'add-port';\n      sel_btn.textContent = '✓ use this directory';\n      sel_btn.style.cssText = 'display:block;width:100%;margin-bottom:8px;' +\n        'color:#4caf7d;border-color:#4caf7d;';\n      sel_btn.onclick = () => on_select(result.path);\n      container.appendChild(sel_btn);\n\n      // parent directory row (except at filesystem root)\n      if (result.path !== '/') {\n        const up_row = document.createElement('div');\n        up_row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        up_row.textContent = '..';\n        up_row.onclick = () => {\n          // strip last path component\n          const parent = result.path.replace(/\\/[^/]+$/, '') || '/';\n          current_path = parent;\n          render_picker();\n        };\n        container.appendChild(up_row);\n      }\n\n      if (result.dirs.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = '(no subdirectories)';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n      }\n\n      result.dirs.forEach(name => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className   = 'fb-file-row';\n        row.textContent = name + '/';\n        row.onclick = () => {\n          current_path = result.path === '/' ? '/' + name : result.path + '/' + name;\n          render_picker();\n        };\n        container.appendChild(row);\n      });\n    };\n\n    render_picker();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ show_fb_ctx_menu\n  // Displays a small floating context menu; reuses .ctx-item CSS from the global stylesheet.\n  // items: [{label, action, danger?}]\n  function show_fb_ctx_menu(screen_x, screen_y, items) {\n    let menu = document.getElementById('fb-ctx-menu');\n    if (!menu) {\n      menu = document.createElement('div');\n      menu.id = 'fb-ctx-menu';"

    "originalFile":"# 225 — Directory picker: show files alongside dirs, distinguish them visually\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nWhen the user clicks \"+ library dir\" in the file browser, the\ndirectory picker (`show_dir_picker` in `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js`)\nfetches the directory contents via `API.list_dirs(path)`, which\nreturns `{ path, dirs }`. Only the subdirectories are rendered; any\nsource files in the current directory are invisible.\n\nThis makes navigation harder than it should be — there's no visible\nconfirmation that you've reached the right directory until you click\n\"use this directory\" and the file list re-renders.\n\nThe list itself uses the `.fb-file-row` class for both dirs and the\nparent-directory `..` row, so dirs and the (currently absent) files\nwould render identically. There's no visual cue distinguishing\n\"this is a directory I can enter\" from \"this is a file I'd see if I\npicked this directory.\"\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nThe directory picker shows both subdirectories and source files in\nthe current directory.\n\n- **Directories**: clickable, navigate into them on click, render\n  with a visual marker (icon, prefix, color, underline, or\n  combination — see \"Visual differentiation\" below).\n- **Files**: shown as a read-only list — they can't be picked\n  individually here (this is a directory picker), but their\n  presence tells the user what they'd be importing if they picked\n  this directory.\n\n### Visual differentiation: dir vs file\n\nThree approaches; pick one or layer them.\n\n1. **Icon prefix** — a small character before the name. `📁` for\n   dirs and `📄` for files, or pure-text alternatives like `▸ /`\n   and `· `. Friendly to colorblind users.\n2. **Color** — directories in the editor's blue accent\n   (`#4a9eff`), files in dim gray (`#6c72a0`). Easy to do but\n   inaccessible alone.\n3. **Underline** — directories underlined to suggest \"clickable\n   link\". Already a familiar web idiom. Pairs well with color.\n\nRecommendation: layer (1) and (2) — icon prefix for accessibility,\ncolor for at-a-glance identification. The icon doesn't have to be\nemoji; ASCII glyphs like `>` for dirs and `·` for files are\nunambiguous and font-portable.\n\n### Implementation notes\n\nThe server endpoint `/fs/dirs` currently returns `{ path, dirs }`.\nEither:\n\n- Extend the response to `{ path, dirs, files }`, where `files` is\n  an array of source-file basenames in the current directory. The\n  server filters by extension to avoid listing every file (only\n  show `.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`, etc., matching what the language specs\n  declare).\n- Or add a sibling endpoint `/fs/files?path=…` and call both in\n  parallel from the picker.\n\nExtending the existing endpoint is simpler. The filter\n(file-extensions to include) lives server-side and references\n`langs/*/spec.so`'s `file_ext` field at startup once phase 3\nships; in phase 2 we hard-code the current set\n(`.lua`, `.c`, `.sh`).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/006-server-main.lua` — extend the `/fs/dirs` handler to also\n   return matching source files. Filter by a small allowlist of\n   extensions for now.\n2. `assets/js/003-api.js::list_dirs` — already returns the response\n   verbatim, so just consume the new `files` field.\n3. `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::show_dir_picker` — render files\n   below the directory list, in dim color, non-clickable.\n4. `assets/index.html` — add CSS classes `.fb-dir-row` and\n   `.fb-file-row-readonly` (or reuse the existing `.fb-file-row`\n   with a modifier class). Icon prefix added via a `::before`\n   pseudo-element or a leading span.\n5. The same icon/color treatment optionally applies to the main\n   file list (`render` function), which currently uses\n   `.fb-file-row` for clickable file entries — they'd get the file\n   icon + dim color while keeping their click behavior.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should files in the dir picker be clickable to \"preview\" their\n  contents (open the source viewer from issue 215)? Probably not —\n  it adds a click target where there shouldn't be one. The user is\n  picking a directory, not a file. Defer.\n- Which icon set: ASCII (`>`, `·`) or unicode glyphs (`▸`, `·`) or\n  emoji (`📁`, `📄`)? ASCII / unicode for portability; emoji\n  rendering varies wildly across systems.\n- Should the file list hide when collapsed (collapsible group\n  header)? Probably not necessary for the picker — the file list\n  is informational, and short.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js` — `show_dir_picker`, file rendering\n- `src/006-server-main.lua` — `/fs/dirs` handler\n- `assets/js/003-api.js` — `list_dirs` API call\n- `assets/index.html` — CSS for `.fb-file-row` etc.\n- `issues/completed/207-source-file-browser-and-port-population.md`\n  — original file browser issue\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",

Phase 3 will\nswap the hard-coded list for whatever the language specs declare.\n\nClient-side:\n- `assets/js/007-filebrowser.js::show_dir_picker` renders dirs and\n  files separately.     "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // Output rows: iterator boxes have N named slots (issue 221);\n    // comparator active: 3 dots (lt/eq/gt); sink: 0; otherwise 1.\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      n_out = box.iterator_outputs.length;\n    } else if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      n_out = 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226). No output\n      // port, no wire-grab target, nothing for the inspector to render.\n      out_pts = [];\n    } else if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      // iterator box (issue 221) — N named output dots stacked down\n      // the right edge, one per declared slot. Slot names land in the\n      // `name` field, so the wire's `from_branch` will pick them up\n      // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n      out_pts = box.iterator_outputs.map((slot, i) => ({\n        name: slot, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const y = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const w = BOX_W;\n    const h = box_height(box);\n    const kind  = box.kind || 'call';\n    const color = KIND_COLOR[kind] || '#888';\n\n    // shadow when selected\n    if (selected) {\n      ctx.shadowColor = color;\n      ctx.shadowBlur  = 12;\n    }\n\n    // body\n    ctx.fillStyle   = '#1e2130';\n    ctx.strokeStyle = selected ? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // label branch name ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') to the left of the dot; nothing for single wire\n      if (p.name) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_box\n  // Returns box id if (wx,wy) is inside a box body, or null.\n  function hit_test_box(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const b = boxes[id];\n      const x = b.ui?.x ?? 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ? inputs : outputs;\n    const p = list.find(p => p.name === port_name);\n    return p ? { x: p.x, y: p.y } : null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return {\n    boxes, BOX_W, BOX_HEADER, PORT_R,\n    box_height, port_positions,\n    draw_all, draw_box, hit_test_port, hit_test_box, get_port_world_pos,\n  };\n})();\n",
    "oldString":"    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(p.name, p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });",
    "newString":"    // Input port labels are rendered as DOM overlays now (issue 224)\n    // so the user can edit them inline. We only draw the dot here;\n    // the overlay positions an editable input next to it.\n    in_pts.forEach(p => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n    });",

        "input":{
          "content":"// DOM overlays for editable input port names (issue 224).\n//\n// The canvas renders the box body and port dots; this module floats\n// HTML <input> elements next to each input port so the user can\n// rename them inline. Names used to be read-only labels (issue 208);\n// the rationale for that decision was preventing typo drift between\n// source code and box JSON, but the file browser still re-populates\n// names on every re-pick, and a typo now produces an explicit\n// runtime error rather than a silent skip — so editability is back.\n//\n// Literal values stay in the inspector's port display; only the\n// name lives on the canvas.\n//\n// Lifecycle:\n//   - redraw() runs in the main render loop after Boxes.draw_all,\n//     so positions stay aligned with the camera and any box drag.\n//   - Per-box overlays are created lazily on first sight and torn\n//     down when the box leaves Boxes.boxes.\n//   - Per-port rows rebuild whenever the port count changes\n//     (variadic add/remove); otherwise their <input> elements\n//     persist so user typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n//   - Updates skip any input that currently has focus, again to\n//     avoid stomping on in-progress edits.\n\nconst Overlays = (() => {\n  // overlays: { [box_id]: { container, rows: [{ row, name_inp, port_idx }] } }\n  const overlays = {};\n  let root = null;\n\n  // {{{ ensure_root\n  function ensure_root() {\n    if (root) return;\n    root = document.getElementById('box-overlays');\n    if (!root) {\n      root = document.createElement('div');\n      root.id = 'box-overlays';\n      // The canvas takes the entire viewport; the overlay layer sits\n      // on top of it. pointer-events:none lets canvas clicks pass\n      // through whitespace; individual <input>s opt back in.\n      root.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;' +\n        'height:100%;pointer-events:none;overflow:hidden;';\n      // Insert before the inspector so the overlay layer doesn't\n      // capture events meant for the right-side panel.\n      const canvas_el = document.getElementById('canvas');\n      canvas_el.parentNode.insertBefore(root, canvas_el.nextSibling);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ build_row\n  // Each row is one editable <input> for a single port name.\n  // commit-on-blur (and Enter) — typing alone doesn't fire the\n  // rename, so users can clear-and-retype without triggering wire\n  // rewrites mid-edit.\n  function build_row(box, port_idx) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'box-overlay-row';\n\n    const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    name_inp.type      = 'text';\n    name_inp.className = 'box-overlay-name';\n    name_inp.value     = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n\n    const commit = async () => {\n      const new_name = name_inp.value.trim();\n      const ok = await Inspector.rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name);\n      if (!ok) {\n        // restore to the box's actual name (which rename_port left\n        // unchanged on rejection) so the field doesn't keep\n        // displaying the rejected text\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n      }\n    };\n    name_inp.addEventListener('blur', commit);\n    name_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n      if (e.key === 'Enter')   { e.preventDefault(); name_inp.blur(); }\n      if (e.key === 'Escape')  {\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n        name_inp.blur();\n      }\n    });\n\n    row.appendChild(name_inp);\n    return { row, name_inp };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ ensure_overlay\n  function ensure_overlay(box) {\n    let ov = overlays[box.id];\n    if (!ov) {\n      const container = document.createElement('div');\n      container.className = 'box-overlay';\n      ov = { container, rows: [] };\n      overlays[box.id] = ov;\n      root.appendChild(container);\n    }\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    if (ov.rows.length !== inputs.length) {\n      // Port count changed — rebuild rows. Cheap (small N), and it\n      // skips the bookkeeping of which slots got renamed/removed.\n      ov.container.innerHTML = '';\n      ov.rows = inputs.map((_, i) => {\n        const r = build_row(box, i);\n        ov.container.appendChild(r.row);\n        return { ...r, port_idx: i };\n      });\n    } else {\n      // Same shape, possibly different names — sync values for\n      // inputs that aren't focused (don't clobber in-progress edits).\n      ov.rows.forEach((r, i) => {\n        if (document.activeElement !== r.name_inp) {\n          r.name_inp.value = inputs[i].name || '';\n        }\n      });\n    }\n    return ov;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ position_overlay\n  // The overlay isn't a single transformed element — each port row\n  // is positioned individually so the <input> sizing stays in\n  // screen pixels regardless of zoom (consistent with most node\n  // editors).\n  function position_overlay(box, ov) {\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const screen = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(box.id, p.name, 'input');\n      if (!screen) return;\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(screen.x, screen.y);\n      const row = ov.rows[i].row;\n      // dot + 6px gap; vertically center the input on the dot\n      row.style.left = (s.x + 10) + 'px';\n      row.style.top  = (s.y - 9)  + 'px';\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ redraw\n  // Called from the main render loop. Reconciles overlay set with\n  // Boxes.boxes, then repositions every visible row.\n  function redraw() {\n    ensure_root();\n\n    const live = new Set();\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      live.add(id);\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const ov  = ensure_overlay(box);\n      position_overlay(box, ov);\n    }\n    for (const id in overlays) {\n      if (!live.has(id)) {\n        overlays[id].container.remove();\n        delete overlays[id];\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ remove\n  // Called when a box is deleted explicitly so the overlay is gone\n  // before the next frame catches up via redraw's reconciliation.\n  function remove(box_id) {\n    if (overlays[box_id]) {\n      overlays[box_id].container.remove();\n      delete overlays[box_id];\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { redraw, remove };\n})();\n",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/009-box-overlays.js"

    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/009-box-overlays.js",
    "content":"// DOM overlays for editable input port names (issue 224).\n//\n// The canvas renders the box body and port dots; this module floats\n// HTML <input> elements next to each input port so the user can\n// rename them inline. Names used to be read-only labels (issue 208);\n// the rationale for that decision was preventing typo drift between\n// source code and box JSON, but the file browser still re-populates\n// names on every re-pick, and a typo now produces an explicit\n// runtime error rather than a silent skip — so editability is back.\n//\n// Literal values stay in the inspector's port display; only the\n// name lives on the canvas.\n//\n// Lifecycle:\n//   - redraw() runs in the main render loop after Boxes.draw_all,\n//     so positions stay aligned with the camera and any box drag.\n//   - Per-box overlays are created lazily on first sight and torn\n//     down when the box leaves Boxes.boxes.\n//   - Per-port rows rebuild whenever the port count changes\n//     (variadic add/remove); otherwise their <input> elements\n//     persist so user typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n//   - Updates skip any input that currently has focus, again to\n//     avoid stomping on in-progress edits.\n\nconst Overlays = (() => {\n  // overlays: { [box_id]: { container, rows: [{ row, name_inp, port_idx }] } }\n  const overlays = {};\n  let root = null;\n\n  // {{{ ensure_root\n  function ensure_root() {\n    if (root) return;\n    root = document.getElementById('box-overlays');\n    if (!root) {\n      root = document.createElement('div');\n      root.id = 'box-overlays';\n      // The canvas takes the entire viewport; the overlay layer sits\n      // on top of it. pointer-events:none lets canvas clicks pass\n      // through whitespace; individual <input>s opt back in.\n      root.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;' +\n        'height:100%;pointer-events:none;overflow:hidden;';\n      // Insert before the inspector so the overlay layer doesn't\n      // capture events meant for the right-side panel.\n      const canvas_el = document.getElementById('canvas');\n      canvas_el.parentNode.insertBefore(root, canvas_el.nextSibling);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ build_row\n  // Each row is one editable <input> for a single port name.\n  // commit-on-blur (and Enter) — typing alone doesn't fire the\n  // rename, so users can clear-and-retype without triggering wire\n  // rewrites mid-edit.\n  function build_row(box, port_idx) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'box-overlay-row';\n\n    const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    name_inp.type      = 'text';\n    name_inp.className = 'box-overlay-name';\n    name_inp.value     = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n\n    const commit = async () => {\n      const new_name = name_inp.value.trim();\n      const ok = await Inspector.rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name);\n      if (!ok) {\n        // restore to the box's actual name (which rename_port left\n        // unchanged on rejection) so the field doesn't keep\n        // displaying the rejected text\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n      }\n    };\n    name_inp.addEventListener('blur', commit);\n    name_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n      if (e.key === 'Enter')   { e.preventDefault(); name_inp.blur(); }\n      if (e.key === 'Escape')  {\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n        name_inp.blur();\n      }\n    });\n\n    row.appendChild(name_inp);\n    return { row, name_inp };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ ensure_overlay\n  function ensure_overlay(box) {\n    let ov = overlays[box.id];\n    if (!ov) {\n      const container = document.createElement('div');\n      container.className = 'box-overlay';\n      ov = { container, rows: [] };\n      overlays[box.id] = ov;\n      root.appendChild(container);\n    }\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    if (ov.rows.length !== inputs.length) {\n      // Port count changed — rebuild rows. Cheap (small N), and it\n      // skips the bookkeeping of which slots got renamed/removed.\n      ov.container.innerHTML = '';\n      ov.rows = inputs.map((_, i) => {\n        const r = build_row(box, i);\n        ov.container.appendChild(r.row);\n        return { ...r, port_idx: i };\n      });\n    } else {\n      // Same shape, possibly different names — sync values for\n      // inputs that aren't focused (don't clobber in-progress edits).\n      ov.rows.forEach((r, i) => {\n        if (document.activeElement !== r.name_inp) {\n          r.name_inp.value = inputs[i].name || '';\n        }\n      });\n    }\n    return ov;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ position_overlay\n  // The overlay isn't a single transformed element — each port row\n  // is positioned individually so the <input> sizing stays in\n  // screen pixels regardless of zoom (consistent with most node\n  // editors).\n  function position_overlay(box, ov) {\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const screen = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(box.id, p.name, 'input');\n      if (!screen) return;\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(screen.x, screen.y);\n      const row = ov.rows[i].row;\n      // dot + 6px gap; vertically center the input on the dot\n      row.style.left = (s.x + 10) + 'px';\n      row.style.top  = (s.y - 9)  + 'px';\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ redraw\n  // Called from the main render loop. Reconciles overlay set with\n  // Boxes.boxes, then repositions every visible row.\n  function redraw() {\n    ensure_root();\n\n    const live = new Set();\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      live.add(id);\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const ov  = ensure_overlay(box);\n      position_overlay(box, ov);\n    }\n    for (const id in overlays) {\n      if (!live.has(id)) {\n        overlays[id].container.remove();\n        delete overlays[id];\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ remove\n  // Called when a box is deleted explicitly so the overlay is gone\n  // before the next frame catches up via redraw's reconciliation.\n  function remove(box_id) {\n    if (overlays[box_id]) {\n      overlays[box_id].container.remove();\n      delete overlays[box_id];\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { redraw, remove };\n})();\n"
  },

    "originalFile":"// DOM overlays for editable input port names (issue 224).\n//\n// The canvas renders the box body and port dots; this module floats\n// HTML <input> elements next to each input port so the user can\n// rename them inline. Names used to be read-only labels (issue 208);\n// the rationale for that decision was preventing typo drift between\n// source code and box JSON, but the file browser still re-populates\n// names on every re-pick, and a typo now produces an explicit\n// runtime error rather than a silent skip — so editability is back.\n//\n// Literal values stay in the inspector's port display; only the\n// name lives on the canvas.\n//\n// Lifecycle:\n//   - redraw() runs in the main render loop after Boxes.draw_all,\n//     so positions stay aligned with the camera and any box drag.\n//   - Per-box overlays are created lazily on first sight and torn\n//     down when the box leaves Boxes.boxes.\n//   - Per-port rows rebuild whenever the port count changes\n//     (variadic add/remove); otherwise their <input> elements\n//     persist so user typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n//   - Updates skip any input that currently has focus, again to\n//     avoid stomping on in-progress edits.\n\nconst Overlays = (() => {\n  // overlays: { [box_id]: { container, rows: [{ row, name_inp, port_idx }] } }\n  const overlays = {};\n  let root = null;\n\n  // {{{ ensure_root\n  function ensure_root() {\n    if (root) return;\n    root = document.getElementById('box-overlays');\n    if (!root) {\n      root = document.createElement('div');\n      root.id = 'box-overlays';\n      // The canvas takes the entire viewport; the overlay layer sits\n      // on top of it. pointer-events:none lets canvas clicks pass\n      // through whitespace; individual <input>s opt back in.\n      root.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;' +\n        'height:100%;pointer-events:none;overflow:hidden;';\n      // Insert before the inspector so the overlay layer doesn't\n      // capture events meant for the right-side panel.\n      const canvas_el = document.getElementById('canvas');\n      canvas_el.parentNode.insertBefore(root, canvas_el.nextSibling);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ build_row\n  // Each row is one editable <input> for a single port name.\n  // commit-on-blur (and Enter) — typing alone doesn't fire the\n  // rename, so users can clear-and-retype without triggering wire\n  // rewrites mid-edit.\n  function build_row(box, port_idx) {\n    const row = document.createElement('div');\n    row.className = 'box-overlay-row';\n\n    const name_inp = document.createElement('input');\n    name_inp.type      = 'text';\n    name_inp.className = 'box-overlay-name';\n    name_inp.value     = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n\n    const commit = async () => {\n      const new_name = name_inp.value.trim();\n      const ok = await Inspector.rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name);\n      if (!ok) {\n        // restore to the box's actual name (which rename_port left\n        // unchanged on rejection) so the field doesn't keep\n        // displaying the rejected text\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n      }\n    };\n    name_inp.addEventListener('blur', commit);\n    name_inp.addEventListener('keydown', e => {\n      if (e.key === 'Enter')   { e.preventDefault(); name_inp.blur(); }\n      if (e.key === 'Escape')  {\n        name_inp.value = (box.inputs[port_idx] && box.inputs[port_idx].name) || '';\n        name_inp.blur();\n      }\n    });\n\n    row.appendChild(name_inp);\n    return { row, name_inp };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ ensure_overlay\n  function ensure_overlay(box) {\n    let ov = overlays[box.id];\n    if (!ov) {\n      const container = document.createElement('div');\n      container.className = 'box-overlay';\n      ov = { container, rows: [] };\n      overlays[box.id] = ov;\n      root.appendChild(container);\n    }\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    if (ov.rows.length !== inputs.length) {\n      // Port count changed — rebuild rows. Cheap (small N), and it\n      // skips the bookkeeping of which slots got renamed/removed.\n      ov.container.innerHTML = '';\n      ov.rows = inputs.map((_, i) => {\n        const r = build_row(box, i);\n        ov.container.appendChild(r.row);\n        return { ...r, port_idx: i };\n      });\n    } else {\n      // Same shape, possibly different names — sync values for\n      // inputs that aren't focused (don't clobber in-progress edits).\n      ov.rows.forEach((r, i) => {\n        if (document.activeElement !== r.name_inp) {\n          r.name_inp.value = inputs[i].name || '';\n        }\n      });\n    }\n    return ov;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ position_overlay\n  // The overlay isn't a single transformed element — each port row\n  // is positioned individually so the <input> sizing stays in\n  // screen pixels regardless of zoom (consistent with most node\n  // editors).\n  function position_overlay(box, ov) {\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n    inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const screen = Boxes.get_port_world_pos(box.id, p.name, 'input');\n      if (!screen) return;\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(screen.x, screen.y);\n      const row = ov.rows[i].row;\n      // dot + 6px gap; vertically center the input on the dot\n      row.style.left = (s.x + 10) + 'px';\n      row.style.top  = (s.y - 9)  + 'px';\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ redraw\n  // Called from the main render loop. Reconciles overlay set with\n  // Boxes.boxes, then repositions every visible row.\n  function redraw() {\n    ensure_root();\n\n    const live = new Set();\n    for (const id in Boxes.boxes) {\n      live.add(id);\n      const box = Boxes.boxes[id];\n      const ov  = ensure_overlay(box);\n      position_overlay(box, ov);\n    }\n    for (const id in overlays) {\n      if (!live.has(id)) {\n        overlays[id].container.remove();\n        delete overlays[id];\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ remove\n  // Called when a box is deleted explicitly so the overlay is gone\n  // before the next frame catches up via redraw's reconciliation.\n  function remove(box_id) {\n    if (overlays[box_id]) {\n      overlays[box_id].container.remove();\n      delete overlays[box_id];\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { redraw, remove };\n})();\n",
    "oldString":"      // Insert before the inspector so the overlay layer doesn't\n      // capture events meant for the right-side panel.\n      const canvas_el = document.getElementById('canvas');\n      canvas_el.parentNode.insertBefore(root, canvas_el.nextSibling);",
    "newString":"      // Layer inside the same wrapper as the canvas so it rides\n      // along with any future canvas-wrap repositioning. The wrapper\n      // is the one with #canvas-wrap; appending puts the overlay on\n      // top of the canvas in z-order.\n      const wrap = document.getElementById('canvas-wrap');\n      wrap.appendChild(root);",

    "structuredPatch":[{
        "newStart":1,
        "newLines":68,
        "lines":[" # 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing"," "," ## Status","-open","+complete (scope adjusted: name-edit moved, value-edit stays)"," ","+## Scope adjustment","+","+The value field stays in the inspector. Only the port-name editing","+moved to the canvas overlay — the rest of issue 208's read-only-name","+decision stays reversed (names are now editable), but the overlay","+implementation only carries the name input. Values on the canvas","+were the more disruptive half of the change and the user opted out;","+keeping values in the inspector also keeps the variadic auto-grow","+flow exactly where it already lives.","+","+## Implementation notes","+","+New module `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` floats an editable","+`<input>` per input port next to its dot. Lifecycle:","+- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after","+  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is","+  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).","+- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears","+  down orphans.","+- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic","+  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user","+  typing isn't clobbered between frames.","+- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.","+- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing","+  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite","+  cost is paid once per change.","+","+Inspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:","+- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),","+  unique within the box.","+- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port","+  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson","+  from 217).","+- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on","+  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the","+  new name without the user having to re-click.","+","+`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —","+the overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator","+slot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this","+issue.","+","+CSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,","+`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent","+with most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom).","+","+### Edge cases","+","+- **Variadic slot rename**: rename_port accepts `base_N`-shaped","+  names, so the user can technically rename a non-variadic port to","+  match a variadic-slot pattern. The variadic helpers detect the","+  shape on subsequent operations; if the user creates one by","+  accident the recovery is to rename it back.","+- **Renamed port had a wire**: the wire's `to_input` rewrites on","+  both endpoints; the canvas re-renders with the new label without","+  losing the connection.","+- **Typo'd a name to something the function doesn't expect**: this","+  is the intentional tradeoff from issue 208. The runtime error","+  surfaces clearly rather than silently skipping.","+"," ## Current behavior"," "," Input port names are read-only labels in the inspector — derived from"],
        "oldStart":1,
        "oldLines":8
      }],
    "originalFile":"# 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput port names are read-only labels in the inspector — derived from\nthe function's parameter names when the file browser populates the\nbox (issue 207, 208). Each port row in the inspector also carries a\nliteral value input. With variadic inputs (issue 217), a box with\nseveral slots produces a tall, narrow list of name+type+value rows\nthat crowds the sidebar.\n\nThe canvas already renders port names next to their dots, so the\nname appears twice — once on the canvas (read-only label) and once\nin the inspector (read-only label).\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nMove both the port name and the literal value input out of the\ninspector and onto the canvas next to the port dot. The inspector\nkeeps only the variadic toggle / remove-slot buttons and any\nnon-port box-level fields (ref / fn / comparator).\n\n### Why\n\n- The inspector is crowded with redundant data (the canvas already\n  shows port names).\n- Literal values often need more horizontal room than a 72px input\n  field allows, especially for prompts, paths, or JSON snippets.\n- Reading the box's full configuration without clicking through the\n  inspector becomes possible — every input's name and value is\n  visible directly on the canvas.\n- 208's \"read-only port names\" decision was about preventing typo\n  drift between source code and box JSON; the file browser still\n  populates names from the parsed signature, but the user should be\n  free to override them after the fact.\n\n### Reverses 208's read-only-name decision\n\nIssue 208 made input port names non-editable on the principle that\nthey should match the parsed function signature exactly. This issue\nflips that — names become editable again, with the trade-off that a\ntypo can desynchronize the editor's record from the function the box\ncalls. The cost is a per-box runtime error rather than a hidden\nsilent skip, so it surfaces clearly. The benefit is that users can\nrename inputs freely (renaming a Lua function's parameter and then\nupdating the box does not require re-browsing).\n\n### Layout\n\nEach input port row on the canvas becomes:\n\n```\n●  text_0    ┌──────────────────┐\n             │ \"hello world\"    │\n             └──────────────────┘\n```\n\n- The port dot stays on the box's left edge (unchanged).\n- The port name is an editable text field, rendered as an HTML\n  overlay positioned next to the dot. Pan and zoom adjust the\n  overlay's transform to match the canvas.\n- The literal value field is another HTML overlay below or to the\n  right of the name.\n\n### HTML overlays over the canvas\n\nCanvas 2D doesn't do native text inputs, so the editable fields are\nDOM `<input>` elements absolutely positioned over the canvas. A\nsmall per-box overlay container holds them, transforms with the\ncamera (CSS transform applied on every render frame), and updates\nthe underlying `box.inputs[i]` on input.\n\nThis is the same pattern as the source viewer (issue 215) — DOM\nelements layered over the canvas, with positions computed from\n`Canvas.world_to_screen`. The complexity is keeping overlay state\nin sync with the canvas: they need to be created when a box is\nloaded, destroyed when a box is deleted, repositioned every frame\n(or when pan/zoom changes), and hidden when off-screen.\n\n### Inspector becomes lighter\n\nAfter this change the inspector shows:\n- Box label (editable)\n- ref / fn (with browse / view buttons)\n- For each input: the variadic toggle (`var` / `var ×` / `×`) only.\n  No name field, no value field — those live on the canvas.\n- Output: the comparator toggle and comparand input (unchanged).\n- Delete-box button (unchanged).\n\nRoughly half the height the current inspector takes for variadic\nboxes.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Overlay performance**: dozens of overlays multiplied by frequent\n  pan/zoom updates is a real cost. Tests are needed; a bounding-box\n  cull (only render overlays for visible boxes) is the obvious\n  optimization if it matters.\n- **Value-input width**: the field grows with the input's content, or\n  is a fixed width with horizontal scroll? Probably grow-on-content\n  with a max width clamp, similar to what monospace text does.\n- **Editing port names while wires are connected**: renaming a port\n  while a wire is attached should rename the wire's `to_input` /\n  `from_branch` on both endpoints atomically — same bilateral-update\n  pattern the variadic ops use.\n- **Name validation**: what's a valid port name? Probably `[A-Za-z_][\\w]*`\n  (a Lua / C / shell-compatible identifier). Reject names that start\n  with digits, contain spaces, etc. Reject duplicates within a box.\n- **Backward compat**: existing maps with the current layout work as\n  before — no migration needed. The change is purely UI.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Create `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` (new module) responsible\n   for per-box DOM overlays. Public API: `update_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   to create / refresh overlays for a box, `remove_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   on box deletion, `redraw_overlays()` on pan/zoom.\n2. Wire the overlays into the render loop: after `Boxes.draw_all`,\n   call `redraw_overlays()` to reposition the overlays for the\n   current camera. The overlays themselves don't redraw — only their\n   `style.left` / `style.top` / `style.transform` updates.\n3. Remove the name + value rendering from `mk_port_display` in\n   `004-inspector.js`. Leave only the variadic controls.\n4. Remove the canvas-side port name labels from `002-boxes.js::draw_box`\n   (the overlay's editable input replaces it).\n5. Wire validation: name must be a valid identifier and unique\n   within the box's `inputs`. Validate in the input's `oninput`\n   handler; revert to the previous valid name on rejection.\n6. Test against `maps/hello`, `maps/classify-demo`, and a fresh map\n   with variadic inputs (e.g. via `libs/text.lua`'s concat).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — port name labels move out\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `mk_port_display` simplified\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — pan/zoom triggers overlay reposition\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — render loop calls overlay redraw\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire-connect/rename touches names\n- `issues/completed/208-port-literal-values.md` — the read-only-names\n  decision that this issue flips\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — variadic UI that\n  drove the inspector-crowding observation\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete (scope adjusted: name-edit moved, value-edit stays)\n\n## Scope adjustment\n\nThe value field stays in the inspector. Only the port-name editing\nmoved to the canvas overlay — the rest of issue 208's read-only-name\ndecision stays reversed (names are now editable), but the overlay\nimplementation only carries the name input. Values on the canvas\nwere the more disruptive half of the change and the user opted out;\nkeeping values in the inspector also keeps the variadic auto-grow\nflow exactly where it already lives.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nNew module `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` floats an editable\n`<input>` per input port next to its dot. Lifecycle:\n- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after\n  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is\n  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).\n- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears\n  down orphans.\n- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic\n  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user\n  typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.\n- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing\n  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite\n  cost is paid once per change.\n\nInspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n  unique within the box.\n- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port\n  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n  from 217).\n- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the\n  new name without the user having to re-click.\n\n`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —\nthe overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator\nslot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this\nissue.\n\nCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,\n`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent\nwith most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom).\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Variadic slot rename**: rename_port accepts `base_N`-shaped\n  names, so the user can technically rename a non-variadic port to\n  match a variadic-slot pattern. The variadic helpers detect the\n  shape on subsequent operations; if the user creates one by\n  accident the recovery is to rename it back.\n- **Renamed port had a wire**: the wire's `to_input` rewrites on\n  both endpoints; the canvas re-renders with the new label without\n  losing the connection.\n- **Typo'd a name to something the function doesn't expect**: this\n  is the intentional tradeoff from issue 208. The runtime error\n  surfaces clearly rather than silently skipping.",

      "content":"# 223 — Syntax highlighting in the source viewer via user-written lexers\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe source viewer (issue 215, complete) shows file content as plain\nmonospace text. Users add a new\nlanguage by writing a small JS file.\n\n### Lexer interface\n\nEach lexer is a JS module exporting a single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/lexer.js\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  // Returns an ordered array of tokens covering the entire input.\n  // Tokens must not overlap and together must cover [0, text.length).\n  return [\n    { type: 'keyword', start: 0,  end: 5  },\n    { type: 'plain',   start: 5,  end: 6  },\n    { type: 'string',  start: 6,  end: 17 },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nToken types are convention-only — the viewer applies a CSS class\nnamed `syntax-<type>` to each span. The standard set is:\n\n| type        | typical use                                        |\n|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `keyword`   | language keywords (`function`, `if`, `local`, …)   |\n| `comment`   | line and block comments                            |\n| `string`    | quoted strings, char literals, here-docs           |\n| `number`    | numeric literals                                   |\n| `operator`  | `+`, `-`, `==`, `=`, `:`, …                        |\n| `identifier`| variable / function names                          |\n| `plain`     | everything not classified                          |\n\nA lexer is free to introduce its own token types (`regex`,\n`annotation`, `decorator`, etc.) — the viewer just renders unknown\ntypes with a default `syntax-default` style.\n\n### File location\n\nLexers live next to the language they belong to. For shipped\nlanguages this is `langs/<name>/lexer.js`. The runner doesn't read\nthem — the editor server serves them as static JS files alongside\nthe `spec.c` and `spec.so` files used by the phase 3 runner.\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c          ← runtime spec (issue 306, phase 3)\n    lexer.js        ← editor lexer (this issue)\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/c/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    soramech-c.h\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/bash/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    bash-server.sh\n    Makefile\n```\n\nFor a language whose runtime spec hasn't been written (still in phase\n2), there's no `spec.c` yet — but the editor lexer can land first\nand live in `langs/<name>/lexer.js` waiting for the runtime work.\n\n### Loading\n\nThe source viewer determines a file's language by its extension and\nloads the corresponding lexer on demand. Dynamic ES module import\n(`import('/langs/lua/lexer.js')`) works in modern browsers and lets\nthe editor lazy-load only the lexers it needs.\n\nA small registry inside the viewer caches loaded lexers so each is\nfetched at most once per session:\n\n```\next_to_lang : { \".lua\": \"lua\", \".c\": \"c\", \".sh\": \"bash\", ... }\nloaded      : { \"lua\": <module>, \"bash\": <module>, ... }\n```\n\nFiles with an unknown extension or a missing lexer fall back to\nplain rendering — no error, just no highlighting.\n\n### CSS\n\nToken classes go in the existing `assets/index.html` `<style>` block\nalongside the other source-viewer styles. Default theme:\n\n```css\n.syntax-keyword    { color: #4a9eff; }\n.syntax-comment    { color: #6c72a0; font-style: italic; }\n.syntax-string     { color: #4caf7d; }\n.syntax-number     { color: #ff8c42; }\n.syntax-operator   { color: #c0c4dd; }\n.syntax-identifier { color: #e8eaf6; }\n.syntax-plain      { color: #9ea3c0; }\n.syntax-default    { color: #9ea3c0; }\n```\n\nThese match the existing editor color palette (the comparator\nbranch colors, the inspector accents, etc.) so highlighted code\nvisually belongs.\n\n### Reference lexer (Lua)\n\nThe Lua lexer ships in this issue and serves as the reference\nimplementation. Roughly:\n\n```js\nconst KEYWORDS = new Set([\n  'and','break','do','else','elseif','end','false','for','function',\n  'goto','if','in','local','nil','not','or','repeat','return','then',\n  'true','until','while',\n]);\n\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  const tokens = [];\n  let i = 0;\n  while (i < text.length) {\n    const c = text[i];\n    // ... small state machine for whitespace, comments (-- and --[[ ]]),\n    // strings (\"...\" '...' If we ever\n  add an \"edit in viewer\" mode (currently out of scope, see issue\n  215 open questions), the lexer needs to be cheap enough to run\n  on each keystroke. Hand-rolled lexers comfortably hit that bar.\n- Theme switching: keep the CSS in one place so a future\n  light-theme effort just swaps the color values. No theming\n  abstraction needed yet.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — viewer module that consumes\n  lexer output\n- `assets/index.html` — token-class CSS\n- `langs/lua/lexer.js`, `langs/bash/lexer.js`, `langs/c/lexer.js`\n  — shipped reference lexers (to be written)\n- `issues/215-view-box-source.md` (completed) — the source viewer\n  this builds on\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — runtime spec architecture\n  this mirrors\n- `docs/005-language-specs.md` — to be updated with the lexer\n  interface\n"
    }
  },

    "content":"// C syntax lexer for the source viewer (issue 223).\n//\n// Same shape as the Lua and Bash lexers: returns ordered, gap-free\n// {type, start, end} tokens covering the input. Skips preprocessor\n// nuance (treats #directive lines as a single span tagged keyword).\n\nconst KEYWORDS = new Set([\n  'auto','break','case','char','const','continue','default','do',\n  'double','else','enum','extern','float','for','goto','if','inline',\n  'int','long','register','restrict','return','short','signed',\n  'sizeof','static','struct','switch','typedef','union','unsigned',\n  'void','volatile','while','_Bool','_Complex','_Imaginary',\n  // C99/C11 stuff that shows up in headers\n  'bool','true','false','NULL',\n]);\n\n// {{{ tokenize\nexport function tokenize(text) {\n  const out = [];\n  let i = 0;\n  const N = text.length;\n\n  function push(type, start, end) {\n    if (end > start) out.push({ type, start, end });\n  }\n\n  while (i < N) {\n    const c = text[i];\n\n    // Whitespace\n    if (c === ' ' || c === '\\t' || c === '\\n' || c === '\\r') {\n      const start = i;\n      while (i < N && (text[i] === ' ' || text[i] === '\\t' ||\n                       text[i] === '\\n' || text[i] === '\\r')) i++;\n      push('plain', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Line comments: //\n    if (c === '/' && text[i + 1] === '/') {\n      const start = i;\n      while (i < N && text[i] !== '\\n') i++;\n      push('comment', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Block comments: /* ... */\n    if (c === '/' && text[i + 1] === '*') {\n      const start = i;\n      i += 2;\n      while (i < N && !(text[i] === '*' && text[i + 1] === '/')) i++;\n      if (i < N) i += 2;\n      push('comment', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Preprocessor: # to end of line (with backslash-continuation)\n    if (c === '#') {\n      const prev = i === 0 ? '\\n' : text[i - 1];\n      if (prev === '\\n' || i === 0 || prev === ' ' || prev === '\\t') {\n        const start = i;\n        while (i < N) {\n          if (text[i] === '\\n' && text[i - 1] !== '\\\\') { break; }\n          i++;\n        }\n        push('keyword', start, i);\n        continue;\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Strings and char literals: \"...\" or '...'\n    if (c === '\"' || c === \"'\") {\n      const quote = c;\n      const start = i;\n      i++;\n      while (i < N) {\n        if (text[i] === '\\\\' && i + 1 < N) { i += 2; continue; }\n        if (text[i] === quote) { i++; break; }\n        if (text[i] === '\\n') break;\n        i++;\n      }\n      push('string', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Numbers: 0x..., decimal, suffixes (UL etc.)\n    if ((c >= '0' && c <= '9') ||\n        (c === '.' && text[i + 1] >= '0' && text[i + 1] <= '9')) {\n      const start = i;\n      if (c === '0' && (text[i + 1] === 'x' || text[i + 1] === 'X')) {\n        i += 2;\n        while (i < N && /[0-9A-Fa-f]/.test(text[i])) i++;\n      } else {\n        while (i < N && text[i] >= '0' && text[i] <= '9') i++;\n        if (text[i] === '.') {\n          i++;\n          while (i < N && text[i] >= '0' && text[i] <= '9') i++;\n        }\n        if (text[i] === 'e' || text[i] === 'E') {\n          i++;\n          if (text[i] === '+' || text[i] === '-') i++;\n          while (i < N && text[i] >= '0' && text[i] <= '9') i++;\n        }\n      }\n      // suffixes: u, l, ul, ull, f, etc.\n      while (i < N && /[uUlLfF]/.test(text[i])) i++;\n      push('number', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Identifiers / keywords\n    if ((c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || c === '_') {\n      const start = i;\n      while (i < N && /\\w/.test(text[i])) i++;\n      const word = text.slice(start, i);\n      push(KEYWORDS.has(word) ? 'keyword' : 'identifier', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    // Operators / punctuation\n    if (/[=<>+\\-*\\/%!&|^~?:;,.(){}\\[\\]]/.test(c)) {\n      const start = i;\n      while (i < N && /[=<>+\\-*\\/%!&|^~?:;,.(){}\\[\\]]/.test(text[i])) i++;\n      push('operator', start, i);\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    push('plain', i, i + 1);\n    i++;\n  }\n\n  return out;\n}\n// }}}\n"

    "originalFile":"// Floating, draggable, resizable, scrollable read-only source viewer.\n//\n// open_source_view(ref, anchor_box?) creates an absolutely-positioned\n// window over the canvas showing the file's content. Multiple windows\n// can be open simultaneously; each is independently positioned and\n// closes only when its × button is clicked.\n//\n// The window is confined to the canvas's bounding box: drag and resize\n// operations clamp position and dimensions so the window can't leave\n// the canvas area.\n//\n// Default sizing (per issue 215):\n//   width  = (average line length + 3 chars) × monospace char width\n//   height = canvas height / 2\n\nconst SourceView = (() => {\n  // Track open windows so we can bring-to-front on click and so a future\n  // close-all (e.g. on map switch) can find them. Each entry is the\n  // outer DOM element.\n  const open_windows = [];\n  let z_top = 100;\n\n  // {{{ measure_char_w\n  // Measure the width of a single 12px-monospace character once at module\n  // load. Used for translating \"characters\" into pixels for default sizing.\n  // The measurement node is removed after use; no DOM clutter.\n  function measure_char_w() {\n    const probe = document.createElement('span');\n    probe.style.cssText =\n      'visibility:hidden;position:absolute;font:12px monospace;' +\n      'white-space:pre;left:-9999px;top:-9999px;';\n    probe.textContent = 'M'.repeat(50);\n    document.body.appendChild(probe);\n    const w = probe.getBoundingClientRect().width / 50;\n    probe.remove();\n    return w;\n  }\n  const CHAR_W = measure_char_w();\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ fetch_source\n  // Resolve a box's `ref` to file content. The ref is just a filename or a\n  // path relative to the map; we try the map's main src/ first (stripping\n  // a leading \"src/\" that older boxes sometimes carry), then walk through\n  // any extra source directories the server has registered. Throws if\n  // nothing matches.\n  async function fetch_source(ref) {\n    if (!ref) throw new Error('no ref set on this box');\n\n    const stripped = ref.replace(/^src\\//, '');\n\n    try { return await API.get_src_file(stripped); } catch (e) { /* fall through */ }\n\n    let extras = [];\n    try { extras = await API.list_extra_src(); } catch (e) {}\n    for (let i = 0; i < (extras || []).length; i++) {\n      try { return await API.get_extra_src_file(i, stripped); } catch (e) {}\n    }\n\n    throw new Error('source not found: ' + ref);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ canvas_rect\n  // Bounding box of the canvas in viewport coordinates. Used as the clamp\n  // region for the floating window.\n  function canvas_rect() {\n    return Canvas.el.getBoundingClientRect();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ default_size\n  // Returns the default { w, h } for a window showing the given source\n  // text. Width is the file's longest line clamped to [80, 120] chars —\n  // tiny files don't get pointlessly small windows, big files don't get\n  // pointlessly huge ones, and the user never sees horizontal scroll\n  // for content that already fits in 120 columns. Wires up the drag-from-header behavior and the\n  // close button. Returns the outer element; caller positions and sizes\n  // it.\n  function make_window(title, body_text) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'source-view-window';\n\n    const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n    hdr.className = 'source-view-header';\n\n    const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n    lbl.className   = 'source-view-title';\n    lbl.textContent = title;\n    hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n    const close_btn = document.createElement('button');\n    close_btn.className   = 'source-view-close';\n    close_btn.textContent = '×';\n    close_btn.title       = 'close';\n    close_btn.onclick     = () => {\n      const i = open_windows.indexOf(wrap);\n      if (i >= 0) open_windows.splice(i, 1);\n      wrap.remove();\n    };\n    hdr.appendChild(close_btn);\n\n    wrap.appendChild(hdr);\n\n    const body = document.createElement('pre');\n    body.className   = 'source-view-body';\n    body.textContent = body_text;\n    wrap.appendChild(body);\n\n    // Drag-from-header: anchor at mousedown, every mousemove computes\n    // from the anchor to avoid accumulating error over a long drag.\n    let drag_anchor_mouse = null;\n    let drag_anchor_pos   = null;\n\n    hdr.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n      // Don't start a drag from the close button.\n      if (e.target === close_btn) return;\n      drag_anchor_mouse = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY };\n      const r = wrap.getBoundingClientRect();\n      drag_anchor_pos   = { left: r.left, top: r.top };\n      bring_to_front(wrap);\n      e.preventDefault();\n    });\n\n    window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n      if (!drag_anchor_mouse) return;\n      const cand_left = drag_anchor_pos.left + (e.clientX -
