Fetches the source for `ref` and opens a floating\n  // window. If `anchor_box` is given, the window is centered over that\n  // box's screen position; otherwise it's centered on the canvas.\n  async function open_source_view(ref, anchor_box) {\n    let text;\n    try {\n      text = await fetch_source(ref);\n    } catch (e) {\n      status_msg('view source: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const win  = make_window(ref, text);\n    const size = default_size(text);\n\n    document.body.appendChild(win);\n    win.style.width  = size.w + 'px';\n    win.style.height = size.h + 'px';\n\n    // Default position: centered over anchor_box (if provided) or canvas.\n    const cr = canvas_rect();\n    let cand_left, cand_top;\n    if (anchor_box && anchor_box.ui) {\n      const s = Canvas.world_to_screen(anchor_box.ui.x + Boxes.BOX_W / 2,\n                                       anchor_box.ui.y + Boxes.box_height(anchor_box) / 2);\n      cand_left = cr.left + s.x - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + s.y - size.h / 2;\n    } else {\n      cand_left = cr.left + cr.width  / 2 - size.w / 2;\n      cand_top  = cr.top  + cr.height / 2 - size.h / 2;\n    }\n    const clamped = clamp_position(cand_left, cand_top, size.w, size.h);\n    win.style.left = clamped.left + 'px';\n    win.style.top  = clamped.top  + 'px';\n\n    bring_to_front(win);\n    open_windows.push(win);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { open_source_view };\n})();\n",

        "input":{
          "new_string":"## Editor lexer (`langs/<name>/lexer.js`)\n\nIndependent of the runtime spec, each language carries an editor\nlexer that the source viewer (issue 215) uses to syntax-highlight\nfile content. The lexer ships in the same `langs/<name>/` directory\nas the runtime spec — co-located by language, not by concern.\n\n### Contract\n\nA lexer is an ES module that exports a single function:\n\n```js\nexport function tokenize(text) {\n  return [\n    { type: 'keyword', start: 0,  end: 5 },\n    { type: 'plain',   start: 5,  end: 6 },\n    { type: 'string',  start: 6,  end: 17 },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nThe returned tokens must be ordered, gap-free, and cover the entire\ninput. Each token's `type` is a free-form string; the viewer applies\na CSS class `syntax-<type>`. The standard set is:\n\n| type        | typical use                                      |\n|-------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `keyword`   | language keywords                                |\n| `comment`   | line and block comments                          |\n| `string`    | quoted strings, char literals, here-docs         |\n| `number`    | numeric literals                                 |\n| `operator`  | `+`, `-`, `==`, `=`, `:`, …                      |\n| `identifier`| variable / function names                        |\n| `plain`     | whitespace and unclassified runs                 |\n\nUnknown types fall back to `syntax-default`. Lexers are free to\nintroduce custom types (`regex`, `annotation`, `decorator`); the\nviewer just renders them with the default style unless someone adds\nmatching CSS.\n\n### Loading\n\nThe viewer maps a file's extension to a language name (e.g.\n`.lua` → `lua`, `.sh` → `bash`, `.c` / `.h` → `c`) and dynamically\nimports `/langs/<name>/lexer.js` on first use. Result is cached for\nthe rest of the session. Files with an unknown extension or a\nmissing lexer fall back to plain rendering.\n\n### Reference implementations\n\n- `langs/lua/lexer.js` — hand-rolled state machine, ~150 lines.\n  Covers `--` and `--[[ ]]` comments, single/double/long-bracket\n  strings, hex / decimal / exponent numbers, identifiers,\n  multi-char operators.\n- `langs/bash/lexer.js` — same shape, with `$var` / `${...}` /\n  `$(...)` expansions tagged as identifiers and `#` line comments\n  detected only at line-start or after whitespace (not mid-token).\n- `langs/c/lexer.js` — `//` line and `/* */` block comments,\n  `#directive` lines tagged as keyword spans, hex and float\n  literals with C suffix support.\n\nThe reference lexers are starting points — extend or replace as\nneeded for languages with subtler syntax (regex literals, nested\ntemplate strings, indentation-sensitive parsing).\n\n## Why a stub now",

    "originalFile":"# 223 — Syntax highlighting in the source viewer via user-written lexers\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe source viewer (issue 215, complete) shows file content as plain\nmonospace text. Every box source — Lua, C, Bash, anything else —\nrenders the same: white text on dark background, no syntax cues.\nReading a function in the editor is harder than it should be.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nEach language has its own small JavaScript lexer that turns raw text\ninto a list of typed tokens. The source viewer asks the lexer for the\nfile's tokens, then wraps each token in a span with a CSS class per\ntoken type. Styling is done purely in CSS, so themes are independent\nof lexers.\n\nThis mirrors the runtime language-spec architecture (issue 303):\neach language is responsible for its own concerns, the editor /\nrunner only knows how to call into a shared interface. No\nSoraMech-internal language list, no transpiling. Users add a new\nlanguage by writing a small JS file.\n\n### Lexer interface\n\nEach lexer is a JS module exporting a single function:\n\n```js\n// langs/<name>/lexer.js\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  // Returns an ordered array of tokens covering the entire input.\n  // Tokens must not overlap and together must cover [0, text.length).\n  return [\n    { type: 'keyword', start: 0,  end: 5  },\n    { type: 'plain',   start: 5,  end: 6  },\n    { type: 'string',  start: 6,  end: 17 },\n    // ...\n  ];\n}\n```\n\nToken types are convention-only — the viewer applies a CSS class\nnamed `syntax-<type>` to each span. The standard set is:\n\n| type        | typical use                                        |\n|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|\n| `keyword`   | language keywords (`function`, `if`, `local`, …)   |\n| `comment`   | line and block comments                            |\n| `string`    | quoted strings, char literals, here-docs           |\n| `number`    | numeric literals                                   |\n| `operator`  | `+`, `-`, `==`, `=`, `:`, …                        |\n| `identifier`| variable / function names                          |\n| `plain`     | everything not classified                          |\n\nA lexer is free to introduce its own token types (`regex`,\n`annotation`, `decorator`, etc.) — the viewer just renders unknown\ntypes with a default `syntax-default` style.\n\n### File location\n\nLexers live next to the language they belong to. For shipped\nlanguages this is `langs/<name>/lexer.js`. The runner doesn't read\nthem — the editor server serves them as static JS files alongside\nthe `spec.c` and `spec.so` files used by the phase 3 runner.\n\n```\nlangs/lua/\n    spec.c          ← runtime spec (issue 306, phase 3)\n    lexer.js        ← editor lexer (this issue)\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/c/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    soramech-c.h\n    Makefile\n\nlangs/bash/\n    spec.c\n    lexer.js\n    bash-server.sh\n    Makefile\n```\n\nFor a language whose runtime spec hasn't been written (still in phase\n2), there's no `spec.c` yet — but the editor lexer can land first\nand live in `langs/<name>/lexer.js` waiting for the runtime work.\n\n### Loading\n\nThe source viewer determines a file's language by its extension and\nloads the corresponding lexer on demand. Dynamic ES module import\n(`import('/langs/lua/lexer.js')`) works in modern browsers and lets\nthe editor lazy-load only the lexers it needs.\n\nA small registry inside the viewer caches loaded lexers so each is\nfetched at most once per session:\n\n```\next_to_lang : { \".lua\": \"lua\", \".c\": \"c\", \".sh\": \"bash\", ... }\nloaded      : { \"lua\": <module>, \"bash\": <module>, ... }\n```\n\nFiles with an unknown extension or a missing lexer fall back to\nplain rendering — no error, just no highlighting.\n\n### CSS\n\nToken classes go in the existing `assets/index.html` `<style>` block\nalongside the other source-viewer styles. Default theme:\n\n```css\n.syntax-keyword    { color: #4a9eff; }\n.syntax-comment    { color: #6c72a0; font-style: italic; }\n.syntax-string     { color: #4caf7d; }\n.syntax-number     { color: #ff8c42; }\n.syntax-operator   { color: #c0c4dd; }\n.syntax-identifier { color: #e8eaf6; }\n.syntax-plain      { color: #9ea3c0; }\n.syntax-default    { color: #9ea3c0; }\n```\n\nThese match the existing editor color palette (the comparator\nbranch colors, the inspector accents, etc.) so highlighted code\nvisually belongs.\n\n### Reference lexer (Lua)\n\nThe Lua lexer ships in this issue and serves as the reference\nimplementation. Roughly:\n\n```js\nconst KEYWORDS = new Set([\n  'and','break','do','else','elseif','end','false','for','function',\n  'goto','if','in','local','nil','not','or','repeat','return','then',\n  'true','until','while',\n]);\n\nfunction tokenize(text) {\n  const tokens = [];\n  let i = 0;\n  while (i < text.length) {\n    const c = text[i];\n    // ... small state machine for whitespace, comments (-- and --[[ ]]),\n    // strings (\"...\" '...' [[...]]), numbers, identifiers, operators\n    // ...\n  }\n  return tokens;\n}\n\nexport { tokenize };\n```\n\nHand-rolled, ~150 lines. Bash and C lexers come along once the Lua\none is settled.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Add token-class CSS to `assets/index.html`.\n2. Modify `008-source-view.js` to consult a lexer registry by file\n   extension when rendering text. Plain rendering remains the\n   fallback.\n3. Write `langs/lua/lexer.js` — reference implementation. Smoke\n   test: open a Lua source in the viewer, confirm the colors look\n   sensible.\n4. Add a lazy-loader: `import('/langs/<name>/lexer.js')` on first\n   need, cached.\n5. Server-side (`src/006-server-main.lua`): make sure the\n   `langs/<dir>/<file>` static-serve path is exposed. May already\n   be implicit if the server has a generic static-file handler.\n6. Write `langs/bash/lexer.js`.\n7. Write `langs/c/lexer.js`.\n8. Document the lexer interface in `docs/005-language-specs.md`\n   (currently a stub) so users know how to add their own.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- Should the viewer re-tokenize on every render, or memoize per\n  file content? Files in the viewer don't change between open and\n  close (read-only), so caching the token list per `(ref, content\n  hash)` is trivial and worth doing if a file is large.\n- Live editing: this issue assumes read-only viewing. If we ever\n  add an \"edit in viewer\" mode (currently out of scope, see issue\n  215 open questions), the lexer needs to be cheap enough to run\n  on each keystroke. Hand-rolled lexers comfortably hit that bar.\n- Theme switching: keep the CSS in one place so a future\n  light-theme effort just swaps the color values. No theming\n  abstraction needed yet.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/008-source-view.js` — viewer module that consumes\n  lexer output\n- `assets/index.html` — token-class CSS\n- `langs/lua/lexer.js`, `langs/bash/lexer.js`, `langs/c/lexer.js`\n  — shipped reference lexers (to be written)\n- `issues/215-view-box-source.md` (completed) — the source viewer\n  this builds on\n- `issues/303-language-runtime-spec.md` — runtime spec architecture\n  this mirrors\n- `docs/005-language-specs.md` — to be updated with the lexer\n  interface\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nThree reference lexers shipped under `langs/<name>/lexer.js` —\n`lua`, `bash`, and `c`. Each is a hand-rolled state machine\nexporting a single `tokenize(text)` function per the spec.\n\nServer-side: `src/005-http-server.lua` adds `/langs/<...>` to the\nstatic-serve route so the editor can `import()` the lexer modules.\nThe path traversal block from the existing static handler still\napplies.\n\nClient-side: `assets/js/008-source-view.js` gained a small lexer\nregistry (extension → language → cached module). When opening a\nviewer, the body is set to plain text first as a guaranteed-correct\nbaseline; if a lexer is available for the file's extension it\nre-renders the body asynchronously into syntax-highlighted spans.\nPlain rendering is the fallback for any failure (missing lexer,\nextension not in the map, lexer throw).\n\nCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.syntax-keyword`,\n`.syntax-comment`, `.syntax-string`, `.syntax-number`,\n`.syntax-operator`, `.syntax-identifier`, `.syntax-plain`,\n`.syntax-default` — colors echo the editor's accent palette.\n\n`docs/005-language-specs.md` documents the lexer interface (token\nshape, type conventions, file location, loading model, reference\nimplementations) so users can add lexers for languages that don't\nship by default.\n\n### Memoization deferred\n\nThe open question about caching tokens per-(ref, content-hash) was\nleft for later — re-tokenizing on every viewer open is fast enough\nin practice (the lexers are linear-time, no regex backtracking).\nWorth revisiting if someone opens a 10k-line file and feels lag.",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

## [3344]

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T22:57:12.467Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"Something I noticed is the font size on the input box labels doesn't scale when you zoom in and out.\n\nWhen I remove a variadic input port, it renames the other fields no matter what. The index counter is renaming them when it shouldn't.\n\nAlso, sometimes the variadic input ports aren't auto-growing.\n\nAlso, I tried disabling variadic mode, but some ports that had wires aren't being removed. The first one correctly removed, but subsequent ones didn't. Are they trying to remove them by name maybe?\n\nsyntax highlighting works great. One question - when the user edits a file in their own editor, does our editor pick it up? How would they trigger a refresh, if it doesn't do it automatically? Does it matter? Could we trigger it when they click \"view\"? Does it matter, because the point of the editor is to create the program, not to actually run it, so anytime they go to actually run it, we'd recompile (if a compiled language) or interpret the script dynamically. So it wouldn't matter, right? Except for the view button? So that's when we'd refresh, right?\n\nSo, call type boxes I understand. But data type boxes I'm still a little iffy on - they're basically, \"read a file and output the data\" right? I don't want to encourage global variables so we shouldn't allow users to read one with a data box. A while back I heard that the reason we don't read data files with the... data box... is because different languages have different semantics for how they store strings and such. But, if we're just reading text, wouldn't we pass it between boxes the same as any other string we're passing along? If it's just a text file, it makes sense to just read it and output the value. But if it's json, it also makes sense to parse it. Does that kind of parsing make sense? Or should we just, load the file and let some later function parse it? Either way, can you explain the intended functionality of the data boxes, if what I'm describing isn't what they're originally designed for, because I definitely don't understand them currently.\n\nAlso, if we're editing the input port names on the box, it doesn't make sense to display them in the inspector as well. Can we... just... display them in the inspector, but move the value input field below the name / variadic toggle? Then leave the box as kinda immutable in that respect. It doesn't really work ergonomically... Users might enter text entry mode when they're trying to move the box around. Not ideal.",
    "role":"user"
  },

    "originalFile":"// Box rendering, layout, and hit testing.\n// Each box knows its world-space position; the camera transform is applied by the canvas.\n\nconst Boxes = (() => {\n  const BOX_W         = 180;\n  const BOX_HEADER    = 36;\n  const PORT_ROW_H    = 22;\n  const PORT_R        = 6;   // port dot radius in world units\n  const MIN_BOX_H     = 80;\n\n  const KIND_COLOR = { call: '#4a9eff', data: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // Comparator branch colors: lt=orange, eq=blue, gt=green\n  const BRANCH_COLOR = { lt: '#ff8c42', eq: '#4a9eff', gt: '#4caf7d' };\n\n  // boxes: { [id]: box_data }\n  let boxes = {};\n\n  // {{{ box_height\n  function box_height(box) {\n    const n_in  = (box.inputs || []).length;\n    // Output rows: iterator boxes have N named slots (issue 221);\n    // comparator active: 3 dots (lt/eq/gt); sink: 0; otherwise 1.\n    let n_out;\n    if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      n_out = box.iterator_outputs.length;\n    } else if (box.has_output === false) {\n      n_out = 0;\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      n_out = 3;\n    } else {\n      n_out = 1;\n    }\n    return Math.max(MIN_BOX_H, BOX_HEADER + Math.max(n_in, n_out) * PORT_ROW_H + 8);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ port_positions\n  // Returns world-space {x,y} for each port dot on a box.\n  // Output side: null-named single dot when no comparand; 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' dots when comparand set.\n  function port_positions(box) {\n    const bx = box.ui?.x ?? 0;\n    const by = box.ui?.y ?? 0;\n    const h  = box_height(box);\n    const inputs = box.inputs || [];\n\n    const in_pts = inputs.map((p, i) => ({\n      name: p.name, side: 'input',\n      x: bx,\n      y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n    }));\n\n    let out_pts;\n    if (box.has_output === false) {\n      // sink box — function has no return values (issue 226). No output\n      // port, no wire-grab target, nothing for the inspector to render.\n      out_pts = [];\n    } else if (box.iterator_outputs) {\n      // iterator box (issue 221) — N named output dots stacked down\n      // the right edge, one per declared slot. Slot names land in the\n      // `name` field, so the wire's `from_branch` will pick them up\n      // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n      out_pts = box.iterator_outputs.map((slot, i) => ({\n        name: slot, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else if (box.comparand && box.comparand !== '') {\n      // three comparator dots\n      out_pts = ['lt', 'eq', 'gt'].map((branch, i) => ({\n        name: branch, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + BOX_HEADER + PORT_ROW_H * i + PORT_ROW_H / 2,\n      }));\n    } else {\n      // single output dot, vertically centered in the box\n      out_pts = [{\n        name: null, side: 'output',\n        x: bx + BOX_W,\n        y: by + h / 2,\n      }];\n    }\n\n    return { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_box\n  function draw_box(ctx, box, selected) {\n    const x = box.ui?.x ?? color : '#3a3f55';\n    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || box.id, x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    // Input port labels are rendered as DOM overlays now (issue 224)\n    // so the user can edit them inline. 0, y = b.ui?.y ?? 0;\n      if (wx >= x && wx <= x + BOX_W && wy >= y && wy <= y + box_height(b)) return id;\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ get_port_world_pos\n  function get_port_world_pos(box_id, port_name, side) {\n    const box = boxes[box_id];\n    if (!box) return null;\n    const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(box);\n    const list = side === 'input' ?     "oldString":"  // {{{ mk_port_display\n  // Renders input ports with their variadic toggle / remove buttons.\n  // Port names and literal values now live on the canvas as DOM\n  // overlays (issue 224); the inspector keeps only the controls\n  // that don't fit cleanly next to a port dot.\n  function mk_port_display(ports) {\n    const wrap = document.createElement('div');\n    wrap.className = 'port-display';\n    if (!ports || ports.length === 0) {\n      const empty = document.createElement('span');\n      empty.className   = 'port-display-empty';\n      empty.textContent = '(none)';\n      wrap.appendChild(empty);\n    } else {\n      ports.forEach((p, i) => {\n        const row = document.createElement('div');\n        row.className = 'port-display-row';\n\n        // Variadic context for this port (issue 217 part B):\n        //   in_var_group = is part of a variadic group (one of multiple slots)\n        //   pv           = { base, index } parsed from the slot name\n        //   group_last   = the last index in the group (so we know whether\n        //                  to render the \"+\" button on this row)\n        const pv           = current_box ? String(p.value) : '';\n        val_inp.placeholder = 'value…';\n        val_inp.className   = 'port-val-inp';\n        val_inp.addEventListener('input', async () => {\n          const new_val = val_inp.value === '' ? undefined : val_inp.value;\n          ports[i].value = new_val;\n\n          // a literal value and an incoming wire are contradictory — sever any wires\n          // feeding this port so only one source of truth exists\n          if (new_val !== undefined && current_box) {\n            const port_name = ports[i].name;\n            const box_id    = current_box.id;\n            const to_break  = (current_box.connections || []).filter(\n              c => c.to_box === box_id && c.to_input === port_name\n            );\n            if (to_break.length > 0) {\n              // remove from local box first so save() persists the clean state\n              current_box.connections = current_box.connections.filter(\n                c => !(c.to_box === box_id && c.to_input === port_name)\n              );\n              // remove from each source box (mutate cached object in place)\n              await Promise.all(to_break.map(async conn => {\n                const src = Boxes.boxes[conn.from_box];\n                if (!src) return;\n                const before = src.connections || [];\n                src.connections = before.filter(c =>\n                  !(c.from_box === conn.from_box &&\n                    (c.from_branch ?? null) === (conn.from_branch ?? null) &&\n                    c.to_box    === conn.to_box &&\n                    c.to_input  === conn.to_input)\n                );\n                try {\n                  await API.put_box(conn.from_box, src);\n                } catch (e2) {\n                  src.connections = before;\n                  console.error('failed to sever wire from ' + conn.from_box + ':', e2.message);\n                }\n              }));\n              Canvas.mark_dirty();\n              status_msg('severed ' + to_break.length + ' wire(s) into port \"' + port_name + '\"');\n            }\n          }\n\n          // Auto-grow the variadic group when a value lands on its last\n          // slot.     "replaceAll":false,
    "oldString":"  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Higher slots in the\n  // same group rename down by one. Connections targeting the removed\n  // slot are dropped; connections targeting renamed slots get their\n  // to_input rewritten on both endpoints.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Drop the slot.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n\n    // Rename higher slots down by one.\n    const renames = [];  // [{ old: 'text_3', new: 'text_2' }, ...]\n    current_box.inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const ppv = parse_variadic_name(p.name);\n      if (ppv && ppv.base === pv.base && ppv.index > pv.index) {\n        const new_name = pv.base + '_' + (ppv.index - 1);\n        renames.push({ old: p.name, new: new_name });\n        current_box.inputs[i].name = new_name;\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Drop connections to the removed slot. Renames go in ascending\n    // order so we never collide with an existing slot's name (we just\n    // freed it up by the previous rename).\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n    renames.sort((a, b) => parse_variadic_name(a.old).index - parse_variadic_name(b.old).index);\n    for (const r of renames) {\n      await update_target_connections([r.old], c => ({ ...c, to_input: r.new }));\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
    "newString":"  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Other slots keep\n  // their existing names — we used to compact `text_2`, `text_3`,\n  // ... down to `text_1`, `text_2`, ... after removing `text_1`,\n  // but that clobbered any user-renamed downstream slot's wiring\n  // and produced surprising sidebar updates. The variadic helpers\n  // tolerate gaps in the index sequence (auto-grow uses the highest\n  // existing index + 1), so leaving holes is harmless.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
    "userModified":false
  },

        "type":"tool_use",
        "name":"Edit",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "new_string":"  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Other slots keep\n  // their existing names — we used to compact `text_2`, `text_3`,\n  // ... down to `text_1`, `text_2`, ... after removing `text_1`,\n  // but that clobbered any user-renamed downstream slot's wiring\n  // and produced surprising sidebar updates. The variadic helpers\n  // tolerate gaps in the index sequence (auto-grow uses the highest\n  // existing index + 1), so leaving holes is harmless.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"  // Remove a single variadic slot at `slot_name`. Higher slots in the\n  // same group rename down by one. Connections targeting the removed\n  // slot are dropped; connections targeting renamed slots get their\n  // to_input rewritten on both endpoints.\n  async function remove_variadic_slot(slot_name) {\n    const pv = parse_variadic_name(slot_name);\n    if (!pv) return;\n\n    // The first slot is permanent — un-variadic instead if you want\n    // to remove it entirely.\n    if (pv.index === 0) {\n      status_msg('cannot remove slot 0 — toggle variadic off instead', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // Drop the slot.\n    current_box.inputs = current_box.inputs.filter(p => p.name !== slot_name);\n\n    // Rename higher slots down by one.\n    const renames = [];  // [{ old: 'text_3', new: 'text_2' }, ...]\n    current_box.inputs.forEach((p, i) => {\n      const ppv = parse_variadic_name(p.name);\n      if (ppv && ppv.base === pv.base && ppv.index > pv.index) {\n        const new_name = pv.base + '_' + (ppv.index - 1);\n        renames.push({ old: p.name, new: new_name });\n        current_box.inputs[i].name = new_name;\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Drop connections to the removed slot. Renames go in ascending\n    // order so we never collide with an existing slot's name (we just\n    // freed it up by the previous rename).\n    await update_target_connections([slot_name], () => null);\n    renames.sort((a, b) => parse_variadic_name(a.old).index - parse_variadic_name(b.old).index);\n    for (const r of renames) {\n      await update_target_connections([r.old], c => ({ ...c, to_input: r.new }));\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }"
        },
        "id":"toolu_014vHVvQNoVLSpHrg634QSw3"
      }]

    "newString":"  async function unmake_variadic(base) {\n    const slots = variadic_slots_for(current_box, base);\n    if (slots.length === 0) return;\n\n    // 1. Lifecycle:\n20\t- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after\n21\t  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is\n22\t  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).\n23\t- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears\n24\t  down orphans.\n25\t- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic\n26\t  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user\n27\t  typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n28\t- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.\n29\t- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing\n30\t  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite\n31\t  cost is paid once per change.\n32\t\n33\tInspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n34\t- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n35\t  unique within the box.\n36\t- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port\n37\t  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n38\t  from 217).\n39\t- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n40\t  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the\n41\t  new name without the user having to re-click.\n42\t\n43\t`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —\n44\tthe overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator\n45\tslot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this\n46\tissue.\n47\t\n48\tCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,\n49\t`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent\n50\twith most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom).",

      "content":"# 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing\n\n## Status\ncomplete (scope adjusted: name-edit moved, value-edit stays)\n\n## Scope adjustment\n\nThe value field stays in the inspector. Only the port-name editing\nmoved to the canvas overlay — the rest of issue 208's read-only-name\ndecision stays reversed (names are now editable), but the overlay\nimplementation only carries the name input. Values on the canvas\nwere the more disruptive half of the change and the user opted out;\nkeeping values in the inspector also keeps the variadic auto-grow\nflow exactly where it already lives.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nNew module `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` floats an editable\n`<input>` per input port next to its dot. Lifecycle:\n- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after\n  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is\n  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).\n- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears\n  down orphans.\n- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic\n  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user\n  typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.\n- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing\n  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite\n  cost is paid once per change.\n\nInspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n  unique within the box.\n- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port\n  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n  from 217).\n- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the\n  new name without the user having to re-click.\n\n`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —\nthe overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator\nslot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this\nissue.\n\nCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,\n`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent\nwith most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom)."

    "originalFile":"# 224 — Editable port names and canvas-side value editing\n\n## Status\ncomplete (scope adjusted: name-edit moved, value-edit stays)\n\n## Scope adjustment\n\nThe value field stays in the inspector. Only the port-name editing\nmoved to the canvas overlay — the rest of issue 208's read-only-name\ndecision stays reversed (names are now editable), but the overlay\nimplementation only carries the name input. Values on the canvas\nwere the more disruptive half of the change and the user opted out;\nkeeping values in the inspector also keeps the variadic auto-grow\nflow exactly where it already lives.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nNew module `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` floats an editable\n`<input>` per input port next to its dot. Lifecycle:\n- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after\n  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is\n  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).\n- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears\n  down orphans.\n- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic\n  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user\n  typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.\n- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing\n  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite\n  cost is paid once per change.\n\nInspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n  unique within the box.\n- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port\n  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n  from 217).\n- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the\n  new name without the user having to re-click.\n\n`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —\nthe overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator\nslot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this\nissue.\n\nCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,\n`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent\nwith most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom).\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Variadic slot rename**: rename_port accepts `base_N`-shaped\n  names, so the user can technically rename a non-variadic port to\n  match a variadic-slot pattern. The variadic helpers detect the\n  shape on subsequent operations; if the user creates one by\n  accident the recovery is to rename it back.\n- **Renamed port had a wire**: the wire's `to_input` rewrites on\n  both endpoints; the canvas re-renders with the new label without\n  losing the connection.\n- **Typo'd a name to something the function doesn't expect**: this\n  is the intentional tradeoff from issue 208. The runtime error\n  surfaces clearly rather than silently skipping.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nInput port names are read-only labels in the inspector — derived from\nthe function's parameter names when the file browser populates the\nbox (issue 207, 208). Each port row in the inspector also carries a\nliteral value input. With variadic inputs (issue 217), a box with\nseveral slots produces a tall, narrow list of name+type+value rows\nthat crowds the sidebar.\n\nThe canvas already renders port names next to their dots, so the\nname appears twice — once on the canvas (read-only label) and once\nin the inspector (read-only label).\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nMove both the port name and the literal value input out of the\ninspector and onto the canvas next to the port dot. The inspector\nkeeps only the variadic toggle / remove-slot buttons and any\nnon-port box-level fields (ref / fn / comparator).\n\n### Why\n\n- The inspector is crowded with redundant data (the canvas already\n  shows port names).\n- Literal values often need more horizontal room than a 72px input\n  field allows, especially for prompts, paths, or JSON snippets.\n- Reading the box's full configuration without clicking through the\n  inspector becomes possible — every input's name and value is\n  visible directly on the canvas.\n- 208's \"read-only port names\" decision was about preventing typo\n  drift between source code and box JSON; the file browser still\n  populates names from the parsed signature, but the user should be\n  free to override them after the fact.\n\n### Reverses 208's read-only-name decision\n\nIssue 208 made input port names non-editable on the principle that\nthey should match the parsed function signature exactly. This issue\nflips that — names become editable again, with the trade-off that a\ntypo can desynchronize the editor's record from the function the box\ncalls. The cost is a per-box runtime error rather than a hidden\nsilent skip, so it surfaces clearly. The benefit is that users can\nrename inputs freely (renaming a Lua function's parameter and then\nupdating the box does not require re-browsing).\n\n### Layout\n\nEach input port row on the canvas becomes:\n\n```\n●  text_0    ┌──────────────────┐\n             │ \"hello world\"    │\n             └──────────────────┘\n```\n\n- The port dot stays on the box's left edge (unchanged).\n- The port name is an editable text field, rendered as an HTML\n  overlay positioned next to the dot. Pan and zoom adjust the\n  overlay's transform to match the canvas.\n- The literal value field is another HTML overlay below or to the\n  right of the name.\n\n### HTML overlays over the canvas\n\nCanvas 2D doesn't do native text inputs, so the editable fields are\nDOM `<input>` elements absolutely positioned over the canvas. A\nsmall per-box overlay container holds them, transforms with the\ncamera (CSS transform applied on every render frame), and updates\nthe underlying `box.inputs[i]` on input.\n\nThis is the same pattern as the source viewer (issue 215) — DOM\nelements layered over the canvas, with positions computed from\n`Canvas.world_to_screen`. The complexity is keeping overlay state\nin sync with the canvas: they need to be created when a box is\nloaded, destroyed when a box is deleted, repositioned every frame\n(or when pan/zoom changes), and hidden when off-screen.\n\n### Inspector becomes lighter\n\nAfter this change the inspector shows:\n- Box label (editable)\n- ref / fn (with browse / view buttons)\n- For each input: the variadic toggle (`var` / `var ×` / `×`) only.\n  No name field, no value field — those live on the canvas.\n- Output: the comparator toggle and comparand input (unchanged).\n- Delete-box button (unchanged).\n\nRoughly half the height the current inspector takes for variadic\nboxes.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Overlay performance**: dozens of overlays multiplied by frequent\n  pan/zoom updates is a real cost. Tests are needed; a bounding-box\n  cull (only render overlays for visible boxes) is the obvious\n  optimization if it matters.\n- **Value-input width**: the field grows with the input's content, or\n  is a fixed width with horizontal scroll? Probably grow-on-content\n  with a max width clamp, similar to what monospace text does.\n- **Editing port names while wires are connected**: renaming a port\n  while a wire is attached should rename the wire's `to_input` /\n  `from_branch` on both endpoints atomically — same bilateral-update\n  pattern the variadic ops use.\n- **Name validation**: what's a valid port name? Probably `[A-Za-z_][\\w]*`\n  (a Lua / C / shell-compatible identifier). Reject names that start\n  with digits, contain spaces, etc. Reject duplicates within a box.\n- **Backward compat**: existing maps with the current layout work as\n  before — no migration needed. The change is purely UI.\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. Create `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` (new module) responsible\n   for per-box DOM overlays. Public API: `update_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   to create / refresh overlays for a box, `remove_overlays_for(box_id)`\n   on box deletion, `redraw_overlays()` on pan/zoom.\n2. Wire the overlays into the render loop: after `Boxes.draw_all`,\n   call `redraw_overlays()` to reposition the overlays for the\n   current camera. The overlays themselves don't redraw — only their\n   `style.left` / `style.top` / `style.transform` updates.\n3. Remove the name + value rendering from `mk_port_display` in\n   `004-inspector.js`. Leave only the variadic controls.\n4. Remove the canvas-side port name labels from `002-boxes.js::draw_box`\n   (the overlay's editable input replaces it).\n5. Wire validation: name must be a valid identifier and unique\n   within the box's `inputs`. Validate in the input's `oninput`\n   handler; revert to the previous valid name on rejection.\n6. Test against `maps/hello`, `maps/classify-demo`, and a fresh map\n   with variadic inputs (e.g. via `libs/text.lua`'s concat).\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` — new module (to be created)\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — port name labels move out\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — `mk_port_display` simplified\n- `assets/js/001-canvas.js` — pan/zoom triggers overlay reposition\n- `assets/js/005-app.js` — render loop calls overlay redraw\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — wire-connect/rename touches names\n- `issues/completed/208-port-literal-values.md` — the read-only-names\n  decision that this issue flips\n- `issues/217-concat-box-and-dynamic-inputs.md` — variadic UI that\n  drove the inspector-crowding observation\n",
    "oldString":"## Status\ncomplete (scope adjusted: name-edit moved, value-edit stays)\n\n## Scope adjustment\n\nThe value field stays in the inspector. Only the port-name editing\nmoved to the canvas overlay — the rest of issue 208's read-only-name\ndecision stays reversed (names are now editable), but the overlay\nimplementation only carries the name input. Values on the canvas\nwere the more disruptive half of the change and the user opted out;\nkeeping values in the inspector also keeps the variadic auto-grow\nflow exactly where it already lives.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\nNew module `assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` floats an editable\n`<input>` per input port next to its dot. Lifecycle:\n- `Overlays.redraw()` runs in the main render loop after\n  `Boxes.draw_all`, gated by `Canvas.start_frame()` so the cost is\n  tied to actual canvas changes (camera, drag, create/delete).\n- Reconciles overlays with `Boxes.boxes` — creates new ones, tears\n  down orphans.\n- Per-port rows rebuild when port count changes (variadic\n  add/remove); otherwise the `<input>` elements persist so user\n  typing isn't clobbered between frames.\n- Updates skip any input that currently has focus.\n- Each input commits on blur or Enter (Escape reverts). Typing\n  doesn't fire the rename — only commit does — so the wire-rewrite\n  cost is paid once per change.\n\nInspector exposes `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n  unique within the box.\n- On rename, rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port\n  (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n  from 217).\n- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n  display, so the read-only name label in the sidebar tracks the\n  new name without the user having to re-click.\n\n`002-boxes.js::draw_box` no longer renders input port name text —\nthe overlay does. Output port labels (comparator branches, iterator\nslot names) still draw on the canvas; those aren't covered by this\nissue.\n\nCSS additions in `assets/index.html`: `.box-overlay-row`,\n`.box-overlay-name` — overlays don't scale with zoom (consistent\nwith most node editors so labels stay legible at any zoom).\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Variadic slot rename**: rename_port accepts `base_N`-shaped\n  names, so the user can technically rename a non-variadic port to\n  match a variadic-slot pattern. The variadic helpers detect the\n  shape on subsequent operations; if the user creates one by\n  accident the recovery is to rename it back.\n- **Renamed port had a wire**: the wire's `to_input` rewrites on\n  both endpoints; the canvas re-renders with the new label without\n  losing the connection.\n- **Typo'd a name to something the function doesn't expect**: this\n  is the intentional tradeoff from issue 208. The runtime error\n  surfaces clearly rather than silently skipping.",
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete (canvas-overlay reverted; name editing in inspector,\nvalue moved below name+variadic row)\n\n## Scope changed twice\n\n**First pass** (canvas-overlay version): moved the editable name\ninput out of the inspector and onto a DOM overlay floating next to\nthe box's input dot.\n\n**Why that was wrong**:\n1. The `<input>` overlay captured pointer events on the box body;\n   users dragging a box from near a port dot landed on the field\n   instead and entered text-edit mode.\n2. The overlay text was frozen at one screen size — it didn't\n   scale with zoom.\n\n**Final design**: keep names on the canvas as plain `ctx.fillText`\nlabels (scale with zoom, ignore clicks). Names are also editable in\nthe inspector — same identity displayed in two places, so the user\nsees what's there at a glance and can edit when the inspector is\nopen. The inspector port row now spans two lines: name + variadic\ntoggle on top, value on a wider second line below, so the value\n(often the longest entry) gets the full sidebar width.\n\n## Implementation notes\n\n`assets/js/004-inspector.js::mk_port_display` rebuilt:\n- Top row: name `<input>` + optional `:type` span + variadic button.\n- Bottom row: full-width value `<input>`.\n- Variadic-slot names disable the name input — variadic ops own\n  the `<base>_<N>` pattern, and freeform renames break the group's\n  membership tracking. The disabled state visually softens the\n  field (no border, dim color) so it reads as \"managed by the\n  toggle\" rather than \"broken.\"\n- Name commit on blur / Enter; Escape reverts to the saved name.\n\n`004-inspector.js` exports `rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name)`:\n- Validation: non-empty, identifier-shaped (`^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$`),\n  unique within the box.\n- Rewrites `to_input` on every wire targeting the port (both\n  endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson from 217).\n- Re-renders the inspector if the renamed box is the one on\n  display.\n\n`002-boxes.js::draw_box` keeps the canvas-rendered port name label\n(it was briefly removed during the overlay experiment).\n\n`assets/js/009-box-overlays.js` and the matching CSS removed; the\noverlay layer is gone.\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Variadic slots can't be renamed in-inspector** — the field is\n  disabled. Toggle the group off if you need to break out of the\n  pattern.\n- **Renamed port had a wire**: the wire's `to_input` rewrites on\n  both endpoints; the canvas re-renders with the new label without\n  losing the connection.\n- **Typo'd a name to something the function doesn't expect**: this\n  is the intentional tradeoff from issue 208. The runtime error\n  surfaces clearly rather than silently skipping.",
    "replaceAll":false,
    "userModified":false
  },

Slots keep their existing indices when you remove a middle one. Auto-grow uses \"highest existing index + 1,\" so gaps are harmless.\n\n**Variadic toggle off not severing all wires** — fixed: now severs every incoming wire to the box (the previous code only matched wires whose port still fit `<base>_<N>`, so any slot you'd renamed escaped the sweep).\n\n**Variadic auto-grow sometimes not firing** — possibly related to the rename issue: a variadic slot renamed off-pattern stops counting toward `last_variadic_index`, and auto-grow then fires on a different slot than the user expects. Now that variadic slot names are disabled in the inspector (the field grays out), the pattern stays intact and auto-grow should fire reliably. If you can repro after this commit, let me know the exact sequence.\n\n**Syntax highlighting + external editor refresh** — `open_source_view` re-fetches every time you click \"view,\" so closing and re-clicking already shows the freshest content. You're right that the editor never *runs* the source — that happens at compile / interpret time, not at view time. The view button is the one path that needs current bytes, and it already does. No change needed.\n\n**Data boxes** — your read of them is more correct than the implementation. Right now the `data` kind is purely cosmetic: green badge, otherwise treated identically to `call` boxes by both schema and loader. There's no \"read a file and output its contents\" semantics — that's exactly what `libs/files.lua` (issue 216) now does, via a regular call box. So the `data` kind as it stands is a leftover category that doesn't earn its keep. Two reasonable next moves:\n\n1. **Drop it.** A call box pointing at `files.read_text` covers the whole \"load a file, emit a string\" pattern, which is what you're describing. Aligned with no-globals — every file load is explicit and visible in the graph.\n2. **Repurpose it** as a dedicated read-only file source (no fn, just a path; runtime emits file contents). Saves a couple of clicks but doesn't add capability `files.read_text` lacks.\n\nI'd lean (1) — fewer concepts, and the existing data files used by `soramech-data` are fine as ordinary library calls. Want me to open an issue to remove the kind?\n\n**Inspector layout** — done in this commit. Two-row port block: name + variadic toggle on top, full-width value below. Names show on the canvas (read-only there) and edit in the inspector. Box body stays click-through for drag."

{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T23:09:07.468Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"When the user is panning with the middle mouse button, and they accidentally scroll a little, it starts zooming whenever they move the mouse. We should disable zoom while pan mode is currently active (when the middle mouse button is held down)\n\nWe should be able to click the FN entry to change what function the box is using. It should just take us to the final step of the \"browse\" pipeline, so if the user wants they could even go back up a step and pick an entirely different file if they wanted to. Also, we should make it look more like a button and less like a text entry field.\n\nCan you tell me how the variadic inputs are interpreted from the source files? Are we relying on a language spec? How would we define that sort of thing in a language spec? What happens if the provider function box provides more values than we're expecting? What happens if it provides fewer?\n\nIn the REF field, we shouldn't have the file-path because it'll be too long. Let's just do the filename, and strip the extension.\n\nSo, just to confirm, there's no way to rename input ports now, we stripped out that functionality right? I don't think it's actually necessary, it was just a user tag anyway.\n\nIf the user tries to remove the final iterator output, it should just toggle off the iterator functionality.\n\n  2. Repurpose it as a dedicated read-only file source (no fn, just a path; runtime emits file contents). Saves a couple of clicks but\n  doesn't add capability files.read_text lacks.\n\nI think this is what we should do. I think it does add capability - it makes the reading of files a language agnostic thing. That could be helpful. We should of course also have a language agnostic WRITING of files as well, which just takes in a string and a file path and writes to that path. Are there any concerns about making it language agnostic or will that design work? If so, can you make an issue file for it in phase 2?",

      "content":"// Canvas viewport: pan + zoom, and the per-frame draw transform.\n//\n// Coordinate model\n//   screen pixel (sx, sy)  ←→  world point (wx, wy)\n//     sx = wx * zoom + pan_x\n//     wx = (sx - pan_x) / zoom\n//\n// `pan_x` / `pan_y` are screen-pixel offsets passed to ctx.translate\n// AFTER scaling: the world is scaled around its origin first, then the\n// result is shifted on screen. They\n// only meet in two functions: world_to_screen and screen_to_world.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  let zoom  = 1;\n  let pan_x = 0;\n  let pan_y = 0;\n\n  let dirty = true;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return { x: wx * zoom + pan_x, y: wy * zoom + pan_y };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return { x: (sx - pan_x) / zoom, y: (sy - pan_y) / zoom };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // -- Pan: middle-click drag, or space + left-click drag.\n  // Pan math is in screen pixels: pan_{x,y} += mouse_delta_in_screen_pixels.\n  // The pan anchors record the state at mousedown so each mousemove\n  // computes the pan from the original anchor, not incrementally — that\n  // way no error accumulates over a long drag.\n  let panning          = false;\n  let pan_anchor_mouse = null;\n  let pan_anchor_pan   = null;\n\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true;  });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      panning          = true;\n      pan_anchor_mouse = mouse_pos(e);\n      pan_anchor_pan   = { x: pan_x, y: pan_y };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (!panning) return;\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    pan_x = pan_anchor_pan.x + (m.x - pan_anchor_mouse.x);\n    pan_y = pan_anchor_pan.y + (m.y - pan_anchor_mouse.y);\n    mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { panning = false; });\n\n  // -- Zoom: scroll wheel, anchored on the cursor.\n  // The world point under the cursor stays under the cursor across zoom\n  // changes. After updating zoom we solve the screen-equation for the\n  // new pan offset:\n  //     m.x = w.x * zoom + pan_x   →   pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n\n    // Direction by sign of deltaY: up (negative) zooms in, down zooms out.\n    const factor   = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    const new_zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, zoom * factor));\n    zoom = new_zoom;\n\n    pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom;\n    pan_y = m.y - w.y * zoom;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  // Backward-compatible `cam` accessor. They\n// only meet in two functions: world_to_screen and screen_to_world.\n\nconst Canvas = (() => {\n  const el  = document.getElementById('canvas');\n  const ctx = el.getContext('2d');\n\n  let zoom  = 1;\n  let pan_x = 0;\n  let pan_y = 0;\n\n  let dirty = true;\n\n  // {{{ resize\n  function resize() {\n    el.width  = window.innerWidth  - (document.getElementById('sidebar').offsetWidth || 0);\n    el.height = window.innerHeight;\n    dirty = true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ world_to_screen\n  function world_to_screen(wx, wy) {\n    return { x: wx * zoom + pan_x, y: wy * zoom + pan_y };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ screen_to_world\n  function screen_to_world(sx, sy) {\n    return { x: (sx - pan_x) / zoom, y: (sy - pan_y) / zoom };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mark_dirty\n  function mark_dirty() { dirty = true; }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ start_frame\n  // Reset the transform, clear, then set up the world-drawing transform.\n  // The explicit setTransform reset is defensive — guarantees no leftover\n  // matrix state can affect this frame even if a previous restore was missed.\n  function start_frame() {\n    if (!dirty) return false;\n    dirty = false;\n    ctx.setTransform(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0);\n    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, el.width, el.height);\n    ctx.save();\n    ctx.translate(pan_x, pan_y);\n    ctx.scale(zoom, zoom);\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ end_frame\n  function end_frame() { ctx.restore(); }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mouse_pos\n  function mouse_pos(e) {\n    const r = el.getBoundingClientRect();\n    return { x: e.clientX - r.left, y: e.clientY - r.top };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // -- Pan: middle-click drag, or space + left-click drag.\n  // Pan math is in screen pixels: pan_{x,y} += mouse_delta_in_screen_pixels.\n  // The pan anchors record the state at mousedown so each mousemove\n  // computes the pan from the original anchor, not incrementally — that\n  // way no error accumulates over a long drag.\n  let panning          = false;\n  let pan_anchor_mouse = null;\n  let pan_anchor_pan   = null;\n\n  let space_down = false;\n  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = true;  });\n  window.addEventListener('keyup',   e => { if (e.code === 'Space') space_down = false; });\n\n  el.addEventListener('mousedown', e => {\n    if (e.button === 1 || (e.button === 0 && space_down)) {\n      panning          = true;\n      pan_anchor_mouse = mouse_pos(e);\n      pan_anchor_pan   = { x: pan_x, y: pan_y };\n      e.preventDefault();\n    }\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => {\n    if (!panning) return;\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    pan_x = pan_anchor_pan.x + (m.x - pan_anchor_mouse.x);\n    pan_y = pan_anchor_pan.y + (m.y - pan_anchor_mouse.y);\n    mark_dirty();\n  });\n\n  window.addEventListener('mouseup', () => { panning = false; });\n\n  // -- Zoom: scroll wheel, anchored on the cursor.\n  // The world point under the cursor stays under the cursor across zoom\n  // changes. After updating zoom we solve the screen-equation for the\n  // new pan offset:\n  //     m.x = w.x * zoom + pan_x   →   pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom\n  el.addEventListener('wheel', e => {\n    e.preventDefault();\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n\n    // Direction by sign of deltaY: up (negative) zooms in, down zooms out.\n    const factor   = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    const new_zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, zoom * factor));\n    zoom = new_zoom;\n\n    pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom;\n    pan_y = m.y - w.y * zoom;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });\n\n  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);\n  resize();\n\n  // Backward-compatible `cam` accessor. External modules read `cam.zoom`\n  // for hit-test tolerance scaling. `cam.x` / `cam.y` here expose the new\n  // screen-pixel pan offsets; that's a semantic change from the previous\n  // world-space camera, but no current consumer outside this module reads\n  // those two — only `cam.zoom`.\n  const cam = {\n    get x()     { return pan_x; },\n    set x(v)    { pan_x = v; mark_dirty(); },\n    get y()     { return pan_y; },\n    set y(v)    { pan_y = v; mark_dirty(); },\n    get zoom()  { return zoom;  },\n    set zoom(v) { zoom  = v;  mark_dirty(); },\n  };\n\n  return { el, ctx, cam, world_to_screen, screen_to_world, mark_dirty,\n           start_frame, end_frame, mouse_pos };\n})();\n",

Middle-click\n    // pans tend to nudge the wheel as a side effect; without this guard\n    // the canvas zooms unexpectedly mid-pan.\n    if (panning) return;\n\n    const m = mouse_pos(e);\n    const w = screen_to_world(m.x, m.y);\n\n    // Direction by sign of deltaY: up (negative) zooms in, down zooms out.\n    const factor   = e.deltaY < 0 ? 1.1 : 0.9;\n    const new_zoom = Math.max(0.15, Math.min(5, zoom * factor));\n    zoom = new_zoom;\n\n    pan_x = m.x - w.x * zoom;\n    pan_y = m.y - w.y * zoom;\n    mark_dirty();\n  }, { passive: false });",

      "content":"  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ render\n  // Renders the full file browser into container.\n  // on_select(filename, fn_obj) called when the user picks a function.\n  // Groups: [{label, path?, files:[string], fetch_file: async fn(filename)->text}]\n  async function render(container, on_select) {\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n\n    // collapsed state: set of group labels\n    const collapsed = new Set();\n\n    // all browseable dirs come from one endpoint — src/ is no longer a special case\n    let src_dirs = [];\n    try {\n      src_dirs = await API.list_extra_src().catch(() => []);\n    } catch (e) {\n      container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note error\">load error: ' + e.message + '</div>';\n      return;\n    }\n\n    // build group list — every entry has a path; no exceptions\n    const groups = [];\n    (src_dirs || []).forEach(d => {\n      if (d.files && d.files.length > 0) {\n        groups.push({\n          label:      d.label + '/',\n          path:       d.path,\n          files:      d.files,\n          fetch_file: f => API.get_extra_src_file(d.index, f),\n        });\n      }\n    });\n\n    const show_file_list = () => {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n\n      // add-library-dir button\n      const add_btn = document.createElement('button');\n      add_btn.textContent = '+ library dir';\n      add_btn.className   = 'fb-add-dir-btn';\n      add_btn.onclick = () => {\n        // open picker at parent of last known dir so the user lands near recent work\n        const last = groups.length > 0 ? groups[groups.length - 1].path : null;\n        const initial = last ? (last.replace(/\\/[^/]+$/, '') || '/') : '/home';\n        show_dir_picker(container,\n          async (path) => {\n            try {\n              const meta = await API.get_meta();\n              // derive current list from groups, not meta.src_dirs:\n              // groups already reflects the server-migrated state (extra_src_dirs + src/),\n              // whereas meta.src_dirs is absent on old maps and would discard prior entries\n              const current = groups.map(g => g.path);\n              if (!current.includes(path)) {\n                current.push(path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: current });\n              }\n              render(container, on_select);\n            } catch(e) {\n              show_file_list();\n              const note = document.createElement('div');\n              note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n              note.textContent = 'could not save dir: ' + e.message;\n              container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n            }\n          },\n          () => show_file_list(),\n          initial\n        );\n      };\n      container.appendChild(add_btn);\n\n      if (groups.length === 0) {\n        const note = document.createElement('div');\n        note.className   = 'fb-note';\n        note.textContent = 'src/ is empty — add source files or a library dir';\n        container.appendChild(note);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      groups.forEach(group => {\n        // use full path as the collapse key for extra dirs so same-named dirs don't share state\n        const collapse_key = group.path || group.label;\n        const is_collapsed = collapsed.has(collapse_key);\n\n        // group header row with toggle\n        const hdr = document.createElement('div');\n        hdr.className = 'fb-group-hdr';\n\n        const toggle = document.createElement('span');\n        toggle.className   = 'fb-group-toggle';\n        toggle.textContent = is_collapsed ? '▶' : '▼';\n        hdr.appendChild(toggle);\n\n        const lbl = document.createElement('span');\n        lbl.className   = 'fb-header';\n        lbl.textContent = group.label;\n        hdr.appendChild(lbl);\n\n        hdr.onclick = () => {\n          if (collapsed.has(collapse_key)) collapsed.delete(collapse_key);\n          else collapsed.add(collapse_key);\n          show_file_list();\n        };\n\n        // right-click on any dir header: offer \"hide directory\"\n        hdr.addEventListener('contextmenu', e => {\n          e.preventDefault();\n          show_fb_ctx_menu(e.clientX, e.clientY, [{\n            label:  'hide directory',\n            danger: true,\n            action: async () => {\n              try {\n                const meta = await API.get_meta();\n                // same migration rationale as add: use groups as source of truth\n                const dirs = groups.map(g => g.path).filter(p => p !== group.path);\n                await API.put_meta({ ...meta, src_dirs: dirs });\n                render(container, on_select);\n              } catch (err) {\n                show_file_list();\n                const note = document.createElement('div');\n                note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n                note.textContent = 'could not hide dir: ' + err.message;\n                container.insertBefore(note, container.firstChild);\n              }\n            },\n          }]);\n        });\n"
    }

Jumps straight to the function picker for the\n  // file at `ref`, with a back button that unwinds to the full\n  // browser. Useful when the user wants to pick a different function\n  // from the same file without re-walking the directory tree.\n  async function render_at_fn_list(container, ref, on_select) {\n    if (!ref) {\n      // No ref to land on — open the full browser instead.\n      return render(container, on_select);\n    }\n\n    container.innerHTML = '<div class=\"fb-note\">loading…</div>';\n    const stripped = ref.replace(/^src\\//, '');\n\n    let content = null;\n    let error_msg = null;\n\n    // Mirror fetch_source's resolution order: main src/ first, then\n    // each extra dir in turn. The first successful fetch wins.\n    try {\n      content = await API.get_src_file(stripped);\n    } catch (e) { /* try extras */ }\n\n    if (content === null) {\n      let extras = [];\n      try { extras = await API.list_extra_src(); } catch (e) {}\n      for (let i = 0; i < (extras || []).length; i++) {\n        try { content = await API.get_extra_src_file(i, stripped); break; }\n        catch (e) {}\n      }\n    }\n\n    if (content === null) {\n      container.innerHTML = '';\n      const note = document.createElement('div');\n      note.className   = 'fb-note error';\n      note.textContent = 'source not found: ' + ref;\n      container.appendChild(note);\n      const back = document.createElement('button');\n      back.className   = 'fb-back';\n      back.textContent = '← browse';\n      back.onclick     = () => render(container, on_select);\n      container.appendChild(back);\n      return;\n    }\n\n    const fns = parse_functions(content, stripped);\n    render_fn_list(container, stripped, fns,\n      (f, fn) => on_select(f, fn),\n      () => render(container, on_select));\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  return { parse_functions, render, render_at_fn_list };\n})();",

Updates the\n  // port name in box.inputs and rewrites `to_input` on every wire\n  // (both endpoints, mutating in place per the stale-cache lesson\n  // from 217). Reverses the read-only-name decision from issue 208;\n  // tradeoff: a typo desynchronizes the box from the function it\n  // calls, but the resulting runtime error surfaces clearly rather\n  // than silently skipping (issue 224).\n  //\n  // Validation: name must be a non-empty identifier-shaped string and\n  // unique within the box's inputs. Variadic-slot names (`base_N`)\n  // are accepted; the editor uses that shape internally and won't\n  // confuse it with a user rename because the variadic operations\n  // own the rename path for those cases.\n  async function rename_port(box, port_idx, new_name) {\n    const port = box.inputs && box.inputs[port_idx];\n    if (!port) return false;\n    const old_name = port.name;\n    if (old_name === new_name) return false;\n\n    if (!new_name || !/^[A-Za-z_]\\w*$/.test(new_name)) {\n      status_msg('invalid port name: must start with a letter or _', 'error');\n      return false;\n    }\n    if (box.inputs.some((p, i) => i !== port_idx && p.name === new_name)) {\n      status_msg('duplicate port name \"' + new_name + '\"', 'error');\n      return false;\n    }\n\n    port.name = new_name;\n\n    // Rewrite every wire that targeted the old name (on both\n    // endpoints).\n    const my_id = box.id;\n    const upstream_ids = new Set();\n    (box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.to_box === my_id && c.to_input === old_name) {\n        c.to_input = new_name;\n        upstream_ids.add(c.from_box);\n      }\n    });\n    for (const up_id of upstream_ids) {\n      const up = Boxes.boxes[up_id];\n      if (!up) continue;\n      (up.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n        if (c.to_box === my_id && c.to_input === old_name) {\n          c.to_input = new_name;\n        }\n      });\n      try { await API.put_box(up_id, up); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('rename: failed to update ' + up_id + ':', e.message); }\n    }\n\n    try { await API.put_box(box.id, box); }\n    catch (e) {\n      status_msg('rename save failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n      return false;\n    }\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    // Refresh the inspector's read-only name label so it reflects the\n    // new name immediately (it caches text on show — without this the\n    // user would see the old name in the sidebar until they re-clicked\n    // the box).\n    if (current_box && current_box.id === box.id) {\n      show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n    }\n    return true;\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ mk_port_display"
        },

    "content":[{

        "name":"Write",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "content":"# 229 — Data box: a language-agnostic file source (and a paired file sink)\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nThe `data` kind is recognized by the schema (`call` and `data` are\nthe two valid kinds) and accepted by the loader, but it has no\nruntime semantics distinct from `call`. It carries a `ref` and an\n`fn` like a call box and runs through whichever language driver\nmatches the file extension. The only difference is the green badge\non the canvas — pure cosmetic.\n\nA user reading the editor reasonably expects `data` to mean \"read\nsome data, emit it\" — \"if it walks like a duck…\" — but the current\nimplementation doesn't deliver that. `libs/files.lua::read_text`\ncovers the actual \"read a text file\" need (issue 216, complete) via\na regular call box.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nRepurpose the `data` kind into a **language-agnostic file source**.\nA data box has:\n- `ref` — an absolute or map-relative path to a file on disk.\n- **No `fn`** — the dispatch layer is the function.\n- **No inputs** — emits whenever its successors fire.\n- A single output wire carrying the file's contents.\n\nThe runtime reads the file at the dispatch layer, encodes the bytes\nas a string (UTF-8), and pushes the value onto the output wire. No\nlanguage driver is invoked. Same shape as the iterator box (issue\n221): kind says \"call,\" presence of a routing field marks the box\nas a primitive the dispatch layer handles directly.\n\n### Why language-agnostic matters\n\nA user writing a Bash function that needs file contents shouldn't\nhave to wire through a Lua read box — and vice versa.     "content":[{
        "type":"text",
        "text":"Done. Now your variadic questions and confirmations:\n\n**Variadic-input detection from source.** Currently it's the file browser's parser in `007-filebrowser.js`, plain JS — not a language spec.\n\n- **Lua**: `parse_lua` matches `function M.name(p1, p2, ...)` and pulls each comma-separated param as one input port. The literal Lua variadic `...` shows up as a port literally named `...`; clicking \"var\" on it renames to `args_0` (the base becomes `args`).\n- **Bash**: `parse_bash_inputs` scans for `local var=\"$N\"` and bare `$N` references, takes the highest N as the arg count. `\"$@\"` / `$#` aren't detected — user marks the port variadic manually.\n- **C**: no parser yet (lexer ships in 223 for highlighting only).\n\nSo variadic-ness is **a user tag**, not a parsed-from-source signal. The \"var\" button records the user's intent in `box.variadic_inputs`.\n\n**Defining it in a language spec (phase 3, issue 303).** The natural extension is for each language spec to expose a `parse_signature(source) → { inputs, outputs, variadic_base? }` callback. The Lua spec would map `...` to `variadic_base = 'args'`; the Bash spec would map `\"$@\"` to `variadic_base = 'args'`; the C spec would map `va_list` / `...` similarly. The editor would auto-flip the variadic toggle when the parser reports a variadic tail. None of that exists yet — phase 2's parser is hand-rolled in JS, and the user's \"var\" toggle is the source of truth.\n\n**Provider provides MORE values than expected.** Doesn't happen in the current model. Each wire carries one value; a variadic group is N wires into N distinct slots. There's no \"spread\" — a source box can't fan one value out into multiple variadic slots. If you want fan-in to a variadic group, you wire N sources to the N slots manually.\n\n**Provider provides FEWER (some slots empty).** A slot with no wire and no literal value resolves to `nil` on the Lua side (or empty string on the Bash side). The receiving function gets the empty/nil arg. Whether that's a runtime error depends on the function — `text.concat(\"\\n\", a, nil, c)` works fine; a function that does `string.upper(b)` with `b=nil` errors.\n\n**Strict-mode for missing args**: doesn't exist. Worth opening if it bites — the natural place is the dispatch layer (issue 304), which already validates input presence per the per-task slot store (issue 302).\n\n---\n\n**Confirmation on input port renames** — yes, gone. Names are read-only labels in the inspector now (just committed). The `rename_port` helper is removed, the variadic-disabled gymnastics gone too. The \"var\" toggle still owns slot naming; user-driven freeform rename is no longer a concept.\n\n**229 opened** — data-box-as-language-agnostic-file-source, with a paired write sink. Captured the design (path field replaces ref/fn, dispatch layer handles read/write directly, no language driver), the migration question for legacy data boxes, the binary-data wrinkle (recommend explicit reject for now), and why JSON parsing belongs to a downstream box rather than to the data box itself. The sink-kind name is the one open bikeshed."
      }]
  },

{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-09T23:19:14.540Z",
  "message":{
    "content":"  Variadic-input detection from source. Currently it's the file browser's parser in 007-filebrowser.js, plain JS — not a language spec.\n\n  - Lua: parse_lua matches function M.name(p1, p2, ...) and pulls each comma-separated param as one input port. The literal Lua variadic ...\n  shows up as a port literally named ...; clicking \"var\" on it renames to args_0 (the base becomes args).\n  - Bash: parse_bash_inputs scans for local var=\"$N\" and bare $N references, takes the highest N as the arg count. \"$@\" / $# aren't detected\n  — user marks the port variadic manually.\n  - C: no parser yet (lexer ships in 223 for highlighting only).\n\n  So variadic-ness is a user tag, not a parsed-from-source signal. The \"var\" button records the user's intent in box.variadic_inputs.\n\n\nwhere is this language specific code implemented? The only place we should be un-agnostic is in the language spec.\n\n  Defining it in a language spec (phase 3, issue 303). The natural extension is for each language spec to expose a parse_signature(source) →\n  { inputs, outputs, variadic_base? } callback. The Lua spec would map ... to variadic_base = 'args'; the Bash spec would map \"$@\" to\n  variadic_base = 'args'; the C spec would map va_list / ... similarly. The editor would auto-flip the variadic toggle when the parser\n  reports a variadic tail. None of that exists yet — phase 2's parser is hand-rolled in JS, and the user's \"var\" toggle is the source of\n  truth.\n\n\nIt's okay if the user's \"var\" toggle is the source of truth. We just need to find a way to interpret what the truth actually means.\n\n  Provider provides FEWER (some slots empty). A slot with no wire and no literal value resolves to nil on the Lua side (or empty string on\n  the Bash side). The receiving function gets the empty/nil arg. Whether that's a runtime error depends on the function — text.concat(\"\\n\",\n  a, nil, c) works fine; a function that does string.upper(b) with b=nil errors.\n\n\nwhere do we define that? In the language spec? When passing values (like nil) between two languages, how do we resolve them?",
    "role":"user"
  },
