    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/233-unified-routing-schema.md",
    "content":"# 233 — Unified `routing` schema for branching boxes\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nTwo different ways to express \"this box has multiple output\nbranches and only fires one per invocation,\" depending on which\nflavor:\n\n- **Comparator**: per-box `comparand: \"<number>\"` field. Output\n  branches are fixed `lt` / `eq` / `gt`. The function still runs;\n  the dispatch layer compares the function's output against\n  `comparand` to pick a branch.\n- **Iterator**: per-box `iterator_outputs: [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"]` field.\n  Output branches are user-named. No function runs; the dispatch\n  layer routes the input to `outputs[counter % N]` (counter from a\n  `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot, issue 302).\n\nBoth are \"branching boxes\" with different routing rules. The\nschema makes them look like unrelated features.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\nparameters:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"worker_a\",\"worker_b\",\"worker_c\"] } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n  \"inputs\": [...] }\n  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n```\n\nAbsence of `routing` means plain call (single unconditional output\nwire). Presence means branched output, with the routing kind\ndeciding how the branch is picked.\n\n### Comparator: kind=\"comparator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"<number-as-string>\" }\n```\n\nFunction runs. Dispatch compares the function's output against\n`comparand`; fires `lt` / `eq` / `gt` branch.\n\n### Iterator: kind=\"iterator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"] }\n```\n\nNo function runs (or function runs and its output passes through\n— design decision below). Dispatch reads a `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`\nslot via `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, len(outputs))`; fires the\nnamed branch at that index.\n\n### Future kinds\n\n- `kind: \"function_decided\"`: function returns `(value, branch_tag)`;\n  dispatch fires the branch tagged. Reserved name; not implemented\n  by phase 3 unless we need it.\n- `kind: \"user_router\"`: spec callback decides the branch given\n  inputs and current state. Reserved.\n\nThe `routing.kind` field is the one place new routing types plug\nin.\n\n## Iterator + function: open question\n\nCurrently iterator boxes have no `ref` / `fn` — they're routing-\nonly. The user has expressed interest in \"functions iterating\ntheir own outputs\" (a function-backed iterator). Two possible\nsemantics under the unified schema:\n\n1. **Iterator passes input through unchanged** (current). The\n   function would be a no-op; not allowed. Box has no `ref`/`fn`.\n2. **Iterator runs function, routes function's output** (new).\n   Box has `ref`/`fn`; function runs; output goes to\n   `outputs[counter % N]`. Counter still drives routing, but the\n   value being routed is the function's return.\n\n(2) is more general and includes (1) as a special case (identity\nfunction). It composes with comparator's structure (function runs,\noutput gets routed). The dispatch action becomes:\n\n```\n1. Read inputs.\n2. If box has ref/fn: invoke spec, take output.\n   Else (iterator-only): take the popped input value.\n3. Pick branch via routing.kind:\n     comparator → compare(value, comparand) → lt/eq/gt\n     iterator   → slot_read_inc(counter_slot, N)\n4. Push value to outputs[picked branch].\n```\n\nThis unifies both paths and makes iterator-with-function natural.\n\nRecommendation: ship (2). The editor can default new iterator\nboxes to no-function (the simple case), but allow attaching a\nfunction via the existing `ref`/`fn` controls.\n\n## Schema migration\n\nExisting maps:\n- Boxes with `comparand` and no `routing` field → migrate to\n  `routing: { kind: \"comparator\", comparand }` at load time.\n- Boxes with `iterator_outputs` and no `routing` field → migrate\n  to `routing: { kind: \"iterator\", outputs: iterator_outputs }`.\n- Plain call boxes (no `comparand`, no `iterator_outputs`) → no\n  routing field, no migration needed.\n\nMigration runs in the loader, in memory. Editor saves migrated\nboxes back to disk on next edit. Old `comparand` / `iterator_outputs`\nfields are accepted on read (legacy) but written under `routing`.\n\n## Inspector UI\n\nA `routing` selector in the inspector replaces the separate\n`compare` toggle and `iterator` toggle:\n\n```\nmode:    [plain ▾ | comparator | iterator]\n```\n\nWhen `comparator` selected: show `comparand` text input + lt/eq/gt\noutput dots.\nWhen `iterator` selected: show editable `outputs` slot list with\nauto-grow (current iterator UI). Optionally allow ref/fn (for the\nfunction-backed iterator semantics if option (2) ships).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua`: accept `routing` field; legacy `comparand`\n   and `iterator_outputs` accepted on read, validated as\n   equivalent.\n2. `src/003-loader.lua` (phase 2 path): migrate legacy fields into\n   `routing` on load.\n3. `src/005-http-server.lua`: PUT handler accepts both shapes\n   (canonical and legacy) and stores canonical.\n4. Phase 3 graph loader (issue 305): same migration.\n5. `assets/js/004-inspector.js`: new mode dropdown replacing the\n   two separate toggles. Conditional UI per `routing.kind`.\n6. `assets/js/002-boxes.js`: render branches based on\n   `routing.kind`.\n7. `assets/js/006-wires.js`: connection's `from_branch` matches\n   `routing.outputs[i]` or `lt`/`eq`/`gt`.\n8. Phase 3 dispatch (issue 304): branch on `routing.kind` for the\n   branch-selection step. Routing logic consolidates from two\n   paths to one.\n\n## Why now\n\n- Editor inspector keeps gaining toggles per routing kind. The function still runs;\n  the dispatch layer compares the function's output against\n  `comparand` to pick a branch.\n- **Iterator**: per-box `iterator_outputs: [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"]` field.\n  Output branches are user-named. The\nschema makes them look like unrelated features.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\nparameters:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"worker_a\",\"worker_b\",\"worker_c\"] } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n  \"inputs\": [...] }\n  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n```\n\nAbsence of `routing` means plain call (single unconditional output\nwire). Presence means branched output, with the routing kind\ndeciding how the branch is picked.\n\n### Comparator: kind=\"comparator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"<number-as-string>\" }\n```\n\nFunction runs. Dispatch compares the function's output against\n`comparand`; fires `lt` / `eq` / `gt` branch.\n\n### Iterator: kind=\"iterator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"] }\n```\n\nNo function runs (or function runs and its output passes through\n— design decision below). Dispatch reads a `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`\nslot via `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, len(outputs))`; fires the\nnamed branch at that index.\n\n### Future kinds\n\n- `kind: \"function_decided\"`: function returns `(value, branch_tag)`;\n  dispatch fires the branch tagged.         "type":"text",
        "text":"Done. Summary:\n\n**Atomic-counter slot** — added to 302 as `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` mode + `slot_read_inc(slot, mod)` op. The slot's \"cell\" is just an atomic uint32 under the hood; the read op atomically fetches-and-adds, returns mod N. Iterator counter moves into this slot; box state loses its `counter` field. Iterators now parallel by default — concurrent `slot_read_inc` calls give each task a unique routing index.\n\n**304** updated to read counter via `slot_read_inc` mid-action rather than at spawn. Task struct shrinks to just `{ box_id }` — no per-task counter snapshot needed because the slot itself is the source of truth.\n\n**Issue 233** opened for Level B: unified `routing: { kind, ... }` field replacing separate `comparand` and `iterator_outputs`. Includes:\n- Schema migration plan for legacy maps (loader-side, transparent).\n- Inspector `mode` dropdown replacing the two separate toggles.\n- An open question about function-backed iterators (recommendation: support; the dispatch flow naturally accommodates \"function runs, output gets routed\" for both comparator and iterator).\n- Level C explicitly noted as deferred follow-on.\n\nSpec interface stays clean — the spec sees only `invoke(bytes_in) → bytes_out`, no awareness of routing or branches. Routing decisions are dispatch-layer concerns; counter values are slot-store concerns. The user-facing concept of \"branching boxes\" is editor + map-file knowledge.\n\nWhere do you want to go next? Implementation order of phase 2 issues we've opened (229, 230, 231, 233), or another design thread to chase?"
      }]

    "snippet":"1\t# 233 — Unified `routing` schema for branching boxes\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Current behavior\n7\t\n8\tTwo different ways to express \"this box has multiple output\n9\tbranches and only fires one per invocation,\" depending on which\n10\tflavor:\n11\t\n12\t- **Comparator**: per-box `comparand: \"<number>\"` field. Output\n13\t  branches are fixed `lt` / `eq` / `gt`. The function still runs;\n14\t  the dispatch layer compares the function's output against\n15\t  `comparand` to pick a branch.\n16\t- **Iterator**: per-box `iterator_outputs: [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"]` field.\n17\t  Output branches are user-named. No function runs; the dispatch\n18\t  layer routes the input to `outputs[counter % N]` (counter from a\n19\t  `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot, issue 302).\n20\t\n21\t-- so in this model, the function WOULD run for the iterative box.\n22\t   basically it's taking a box that already exists, has a function, and is in\n23\t   all respects a perfectly normal box. Then, we add the iterative tag to it\n24\t   (or similar, according to how we do the same for comparator boxes) and then\n25\t   we treat it's outputs, and only it's outputs, differently. For the compare\n26\t   style, we send it's output (if it's a number) to one of three different\n27\t   destinations depending on if it's less than, equal to, or greater than the\n28\t   comparand value. For an iterator, we send it to a different destination in\n29\t   turn, in a round-robin fashion.\n30\t\n31\t-- the iterator is still running a function, just the same as the comparator is.\n32\t   the difference between an iterator and a regular box is that we're round-robin\n33\t   style sending the output to multiple destinations, one at a time.\n34\t\n35\t-- if we wanted to send the output to multiple destinations all at once, each\n36\t   time, we'd just pull several wires out of the same output port. That\n37\t   functionality already exists as far as I know.\n38\t\n39\tBoth are \"branching boxes\" with different routing rules. The\n40\tschema makes them look like unrelated features.\n41\t\n42\t## Intended behavior\n43\t\n44\tA single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\n45\tparameters:\n46\t\n47\t```json\n48\t{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n49\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n50\t  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n51\t  \"inputs\": [...],\n52\t  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n53\t\n54\t{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n55\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n56\t  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"worker_a\",\"worker_b\",\"worker_c\"] } }\n57\t\n58\t{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n59\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n60\t  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n61\t  \"inputs\": [...] }\n62\t  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n63\t```\n64\t\n65\tAbsence of `routing` means plain call (single unconditional output\n66\twire). Presence means branched output, with the routing kind\n67\tdeciding how the branch is picked.\n68\t\n69\t### Comparator: kind=\"comparator\"\n70\t\n71\t```json\n72\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"<number-as-string>\" }\n73\t```\n74\t\n75\tFunction runs. Dispatch compares the function's output against\n76\t`comparand`; fires `lt` / `eq` / `gt` branch.\n77\t\n78\t### Iterator: kind=\"iterator\"\n79\t\n80\t```json\n81\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"outputs\": [\"a\",\"b\",\"c\"] }\n82\t```\n83\t\n84\tNo function runs (or function runs and its output passes through\n85\t— design decision below). Dispatch reads a `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER`\n86\tslot via `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, len(outputs))`; fires the\n87\tnamed branch at that index.\n88\t\n89\t### Future kinds\n90\t\n91\t- `kind: \"function_decided\"`: function returns `(value, branch_tag)`;\n92\t  dispatch fires the branch tagged. Reserved name; not implemented\n93\t  by phase 3 unless we need it.\n94\t\n95\t-- we can't demand or support any alterations to the functions themselves.\n96\t   we should have no idioms that are implemented outside of the editor\n97\t   - or at least, no idioms that are implemented in the library source code.\n98\t\n99\t- `kind: \"user_router\"`: spec callback decides the branch given\n100\t  inputs and current state. Reserved.\n101\t\n102\t-- I don't see how this one would be a good addition. Any other ideas?\n103\t   how about a randomizer? an iterator that sends it's output to a random slot.\n104\t   how about a distributor, that sends an output to the least busy output slot?\n105\t   how about a weighted iterator, that sends 80% of it's outputs to one slot and\n106\t   20% to another? user definable percentages and output port counts of course.\n107\t   there's lots of options. Think along these lines.\n108\t\n109\tThe `routing.kind` field is the one place new routing types plug\n110\tin.\n111\t\n112\t## Iterator + function: open question\n113\t\n114\tCurrently iterator boxes have no `ref` / `fn` — they're routing-\n115\tonly. The user has expressed interest in \"functions iterating\n116\ttheir own outputs\" (a function-backed iterator). Two possible\n117\tsemantics under the unified schema:\n118\t\n119\t1. **Iterator passes input through unchanged** (current). The\n120\t   function would be a no-op; not allowed. Box has no `ref`/`fn`.\n121\t2. **Iterator runs function, routes function's output** (new).\n122\t   Box has `ref`/`fn`; function runs; output goes to\n123\t   `outputs[counter % N]`. Counter still drives routing, but the\n124\t   value being routed is the function's return.\n125\t\n126\t-- option 2 is the one we want.\n127\t\n128\t(2) is more general and includes (1) as a special case (identity\n129\tfunction). It composes with comparator's structure (function runs,\n130\toutput gets routed). The dispatch action becomes:\n131\t\n132\t```\n133\t1. Read inputs.\n134\t2. If box has ref/fn: invoke spec, take output.\n135\t   Else (iterator-only): take the popped input value.\n136\t3. Pick branch via routing.kind:\n137\t     comparator → compare(value, comparand) → lt/eq/gt\n138\t     iterator   → slot_read_inc(counter_slot, N)\n139\t4. Push value to outputs[picked branch].\n140\t```\n141\t\n142\tThis unifies both paths and makes iterator-with-function natural.\n143\t\n144\tRecommendation: ship (2). Phase 3 dispatch (issue 304): branch on `routing.kind` for the\n   branch-selection step. Routing logic consolidates from two\n   paths to one.\n\n## Why now\n\n- Editor inspector keeps gaining toggles per routing kind. A\n  unified mode dropdown scales linearly with kinds; separate\n  toggles don't.\n- Phase 3 dispatch will naturally have a \"select branch\" step;\n  routing it through `routing.kind` is the same code regardless\n  of whether we ship Level B now or refactor later.\n- Schema migration is cheap to do once, expensive to leave for\n  later when more maps exist.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts new field\n- `src/003-loader.lua` — legacy migration on load\n- `src/005-http-server.lua` — PUT handler accepts both shapes\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — mode dropdown\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — branch rendering\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — branch matching\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — counter slot mechanism\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer reads\n  `routing.kind`\n- `issues/completed/210-comparator-wire-branching.md` — original\n  comparator design (likely missing/named differently; dig the\n  history)\n- `issues/completed/221-iterator-box.md` — original iterator\n  design\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Function-backed iterator** semantics — (1) or (2) above.\n  Recommendation: (2).     "content":"# 233 — Unified `routing` schema for branching boxes\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Concept\n\nA \"branching box\" is a regular call box whose output, after the\nfunction runs, is sent to **one of several** downstream\ndestinations rather than to all of them. Same function, same\ninputs, same output value — only the routing decision differs.\nCurrently we have two flavors:\n\n- **Comparator**: routes the function's output by comparing it\n  to a stored threshold. Three fixed branches (`lt` / `eq` /\n  `gt`).\n- **Iterator**: routes the function's output to one of N branches\n  in round-robin fashion, advancing a counter on every call.\n\nThe two are the same shape (function runs → output gets routed)\nwith different rules for picking the branch. The current schema\nhas them as separate top-level fields (`comparand` and\n`iterator_outputs`), which makes them look like unrelated\nfeatures. They aren't.\n\n(For \"send the same value to multiple destinations,\" the user\njust pulls multiple wires out of a single output port — fan-out\nalready works on plain call boxes. No routing decision needed.)\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\nparameters:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/dispatch_msg.lua\", \"fn\": \"dispatch_msg\",\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n  \"inputs\": [...] }\n  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n```\n\nAbsence of `routing` means plain call: one output wire, fires\nunconditionally on every invocation. Presence means branched\noutput, with `routing.kind` deciding which branch fires per call.\n\n**The function always runs**, regardless of routing kind. The\nfunction produces the value; routing decides where the value\ngoes.\n\n### kind=\"comparator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"<number>\" }\n```\n\nThree output ports: `lt`, `eq`, `gt` (fixed names; ports aren't\nrenameable per the editor's port-immutability rule). The\nfunction's output value is compared to `comparand`; the matching\nbranch fires.\n\n#### Multi-band comparator (planned brainstorm)\n\nThe current 3-branch lt/eq/gt design is a special case of \"value\nfalls into a numeric range, fire the corresponding branch.\" A\ngeneralization:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\": \"comparator\",\n  \"thresholds\": [3, 7, 11, 17]\n}\n```\n\nFive output ports get named by the threshold positions —\n`below_3`, `between_3_7`, `between_7_11`, `between_11_17`,\n`above_17`. With `thresholds: [4]` this becomes the current\n3-branch lt/eq/gt (with `eq` being \"exactly 4\"), so the legacy\nshape is one configuration of the new one.\n\nEquality cases (`x == 3` exactly) fall to the lower band by\nconvention; an explicit `eq` band could be added per threshold\nif needed.\n\nDefer the schema specifics — the existing 3-branch case ships\nfirst; multi-band is a follow-on once we have a use case that\nactually needs more than three.\n\n### kind=\"iterator\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n```\n\n`n_outputs` output ports, named conventionally (`out_0`, `out_1`,\n…). Every invocation reads the box's `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot\nvia `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)`; that index picks\nthe branch.\n\nThe function still runs and produces the routed value. Iterator\ndefaults the function to a passthrough identity if the user\nhasn't picked a `ref` / `fn` — but the user is free to attach\nany function whose output should be round-robin-distributed.\n\n### kind=\"randomizer\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"randomizer\", \"n_outputs\": 4 }\n```\n\nPicks a branch uniformly at random per invocation.\nImplementation: hash the counter-slot value into the branch\nindex, so the distribution is deterministic-given-seed but\nspread across branches.\n\n```c\nuint32_t i = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, UINT32_MAX);\nuint32_t branch = hash(i) % n_outputs;\n```\n\n`hash` is a cheap mixing function (xorshift, FNV); not\ncryptographic. The point is breaking up the monotonic counter so\nconsecutive calls don't go to consecutive branches.\n\n### kind=\"weighted\"\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\":    \"weighted\",\n  \"weights\": [0.8, 0.2]\n}\n```\n\nProbability-based distribution. With `[0.8, 0.2]` and two output\nports, 80% of invocations fire branch 0, 20% fire branch 1.\n\nImplementation: at compile time, weights are normalized into a\ncumulative table on a `0..PRECISION-1` integer scale (e.g.\n`PRECISION = 1000`). Per call:\n\n```c\nuint32_t r = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, PRECISION);\n// pre-computed cumulative: [0..799] → branch 0, [800..999] → branch 1\nuint32_t branch = lookup_band(r, cumulative_table);\n```\n\nSame counter-slot machinery as iterator and randomizer; the\ndifference is the mapping from counter to branch.\n\n### kind=\"distributor\" (load-aware)\n\n```json\n\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"distributor\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n```\n\nSends the value to the **least-busy** downstream consumer:\ninspects the fill levels of the input slots wired to each branch\nand picks the branch whose downstream slot has the fewest queued\nvalues.\n\nImplementation: dispatch action peeks the `tail - head` count on\neach downstream input slot and picks the minimum. Tied branches\nfall back to atomic-counter round-robin so ties don't always go\nto the same branch.\n\nThis is the only routing kind that's not purely\nself-contained — it reads downstream slot state — but it doesn't\nadd any new dispatch-layer concept beyond querying slot fill\n(which the slot store already knows).\n\n### Future kinds\n\nThe pattern is: any new routing kind plugs in at one place\n(`routing.kind` value + dispatch-layer branch picker). All\nexisting kinds and any future ones live entirely in the dispatch\nlayer + slot store + editor — never in language specs, never in\nuser-written functions.\n\n## Iterator + function: ships as \"function always runs\"\n\nIterator boxes always run their function. The dispatch action\nbecomes uniform across routing kinds:\n\n```\n1. Read inputs (pop / peek per port mode).\n2. Invoke spec (always — function runs regardless of routing kind).\n3. Pick branch via routing.kind:\n     comparator   → compare(output, comparand)\n     iterator     → slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)\n     randomizer   → hash(slot_read_inc(counter_slot, MAX)) % n_outputs\n     weighted     → cumulative lookup\n     distributor  → argmin(downstream fill)\n     (no routing) → fan to all outgoing wires\n4. Push function output to outputs[picked branch] (or all wires if\n   no routing).\n```\n\nA single dispatch path for all branching boxes; the routing rule\nplugs into step 3.\n\n## Schema migration\n\nFew enough existing maps that we can hand-migrate them. The\nloader does **not** carry a legacy-shape adapter; once this\nships, all map files are expected to use the `routing` field. If\na map with the old shape is opened, the schema validator rejects\nit and the user (or a one-off migration script) updates it.\n\nIf we end up wanting a one-off script, it walks `maps/<name>/boxes/*.json`\nand rewrites:\n- `comparand: X` → `routing: { kind: \"comparator\", comparand: X }`\n- `iterator_outputs: [...]` → `routing: { kind: \"iterator\", n_outputs: len(...) }`\n- everything else → no change\n\nBut for the current map count, manual edits are faster than\nwriting the script.\n\n## Inspector UI\n\nA `routing` selector in the inspector replaces the separate\n`compare` toggle and `iterator` toggle:\n\n```\nmode:    [plain ▾ | comparator | iterator | randomizer | weighted | distributor]\n```\n\nPer-kind controls below the dropdown:\n- **plain**: nothing extra.\n- **comparator**: numeric `comparand` input. (Multi-band UI is\n  the brainstorm above; ships single-threshold first.)\n- **iterator**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n- **randomizer**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n- **weighted**: editable list of weight values (one per output);\n  N derived from list length.\n- **distributor**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n\nOutput ports re-render to match the routing kind: 1 dot for\nplain, 3 fixed dots (lt/eq/gt) for comparator, N dots for the\ncounter-based kinds. Port names follow the routing kind's\nconvention; not user-renameable (issue 224's read-only-port-name\nrule).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua`: accept `routing` field; reject legacy\n   `comparand` and `iterator_outputs` shapes.\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js`: mode dropdown replacing the two\n   toggles; per-kind controls.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js`: render branches based on\n   `routing.kind`.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js`: connection's `from_branch` matches\n   the routing kind's port naming.\n5. Phase 3 dispatch (issue 304): branch on `routing.kind` for the\n   branch-selection step. Five rule paths (one per kind shipped),\n   plus the no-routing-field plain path.\n\nHand-migrate existing maps before merging.\n\n## Why now\n\n- Editor inspector keeps gaining toggles per routing kind. A\n  unified mode dropdown scales linearly with kinds; separate\n  toggles don't.\n- Phase 3 dispatch will naturally have a \"select branch\" step;\n  routing it through `routing.kind` is the same code regardless\n  of whether we ship Level B now or refactor later.\n- The new routing kinds (randomizer, weighted, distributor) only\n  make sense in the unified schema. Adding them as separate\n  top-level fields would be unmaintainable.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts new field\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — mode dropdown\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — branch rendering\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — branch matching\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — counter slot mechanism\n  used by iterator / randomizer / weighted\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer's branch\n  picker dispatches on `routing.kind`\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Distributor under fan-out**: if a branch wire goes to\n  multiple consumers (fan-out), the \"fill level\" of that branch\n  is ambiguous. Use the max of the consumers' fills, or the sum,\n  or something else. Probably max — the bottleneck is the\n  slowest consumer.\n- **Multi-band comparator threshold edges**: `x == threshold`\n  goes to which side of the cut? Lean toward \"less-than-or-equal\"\n  for consistency. Need to nail down before implementation.\n- **Weighted ties**: floating-point weights summing to `1.0`\n  doesn't always discretize cleanly. Compile-time normalization\n  picks an integer scale (1000) and rounds; the last band\n  absorbs any leftover so the ranges always sum to PRECISION.\n\n## Level C example (deferred)\n\nThe big follow-on after this issue ships is a fully data-driven\nrouter: one dispatch path that reads a small rule expression\nfrom the box JSON and evaluates it. Example shape:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\": \"rules\",\n  \"rules\": [\n    { \"when\": \"output < 3\",                   \"to\": \"small\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 3 and output < 7\",   \"to\": \"medium\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 7\",                  \"to\": \"large\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe dispatch layer ships a small expression evaluator (a few\ndozen lines: variables = `output`, `counter`, `fill[i]`;\noperators = comparisons, boolean conjunction, arithmetic). Every\nexisting routing kind reduces to a \"rules\" expression:\n\n- comparator → three rules with `when: output < c / output == c / output > c`\n- iterator → one rule using `counter % N` as the band index\n- randomizer → one rule using `hash(counter) % N`\n- weighted → cumulative-band rules\n\nThe benefit: one code path in dispatch instead of five. Custom\nrouting without writing a spec callback or modifying user\nfunctions. The cost: a small evaluator (still entirely in C, no\nspec involvement).\n\nWorth pursuing once Level B has shipped and we have real maps\nusing the kinds — at that point the consolidation is concrete\nrather than speculative. Open as a separate issue when ready.\n"
  },

Adding them as separate\n  top-level fields would be unmaintainable.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts new field\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — mode dropdown\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — branch rendering\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — branch matching\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — counter slot mechanism\n  used by iterator / randomizer / weighted\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer's branch\n  picker dispatches on `routing.kind`\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Distributor under fan-out**: if a branch wire goes to\n  multiple consumers (fan-out), the \"fill level\" of that branch\n  is ambiguous. Use the max of the consumers' fills, or the sum,\n  or something else. Probably max — the bottleneck is the\n  slowest consumer.\n- **Multi-band comparator threshold edges**: `x == threshold`\n  goes to which side of the cut? Lean toward \"less-than-or-equal\"\n  for consistency. Need to nail down before implementation.\n- **Weighted ties**: floating-point weights summing to `1.0`\n  doesn't always discretize cleanly. Compile-time normalization\n  picks an integer scale (1000) and rounds; the last band\n  absorbs any leftover so the ranges always sum to PRECISION.\n\n## Level C example (deferred)\n\nThe big follow-on after this issue ships is a fully data-driven\nrouter: one dispatch path that reads a small rule expression\nfrom the box JSON and evaluates it. Example shape:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\": \"rules\",\n  \"rules\": [\n    { \"when\": \"output < 3\",                   \"to\": \"small\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 3 and output < 7\",   \"to\": \"medium\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 7\",                  \"to\": \"large\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe dispatch layer ships a small expression evaluator (a few\ndozen lines: variables = `output`, `counter`, `fill[i]`;\noperators = comparisons, boolean conjunction, arithmetic). Every\nexisting routing kind reduces to a \"rules\" expression:\n\n- comparator → three rules with `when: output < c / output == c / output > c`\n- iterator → one rule using `counter % N` as the band index\n- randomizer → one rule using `hash(counter) % N`\n- weighted → cumulative-band rules\n\nThe benefit: one code path in dispatch instead of five. Custom\nrouting without writing a spec callback or modifying user\nfunctions. The cost: a small evaluator (still entirely in C, no\nspec involvement).\n\nWorth pursuing once Level B has shipped and we have real maps\nusing the kinds — at that point the consolidation is concrete\nrather than speculative. Open as a separate issue when ready.\n",

Dispatch by box mode\nThe action now branches on the box's mode:\n\n- **Plain call box**: proceed to phase 4 (invoke) and phase 5 (write\n  output) as below.\n- **Comparator box**: a call box that *also* carries a `comparand`\n  field. The function still runs (phase 4 + 5 happen), so the box\n  has a `ref` / `fn` like any other call box. The difference shows\n  up at routing time (phase 7): instead of one output wire, three\n  branches `lt` / `eq` / `gt` are available, and the dispatch layer\n  picks which one to fire by comparing the function's *output value*\n  to `comparand`. The function is unchanged from a plain call box's\n  perspective; it just produced the value the routing layer compares.\n- **Iterator box**: skip invoke entirely. Copy the input value\n  straight into the output slot, and proceed to phase 7. Iterators\n  have no `ref` / `fn`; the routing-by-counter is the entire point\n  of the box.\n\nIterator semantics live in the dispatch layer (no spec involvement).\nComparator semantics live partly in the dispatch layer (the\noutput-vs-comparand comparison and branch fire) and partly in the\nspec (the function still runs to produce the value being compared).\n\n### 4. Invoke (plain call AND comparator call boxes)",
    "newString":"### 3. Dispatch is uniform across routing kinds\n\nEvery call box runs its function (phase 4) and pushes the\nfunction's output (phase 5). The only thing that varies is which\ndownstream branch receives the push (phase 5b — the branch-pick).\n\nBoxes carry an optional `routing` field (issue 233):\n- No `routing`: plain call. Function runs; output fans to all\n  outgoing wires unconditionally.\n- `routing.kind: \"comparator\"`: function runs; output is\n  compared to `comparand`; only the matching `lt` / `eq` / `gt`\n  branch fires.\n- `routing.kind: \"iterator\"`: function runs; output is routed to\n  `outputs[slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)]`.\n- `routing.kind: \"randomizer\" / \"weighted\" / \"distributor\"`:\n  function runs; output is routed by the kind-specific rule.\n\nThe function always runs. There is no \"iterator skips invoke\"\ncase — the iterator differs from a plain call only in how the\nfunction's output is routed, not in whether the function runs.\nIterators that want passthrough behavior use an identity function\n(or the editor defaults to one when no `ref`/`fn` is set).\n\n### 4. Invoke (every call box)",

      "content":"\n### 5. Write output (push to downstream input slots)\n\nOutput is a routing event. The action walks the box's outgoing\nconnection list and calls `slot_push(downstream.input_slot,\noutput_buf, output_size)` for each one — copying the output bytes\ninto every consumer's input slot.\n\nFor comparator boxes: only push to the connection whose\n`from_branch` matches the lt/eq/gt result. For iterator boxes:\nonly push to the connection whose `from_branch` matches\n`iterator_outputs[counter]`.\n\nAfter each push, the spawn-on-input-ready check (issue 302) fires\non the receiving box. If that push completes its input set, a\nfresh task spawns for the consumer.\n\n### 6. (No phase 6)\n\nSlots are durable for the run; tasks don't unref. Run termination\nis governed by the pool's active-task counter (issue 301). The\ndispatch action goes from phase 5 directly to phase 7.\n\n### 7. Post-action: nothing for the action itself\n\nRouting happened in phase 5. The iterator counter was already\nincremented at task **spawn** time, not here — the spawn-time\natomic increment is what makes parallel iterator tasks possible\n(see \"Iterator counter and parallel iteration\" below). All boxes\ndo nothing in phase 7."

        "content":"258\t\n259\t## Comparator vs iterator vs plain call\n260\t\n261\tThree box modes drive routing differently:\n262\t\n263\t| Mode        | Output kind   | Invoke spec? | Routing behavior                                                    |\n264\t|-------------|---------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|\n265\t| Plain call  | single value  | yes          | fire all outgoing connections                                       |\n266\t| Comparator  | passthrough   | no           | dispatch layer compares input to threshold, fires lt / eq / gt only |\n267\t| Iterator    | passthrough   | no           | fire connection matching counter, increment counter, re-spawn       |\n268\t\n269\tThe dispatch action branches on box mode early (phase 3) and\n270\tdispatches into the appropriate helper. Three small functions, not a\n271\tsingle switch, keep each mode's logic isolated.\n272\t\n273\t## Open questions\n274\t\n275\t(none currently — earlier questions resolved as follows:)\n276\t\n277\t- Output buffer sizing: heap-allocated to the box's declared output\n278\t  size at runtime. No fixed cap. Variable-size outputs go through the\n279\t  large-value heap (issue 302).\n280\t- Queued-input slot lifetime: producers hold refs while alive,\n281\t  consumer holds a ref while consuming, slot freed when all drop.\n282\t  References are the producer-liveness tracking mechanism.",
        "type":"tool_result"

      "content":"\n## Comparator vs iterator vs plain call\n\nThree box modes drive routing differently:\n\n| Mode        | Output kind   | Invoke spec? | Routing behavior                                                    |\n|-------------|---------------|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|\n| Plain call  | single value  | yes          | fire all outgoing connections                                       |\n| Comparator  | passthrough   | no           | dispatch layer compares input to threshold, fires lt / eq / gt only |\n| Iterator    | passthrough   | no           | fire connection matching counter, increment counter, re-spawn       |\n\nThe dispatch action branches on box mode early (phase 3) and\ndispatches into the appropriate helper. Three small functions, not a\nsingle switch, keep each mode's logic isolated.\n\n## Open questions\n\n(none currently — earlier questions resolved as follows:)\n\n- Output buffer sizing: heap-allocated to the box's declared output\n  size at runtime. No fixed cap. Variable-size outputs go through the\n  large-value heap (issue 302).\n- Queued-input slot lifetime: producers hold refs while alive,\n  consumer holds a ref while consuming, slot freed when all drop.\n  References are the producer-liveness tracking mechanism."

Routing kinds differ only in\nhow the function's output is dispatched to downstream\nconnections:\n\n| `routing.kind`   | Output ports        | Branch picker                                                |\n|------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|\n| (absent / plain) | single port         | fan to all outgoing connections                              |\n| `comparator`     | `lt` / `eq` / `gt`  | compare(output, comparand) → lt/eq/gt                        |\n| `iterator`       | `out_0` … `out_N-1` | `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, N)`                             |\n| `randomizer`     | `out_0` … `out_N-1` | `hash(slot_read_inc(counter_slot, MAX)) % N`                 |\n| `weighted`       | `out_0` … `out_N-1` | cumulative-band lookup against a counter scaled to PRECISION |\n| `distributor`    | `out_0` … `out_N-1` | argmin over downstream slot fill levels                      |\n\nPlain call (no `routing` field) skips the branch picker entirely\n— phase 5 fans the output to all wires. The function still runs\nthe same as for any branched call. Issue 233 carries the schema\nand the per-kind UI.",

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Done. Summary of what your annotations changed in 233:\n\n**Iterator runs its function** — no more \"iterator passes input through unchanged\" option. Every branching box runs its function; the routing kind only picks where the function's output goes. The ticket reads this as the canonical single behavior, not as one of two options.\n\n**Dropped speculative kinds** — `function_decided` and `user_router` are gone. Both leaked language-spec or function-author concerns into the routing layer; they violate \"routing logic is dispatch + editor only, never spec.\"\n\n**New kinds added per your brainstorm**:\n- `randomizer` — hash the atomic counter, mod N. Spread distribution from a deterministic-given-seed counter.\n- `weighted` — user-defined percentages per branch (e.g., `[0.8, 0.2]`); compile-time normalized to a cumulative band table; lookup against the counter scaled to a 1000-step precision.\n- `distributor` — argmin over downstream slot fill levels. Sends to the least-busy branch. Ties fall back to round-robin.\n\nAll three reuse the same `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` machinery introduced in 302 — they're variations on \"read the counter, do something kind-specific.\"\n\n**Multi-band comparator** captured as a brainstorm section (your range example: `< 3`, `3-7`, `7-11`, `11-17`, `> 17`). Defers schema specifics; ships single-threshold first; multi-band lands once a real use case demands it.\n\n**Migration simplified** — manual hand-edit of the existing maps; no loader-side legacy adapter. The schema validator can outright reject the old `comparand` / `iterator_outputs` shapes once the unified field ships.\n\n**Inspector port-naming** — comparator stays `lt/eq/gt`, iterator/randomizer/weighted/distributor use `out_0..out_N-1` conventions; ports are not renameable per the editor's existing rule (issue 224).\n\n**Level C example** — replaced the vague \"deferred follow-on\" with a concrete sketch: a `routing.kind: \"rules\"` with a list of `{ when: <expr>, to: <branch> }` evaluated by a small in-dispatch expression evaluator. Every existing kind reduces to a \"rules\" expression. Ships when Level B is in production and we have real maps showing the consolidation pays off.\n\n**304** updated to match: dispatch action runs the function for every call box; routing-kind table replaces the old plain/comparator/iterator three-mode framing; phase 3 (the old \"skip invoke for iterators\" branch) is gone — there's just one uniform path with a kind-specific branch picker in phase 5.\n\nWant to start implementing 233 now, or polish more of its open questions first (multi-band edges, distributor under fan-out, weighted ties)?"
      }]
  },

```json
{
  "timestamp":"2026-05-10T03:38:41.200Z",
  "uuid":"d9885575-3e2e-4f9b-b03d-35bee5c708cf",
  "userType":"external",
  "slug":"snug-booping-dove",

  "parentUuid":"261de90f-2911-4275-88e4-06471b6cfd3f",

  "type":"attachment",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "attachment":{
    "type":"edited_text_file",
    "snippet":"1\t# 233 — Unified `routing` schema for branching boxes\n2\t\n3\t## Status\n4\topen\n5\t\n6\t## Concept\n7\t\n8\tA \"branching box\" is a regular call box whose output, after the\n9\tfunction runs, is sent to **one of several** downstream\n10\tdestinations rather than to all of them. Same function, same\n11\tinputs, same output value — only the routing decision differs.\n12\tCurrently we have two flavors:\n13\t\n14\t- **Comparator**: routes the function's output by comparing it\n15\t  to a stored threshold. Three fixed branches (`lt` / `eq` /\n16\t  `gt`).\n17\t- **Iterator**: routes the function's output to one of N branches\n18\t  in round-robin fashion, advancing a counter on every call.\n19\t\n20\tThe two are the same shape (function runs → output gets routed)\n21\twith different rules for picking the branch. The current schema\n22\thas them as separate top-level fields (`comparand` and\n23\t`iterator_outputs`), which makes them look like unrelated\n24\tfeatures. They aren't.\n25\t\n26\t(For \"send the same value to multiple destinations,\" the user\n27\tjust pulls multiple wires out of a single output port — fan-out\n28\talready works on plain call boxes. No routing decision needed.)\n29\t\n30\t-- question, in an iterator / comparator box, if the user pulls multiple wires\n31\t   out of one of their output ports, does it also fan out for that case?\n32\t   for example, if the lt output port is called, and lt's output port goes to\n33\t   3 different boxes, will it arrive at all three? And if eq is called on a\n34\t   subsequent invocation, will it still just go to the destinations that eq is\n35\t   assigned?\n36\t\n37\t## Intended behavior\n38\t\n39\tA single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\n40\tparameters:\n41\t\n42\t```json\n43\t{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n44\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n45\t  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n46\t  \"inputs\": [...],\n47\t  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n48\t\n49\t{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n50\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n51\t  \"ref\": \"src/dispatch_msg.lua\", \"fn\": \"dispatch_msg\",\n52\t  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 } }\n53\t\n54\t{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n55\t  \"kind\": \"call\",\n56\t  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n57\t  \"inputs\": [...] }\n58\t  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n59\t```\n60\t\n61\tAbsence of `routing` means plain call: one output wire, fires\n62\tunconditionally on every invocation. Presence means branched\n63\toutput, with `routing.kind` deciding which branch fires per call.\n64\t\n65\t-- I'd prefer if we explicitely defined the routing variable. It's better to\n66\t   be consistent and explicit.\n67\t\n68\t**The function always runs**, regardless of routing kind. The\n69\tfunction produces the value; routing decides where the value\n70\tgoes.\n71\t\n72\t### kind=\"comparator\"\n73\t\n74\t```json\n75\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": \"<number>\" }\n76\t```\n77\t\n78\tThree output ports: `lt`, `eq`, `gt` (fixed names; ports aren't\n79\trenameable per the editor's port-immutability rule). The\n80\tfunction's output value is compared to `comparand`; the matching\n81\tbranch fires.\n82\t\n83\t#### Multi-band comparator (planned brainstorm)\n84\t\n85\tThe current 3-branch lt/eq/gt design is a special case of \"value\n86\tfalls into a numeric range, fire the corresponding branch.\" A\n87\tgeneralization:\n88\t\n89\t```json\n90\t\"routing\": {\n91\t  \"kind\": \"comparator\",\n92\t  \"thresholds\": [3, 7, 11, 17]\n93\t}\n94\t```\n95\t\n96\tFive output ports get named by the threshold positions —\n97\t`below_3`, `between_3_7`, `between_7_11`, `between_11_17`,\n98\t`above_17`. With `thresholds: [4]` this becomes the current\n99\t3-branch lt/eq/gt (with `eq` being \"exactly 4\"), so the legacy\n100\tshape is one configuration of the new one.\n101\t\n102\tEquality cases (`x == 3` exactly) fall to the lower band by\n103\tconvention; an explicit `eq` band could be added per threshold\n104\tif needed.\n105\t\n106\t-- we would have to. Maybe if we set the greater than and less than value to 3\n107\t   in that example, it'd resolve to an eq? As long as the editor faked it, we\n108\t   could handle it behind the scenes however we please...\n109\t\n110\tDefer the schema specifics — the existing 3-branch case ships\n111\tfirst; multi-band is a follow-on once we have a use case that\n112\tactually needs more than three.\n113\t\n114\t### kind=\"iterator\"\n115\t\n116\t```json\n117\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n118\t```\n119\t\n120\t`n_outputs` output ports, named conventionally (`out_0`, `out_1`,\n121\t…). Every invocation reads the box's `SLOT_ATOMIC_COUNTER` slot\n122\tvia `slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)`; that index picks\n123\tthe branch.\n124\t\n125\tThe function still runs and produces the routed value. Iterator\n126\tdefaults the function to a passthrough identity if the user\n127\thasn't picked a `ref` / `fn` — but the user is free to attach\n128\tany function whose output should be round-robin-distributed.\n129\t\n130\t### kind=\"randomizer\"\n131\t\n132\t```json\n133\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"randomizer\", \"n_outputs\": 4 }\n134\t```\n135\t\n136\tPicks a branch uniformly at random per invocation.\n137\tImplementation: hash the counter-slot value into the branch\n138\tindex, so the distribution is deterministic-given-seed but\n139\tspread across branches.\n140\t\n141\t```c\n142\tuint32_t i = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, UINT32_MAX);\n143\tuint32_t branch = hash(i) % n_outputs;\n144\t```\n145\t\n146\t`hash` is a cheap mixing function (xorshift, FNV); not\n147\tcryptographic. The point is breaking up the monotonic counter so\n148\tconsecutive calls don't go to consecutive branches.\n149\t\n150\t### kind=\"weighted\"\n151\t\n152\t```json\n153\t\"routing\": {\n154\t  \"kind\":    \"weighted\",\n155\t  \"weights\": [0.8, 0.2]\n156\t}\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\tProbability-based distribution. With `[0.8, 0.2]` and two output\n160\tports, 80% of invocations fire branch 0, 20% fire branch 1.\n161\t\n162\tImplementation: at compile time, weights are normalized into a\n163\tcumulative table on a `0..PRECISION-1` integer scale (e.g.\n164\t`PRECISION = 1000`). Per call:\n165\t\n166\t```c\n167\tuint32_t r = slot_read_inc(counter_slot, PRECISION);\n168\t// pre-computed cumulative: [0..799] → branch 0, [800..999] → branch 1\n169\tuint32_t branch = lookup_band(r, cumulative_table);\n170\t```\n171\t\n172\tSame counter-slot machinery as iterator and randomizer; the\n173\tdifference is the mapping from counter to branch.\n174\t\n175\t-- the UI for this could be a slider with a variable amount of knobs, each\n176\t   defining a range. A larger slice of the slider (which of course displays\n177\t   below in percentages, one per line, one line per knob) a larger slice means\n178\t   x% of the time it'll flow down that path.\n179\t\n180\t-- something like: \"output name, percentage\" per line\n181\t\n182\t### kind=\"distributor\" (load-aware)\n183\t\n184\t```json\n185\t\"routing\": { \"kind\": \"distributor\", \"n_outputs\": 3 }\n186\t```\n187\t\n188\tSends the value to the **least-busy** downstream consumer:\n189\tinspects the fill levels of the input slots wired to each branch\n190\tand picks the branch whose downstream slot has the fewest queued\n191\tvalues.\n192\t\n193\tImplementation: dispatch action peeks the `tail - head` count on\n194\teach downstream input slot and picks the minimum. Tied branches\n195\tfall back to atomic-counter round-robin so ties don't always go\n196\tto the same branch.\n197\t\n198\tThis is the only routing kind that's not purely\n199\tself-contained — it reads downstream slot state — but it doesn't\n200\tadd any new dispatch-layer concept beyond querying slot fill\n201\t(which the slot store already knows).\n202\t\n203\t### Future kinds\n204\t\n205\tThe pattern is: any new routing kind plugs in at one place\n206\t(`routing.kind` value + dispatch-layer branch picker). All\n207\texisting kinds and any future ones live entirely in the dispatch\n208\tlayer + slot store + editor — never in language specs, never in\n209\tuser-written functions.\n210\t\n211\t## Iterator + function: ships as \"function always runs\"\n212\t\n213\tIterator boxes always run their function. The dispatch action\n214\tbecomes uniform across routing kinds:\n215\t\n216\t```\n217\t1. Read inputs (pop / peek per port mode).\n218\t2. Invoke spec (always — function runs regardless of routing kind).\n219\t3. The dispatch action\nbecomes uniform across routing kinds:\n\n```\n1. Read inputs (pop / peek per port mode).\n2. Invoke spec (always — function runs regardless of routing kind).\n3. Pick branch via routing.kind:\n     comparator   → compare(output, comparand)\n     iterator     → slot_read_inc(counter_slot, n_outputs)\n     randomizer   → hash(slot_read_inc(counter_slot, MAX)) % n_outputs\n     weighted     → cumulative lookup\n     distributor  → argmin(downstream fill)\n     (no routing) → fan to all outgoing wires\n4. Push function output to outputs[picked branch] (or all wires if\n   no routing).\n```\n\nA single dispatch path for all branching boxes; the routing rule\nplugs into step 3.\n\n## Schema migration\n\nFew enough existing maps that we can hand-migrate them. The\nloader does **not** carry a legacy-shape adapter; once this\nships, all map files are expected to use the `routing` field. If\na map with the old shape is opened, the schema validator rejects\nit and the user (or a one-off migration script) updates it.\n\nIf we end up wanting a one-off script, it walks `maps/<name>/boxes/*.json`\nand rewrites:\n- `comparand: X` → `routing: { kind: \"comparator\", comparand: X }`\n- `iterator_outputs: [...]` → `routing: { kind: \"iterator\", n_outputs: len(...) }`\n- everything else → no change\n\nBut for the current map count, manual edits are faster than\nwriting the script.\n\n## Inspector UI\n\nA `routing` selector in the inspector replaces the separate\n`compare` toggle and `iterator` toggle:\n\n```\nmode:    [plain ▾ | comparator | iterator | randomizer | weighted | distributor]\n```\n\nPer-kind controls below the dropdown:\n- **plain**: nothing extra.\n- **comparator**: numeric `comparand` input. (Multi-band UI is\n  the brainstorm above; ships single-threshold first.)\n- **iterator**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n- **randomizer**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n- **weighted**: editable list of weight values (one per output);\n  N derived from list length.\n- **distributor**: `n_outputs` integer input.\n\nOutput ports re-render to match the routing kind: 1 dot for\nplain, 3 fixed dots (lt/eq/gt) for comparator, N dots for the\ncounter-based kinds. Port names follow the routing kind's\nconvention; not user-renameable (issue 224's read-only-port-name\nrule).\n\n## Suggested implementation sequence\n\n1. `src/001-schema.lua`: accept `routing` field; reject legacy\n   `comparand` and `iterator_outputs` shapes.\n2. `assets/js/004-inspector.js`: mode dropdown replacing the two\n   toggles; per-kind controls.\n3. `assets/js/002-boxes.js`: render branches based on\n   `routing.kind`.\n4. `assets/js/006-wires.js`: connection's `from_branch` matches\n   the routing kind's port naming.\n5. Phase 3 dispatch (issue 304): branch on `routing.kind` for the\n   branch-selection step. Five rule paths (one per kind shipped),\n   plus the no-routing-field plain path.\n\nHand-migrate existing maps before merging.\n\n-- when we implement, we should leave behind issue files for the additional\n   routing styles.\n\n## Why now\n\n- Editor inspector keeps gaining toggles per routing kind. A\n  unified mode dropdown scales linearly with kinds; separate\n  toggles don't.\n- Phase 3 dispatch will naturally have a \"select branch\" step;\n  routing it through `routing.kind` is the same code regardless\n  of whether we ship Level B now or refactor later.\n- The new routing kinds (randomizer, weighted, distributor) only\n  make sense in the unified schema. Adding them as separate\n  top-level fields would be unmaintainable.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — schema accepts new field\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — mode dropdown\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — branch rendering\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — branch matching\n- `issues/302-wire-value-slot-store.md` — counter slot mechanism\n  used by iterator / randomizer / weighted\n- `issues/304-task-dispatch-layer.md` — dispatch layer's branch\n  picker dispatches on `routing.kind`\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Distributor under fan-out**: if a branch wire goes to\n  multiple consumers (fan-out), the \"fill level\" of that branch\n  is ambiguous. Use the max of the consumers' fills, or the sum,\n  or something else. Probably max — the bottleneck is the\n  slowest consumer.\n- **Multi-band comparator threshold edges**: `x == threshold`\n  goes to which side of the cut? Lean toward \"less-than-or-equal\"\n  for consistency. Need to nail down before implementation.\n- **Weighted ties**: floating-point weights summing to `1.0`\n  doesn't always discretize cleanly. Compile-time normalization\n  picks an integer scale (1000) and rounds; the last band\n  absorbs any leftover so the ranges always sum to PRECISION.\n\n## Level C example (deferred)\n\nThe big follow-on after this issue ships is a fully data-driven\nrouter: one dispatch path that reads a small rule expression\nfrom the box JSON and evaluates it. Example shape:\n\n```json\n\"routing\": {\n  \"kind\": \"rules\",\n  \"rules\": [\n    { \"when\": \"output < 3\",                   \"to\": \"small\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 3 and output < 7\",   \"to\": \"medium\" },\n    { \"when\": \"output >= 7\",                  \"to\": \"large\" }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nThe dispatch layer ships a small expression evaluator (a few\ndozen lines: variables = `output`, `counter`, `fill[i]`;\noperators = comparisons, boolean conjunction, arithmetic). Every\nexisting routing kind reduces to a \"rules\" expression:\n\n- comparator → three rules with `when: output < c / output == c / output > c`\n- iterator → one rule using `counter % N` as the band index\n- randomizer → one rule using `hash(counter) % N`\n- weighted → cumulative-band rules\n\nThe benefit: one code path in dispatch instead of five. Custom\nrouting without writing a spec callback or modifying user\nfunctions. The cost: a small evaluator (still entirely in C, no\nspec involvement).\n\nWorth pursuing once Level B has shipped and we have real maps\nusing the kinds — at that point the consolidation is concrete\nrather than speculative.     "newString":"(For \"send the same value to multiple destinations,\" the user\njust pulls multiple wires out of a single output port — fan-out\nalready works on plain call boxes.           "type":"direct"
        },
        "input":{
          "new_string":"Every call box carries a `routing` field. No implicit defaulting:\nplain boxes have `routing: { \"kind\": \"plain\" }`, the same way\nbranched boxes carry their own kind. Explicit and consistent —\nno \"what if I forget the routing field\" surprises at validation\ntime.\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"plain\" } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/dispatch_msg.lua\", \"fn\": \"dispatch_msg\",\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 } }\n```\n\nFive shipped routing kinds: `plain`, `comparator`, `iterator`,\n`randomizer`, `weighted`, `distributor`. The `routing.kind` field\npicks which dispatch-layer rule decides the branch. Schema\nvalidates the kind value and the kind-specific parameters\ntogether.\n\n**The function always runs**, regardless of routing kind. The\nfunction produces the value; routing decides where the value\ngoes.",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/233-unified-routing-schema.md",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"A single `routing` field on the box, with kind-specific\nparameters:\n\n```json\n{ \"id\": \"score-router\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/score.lua\", \"fn\": \"score\",\n  \"inputs\": [...],\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"comparator\", \"comparand\": 4 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"round-robin\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"src/dispatch_msg.lua\", \"fn\": \"dispatch_msg\",\n  \"routing\": { \"kind\": \"iterator\", \"n_outputs\": 3 } }\n\n{ \"id\": \"plain-call\",\n  \"kind\": \"call\",\n  \"ref\": \"...\", \"fn\": \"...\",\n  \"inputs\": [...] }\n  // no routing field — single output wire, fires unconditionally\n```\n\nAbsence of `routing` means plain call: one output wire, fires\nunconditionally on every invocation. Presence means branched\noutput, with `routing.kind` deciding which branch fires per call.\n\n-- I'd prefer if we explicitely defined the routing variable. It's better to\n   be consistent and explicit.\n\n**The function always runs**, regardless of routing kind. The\nfunction produces the value; routing decides where the value\ngoes."
        },
        "id":"toolu_01Ue2B12rjJcdziAVDjK2syW"
      }]

        "type":"text",
        "text":"Done. Summary of the latest annotation pass:\n\n**Branch-level fan-out** — added a section clarifying that fan-out works on a per-branch basis. If the comparator's `lt` port has three wires, then each time the routing decision picks `lt`, all three wires fire (a copy is pushed into each consumer's slot). On the next invocation if `eq` is picked, only `eq`'s wires fire. Each branch port acts as its own little plain-output port when activated.\n\n**Always-explicit `routing` field** — removed the \"absence means plain\" default. Plain boxes carry `routing: { \"kind\": \"plain\" }` exactly the same way branched boxes carry `routing: { \"kind\": \"comparator\", ... }`. Schema rejects boxes without a routing field. New `kind=\"plain\"` section added.\n\n**Doubled-threshold equality** — folded your encoding into the multi-band comparator brainstorm. `thresholds: [3, 3]` means \"less than 3, exactly 3, greater than 3\" via a zero-width point band. This makes the legacy lt/eq/gt exactly `thresholds: [c, c]` — the editor can present a single-comparand UI but store the doubled form, so the dispatch layer has one consistent representation.\n\n**Weighted UI** — captured your slider+knob design with a per-port line: visual band in the middle, output port name on the left, percentage on the right. Knob drag updates percentages live; percentages are also directly editable.\n\n**Implementation scope tightened** — this issue ships **only** `plain`, `comparator`, and `iterator` (the surface area already in production). The other kinds (randomizer, weighted, distributor, multi-band comparator) get their own follow-on issue files opened at merge time. Designs stay in 233 for context but don't gate this issue's completion.\n\nThe dispatch table in 304 still lists all six kinds since it's a reference for the dispatch layer's eventual full surface area; 233 controls which of those land in phase 2.\n\nWant to start implementing 233 now, or open the four follow-on issue files first so the design gets preserved as separate trackable tickets?"
      }]
